# Notes on the Screen Presentation

You are reading this e-book in a file format (EPUB or Mobi) that makes the book content adaptable to the display options of your reading device and to your personal needs. That’s a great thing; but unfortunately not every device displays the content in the same way and the rendering of features such as pictures and tables or hyphenation can lead to difficulties. This e-book was optimized for the presentation on as many common reading devices as possible.

If you want to zoom in on a figure (especially in iBooks on the iPad), tap the respective figure once. By tapping once again, you return to the previous screen. You can find more recommendations on the customization of the screen layout on the [Service Pages](#service.xhtml).

# Introduction

This book contains short descriptions of the most important Linux commands for managing the file system, for starting and terminating processes, for editing text files, for other administrative tasks, and for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> programming. The book also summarizes the syntax of basic configuration files and contains a keyboard shortcut reference for the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">emacs</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nano</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vi</samp> editors, as well as some other interactive commands such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">info</samp>.

The aim of this book is to provide a compact reference work for using Linux in the terminal. The basic principle of this book is: less is more. The book cannot and is not intended to replace the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">info</samp> pages of complex commands! Thus, you will still have to look up or research exotic options yourself.

With this book, however, I’m trying to relieve you of the work of searching through the often dozens of pages of original documentation for options for everyday use. Numerous examples also show the basic use of a command at a glance.

Sometimes, you’re looking for a command for a specific task, but don't know its name or have just forgotten it. The thematically organized table of contents is intended for these cases.

Depending on which distribution you are using, some commands aren’t available by default and must be installed separately. There are also distribution-specific commands that are only available in certain distributions, such as the package management commands <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dpkg</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt</samp> (Debian, Ubuntu), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rpm</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yum</samp> (Fedora, Red Hat), and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zypper</samp> (SUSE). This is pointed out in the respective command description.

#### What Is a Command?

Linux doesn’t distinguish between commands (as described in this book) and programs such as Firefox, LibreOffice, or GIMP. Here, “command” refers to programs without a graphical user interface, which are usually executed in a terminal window.

In this book, I also describe some commands that aren’t real programs at all, but only commands of the currently active shell. I assume that you’re using the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp> (Bourne Again Shell) or the largely compatible <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zsh</samp>. These shells are used in most Linux distributions for the interactive execution of commands. An example of a shell command is <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp> to change the current directory.

#### Options

Most of the commands described in this book are controlled by options. The options are specified before all other parameters. There are two ways of notation for many commands: <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-x</samp> for short options (one letter) and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--xyz</samp> for long options (multiple letters).

Thus, the following two <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> commands are equivalent and display all files and directories in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr</samp> directory:

```
user$ ls -l -A /usr
user$ ls --format=long --almost-all /usr 
```

For some commands, multiple options can be specified as a group (i.e., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-ab</samp> instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-a -b</samp>). Some commands also work with options that are specified after the actual parameter(s). However, this shouldn’t lead you to the conclusion that this applies to all commands!

```
user$ ls -lA /usr
user$ ls /usr -lA 
```

For a few commands, the order of the parameters has an influence on how the command is executed. If options are specified that are logically mutually exclusive, the last option specified applies.

#### man, info, and help

To avoid making this book unnecessarily long, I’ll only describe the most important options. A complete overview of all options for the majority of commands is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command name --help</samp>. More detailed information is usually contained in the manual pages, which you can access via [](#05_001.xhtml_man)<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man 1</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>. For some commands, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> pages only contain a reference to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">info</samp> texts, which are displayed accordingly via [](#05_001.xhtml_info)<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>.

For commands that are directly integrated into the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp>), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> leads to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>. The command is actually described there, but searching through the very long documentation is tedious. In this context, it’s more helpful to use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">help</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>.

The help texts from <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">info</samp> sometimes overshoot the mark. If you’re just looking for a few examples of how to use a command, you should use either this book or the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tldr</samp> command. Incidentally, the command name stands for Too long, didn’t read. :-)

# Commands from A to Z

## A

### aa-complain program

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aa-complain</samp> command activates the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">complain</samp> mode for the AppArmor profile of the specified program. Rule violations are logged but not punished, that is, the program continues to run undisturbed.

Like all other <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aa-xxx</samp> commands, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aa-complain</samp> is only available for distributions that use the AppArmor security system (Debian, SUSE, and Ubuntu). On Ubuntu systems, the command can be found in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apparmor-utils</samp> package, which must be installed separately.

#### Example

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dovecot</samp> program is still monitored, but rule violations are only recorded in a logging file:

```
root# aa-complain /usr/sbin/dovecot
Setting /usr/sbin/dovecot to complain mode. 
```

### aa-disable program

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aa-disable</samp> deactivates the AppArmor profile for the specified program. The program is therefore no longer monitored by AppArmor. To reactivate this, you can use [aa-enforce](#A_001.xhtml_aa-enforce) or [aa-complain](#A_001.xhtml_aa-complain).

### aa-enforce program

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aa-complain</samp> command activates the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enforce</samp> mode for the AppArmor profile of the specified program. AppArmor thus prevents file or network access that is prohibited by AppArmor rules.

### aa-status [option]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aa-status</samp> provides a summary of the status of the AppArmor system. By specifying exactly one option from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--complaining</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--enabled</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--enforced</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--profiled</samp>, you can shorten the output to detailed information.

#### Example

AppArmor is active on the test computer. Although 50 rule profiles are loaded, only 5 of them actually monitor running programs.

```
root# aa-status
50 profiles are loaded.
48 profiles are in enforce mode.
   /snap/snapd/20674/usr/lib/snapd/snap-confine
   /snap/snapd/20674/.../mount-namespace-capture-helper
   /usr/bin/evince
   /usr/bin/evince-previewer
5 processes are in enforce mode.
   /usr/sbin/cups-browsed (856)
   /usr/sbin/cupsd (552)
   /usr/sbin/libvirtd (566) libvirtd
   /snap/snapd-desktop-.../snapd-desktop-integration (1902)
   /snap/snapd-desktop-.../snapd-desktop-integration (1975) 
```

### ack [options] search term

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp> is a variant of [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep) optimized for programmers and administrators. Unlike the original, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp> ignores GIT and SVN directories, backup files, and binary files. In many distributions, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp> can be found in the package of the same name or in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack-grep</samp>. Alternatively, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp> can also be installed as a Perl module (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cpan App::Ack</samp>).

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp> is compatible with [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep), but searches all files in the current directory recursively by default (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grep -r</samp>). The command is most frequently called in the forms <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp> search term or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack -i</samp> search term (not case-sensitive). A reference of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp>-specific options is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack --help</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man ack</samp>.

An alternative to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ack</samp> variant is the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ag</samp> command. Some distributions provide the command in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">silversearcher-ag</samp> package. Alternatively, you can clone the program from GitHub and then compile it yourself:

[https://github.com/ggreer/the_silver_searcher/wiki](https://github.com/ggreer/the_silver_searcher/wiki)

#### Example

The following example searches for files in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc</samp> that contain the search term <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">localhost</samp> and displays the corresponding hits together with the line numbers:

```
root# cd /etc
root# ack localhost
security/pam_env.conf
  52:# to "localhost" rather than not being set at all
  53:#REMOTEHOST  DEFAULT=localhost OVERRIDE=@{PAM_RHOST
  64:#NNTPSERVER  DEFAULT=localhost
speech-dispatcher/speechd.conf
  38:# for connections coming from localhost. If LocalhostAccessOnly is set
        to 0 it disables this
 199:#AudioNASServer "tcp/localhost:5450"
speech-dispatcher/modules/festival.conf
   7:#FestivalServerHost  "localhost"
... 
```

### acme.sh [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> is a script that helps with the installation of certificates. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> uses certificate authority (CA) [https://zerossl.com](https://zerossl.com) by default. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--server</samp> option can be used to set alternative CAs, including Let’s Encrypt ([https://letsencrypt.org](https://letsencrypt.org)).

The script is a useful alternative to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">certbot</samp> command, whose Python dependencies have often led to installation problems in the past.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> must also be installed. But this can be done with almost no effort:

```
user$ sudo apt/dnf/yum/zypper install curl socat
user$ curl https://get.acme.sh -o acme-setup
user$ less acme-setup    
(briefly check the script code)
user$ sudo sh acme-setup email=name@myhostname.com
  ...
  Installed to /root/.acme.sh/acme.sh
  Installing alias to '/root/.bashrc'
  OK, Close and reopen your terminal to start using acme.sh 
```

As part of the installation, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/spool/cron/root</samp> is extended by one line. This makes Cron take care of calling <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh --cron</samp> on a regular basis and thus automatically renewing all certificates set up by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--cron</samp>
    Renews all certificates installed via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> that are older than 60 days. The additional <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--force</samp> option can be used to force a premature renewal.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--install-cert -d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">domain</samp>

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[--cert-file</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path/to/certfile</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[--key-file</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path/to/keyfile</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[--fullchain-file</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path/to/fullchainfile</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[--reloadcmd "</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">systemctl restart httpd</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"]</samp>

    Copies the certificates previously generated with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh --issue</samp> to a location where the web server can access them and then restarts the web server. Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">systemctl restart httpd</samp>, you must enter a command suitable for your distribution to restart the web server.

    Note that it’s not advisable to copy the certificates stored in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/root/.acme.sh</samp> to another directory yourself. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> remembers the paths and the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reload</samp> command for automatic certificate renewal.

    <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> doesn’t change the configuration files of your web server! You must add the statements with the paths to the certificate files yourself.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--issue -d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">domain</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">webrootdir</samp>
    Sets up a certificate for the specified domain. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp> option can be used multiple times to create a certificate for related domains (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d a-company.com –d www.a-company.com</samp>). If you want a wildcard certificate, you need to pass <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d a-company.com -d *.a-company.com</samp>, for example. The certificates are saved in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/root/.acme.sh</samp> directory.

    If no web server is running on the computer, you should specify the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--standalone</samp> option instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">webrootdir</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> itself will then temporarily act as a web server. This assumes that port 80 isn’t blocked by any program.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--remove -d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">domain</samp>
    Deactivates the certificate renewal for the specified domain, which takes place automatically every 60 days. Although the name of the option suggests otherwise, the certificates themselves won’t be deleted. However, you can then delete the corresponding <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/root/.acme.sh/domain</samp> directory yourself.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--server letsencrypt|buypass|google|sslcom|zerossl</samp>
    Specifies the CA to be used. If this option isn’t used, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zerossl</samp> applies, that is, free certificates are obtained from [http://zerossl.com](http://zerossl.com).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--upgrade</samp>
    Updates the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp> script.

#### Example

The following commands generate a certificate for the domains <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">a-company.com</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">www.a-company.com</samp> and copy the certificates to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/acme-letsencrypt</samp> directory set up for this purpose:

```
root# mkdir /etc/acme-letsencrypt
root# acme.sh --issue --server letsencrypt -d a-company.com -w /var/www/html
  Your cert is in      /root/.acme.sh/a-company.com/a-company.com.cer
  Your cert key is in  /root/.acme.sh/a-company.com/a-company.com.key
  The intermediate CA cert is in      /root/.acme.sh/a-company.com/ca.cer
  And the full chain certs is there:  /root/.acme.sh/a-company.com/
                                      fullchain.cer
root# acme.sh --install-cert -d a-company.com \
         --cert-file      /etc/acme-letsencrypt/a-company.com.cert \
         --key-file       /etc/acme-letsencrypt/a-company.com.key \
         --fullchain-file /etc/acme-letsencrypt/a-company.com.fullchain
         --reloadcmd 'systemctl restart httpd'
  Installing cert to:       /etc/acme-letsencrypt/a-company.com.cert
  Installing key to:        /etc/acme-letsencrypt/a-company.com.key
  Installing full chain to: /etc/acme-letsencrypt/a-company.com.fullchain
  Run reload cmd: systemctl restart httpd
  Reload success 
```

#### Alternatives

In the past, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">certbot</samp> was often used instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acme.sh</samp>. This Python script is still in use, but often causes problems during installation. Another alternative is <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getssl</samp> (see [https://github.com/srvrco/getssl](https://github.com/srvrco/getssl)).

### acpi [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acpi</samp> provides information on the computer’s power supply:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Indicates whether the computer is connected to the power supply.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Indicates the battery status.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp>
    Displays the temperature of the battery.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-V</samp>
    Displays all available information.

### add-apt-repository ppa:name

The Ubuntu-specific <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">add-apt-repository</samp> command from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">software-properties- common</samp> package sets up a new package source for a personal package archive (PPA). PPAs are unofficial package sources from Ubuntu developers, which often contain the latest versions or developer versions of popular programs.

#### Example

The following command sets up a package source for the latest version of LibreOffice:

```
root# add-apt-repository ppa:libreoffice/ppa 
```

### addgroup [options] name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">addgroup</samp> sets up a new group on Debian and Ubuntu systems, taking into account the settings from [adduser](#A_001.xhtml_adduser). In Fedora and Red Hat, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">addgroup</samp> is a link to the [groupadd](#G_001.xhtml_groupadd) command with its own syntax.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--gid</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Assigns the specified GID (Group Identifier) to the group.

### adduser [options] name
adduser name group

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">adduser</samp> sets up a new user on Debian and Ubuntu systems, taking into account the settings from [etc/adduser.conf](#04_001.xhtml_adduser.conf). In particular, a group with the same name is created for each user and assigned to the new user. In the second syntax variant, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">adduser</samp> adds the existing user to an additional group.

In Fedora and Red Hat, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">adduser</samp> is a link to the [useradd](#U_001.xhtml_useradd) command, which means a different syntax applies there. On (open)SUSE, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">adduser</samp> isn’t available, and you have to use [useradd](#U_001.xhtml_useradd) instead.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--disabled-login</samp>
    Dispenses with the password prompt. It’s impossible to log in until the password has been set.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--gecos '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">full name</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp>
    Doesn’t ask for the full name, (office) room, phone numbers, and other information.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--group</samp>
    Only creates a new group (no user). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">adduser --group</samp> corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">addgroup</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--home</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp>
    Specifies the desired home directory if that isn’t supposed to be <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/home/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--system</samp>
    Sets up a system user. The UID is selected from the range for system users (usually 100–999), and the login is blocked (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/bin/false</samp> shell). No password can be entered. The system user is also not assigned a valid home directory. These precautionary measures are intended to prevent a misuse of the account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--uid</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Assigns the specified UID (User Identifier) to the user.

#### Example

The following command sets up the new user <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kofler</samp> on a Debian/Ubuntu system and then adds it to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirtd</samp> group:

```
root# adduser --gecos 'Michael Kofler' kofler
root# adduser kofler libvirtd 
```

To set up a user that can’t log in (e.g., for a mail account), you should proceed as follows:

```
root# adduser --shell /bin/false --gecos ,,, mailuser 
```

### alias abbreviation=command

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alias</samp> shell command defines a new abbreviation or displays an existing abbreviation. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alias</samp> is used without any other parameters, all defined abbreviations are displayed.

On Fedora and Red Hat systems, there are some predefined aliases for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>. These are loaded from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/root/.bashrc</samp> file when you log in.

#### Example

The following command defines the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ll</samp> abbreviation for the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls -l</samp> command:

```
user$ alias ll='ls -l' 
```

### alien [options] package file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alien</samp> converts the specified package file into a different format. The desired format is specified by the options <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--to-deb</samp> (Debian), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--to-rpm</samp> (RPM), or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--to-tgz</samp> (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">tar archive</samp>). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alien</samp> must be run by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp> so that the owners and access rights of the new packages are set correctly.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alien</samp> only works without problems for simple packages. However, if a package uses installation scripts or other specific features of the respective package format, the installation of the previously converted package will most likely fail.

### alsactl [options] [command] [card/id/device]

You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsactl</samp> to display, save, and restore the status of the audio system. The command also provides some advanced control options that aren’t available in the simpler [amixer](#A_001.xhtml_amixer) command.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsactl</samp> generally applies to all audio devices, unless you explicitly specify the number or the device name of the audio device when calling the command (see also the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/asound/cards</samp> file).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Runs <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsactl</samp> in the background. This option helps the init system to start <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsactl</samp> as a background service.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Specifies which file should be read by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">asactl</samp> or used for saving (by default, this is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/alsa/asound.state</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp>
    Uses the syslog service to log messages, warnings, and errors.

The most important commands of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsactl</samp> are listed here. There are a few other commands that are specifically intended for use as a background service and are rarely of interest for interactive calls or scripts.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">init</samp>
    Initializes the audio system with default settings.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">monitor</samp>
    Tracks all changes to the audio system and displays them until the command is ended using Ctrl+C.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">restore</samp>
    Restores a previously saved state of the audio system. The data is read from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/alsa/asound.state</samp> or from the file specified by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">store</samp>
    Saves the state of the audio system in the text file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/alsa/asound.state</samp> or in another file specified by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp>.

### alsamixer [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsamixer</samp> is an interactive command in which you can set the volume or recording level of the audio channels using the function and cursor keys. Esc terminates the program. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsamixer</samp> isn’t suitable for script programming. For this purpose, you can use [amixer](#A_001.xhtml_amixer).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Selects the desired audio card if there is more than one. The audio cards are numbered consecutively, starting with 0\. If necessary, you should take a look at the file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/asound/cards</samp>, which lists all audio cards.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-D</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Selects the audio system. For example, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-D pulse</samp> to change the PulseAudio system settings. Without this option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsamixer</samp> controls the ALSA system directly.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-V playback|capture|all</samp>
    Determines which controllers are initially displayed: for audio playback, for recording, or all of them. When <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alsamixer</samp> is running, you can switch between these display formats using F3, F4, and F5.

### alternatives [options] command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alternatives</samp> is the Red Hat or Fedora version of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">update-alternatives</samp>. The syntax of the two commands is largely identical and is described in the [update-alternatives](#U_001.xhtml_update-alternatives) command.

### amixer [options] [command]

You can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">amixer</samp> command to change the volume or level of the audio system channels by using options. If you want to adjust the volume or other settings interactively, you can use the [alsamixer](#A_001.xhtml_alsamixer) command with a simple, text-based user interface.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Selects the desired audio card. The audio cards are numbered consecutively, starting with 0\. If necessary, you can take a look at the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/#asound/cards</samp> file, which lists all audio cards. If the option is missing, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">amixer</samp> processes the default audio device.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-D</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Selects the audio system (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-D pulse</samp> for the PulseAudio system). Without this option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">amixer</samp> controls the ALSA system directly.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-q</samp>
    Doesn’t output the new status after the settings have been changed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp>
    Reads the commands to be executed from the standard input. Only the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sset</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cset</samp> commands are taken into account.

The following list describes the most important <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">amixer</samp> commands:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cget</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">id</samp>
    Indicates the status of a switch. The switch can be designated by one or more parameters, for example, as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">numid=3</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iface=MIXER,name='Headphone Playback Switch'</samp>. A list of all controls and switches, including the corresponding ID data, is created by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">amixer controls</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">controls|scontents|scontrols</samp>
    Lists all the controls and switches in varying degrees of detail and indicates their current status.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cset</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">id parameter</samp>
    Changes the status of a switch. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">amixer cset numid=3 1</samp> switches on the audio output on Raspberry Pi.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp>
    Displays a brief description of the audio card.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sget '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">',</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Returns the status of the specified control. Controls are described by a combination of character string and number, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'Master',0</samp>. The number is usually <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>, unless an audio card provides multiple controls with the same name, which are then numbered consecutively.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sset '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">',</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n parameter</samp>
    Changes the status of the control. In the simplest case, you can enter a percentage value as a parameter, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">50%</samp>. If it’s a stereo control, you can set the two channels separately using a pair of numbers, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">40%,55%</samp>. Alternatively, many controls that have the suffix <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dB</samp> can also be set in decibels, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-12.5dB</samp>.

    You can also use trailing plus or minus signs to change controls in relative terms. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">5%+</samp> increases the volume or recording level by five percentage points, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">5%-</samp> reduces the volume or level by five percentage points.

    You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mute</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">unmute</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">toggle</samp> to change the mute mode. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cap</samp> activates the recording (capture), while <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nocap</samp> deactivates this function.

    If the control supports multiple channels, you can select them with the additional parameters <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">front</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rear</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">center</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">woofer</samp>.

#### Example

On the test computer, the third audio device (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-c 2</samp>, the numbering starts with 0) is a USB headset. There are only two simple controls for controlling the headphones and the microphone. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">amixer sset</samp> then sets the headphones to a medium volume.

```
user$ amixer -c 2 scontrols
Simple mixer control 'Headphone',0
Simple mixer control 'Mic',0
user$ amixer -c 2 sset 'Headphone',0 50% unmute
Simple mixer control 'Headphone',0
  Capabilities: pvolume pswitch pswitch-joined
  Playback channels: Front Left - Front Right
  Limits: Playback 0 – 41
  Front Left: Playback 21 [51%] [-20.00dB] [on]
  Front Right: Playback 21 [51%] [-20.00dB] [on] 
```

### apk command

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apk</samp> command is used for package management in Alpine Linux. This minimalist Linux distribution is particularly popular in the Docker context.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">add</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Installs the specified package. If the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--update</samp> option is passed to the command, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apk</samp> updates the package cache beforehand (as with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apk update</samp>). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--no-cache</samp> has almost the same effect, but the cache is deleted immediately afterwards to save space.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">del</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Removes the specified package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp>
    Lists all installed packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search term</samp>
    Searches for packages whose package name matches the search term.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status</samp>
    Shows how many packages are currently installed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update</samp>
    Updates the cache of all package sources listed in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/apk/repositories</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">upgrade</samp>
    Updates all installed packages.

#### Example

The following command first updates the cache of the package sources and then installs the two packages <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">build-base</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">python-dev</samp>:

```
root# apk add --update build-base python-dev 
```

### apropos topic

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apropos</samp> provides a list of all <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> texts that contain information on the specified topic. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apropos</samp> doesn’t work, the underlying databases that can be created via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mandb</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">makewhatis</samp> are probably missing.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apropos editor</samp> provides a list of various installed edit commands:

```
user$ apropos editor
ed (1)     - line-oriented text editor
editor (1) - Vi IMproved, a programmer's text editor
ex (1)     - Vi IMproved, a programmer's text editor
jmacs (1)  - Joe's Own Editor
joe (1)    - Joe's Own Editor
... 
```

### apt command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt</samp> is the most popular command for package management on Debian-based distributions. This also applies to Linux Mint, Raspberry Pi OS, and Ubuntu. Possible alternatives are the previously very popular [apt-get](#A_001.xhtml_apt-get) command (it’s still preferable for automated installations and script programming) and [aptitude](#A_001.xhtml_aptitude) with a text-based graphical user interface.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt</samp> installs, updates, and removes packages, taking into account all packages in the package sources defined in [etc/apt/sources.list](#04_001.xhtml_sources.list). The following list describes the most important commands:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">autoclean</samp>
    Only removes packages from the package cache for which a newer version is already available.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">autoremove</samp>
    Uninstalls all packages that are no longer required and have been installed due to dependencies.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">full-upgrade</samp>
    Works in a similar way to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">upgrade</samp>, but also carries out updates for which packages have to be removed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1 name2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Searches for the packages <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name2</samp>, and so on in all APT package sources; downloads them; and installs them. If necessary, additional packages are also loaded and installed or updated to fulfill package dependencies.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">./filename.deb</samp>
    Installs a Debian package previously downloaded locally. All APT package sources are still used to resolve package dependencies. It’s important that the path to the file is recognizable as such and begins with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">./</samp> for the local directory or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp> for an absolute path. Otherwise, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">apt</samp> thinks it’s a package name, searches for it in the package sources, and finally returns an error message.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp>
    Lists all available packages. With the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--installed</samp> option, the command only returns the currently installed packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">remove</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1 name2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Uninstalls the specified packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search term</samp>
    Lists all packages whose name or description contains the search term.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">show</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1</samp>
    Displays information on the specified package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update</samp>
    Updates the package lists of the archives specified in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sources.list</samp>. Only the metadata of the package sources is read and entered in APT cache files. However, no packages are downloaded or updated! The sole purpose of this command is to let <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt</samp> know which packages are available on the internet. The command should be run before any other <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt</samp> command. Note: If you want to update only one package (not all packages), you need to run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt install</samp> name, instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt update</samp> name!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">upgrade</samp>
    Updates all installed packages if newer versions are available in the package sources. If necessary, additional packages are also installed for the update. However, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt upgrade</samp> doesn’t perform updates for which it’s necessary to remove packages.

#### Example

The following commands show how you can use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">apt</samp>:

```
root# apt update           
(update package sources)
root# apt full-upgrade     
(update all installed packages)
root# apt install apache2  
(install Apache web server) 
```

### apt-cache command

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-cache</samp> command, which is specific to Debian and Ubuntu, provides information about available or previously installed packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">madison</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Provides a one-line summary of the results of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-cache policy</samp> (see below).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">policy</samp>
    Displays a detailed list of all package sources.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">policy</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Shows which package source the currently installed package comes from and which package sources may provide alternative versions of the package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp>
    Returns a list of all available packages (regardless of whether they have already been installed or not) whose package name or package short description contains the search text pattern. The additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--names-only</samp> option restricts the search to the package name.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">show</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Provides a short package description. This also works for packages that aren’t installed, as long as the package description is in the cache.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">showpkg</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Displays the dependency information for the package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">stats</samp>
    Provides statistics on the number of installed and available packages.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-cache</samp> can’t provide detailed information about the specific contents of a package or establish an association between a file and the corresponding package. If you’re interested in this information, you must use [dpkg](#D_001.xhtml_dpkg).

#### Examples

The following command returns a sorted list of all packages whose names contain <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gimp</samp>:

```
root# apt-cache search --names-only gimp | sort
  gimp-cbmplugs    - Extensions for GIMP to import/export
                     Commodore-64 files
  gimp-data        - Data for GIMP
  gimp-data-extras - Extra brushes and patterns for GIMP
  ... 
```

The second example shows which version of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openjdk-17-jre</samp> package is installed and whether there are alternative versions. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-cache</samp> only finds an older version (17.0.2 instead of 17.0.10):

```
user$ apt-cache policy openjdk-11-jre
openjdk-17-jre:
  Installed: 17.0.10+7-1~22.04.1
  Candidate: 17.0.10+7-1~22.04.1
  Version table:
  ** 17.0.10+7-1~22.04.1 500
        500 http://de.../ubuntu-ports jammy-updates/universe arm64 Packages
        500 http://ports... jammy-security/universe arm64 Packages
        100 /var/lib/dpkg/status
     17.0.2+8-1 500
        500 http://de../ubuntu-ports jammy/universe arm64 Packages 
```

### apt-file [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-file</samp> command from the package of the same name makes it possible to search for a file that is contained in a Debian package—even if the package hasn’t yet been installed.

#### Example

The following commands first create or update the local database and then search for packages with files containing <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main.cf</samp>:

```
root# apt-file update
user$ apt-file find main.cf
postfix:     /usr/share/postfix/main.cf.debian
postfix:     /usr/share/postfix/main.cf.dist
postfix:     /usr/share/postfix/main.cf.tls
postfix-doc: /usr/share/doc/postfix/examples/main.cf.default
postsrsd:    /usr/share/doc/postsrsd/main.cf.ex
... 
```

### apt-get [options] command

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get</samp> command, which is specific to Debian and Ubuntu, installs, updates, and removes packages. For interactive use, the [apt](#A_001.xhtml_apt) command is recommended today instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get</samp>. It has been optimized for ease of use and also provides subcommands for package search (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt show</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt search</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt list</samp>), which are missing in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get</samp>.

However, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get</samp> isn’t obsolete. It can still be used on all Debian- and Ubuntu-based distributions. Its use is particularly recommended if you want to automate package management in scripts. The following list describes the most important commands:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">autoclean</samp>
    Removes only those packages from the package cache for which a newer version is already available.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">autoremove</samp>
    Uninstalls all packages that are no longer required and have been installed due to dependencies.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">check</samp>
    Updates the cache of all installed packages and detects any existing package conflicts and unresolved dependencies. This is only necessary if packages have been (de)installed without APT and conflicts have occurred as a result.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">clean</samp>
    Removes all downloaded packages from the package cache.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dist-upgrade</samp>
    Works in a similar way to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">upgrade</samp> but also installs new packages if required.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1 name2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Installs the packages <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name2</samp>, and so on, and also takes package dependencies into account. If a package has already been installed, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> will update this package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">remove</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1 name2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Uninstalls the specified packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">source</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Installs the source code of the package in the current directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update</samp>
    Updates the package lists of the archives specified in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sources.list</samp>. (Further details are given in [apt](#A_001.xhtml_apt) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">update</samp> .)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">upgrade</samp>
    Updates all installed packages if newer versions are available in the package sources.

The detailed behavior of the commands is controlled by options:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--download-only</samp>
    Only downloads the packages to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/cache/apt/archives</samp> directory, but doesn’t install them.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-install-recommends</samp>
    Dispenses with the installation of recommended packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--simulate</samp>
    Simulates the installation, but doesn’t make any actual changes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-y</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--assume-yes</samp>
    Answers all questions with yes, enabling the command to be used in a script.

#### Example

The following commands show how you can use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">apt-get</samp>:

```
root# apt-get update && apt-get dist-upgrade   
(perform complete update)
root# apt-get remove -y emacs                  
(remove emacs without asking) 
```

### apt-key command

Although the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-key</samp> command is still mentioned in countless internet manuals, it’s outdated. In the past, the command helped to manage the keys of package sources. It was usually executed in the form <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-key add keyfile</samp>.

The command is no longer available in current distributions. The key files must now be saved manually in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d</samp> directory. In addition, when specifying the package source in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/apt/sources.list</samp> or in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/apt/sources.d/repo.list</samp>, the key file must be explicitly referenced using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">signed-by</samp>:

```
# /etc/apt/sources.d/myrepo.list
deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/myrepo.asc] https://apt.myrepo.com ... 
```

### aptitude [options] [command]

The Debian-specific <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude</samp> command installs, updates, and removes packages, as well as accesses the APT infrastructure like [apt](#A_001.xhtml_apt) and [apt-get](#A_001.xhtml_apt-get). The advantage compared to these two commands is that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude</samp> remembers dependent packages during the installation process and automatically removes them when uninstalling.

All package management functions are performed in the form of commands (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude install</samp> package name). The basic commands correspond to those in [apt-get](#A_001.xhtml_apt-get) and are described there. However, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">check</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">autoremove</samp> commands aren’t available in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude</samp>. The powerful <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">search</samp> command is available for this purpose.

Alternatively, you can also use the program with a text user interface in a console by simply starting the program without any additional parameters. Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+T to select the menu. Despite the menu, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude</samp> isn’t really intuitive to use which is why most users use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude</samp>, like <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get</samp>, simply to run individual commands.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude</samp> isn’t installed by default in most distributions and must be installed via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get</samp> before it can be used.

#### aptitude search

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude search</samp> provides comprehensive options for searching the package database. In the simplest form, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aptitude search</samp> search term to search for packages whose name contains the search term. You can use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">~</samp> and a letter to formulate various search criteria. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">~i</samp> restricts the search to installed packages, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">~U</samp> displays packages for which updates are available. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-F</samp> option allows you to control which details of the search result are to be displayed in columns of a specific width.

A number of other search options are described in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/share/doc/aptitude/README</samp> and on the following page:

[www.debian.org/doc/manuals/aptitude/ch02s04s05.en.html](http://www.debian.org/doc/manuals/aptitude/ch02s04s05.en.html)

#### Examples

The following two commands first install the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql-server</samp> package and then remove it again. It’s noteworthy that the second command removes almost all dependent packages installed together with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql-server</samp>. (However, the client tools and libraries that are independent of the server are retained).

```
root# aptitude install mysql-server
The following NEW packages will be installed:
   libcgi-fast-perl{a} libcgi-pm-perl{a} libevent-core-2.1-7{a} ...
   mysql-server mysql-server-8.0{a} mysql-server-core-8.0{a}
0 packages upgraded, 19 newly installed
...
root# aptitude remove mysql-server
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  libcgi-fast-perl{u} ... mysql-server-core-8.0{u}
0 packages upgraded, 0 newly installed, 19 to remove 
```

The following command provides a list of all installed packages. The package group or package source is specified in the first column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%20s</samp>, Source, with a column width of 20 characters), and the package name is specified in the second column.

```
user$ aptitude search ~i -F "%20s  %p"
utils               acl
admin               adduser
gnome               adwaita-icon-theme
games               aisleriot
... 
```

You can use [egrep](#E_001.xhtml_egrep) to filter those packages from the result that originate from the Ubuntu package sources <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">universe</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">multiverse</samp>.

```
user$ aptitude search ~i -F "%20s  %p" | egrep "universe|multiverse"
universe/admin          aptitude
universe/admin          aptitude-common
universe/introspection  gir1.2-gtk-vnc-2.0
universe/editors        joe
universe/libs           libburn4
... 
```

### arp [options] [hosts/ipaddresses/network]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">arp</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">net-tools</samp> package helps to manage the cache for the address resolution protocol (ARP). This cache contains a list of local network devices and allows the assignment to their MAC addresses. Without any further parameters, the command returns the current cache content. With the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> option, the corresponding IP addresses are displayed instead of host names.

```
user$ arp
Address                  HWtype  HWaddress           Flags Mask  Iface
fritz.box                ether   3c:37:12:b7:a1:cb   C           enp0s1
Archer-C6.fritz.box      ether   d8:07:b6:4f:19:af   C           enp0s1
m3.fritz.box             ether   80:a9:97:32:c5:d7   C           enp0s1
BRN001BA99C5DA4.fritz.b  ether   00:1b:a9:9c:5d:a4   C           enp0s1
user$ arp -n
Address                  HWtype  HWaddress           Flags Mask  Iface
192.168.178.1            ether   3c:37:12:b7:a1:cb   C           enp0s1
192.168.178.21           ether   d8:07:b6:4f:19:af   C           enp0s1
192.168.178.146          ether   80:a9:97:32:c5:d7   C           enp0s1
192.168.178.20           ether   00:1b:a9:9c:5d:a4   C           enp0s1 
```

### arp-scan [options] [hosts/ipadresses/network]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">arp-scan</samp> sends address resolution protocol (ARP) packets to the specified hosts or IP addresses and displays the resulting responses. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">arp-scan</samp> thus provides an extremely fast way of finding out which hosts or IP addresses are running active devices and which MAC addresses they have. As usual, the address range can also be specified in the form 10.17.0.0/16.

The [nmap](#N_001.xhtml_nmap) command provides similar functions, albeit on a completely different technical basis. In short, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> is slower but more thorough.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--file=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename</samp>
    Loads the hosts or IP addresses from the specified file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-I</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--interface=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp>
    Explicitly selects the network interface via which the ARP packets are to be sent. If this option isn’t specified, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">arp-scan</samp> simply uses the first interface, ignoring the loopback interface.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--localnet</samp>
    Searches the entire local network. There is then no need to specify hosts or IP addresses.

#### Example

The following <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">arp-scan</samp> command is used to perform a network scan for the IP addresses 10.0.0.*:

```
root# arp-scan --interface=enp0s3 10.0.0.0/24
Interface: enp0s3, datalink type: EN10MB (Ethernet)
Starting arp-scan 1.9 with 256 hosts
10.0.0.9        00:16:b6:9d:ff:4b       Cisco-Linksys
10.0.0.22       b8:27:eb:11:44:2e       Raspberry Pi Foundation
10.0.0.39       ac:87:a3:1e:4a:87       (Unknown)
...
7 packets received by filter, 0 packets dropped by kernel
Ending arp-scan 1.9: 256 hosts scanned in 1.825 seconds
  (140.27 hosts/sec). 7 responded 
```

### at [options] time

You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at</samp> to specify that one or more commands are to be run at a later time. The commands are entered interactively after the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">at</samp> command; the input ends with Ctrl+D.

If the job produces a standard output, the output is sent by email to the user who executed <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at</samp> once it has been completed. This requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/sbin/sendmail</samp> to be installed on the computer.

#### Time Specification

There are a number of variants for the time specification, the most important of which are presented here using examples:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">3:45 [tomorrow]</samp>
    Runs the commands at 3:45 am—today, if it’s earlier, or tomorrow, if 3:45 am has already passed. You can explicitly specify a time on the next day with a subsequent <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tomorrow</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[16:30] [2025-]12-31</samp>
    Runs the commands on the specified day and at the specified time. The year and time are optional. If this data is missing, the current year and the current time are used. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">at 11-30</samp> therefore means the following: on November 30 of this year at the same time at which the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">at</samp> command was executed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">noon | teatime | midnight</samp>
    Corresponds to the times 12:00, 16:00, and 0:00.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">now</samp>
    Runs the commands immediately. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">now</samp> is often combined with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+ xxx</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">... + 2 days</samp>
    Adds two days to the preceding time specification. Permissible time units are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">minutes</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hours</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">days</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">weeks</samp>. The grammatically questionable statement <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">at now + 1 hours</samp> therefore means the following: in one hour. (Time units should always be given in the plural.)

#### Options

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Runs the command as soon as the system has a low workload. The time specification is omitted with this option. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at -b</samp> corresponds to the [batch](#B_001.xhtml_batch) command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies which commands are run by the job with the specified number. You can determine the job numbers via [atq](#A_001.xhtml_atq).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Removes the job specified by its number from the list of marked jobs. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at -d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at -r</samp> corresponds to [atrm](#A_001.xhtml_atrm).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Loads the commands to be executed from the specified file, not from the standard input.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Lists all jobs. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at -l</samp> corresponds to the [atq](#A_001.xhtml_atq) command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp>
    Always sends a mail, even if the job doesn’t return any output.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-M</samp>
    Doesn’t send an email after completing the job.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-q</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x</samp>
    Assigns the job to queue <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x</samp>, where <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x</samp> can be a lowercase or uppercase letter. The letters <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">a</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">b</samp> are used for ordinary <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">at</samp> jobs and for [batch](#B_001.xhtml_batch) jobs. The higher the selected queue letter, the higher the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp> value with which the job is executed. As a result, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-qz</samp> is suitable for jobs with very low urgency.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">YYYYMMDDhhmm</samp>
    Runs the job at the specified time. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp> option is an alternative to the other forms of time specification.

#### Example

Changes have been made to the configuration of the web server, which will only take effect after a restart. However, to prevent active users of the website from losing session data, the web server shouldn’t be restarted immediately, but at 1:00 am the following day. The service name <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apache2</samp> applies to Debian and Ubuntu. On Fedora and RHEL, you must enter <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">httpd</samp> instead.

```
root# at 1:00
service apache2 restart
<Ctrl>+<D> 
```

### atq

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">atq</samp> lists all jobs that have been set up using [at](#A_001.xhtml_at) for execution at a future point in time. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">atq</samp> is run by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>, it displays the jobs of all users; otherwise, only its own jobs are displayed.

### atrm n

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">atrm</samp> deletes the job specified by its number. You can use [atq](#A_001.xhtml_atq) to determine the numbers of all jobs that have been set up for future execution.

### attr [options] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">attr</samp> determines or changes the extended access attributes of the specified files or directories. This only works if the file system supports extended attributes (EAs). For ext3/ext4 file systems, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> option <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user_xattr</samp> must be used.

Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">attr</samp>, you should prefer the [getfattr](#G_001.xhtml_getfattr) or [setfattr](#S_001.xhtml_setfattr) commands. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">attr</samp> is only available for reasons of compatibility with IRIX SGI.

### awk [options] 'code' text files
awk [options] -f code file text files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">awk</samp> isn’t a simple command, but a separate programming language that helps with the processing and analysis of structured texts. For example, you can use it to search a text file for keywords and extract a text column from the subsequent text section. You can either enter the program code directly or read it from a code file using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp> option. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">awk</samp> then processes all text files passed as parameters line by line and writes the result to the standard output.

The program code to be processed by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">awk</samp> follows this simplified syntax:

```
/searchpattern1/ {actions}
/searchpattern2/ {more actions}
condition     {even more actions} 
```

The same rules that are described in the [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep) command apply to the structure of the search pattern. Multiple actions are separated by semicolons. If the search pattern is missing, the action applies to every line of the text file. Conversely, if the action is missing, the text captured by the pattern simply gets output.

A comprehensive description of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">awk</samp> and its capabilities isn’t possible here for reasons of space. Instead, I will restrict myself to a few examples. If you want to familiarize yourself more deeply with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">awk</samp>, the following tutorial is a good introduction:

[www.grymoire.com/Unix/Awk.html](http://www.grymoire.com/Unix/Awk.html)

The official User’s Guide goes into more detail, but with almost 500 pages, it may put off beginners:

[www.gnu.org/software/gawk/manual/gawk.pdf](http://www.gnu.org/software/gawk/manual/gawk.pdf)

#### Examples

This excerpt from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/passwd</samp> serves as the starting point for the following examples:

```
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
bin:x:1:1:bin:/bin:/sbin/nologin
daemon:x:2:2:daemon:/sbin:/sbin/nologin
adm:x:3:4:adm:/var/adm:/sbin/nologin
lp:x:4:7:lp:/var/spool/lpd:/sbin/nologin
... 
```

The first <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">awk</samp> example only returns the first and seventh column from <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">/etc/passwd</samp>, that is, the login name and the assigned shell. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-F</samp> option specifies that the columns are separated by colons and not by spaces and tab characters:

```
user$ awk -F':' '{print $1,$7}' /etc/passwd
root /bin/bash
bin /sbin/nologin
daemon /sbin/nologin ... 
```

The second example determines the home directory and the shell of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kofler</samp>:

```
user$ awk -F':' '/kofler/ {print $6; print $7;}' /etc/passwd
/home/kofler
/bin/bash 
```

The third example displays the login names of all users with a UID greater than or equal to 1000:

```
user$ awk -F':' '$3>=1000 {print $1}' /etc/passwd
nfsnobody
kofler
test 
```

The last example extracts the file size and the file name from the output of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls -l</samp>. Note, however, that this only works for file names that don’t contain spaces.

```
user$ ls -l *.txt | awk '{print $5,$9}'
123 file1.txt
213231 file2.txt
... 
```

### aws [options] main command [subcommand] [parameter]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> command helps with the administration of various Amazon cloud services. As these services are often used from Linux computers, many administrators come into contact with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp>.

This section refers to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> version 2 recommended by Amazon. You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws --version</samp> to make sure that you haven’t installed the still widely used version 1! Both <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aws</samp> versions use the same command name and are largely compatible with each other, but there are also some differences:

[https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cliv2-migration.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cliv2-migration.html)

#### Installation and Commissioning

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> isn’t installed by default and usually isn’t available as a package in your distribution. Instead, you must run the following commands for installation. On computers with ARM CPUs, you need to replace <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x86_64</samp> with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aarch64</samp>.

```
user$ sudo apt/dnf/yum/zypper install curl
user$ curl "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip" \
       -o "awscliv2.zip"
user$ unzip awscliv2.zip
user$ sudo ./aws/install 
```

The ZIP file contains a minimal Python 3 distribution with all the required packages. This means that there are neither dependencies on Python packages in your distribution nor conflicts due to differing version numbers. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> is installed in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/local/bin</samp> directory. If this directory isn’t part of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PATH</samp>, you must specify the path explicitly.

```
root# aws --version
aws-cli/2.15.28 Python/3.11.8 Linux/6.1.0-18-arm64 exe/aarch64.debian.12 
```

The connection to the Amazon cloud services is encrypted. Before you can configure the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> command for further use, you must set up a user and group on the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) page. The group should be linked to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">AmazonS3Full Access</samp> policy and to the new user. You can find the AWS page at:

[https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam)

Now run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws configure</samp> in the terminal, and enter the Access Key ID and the Secret Access Key you received when setting up the user. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> saves this data and the other options in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.aws/credentials</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.aws/config</samp>.

```
root# aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]:     AKxxxxxxx
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: ZRxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Default region name [None]:   eu-central-1
Default output format [None]: 
```

#### Syntax and Online Help

You usually pass a main command to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> command, which selects the desired AWS service, as well as a subcommand that applies specifically to the service in question. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws s3 ls</samp> lists your buckets in the S3 service. For reasons of space, I’ll restrict this to a few commands for the EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) and S3 (Simple Storage Service) services.

There is no <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page available for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp>. Instead, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws help</samp> provides an overview of the syntax. An overview of the commands for a specific service is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws <service> help</samp>, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws ec2 help</samp>. Details of a subcommand can be found in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws <service> <subcommand> help</samp>, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws s3 cp help</samp>.

#### S3 Administration

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aws s3 ls [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Lists all S3 buckets without further parameters or displays the content of a bucket directory or a file located there. Paths are entered in the form <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">s3://<bucketname>/<directory>/<file></samp> (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">s3://my-bucket/my-dir/my-file</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aws s3 cp</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path1 path2</samp>
    Copies a local file to an S3 bucket and from there back to the local file system. You can also copy an S3 file to another S3 location. You can use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--recursive</samp> option to copy directories recursively. For testing purposes, you need to pass <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--dryrun</samp>: the command then shows what it would do, but doesn’t change anything.

    If you use S3 for data backup, it’s recommended that you only upload files to S3 that you’ve previously encrypted yourself. In the past, configuration errors have repeatedly occurred so that supposedly private buckets were publicly accessible after all. In addition, the possibility of intelligence services gaining access can’t be ruled out.
