*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aws s3 mv</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path1 path2</samp>
    As in the previous entry, but moves the file or renames a file that is already in the S3 memory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aws s3 sync</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path1 path2</samp>
    Synchronizes two directories: one local and one in the S3 storage. This is faster than <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws s3 cp</samp> because unchanged files won’t be transferred again. Files deleted in the source path are retained in the target path. If you don’t want this, you must pass the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--delete</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aws s3 mb</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newbucket</samp>
    Creates a new bucket, specifying the name in the usual manner (i.e., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">s3://<bucketname></samp>). The name must be unique worldwide.

    With the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--region</samp> option, you can specify the data center in which the bucket is to be set up, which differs from the region preset in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws configure</samp>.

    The new bucket isn’t publicly accessible by default. Access rights and access rules (ACLs, i.e., Access Control Lists) must be set via the AWS web console.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aws s3 rb</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bucket</samp>
    Deletes the specified bucket. The operation is only successful if the bucket is empty. Otherwise, you can force the deletion using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--force</samp>.

#### EC2 Administration

While the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws</samp> commands for S3 administration are easy to use, this unfortunately doesn’t apply to EC2: The number of subcommands alone is daunting—there are more than 400 of them. Many commands also provide or expect JSON data structures and are therefore only intended for script programming, but not for use by humans. You can try out <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aws ec2 describe instances</samp> as a starting point. The command provides a list of all your instances already set up as a JSON document:

```
root# aws ec2 describe-instances
{
    "Reservations": [
        {
            "Groups": [],
            "Instances": [
                {
                    "AmiLaunchIndex": 0,
                    "ImageId": "ami-02fc41eea1852",
                    ... 
```

#### Example

The following two commands set up a new bucket and copy all files from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc</samp> directory to it:

```
root# aws s3 mb s3://info.kofler.etcbak
root# aws s3 sync /etc s3://info.kofler.etcbak 
```

## B

### badblocks device

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">badblocks</samp> performs a low-level check of the data medium. This is only useful if you suspect that your hard disk or SSD may be defective. If you intend to set up an ext file system on the hard disk (partition), it’s better to perform the check using [](#M_001.xhtml_mkfs.ext2)<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-c</samp> as part of the formatting.

Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">badblocks</samp> doesn’t destroy any data and only performs a read-only test. You can carry out more thorough tests by adding the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp> options:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp>
    Performs read and write tests, but restores the original content of the data blocks. The option can’t be used if the data medium or partition is currently being used, that is, is being included in the directory tree via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp>
    Performs write tests with bit patterns. Caution: The contents of the data medium or partition will be deleted!

### basename string [ending]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">basename</samp> returns the file name of the transferred path. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">basename /etc/X11/Xmodmap</samp> thus leads to the result <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Xmodmap</samp>. If a file extension is specified as an additional parameter, this file extension (if present) will be removed from the file name.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">basename</samp> eliminates the path and the identifier <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.jpg</samp>. What remains is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">white</samp>.

```
user$ basename /home/kofler/Bilder/Wallpapers/white.jpg .jpg
 white 
```

### bat text file

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bat</samp> command from the package of the same name is a variant of the [cat](#C_001.xhtml_cat) command. In contrast to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bat</samp> attempts to recognize the content of the text and then performs colored syntax highlighting when it’s displayed. In some distributions (e.g., Debian), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bat</samp> must be called under the name <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">batcat</samp> to avoid a name conflict.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bat</samp> relies on your terminal to use a dark background by default. If you use a light background, you must pass a corresponding option to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bat</samp> (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--theme gruvbox-light</samp>) or permanently set the color theme in configuration file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.config/bat/config</samp>.

### batch

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">batch</samp> marks a job order for later execution. As with [at](#A_001.xhtml_at), the commands to be executed are then entered interactively. The entry must be completed using Ctrl+D. Unlike <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at</samp>, there’s no time specification for when the job is supposed to be run. Instead, the background daemon <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">atd</samp> waits until the system has a low load. The threshold is defined as a <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">load</samp> average of 1.5\. If the job provides an output, this is sent to the user via email, which requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/sbin/sendmail</samp> to be available on the computer.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">batch</samp> processes neither options nor parameters. If you want to read the job order from a file, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">at -qb -f file now</samp>.

#### Example

The execution of the backup script is started as soon as the system load is low:

```
user$ batch
./backup-script
<Ctrl>+<D> 
```

### bc [file]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bc</samp> stands for basic calculator and is a command-oriented pocket calculator. It can be used interactively to perform simple calculations. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bc</samp> is also useful in scripts if the limited calculation functions of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> are insufficient. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bc</samp> expects the calculation statements from the standard input or from a file.

#### Examples

The following examples show both the interactive use of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bc</samp> and its use in commands. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">`scale=3`</samp> statement controls the number of decimal places in the output.

```
user bc
> 2+3
5
> <Ctrl>+<D>
user$ echo "5 + 3 * 7" | bc
26
user$ echo "scale=3; sqrt(2)" | bc
1.414 
```

#### Alternatives

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bc</samp> only knows a few advanced mathematical functions. For more complex calculations, it’s better to use [qalc](#Q_001.xhtml_qalc). However, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">qalc</samp> has the disadvantage that it has to be installed separately.

### bg [process]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bg</samp> shell command continues an interrupted process in the background. If no process number is specified, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bg</samp> applies to the last process that was interrupted using Ctrl+Z. Otherwise, the process must be specified by its name or by the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>-internal job number (not by the PID!).

### blkid [options] [device]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">blkid</samp> provides information about the block device specified by the device name, for example, about hard disk partitions, logical volumes, or RAID devices. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">blkid</samp> specifies the file system type, the UUID, and the name (label) of the file system. If the device specification is missing when <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">blkid</samp> is called, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">blkid</samp> provides this information for all active partitions and logical volumes. By specifying options, you can search for specific file systems:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-k</samp>
    Lists all file system types supported by the kernel.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">label</samp>
    Searches for file systems with the specified name.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fstyp1,fstyp2,fstyp3</samp>
    Searches for file systems that correspond to the specified types.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name=value</samp>
    Searches for file systems that match the search criterion. Permitted criteria are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">TYPE</samp> (file system type), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LABEL</samp> (name of the file system), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PARTLABEL</samp> (name of the partition), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">UUID</samp> (UUID of the file system), and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PARTUUID</samp> (UUID of the partition). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">blkid -t TYPE=ext4</samp> corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">blkid -n ext4</samp> and returns a list of all ext4 file systems.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-U</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uuid</samp>
    Searches for file systems with the specified UUID.

#### Examples

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sda1</samp> partition contains an ext4 file system with the UUID 2716...19e4:

```
root# blkid /dev/sda1
/dev/sda1: UUID="27162884-8fe9-4fa9-8b5e-712ab82d19e4" TYPE="ext4" 
```

The search for a partition with the label <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lvm2</samp> returns <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdb2</samp>:

```
root# blkid -t PARTLABEL=lvm2
/dev/sdb2: PARTLABEL="lvm2" PARTUUID="371cc374-847f-407a-bb5b-7ff015722383" 
```

### bluetoothctl

On desktop systems, a Bluetooth configuration is usually done via graphical user interfaces. If that’s not available (e.g., on Raspberry Pi to which no monitor is connected) or doesn’t work, the configuration with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bluetoothctl</samp> can also be performed in text mode. For this purpose, you need to start an interactive session with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bluetoothctl</samp> and then run commands to find and pair the Bluetooth device.

You can run the commands described in the following list within a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bluetoothctl</samp> session. It’s important to keep pressing the Bluetooth button (pairing button) on Bluetooth devices that you want to reconfigure, so that the device signals to the environment that it’s ready to connect. On many devices, a blue LED then flashes. If there’s no such button, you can also try turning the device off and on again.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">agent on/off</samp>
    (De)activates the Bluetooth agent. This software component takes care of authorizing new devices and allows, for example, the keypad entry of a pairing code.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">connect</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xx:xx:xx</samp>
    Establishes the connection. (This only works if <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pair</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">trust</samp> have been executed beforehand!) If everything works out, the response is connection successful. The device can now be used.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">exit</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">quit</samp>
    Ends the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bluetoothctl</samp> session.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xx:xx:xx</samp>
    Shows the connection status and various other information about the device.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pair</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xx:xx:xx</samp>
    Initiates the connection to a device. If you use a keypad, you’ll be prompted to enter a multi-digit code. Don’t forget to finish the input by pressing Enter! You can recognize successful pairing by the pairing successful message. Devices without an input option (mouse, headset, loudspeaker, etc.) can be paired without entering a code.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pairable on/off</samp>
    Activates/deactivates the coupling mode.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">scan on/off</samp>
    (De)activates the scan mode. In scan mode, the program lists all devices. This process can take some time and individual devices are displayed again and again. When you’ve found the desired device, you should switch the mode off again via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">scan off</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">trust</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xx:xx:xx</samp>
    Trusts the specified device.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bluetoothctl</samp> saves the Bluetooth configuration for a specific device permanently in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/bluetooth/id1/id2/info</samp>. There, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">id1</samp> is the ID of the Bluetooth controller, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">id2</samp> is the ID of the Bluetooth device.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bluetoothctl</samp> is actually intended for interactive use. To run a single command immediately, you can proceed as follows:

```
root# echo -e "connect FC:58:FA:A0:4D:E7\nquit" | bluetoothctl 
```

#### Example

The following lines show in slightly abbreviated form the inputs and outputs for configuring a Bluetooth keyboard:

```
user$ bluetoothctl
[bluetooth]# agent on
[bluetooth]# pairable on
[bluetooth]# scan on
Discovery started
[CHG] Controller 00:1A:7D:DA:71:13 Discovering: yes
[NEW] Device 70:10:00:1A:92:20 70-10-00-1A-92-20
[CHG] Device 70:10:00:1A:92:20 Name: Bluetooth 3.0 Keyboard
...
[bluetooth]# scan off
[bluetooth]# pair 70:10:00:1A:92:20
Attempting to pair with 70:10:00:1A:92:20
[CHG] Device 70:10:00:1A:92:20 Connected: yes
[agent] PIN code: 963064
[CHG] Device 70:10:00:1A:92:20 Paired: yes
Pairing successful
[bluetooth]# trust 70:10:00:1A:92:20
[bluetooth]# connect 70:10:00:1A:92:20
[bluetooth]# info 70:10:00:1A:92:20
Device 70:10:00:1A:92:20
        Name: Bluetooth 3.0 Keyboard
        Paired: yes
        Trusted: yes
        Connected: yes
    ...
[bluetooth]# exit 
```

### boltctl command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">boltctl</samp> controls devices connected via the Thunderbolt interface. Thunderbolt is currently mainly used in notebooks with Intel CPUs. It’s likely to become more widespread in the future because Thunderbolt is part of the new USB4 standard.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">authorize</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Allows the use of a Thunderbolt device once. You can determine a list of all connected devices via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">boltctl list</samp>. To give permanent permission, you must use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">boltctl enroll</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">key</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">key newvalue</samp>
    Loads or changes configuration options (requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions). A list of all options is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">boltctl config --describe</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enroll [--policy auto|manual|default]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Allows the device to communicate permanently via the Thunderbolt interface. Explicit permission is only required for devices that use the PCI bus via Thunderbolt (e.g., for a docking station) and only if strict Thunderbolt security guidelines are set in the BIOS/EFI.

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">auto</samp> means that the device can be used in the future without further queries. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">manual</samp> requires confirmation using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">boltctl authorize</samp> each time it’s reconnected. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">default</samp> accepts the Thunderbolt daemon’s specifications (usually this is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">auto</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">forget</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Removes the ID of a device from the enroll database and thus reverses <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">boltctl enroll</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Displays detailed information on the specified device.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list -a</samp>
    Lists all connected devices.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">monitor</samp>
    Tracks and logs which devices are connected or removed until the command is ended using Ctrl+C.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">power</samp>
    Activates a Thunderbolt controller that is in sleep mode.

### break [n]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">break</samp> prematurely terminates a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">for</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">while</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">until</samp> loop in shell scripts. The shell program then continues with the next command after the end of the loop. By specifying an optional numerical value, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> loop levels can be canceled.

### btrfs command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs</samp> is the central administration command for Btrfs file systems. Provided there are no ambiguities, you can abbreviate the commands described in this section and save yourself a lot of typing. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs fi sh</samp> corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs filesystem show</samp>.

The administration of Btrfs file systems is exceptionally complex. For this reason, only the most important commands are summarized here. There’s just not enough space here to describe the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">btrfs</samp> basics in detail.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">balance start|pause|resume|cancel|status</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount directory</samp>
    Distributes the data evenly across all devices in the file system. This process takes a very long time and is carried out in the background. It can be interrupted via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs balance pause</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">resumed</samp> with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs balance resume</samp>, or stopped completely using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs balance cancel</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs balance status</samp> provides information on how far the balancing process has progressed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device add</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">devicename mount directory</samp>
    Adds another device to an active Btrfs file system and thus increases its data pool.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device delete</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">devicename mount directory</samp>
    Removes a device from the data pool of a Btrfs file system. The data contained on the device is transferred to other devices in the file system, which, of course, takes a long time with large file systems.

    If you want to remove a defective (no longer available) device, you should enter <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">missing</samp> as the device name. For RAID-1 systems, you must first add a replacement device and run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs filesystem balance</samp>!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filesystem df</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp>
    Displays detailed information about how much space is reserved for data, metadata, and system data and how much of this space is already in use. However, the command doesn’t provide any information about how much unreserved memory space is still available, which makes it difficult to interpret the data correctly.

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filesystem resize [+/-]size</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount directory</samp>
    Enlarges or reduces the file system during operation. The new size can be specified either in absolute or relative terms. The abbreviations <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">k</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">m</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">g</samp> for KiB, MiB, and GiB are allowed. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Max</samp> is also permitted as a size specification—the file system then uses the entire size of the underlying device in future. Remember that you may have to adjust the size of the underlying device before enlarging the file system, but after reducing it!

    Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">resize</samp>, it’s easier to add an additional device to Btrfs file systems (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs add</samp> device).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filesystem show [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Displays basic information on Btrfs devices. Among other things, the command provides information on how large the devices are and how much space is available on the devices that hasn’t yet been reserved for data, metadata, or system data.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filesystem sync</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp>
    Synchronizes the content of the file system or one of its directories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">scrub start|cancel|resume|status</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Controls the scrub process. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">scrub start</samp> loads all files in the file system and checks their integrity using checksums. This process runs in the background. Its progress can be checked using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">scrub status</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">scrub cancel</samp> interrupts the scrub process, while <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">scrub resume</samp> resumes it.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">subvolume create</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Creates the subvolume <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> directory or a directory within the Btrfs file system must be specified as the directory. If no directory is specified, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">btrfs</samp> uses the current directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">subvolume delete</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Deletes the specified subvolume or the specified snapshot. However, the occupied memory is only gradually released by a background process.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">subvolume list</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount directory</samp>
    Lists all subvolumes and snapshots. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> directory of the file system is specified as the directory. The output can be influenced by several options. The combination <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-a -p -t</samp> has proven to be recommendable. It causes the location of the subvolume within the directory hierarchy to be specified exactly, the parent subvolume to also be specified for each subvolume or snapshot, and the result to be formatted as a table.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">subvolume set-default</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">id mount directory</samp>
    Determines which subvolume or snapshot will be used by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> by default in the future. You can determine the volume ID via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs subvolume list</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">subvolume snapshot [-r]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">source directory target directory</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Creates the snapshot <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> directory of the file system or the directory of an existing subvolume or snapshot must be specified as the source directory. The target directory must be located within the Btrfs file system.

    Usually, the snapshot is mutable (i.e., the file system is split into two branches, both of which are separately mutable). If you want a read-only snapshot for backups, you must use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-r</samp> option.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs subvolume list</samp> shows the subvolumes set up by default in an (open)SUSE system as well as all snapshots:

```
root# btrfs subvolume list / -p -a –t
ID    gen     parent  top level  path
-–    ---     ------  ---------  ----
257   106     5       5          <FS_TREE>/@
260   106     257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/boot/grub2/i386-pc
261   106     257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/boot/grub2/x86_64-efi
262   1305    257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/home
...
268   106     257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/var/lib/libvirt/images
269   106     257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/var/lib/mailman
270   106     257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/var/lib/mariadb
271   106     257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/var/lib/mysql
...
258   1158    257     257        <FS_TREE>/@/.snapshots
259   1310    258     258        <FS_TREE>/@/.snapshots/1/snapshot
283   106     258     258        <FS_TREE>/@/.snapshots/2/snapshot
304   669     258     258        <FS_TREE>/@/.snapshots/20/snapshot
... 
```

To create a backup of the MariaDB database files during operation, a read-only snapshot is temporarily created for subvolume <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/mariadb</samp>:

```
root# btrfs subvolume snapshot -r /var/lib/mariadb/ /var/lib/mariadb-backup
Create a readonly snapshot of '/var/lib/mariadb/' in '/var/lib/mariadb-backup' root# cd /var/lib/mariadb-backup
root# tar czf /home/kofler/mariadb.tgz .  
(create backup)
root# cd                                  
(leave directory)
root# btrfs subvolume delete /var/lib/mariadb-backup
Delete subvolume (no-commit): '/var/lib/mariadb-backup' 
```

#### Documentation

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> pages for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs</samp> are spread over several pages, each with a name consisting of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs</samp>, a hyphen, and a main command. Details on <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">btrfs scan</samp> can therefore be read via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man btrfs-scan</samp>.

### bunzip2 file.bz2

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bunzip2</samp> decompresses a file that has previously been compressed using [](#B_001.xhtml_bzip2). The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.bz2</samp> identifier is automatically removed from the file name. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bunzip</samp> is a link to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bzip2</samp>, whereby the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp> option is automatically activated.

### bzip2 file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bzip2</samp> compresses the specified files and adds the extension <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.bz2</samp> to them. The command usually produces files that are 20% to 30% smaller than files compressed using [gzip](#G_001.xhtml_gzip). However, the computing time required for compression is significantly longer with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bzip2</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-1</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-9</samp>
    Specifies how much memory (RAM) the compression algorithm is allowed to use. The default setting is <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-9</samp> and provides the best results.

    If only a small amount of RAM is available, you should select a smaller value; however, compression will then also be slightly worse.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--stdout</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--to-stdout</samp>
    Leaves the file to be (de)compressed unchanged and redirects the result to the standard output. From there, it can be redirected to any file by using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">></samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--decompress</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--uncompress</samp>
    Decompresses the specified file instead of compressing it (corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bunzip2</samp>).

#### Example

The first command compresses <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file.eps</samp>. The new file name is now <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file.eps.bz2</samp>. The second command restores the original file.

```
user$ bzip2 file.eps
user$ bunzip2 file.eps.bz2 
```

## C

### cadaver [options] [files]

The command with the strange name of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cadaver</samp> from the package of the same name is a WebDAV client. You can use it to download or upload files in a similar way to [ftp](#F_001.xhtml_ftp).

Most of the commands within <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cadaver</samp> correspond to FTP commands, that is, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">get</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mget</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">put</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mput</samp>, and so on (see [ftp](#F_001.xhtml_ftp)). The decisive difference is that the WebDAV protocol based on HTTP(S) is used.

#### Example

In the following command, a WebDAV connection is first established to the HTTP server with the IP address 172.28.128.5 on port 8585\. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">test.php</samp> file is then uploaded to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uploads</samp> directory.

```
user$ cadaver http://172.28.128.5:8585/uploads
dav:/uploads/> put test.php
  Uploading test.php to /uploads/test.php:
  Progress: ... 100,0% of 20 bytes succeeded.
dav:/uploads/> <Strg>+<D>
  Connection to 172.28.128.5 closed. 
```

### canonical-livepatch [command]

If the snap package of the same name is installed, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">canonical-livepatch</samp> controls the Ubuntu-specific kernel live patch functions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config</samp>
    Sets up the live patch function or changes its configuration. This command requires an Ubuntu One account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enable/disable</samp>
    Activates or deactivates the live patch system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">refresh</samp>
    Checks whether updates are available, downloads them if necessary, and applies them to the running kernel. This is done automatically at regular intervals.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status</samp>
    Shows the status of the live patch system.

#### Example

All available kernel patches are already applied to this server:

```
root# canonical-livepatch status
last check:      52 minutes ago
kernel:          5.4.0-173.191-generic
server check-in: succeeded
kernel state:    kernel series 5.4 is covered by Livepatch
patch state:     no livepatches available for kernel 5.4.0-173.191-generic 
```

### case expression in
pattern1 ) commands;;
pattern2 ) commands;;
...
esac

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">case</samp> construct of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> shell forms multiple branches in scripts, whereby a character string is specified as a criterion for the branch—often a variable or a parameter that is passed to the shell program. This character string is compared in sequence with the patterns, whereby the wildcard characters for file names (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*?[]</samp>) can be used in these patterns. Multiple patterns separated by the pipe operator (|) can also be specified in a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">case</samp> branch. As soon as a pattern matches, the commands that follow between the closing parenthesis (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">)</samp>) and the two semicolons (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">;;</samp>) are executed. The program then continues according to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">esac</samp>.

#### Example

In the following listing, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">case</samp> is used to classify the transferred parameters into file names and options. Within a loop, each individual parameter is analyzed using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">case</samp>. If the parameter begins with a hyphen, the parameter is added to the end of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">opt</samp> variable; otherwise, it’s added to the end of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dat</samp>.

```
#!/bin/bash
for i do    # Loop for all transferred parameters
  case "$i" in
    -* ) opt="$opt $i";;
    *  ) dat="$dat $i";;
  esac
done        # End of the loop
echo "Options: $opt"
echo "Files:  $dat" 
```

### cat [options] [files]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp> displays the content of the specified text file. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp> is also often used to combine multiple files into one larger file. For this purpose, the standard output must be redirected to a file by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">></samp> (see example). If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp> is to read from standard input, you shouldn’t enter a file name or enter the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-</samp> character.

For longer texts, you should use the [less](#L_001.xhtml_less) command instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp> because this allows you to scroll through the text line by line or page by page.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp>
    Reduces multiple empty lines to a single empty line.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T</samp>
    Displays tab characters as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">^I</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Displays nonprintable characters in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">^xxx</samp> notation.

#### Examples

The following command combines the individual <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">part1.tex</samp> file, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">part2.tex</samp> file, and so on into a total file called <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">total.tex</samp>. The individual files are processed in alphabetical order.

```
user$ cat part*.tex > total.tex 
```

In the second example, the standard input is redirected to a new file.

Once you’ve confirmed the command by pressing Enter, all further entries will be written to the new file. Ctrl+D terminates the input, so <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp> can be used to create a new text file without an editor.

```
root# cat > newfile
line 1
line 2
<Ctrl>+<D> 
```

#### Variants

There are countless variants of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp>:

*   The [bat](#B_001.xhtml_bat) and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ccat</samp> commands display code files in common programming languages in color with syntax highlighting.

*   The [more](#M_001.xhtml_more) and [less](#L_001.xhtml_less) commands allow you to scroll through the text line by line and page by page.

*   The [tac](#T_001.xhtml_tac) command outputs the text in reverse order, that is, the last line first.

*   The [zcat](#Z_001.xhtml_zcat) and [<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zless</samp>](#Z_001.xhtml_zcat) commands make it possible to display compressed text files directly.

### cd [directory]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp> shell command changes to the specified directory. If no directory is specified, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp> changes to the home directory. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd -</samp> activates the last valid directory.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pwd</samp> displays the path of the current directory. Modern alternatives to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp> are <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">j</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp>. Both commands memorize frequently used directories and allow you to change them with a minimum of typing work.

### cfdisk [options] device

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cfdisk</samp> helps with the formatting of hard disks and SSDs. It supports partition tables in MBR and GPT formats. Its operation is somewhat more convenient compared to the more familiar [fdisk](#F_001.xhtml_fdisk) and [parted](#P_001.xhtml_parted) commands because the current partition table is displayed as a menu. You can then use the cursor keys to select the partition to be edited. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cfdisk</samp> is only intended for interactive use and isn’t suitable for script programming.

### chacl [options] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chacl</samp> determines or changes the extended access rights of the specified files or directories. This only works if the file system supports ACLs (Access Control Lists). For ext3/ext4 file systems, you must use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount option acl</samp>.

If possible, you should use [getfacl](#G_001.xhtml_getfacl) or [setfacl](#S_001.xhtml_setfacl) instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chacl</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chacl</samp> is only available for reasons of compatibility with IRIX SGI.

### chage [options] loginname

You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chage</samp> to set how long a user account may be used, when its password expires and must be changed, and how often the password may or must be changed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">date</samp>
    Specifies the date on which the password was last changed. The date is entered in the notation YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">2020-12-31</samp>). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d 0</samp> means that the user must change their password immediately after the first login. The user can’t run a command until the password has been changed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-E</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">date</samp>
    Determines the date on which the account expires. After this date, it will no longer be possible to log in. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-E -1</samp> means that no expiration date has been set. Expired accounts can be reactivated using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">passwd -u</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-I</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies how many days after the password has been expired an account will be deactivated. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-I -1</samp> prevents deactivation.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Displays the current settings.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the minimum number of days that must elapse before a changed password can be changed again. The default setting <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> means that users can change their password at any time.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-M</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the maximum number of days after which the password must be changed. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-1</samp> means that the password remains valid indefinitely. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">183</samp> means that the password must be changed twice a year.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-W</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies how many days prior to the password expiry a warning will be displayed (the default setting is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">7</samp>).

#### Examples

You can use the following commands to set up a new user, define their initial password, and force them to change their password immediately when they log in for the first time and at least once a year in future. The password expiry warning appears one month in advance.

```
root# useradd peter
root# passwd peter
New password: ********
Retype new password: ********
root# chage -d 0 -M 365 -W 31 peter 
```

The expiration date of an account (option <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-E</samp>) must be specified in ISO format. Relative times aren’t possible. However, you can calculate the date using [date](#D_001.xhtml_date). The following command causes the account to be deactivated in 100 days:

```
root# chage -E $(date -d +180days +%Y-%m-%d) peter 
```

### chattr [options] +-=[aAcCdDeijsStTu] files

In Linux file systems (ext2 to ext4, Btrfs, XFS, etc.), some additional attributes can be saved with each file in addition to the user information (see [chmod](#C_001.xhtml_chmod) and [chown](#C_001.xhtml_chown)). For example, these attributes with the letter codes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aAcCdDeijsStTu</samp> control whether files are to be compressed or whether changes to files are to be made using the copy-on-write procedure.

A short description of the attributes is provided in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">man chattr</samp>. However, only a few of the planned attributes are actually being used at the moment. To load the attributes, you can use [lsattr](#L_001.xhtml_lsattr).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp>
    Changes the attributes recursively in all files of the directory tree.

#### Example

An important use of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chattr</samp> is in Btrfs file systems where you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chattr +C</samp> to deactivate the automatically active copy-on-write (COW) procedure and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chattr -C</samp> to reactivate it. The deactivation of COW is required to efficiently store image files from virtualization programs or large database files in Btrfs file systems.

You can pass individual files or entire directories to the command. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-R</samp>, the command changes the attribute recursively in directory trees:

```
root# chattr +C -R /var/lib/mysql 
```

However, the attribute only applies to new files. To disable COW on existing files with a size not equal to 0 bytes, you must copy the files:

```
root# mv dir backup
root# mkdir dir
root# chattr +C dir
root# cp -a backup/* dir
root# rm -rf backup 
```

### chcon [options] context files
chcon [options] --reference=reference file files
chcon [options] [-u user] [-r role] [-t type] [-l level] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chcon</samp> changes the SELinux context of the specified files. The new context can be specified in three ways: in the notation <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user:role:type:level</samp>, by specifying a reference file, or by using the options <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-u</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-r</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-l</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp>. The third variant has the advantage that only part of the entire context can be changed.

A manual setting of the SELinux context is normally required if you save files or directories in locations other than those specified by the SELinux rules—for example, Apache files in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/disk2/var/www/html</samp> instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/www/html</samp>.

If you’re only interested in correcting the SELinux context of files that are already located in the intended directory, [restorecon](#R_001.xhtml_restorecon) is less complicated. To determine the SELinux context of existing files, you should use the [ls](#L_001.xhtml_ls) command with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Z</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">level</samp>
    Changes the level of the SELinux context. Levels aren’t used in the rules that usually apply on RHEL and Fedora (targeted security). The context level is generally <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">s0</samp> (see also the file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/selinux/targeted/setrans.conf</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">role</samp>
    Changes the role of the SELinux context. SELinux roles determine which “domain” the file is assigned to. SELinux domains in turn determine which rights a process has.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--reference=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reference file</samp>
    Reads the SELinux context of the reference file and transfers it to the other specified files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp>
    Also takes into account all subdirectories (recursive).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type</samp>
    Changes the type of the SELinux context. SELinux types determine the rights of a file, just as SELinux domains control the rights of a process.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user</samp>
    Changes the user information of the SELinux context. The SELinux user is an identity known to the SELinux rules. Ordinary Linux users are connected (“mapped”) to SELinux identities by SELinux rules.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Displays the changes made (verbose).

#### Examples

By default, Apache on RHEL has read-only rights in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/www/html</samp> directory. To allow the web server to change files in a specific directory, you must run the following command:

```
root# chcon -R system_u:object_r:httpd_sys_content_rw_t:s0 \
         /var/www/html/wordpress 
```

If you want to enable Apache to access web files (read-only this time) that are located in a directory on another data medium, you should proceed as follows:

```
root# chcon -R system_u:object_r:httpd_sys_content_t:s0 /disk2/var/www/html/ 
```

### chgrp [options] group files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chgrp</samp> changes the group membership of files. The owner of a file can assign this file only to his or her own groups, whereas <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp> can make any assignments.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--recursive</samp>
    Also changes the group assignment of files in all subdirectories.

#### Example

The following command assigns all files in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/www</samp> directory to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">www-data</samp> group. The Apache web server runs under this account on Debian and Ubuntu.

```
root# chgrp -R www-data /var/www/ 
```

### chkrootkit [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chkrootkit</samp> command from the package of the same name searches the system for known rootkits. The procedure is pretty simple: the command attempts to detect the malware by using simple criteria or signatures (e.g., the presence of certain character strings in binary files).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp>
    Ignores NFS directories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp>
    Uses the specified directory as the starting point (as the root directory).

Although the project is still active, further development is only taking place in small steps. Both false positives and the failure to detect genuine threats are possible.

#### Example

```
root# chkrootkit
ROOTDIR is /
Checking amd...                               not found
Checking basename...                          not infected
Checking biff...                              not found
Checking chfn...                              not infected
Searching for sniffer's logs ...              nothing found
Searching for rootkit HiDrootkit's files...   nothing found
Searching for rootkit t0rn's default files... nothing found
Checking asp...                               not infected
Checking bindshell...                         not infected
Checking lkm...                               chkproc: nothing detected
... 
```

#### Variants

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chkrootkit</samp> can be the starting point of a rootkit search due to its ease of use. Alternative or supplementary tools are, for example, [rkhunter](#R_001.xhtml_rkhunter) and the commercial tools Lynis and Snort. The latter two programs each have an open-source kernel that can be used free of charge.

### chmod [options] changes files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod</samp> changes the nine access bits of files. Together with each file, it’s stored whether the owner (user), the group members (group), and other users (others) are allowed to read, write, and execute the file.

The access bits can be changed using the character combination group <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">+/-</samp> access type, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">g+w</samp>, to give all group members write permission. You specify the group with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">u</samp> (user), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">g</samp> (group), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">o</samp> (others), or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">a</samp> (all); you specify the access type with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">r</samp> (read), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">w</samp> (write), or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">x</samp> (execute).

#### setuid, setgid, and sticky Bits

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setuid</samp> bit, which is often also referred to as the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">suid</samp> bit, causes programs to be executed as if the owner themselves had started the program. If the owner of a program is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>, then anyone can run the program as if they were <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>.

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setgid</samp> bit has the same function for programs as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setuid</samp>, but for group membership. For directories, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setgid</samp> bit causes newly created files in this directory to belong to the group of the directory and not, as usual, to the group of the user who created the file.

For directories in which everyone is allowed to change the files, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sticky</samp> bit makes sure that everyone is only allowed to delete their own files and not those of other users. For example, the bit is set for the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/tmp</samp> directory. Every user is allowed to create temporary files in this directory. However, it must be avoided that every user can also rename or delete external files.

To set the special bits <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setuid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setgid</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sticky</samp> with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod</samp>, the following character combinations are provided:

```
setuid: u+s setgid: g+s sticky: +t 
```

For <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setuid</samp> to work, the x-bit for the owner must also be set (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">u+x</samp>).

For <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setgid</samp> to work, the x bit for the group must also be set (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">g+x</samp>).

#### Octal Notation

Instead of using letters, the access type can also be specified using an octal number that consists of a maximum of four digits. For the access bits, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">u</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">g</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">o</samp> are each assigned a digit. Each digit is composed of the values <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">4</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">2</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">1</samp> for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">r</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">w</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">x</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">660</samp> thus means <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rw-rw----</samp>, while <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">777</samp> stands for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">rwxrwxrwx</samp>.

The three special bits <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setuid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setgid</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sticky</samp> have the octal values 4000, 2000, and 1000\. While setting these bits in octal notation is simple, a security mechanism prevents the bits from being inadvertently deactivated for directories. After <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod 2770 dir</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod 770 dir</samp>, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setgid bit</samp> remains set! To remove it, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod g-s dir</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod 00770 dir</samp> (with two leading zeros).

To determine the access bits of an existing file or directory in octal notation, you must use the [stat](#S_001.xhtml_stat) command.

#### Options

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--silent</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--quiet</samp>
    Doesn’t display any error messages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--recursive</samp>
    Additionally changes the access rights of files in all subdirectories.

#### Examples

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">secure</samp> file can now be executed by all users. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">secure</samp> can be a shell script for creating a backup, for example.

```
user$ chmod a+rx secure 
```

The following command revokes the read and write permission for all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.odt</samp> files in the current directory for all users outside of your own group:

```
user$ chmod o-rw *.odt 
```

Only <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> is allowed to read the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">server.key</samp> file, nobody can change it:

```
root# chown root:root server.key
root# chmod 400 server.key 
```

### chown [options] user[:group] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chown</samp> changes the owner and (optionally) also the group membership of a file. The owner of a file can only be changed by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>, while the group can also be set by other users (see [chgrp](#C_001.xhtml_chgrp)).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--recursive</samp>
    Also changes the group assignment of files in all subdirectories.

#### Example

The following commands ensure that all files within <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/mysql</samp> are assigned to the user and the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mysql</samp> group so that only the MySQL server process can read and modify the files:

```
root# chown -R mysql:mysql /var/lib/mysql
root# chmod -R o-rwx /var/lib/mysql 
```

### chpasswd [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chpasswd</samp> makes it possible to change passwords in scripts, that is, in contrast to [passwd](#P_001.xhtml_passwd), without user interaction. The command reads the usernames and passwords from the standard input, whereby the information must be entered line by line in the form <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name:password</samp>. The command is often called in the form <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chpasswd < pwfile.txt</samp> to process the combinations of names and passwords stored in a file.

You can use options to control how the passwords are encrypted (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man chpasswd</samp>). However, usually it’s not advisable to use these options. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chpasswd</samp> then uses the default settings specified by the distribution in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/logins.def</samp> file.

#### Example

The following script uses [useradd](#U_001.xhtml_useradd) to set up 30 accounts: <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">user01</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">user30</samp>. For each account, a password generated via [mkpasswd](#M_001.xhtml_mkpasswd) is set. For this purpose, the name and password are output using [echo](#E_001.xhtml_echo), and the output is passed directly to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chpasswd</samp> using the pipe operator. All account names and the corresponding passwords are also saved in the text file, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">students.txt</samp>. Finally, [chage](#C_001.xhtml_chage) is used to define that every user must change their password immediately after the first login.

```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {01..30}; do
  user="user$i"
  pw=$(mkpasswd -l 8 -d 0 -C 0 -s 0)
  echo "Account: $user  Password: $pw" >> students.txt
  useradd $user
  echo "$user:$pw" | chpasswd
  chage -d 0 $user
done 
```

### chroot directory [command]

Without further parameters, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chroot</samp> starts a new shell that uses the specified directory as the root directory (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp>). You can work interactively in this shell. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exit</samp> takes you back to the original shell.

If you specify an optional command, this command is started instead of the shell. During the execution of the command, the specified directory is again used as the root directory.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chroot</samp> is useful for performing administrative tasks in a file system that wasn’t activated at boot time. The following commands assume that you’ve started a computer from a rescue system or a USB flash drive. Then mount the system partition (in the example, it’s <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sda4</samp>) in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/mnt/rescue</samp> directory, make this directory the new root directory, and then reset the forgotten <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> password using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">passwd</samp>:

```
root# mkdir /mnt/rescue
root# mount /dev/sda4 /mnt/rescue
root# chroot /mnt/rescue
root# passwd
Change password for root user.
Enter a new password: **********
Enter the new password again: **********
root# exit
root# reboot 
```

### chsh -s shell [user]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chsh</samp> changes the default shell that is automatically called after logging in. All shells entered in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/shells</samp> are available for selection—usually <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/bin/bash</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/bin/csh</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/bin/zsh</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chsh</samp> command changes the [passwd](#P_001.xhtml_passwd) file and enters the new shell there.

Every user can change their own default shell as they wish. The shell of another user can only be changed by the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp> user. The new shell must be specified with the complete directory. The change will take effect with the next login.

#### Example

The following command sets up the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nologin</samp> program instead of a shell. It prevents a direct login and is useful if you’ve set up a user only for automated (backup) scripts or only to access an email account:

```
root# chsh -s /usr/sbin/nologin mailuser 
```

### chvt n

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chvt</samp> activates the console <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>. In older Linux distributions, the numbers 1 to 6 were reserved for text consoles, while the graphics system of the first user was executed on console 7\. Consoles 8, 9, and so on were used for further parallel logins.

In newer distributions, the display manager usually runs in graphics mode on console 1\. Console 2 is intended for the graphics system of the first user that has logged in first. Consoles 3 to 6 are operated in text mode.

### cksum file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cksum</samp> determines the checksum and the length of the file in bytes. The checksum can be used to quickly determine whether two files are identical. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cksum</samp> provides more reliable results than the related <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sum</samp> command. The [sha](#S_001.xhtml_sha) command is mathematically and cryptographically much more secure.

### clear

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">clear</samp> or Ctrl+ L deletes the content of the console.

### cmp [options] file1 file2

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cmp</samp> compares two files byte by byte and returns the position of the first deviation. If the files are identical, the command doesn’t display any message at all. [diff](#D_001.xhtml_diff) is generally more suitable than <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cmp</samp> for comparing text files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--show-chars</samp>
    Shows the first text character where the files differ from each other.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--verbose</samp>
    Provides a list of all deviations.

### cnf command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cnf</samp> stands for command not found and is a SUSE-specific command that reveals which package doesn’t yet contain the command you’re looking for.

On Red Hat and Fedora distributions, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/libexec/pk-command-not-found</samp> command executed by the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> contains a comparable function; on Ubuntu, this is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/lib/command-not-found</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">command-not-found</samp> package. This package is also available on Debian. However, it must be installed there manually and set up once using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">update-command-not-found</samp> command.

#### Example

```
user$ cnf jmacs
The 'jmacs' program can be found in the following package:
  * joe [ path: /usr/bin/jmacs, Repository: zypp (repo-oss) ]
Try installing with:
    sudo zypper install joe 
```

### column [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">column</samp> reads the specified file, splits each line into several parts, and then outputs all parts in indented columns.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">outseparator</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp>
    Specifies how the columns are to be separated from each other in the output (by default, two spaces are used).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">inseparator</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp>
    Specifies how the data to be imported is separated from each other. By default, whitespace is used as a separator, that is, space and tab characters.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp>
    Formats the output as a table.

### compress [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">compress</samp> compresses or decompresses the specified file. For compressed files, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.Z</samp> identifier is appended to the file name. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">compress</samp> only exists for compatibility reasons. The alternatives [](#B_001.xhtml_bzip2), [](#G_001.xhtml_gzip), and [xz](#X_001.xhtml_xz) are considerably more powerful.

### continue [n]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> construct <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">continue</samp> skips the body of a [for](#F_001.xhtml_for), [while](#W_001.xhtml_while), or [until](#U_001.xhtml_until) loop in shell scripts and continues the loop with the next run. This process can be carried out for several loop levels using the optional numerical value.

### convert or magick [options] image old image new

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert</samp> from the ImageMagick package converts image files from one format to another. In its simplest form, it uses the syntax <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert name.png name.jpg</samp> to convert the specified PNG file into a JPEG file. The original file is retained.

As of version 7, ImageMagick provides the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">magick</samp> command. It will replace <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert</samp> in the future. For compatibility reasons, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert</samp> can still be used with distributions that already provide version 7\. Other distributions haven’t yet made the leap to ImageMagick 7\. That’s why I treat the command in this book under the established name <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert</samp>.

Various image parameters can be changed simultaneously with more than 100 options. The following list is therefore only a selection:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-blur</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">radius</samp>
    Blurs the image.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-colors</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Reduces the number of RGB colors to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-colorspace CMYK|GRAY|RGB|Transparent|YUV</samp>
    Indicates the desired color model (with numerous other models to choose from).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-compress None|BZip|Fax|Group4|JPEG|JPEG2000|Lossless|LZW|RLE|Zip</samp>
    Specifies the desired compression format. However, the actual formats available for selection depend on the image format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-contrast</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+contrast</samp>
    Reduces or increases the contrast of the image.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-crop</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">geometry</samp>
    Cuts out the desired part of the image. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-crop 50x50+100+100</samp> describes a 50×50 pixel area that starts at the coordinate position (100, 100).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-filter Point|Box|Triangle|Hermite|Hanning|Hamming ...</samp>
    Applies the desired filter to the image.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-gaussian</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">radius</samp>
    Blurs the filter with the Gaussian operator.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-normalize</samp>
    Normalizes the color distribution in the image.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-quality</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the desired compression quality. The permissible values for n depend on the image format (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">100</samp> for JPEG).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-resize</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">NxN</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-resize</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n%</samp>
    Changes the resolution of the image.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-rotate</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">angle</samp>
    Rotates the image clockwise by the specified angle in degrees.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-trim</samp>
    Cuts off monochrome image edges if they have the same color as the corner points of the image.

Further options are described in detail on the following website:

[https://imagemagick.org/script/command-line-processing.php](https://imagemagick.org/script/command-line-processing.php)

For security reasons, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert</samp> refuses to process some file types by default (e.g., PDF files). This can be remedied by removing the corresponding line from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">policy.xml</samp>. I’ve commented out the PDF line in the following listing:

```
# file /etc/ImageMagick-6/policy.xml or /etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml
<policymap>
  ...
  <!-- <policy domain="coder" rights="none" pattern="PDF" /> – >
  ...
</policymap> 
```

#### Examples

The following three examples show simple applications of the command:

```
user$ convert -resize 100x100 in.jpg out.png
user$ convert -type Grayscale in.jpg out.eps
user$ convert -quality 80     in.bmp out.jpg 
```

The following command converts a PNG file into an EPS file according to the PostScript Level 2 specification (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert</samp> usually creates files for PostScript Level 3\. These are then often significantly larger without any advantages). All image layers are placed on top of each other. Transparent areas of the PNG file are displayed in white, not black.

```
user$ convert -flatten -alpha remove -background white in.png EPS2:out.eps 
```

The next command creates a PDF file containing all JPEG images from the current directory (one image per page). You can use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--quality</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--density</samp> options to control the quality and size of the resulting PDFs.

```
user$ convert -density 200x200 -quality 80 *.jpg allebilder.pdf 
```

### cp [optionen] source target
cp [options] files target directory

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> copies files and directories. Individual files can be renamed during copying. When editing multiple files (e.g., by specifying wildcards), these can only be copied to another directory, but not renamed. Statements of the type <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp *.tex *.bak</samp> aren’t permitted. Commands comparable to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> are [mv](#M_001.xhtml_mv) for moving and renaming files, and [ln](#L_001.xhtml_ln) for creating links. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> supports the following options, among others:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--archive</samp>
    Retains as many attributes of the files as possible. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-a</samp> is an abbreviation for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-dpR</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--backup</samp>
    Renames existing files to backup files (file name plus <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">~</samp>) instead of overwriting them.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--dereference</samp>
    Only copies the reference for links, but not the file that’s referenced by the link.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--interactive</samp>
    Prompts before existing files are overwritten.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--link</samp>
    Creates hard links instead of copying the files. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> is used with this option, it has the same functionality as [ln](#L_001.xhtml_ln).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--preserve</samp>
    Leaves the information about the owner, the group membership, the access rights and the time of the last modification. Without this option, the copy belongs to those who execute <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> (user and group), and the time is set to the current time.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--recursive</samp>
    Additionally copies subdirectories and the files they contain.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--reflink[=auto]</samp>
    Initially copies only the metadata of the file, that is, creates a shallow copy of the file. The copy therefore takes up almost no space in the file system. Nevertheless, it’s independent of the original: as soon as data blocks of the original or the copy are changed, these blocks are reallocated.

    Shallow copies only work if this function is supported by the file system. This is the case with Btrfs and current versions of XFS, but not with ext4\.
