If the file system isn’t compatible, this option will result in an error unless you specify the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">auto</samp> mode in which <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> itself decides which type of copy is possible.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--symbolic-link</samp>
    Creates symbolic links instead of copying the files or directories. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> therefore has the functionality of [ln](#L_001.xhtml_ln) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--update</samp>
    Copies files only if no file of the same name with a newer date will get overwritten.

#### Copying Directories

If you want to copy an entire directory with all the files and subdirectories it contains, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cp -r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">source directory target directory</samp>. This also copies hidden files and subdirectories. If you want access rights and times to be preserved when copying, you need to use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp> option instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>.

The question of whether the source directory itself or only its content is copied is somewhat difficult. If the target directory already exists, the new subdirectory named <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sourcedirectory</samp> will be created in it, and the entire contents of the source directory will be copied there. However, if the target directory doesn’t yet exist, it will be created; in this case, only the content of the source directory is copied to the newly created target directory, but not the source directory itself. [cpio](#C_001.xhtml_cpio), [rsync](#R_001.xhtml_rsync), and [tar](#T_001.xhtml_tar) are also suitable for copying entire directory trees.

#### Examples

The following command copies all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.tex</samp> files from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">book</samp> subdirectory to the current directory. The dot indicates the current directory as the target directory.

```
user$ cp book/*.tex . 
```

The second command creates a backup copy of the entire <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">book</samp> directory:

```
user$ cp -a book bak-book 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cp</samp> can’t be used to rename multiple files during the copy process. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cp *.xxx *.yyy</samp> therefore doesn’t copy all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.xxx</samp> files to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.yyy</samp> files. To perform such operations, you must use [for](#F_001.xhtml_for) or [sed](#S_001.xhtml_sed). In the following command, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">for</samp> creates a loop over all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.xxx</samp> files. The expression <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">${i%.xxx}.yyy</samp> removes the ending <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.xxx</samp> and replaces it with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.yyy</samp>. If you replace <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cp</samp> with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mv</samp>, the files won’t get copied but renamed.

```
user$ for i in *.xxx; do cp $i ${i%.xxx}.yyy; done 
```

The procedure with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sed</samp> is somewhat more complicated: <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> provides the list of files to be copied and passes it on to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sed</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sed</samp> uses the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">s</samp> command (regular find and replace) to create a list of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cp</samp> commands and passes these on to a new <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sh</samp> shell, which then executes the commands.

```
user$ ls *.xxx | sed 's/\(.*\)\.xxx$/cp & \1.yyy/' | sh 
```

### cpio command [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cpio</samp> combines multiple files into one archive and copies them to another data medium, a streamer, or another directory. Similarly, the command can also be used to reload such data. On Linux, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cpio</samp> is rather uncommon; [tar](#T_001.xhtml_tar) is usually used instead. The major <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cpio</samp> commands are as follows:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp>
    (input) Reads an archive from the standard input and extracts the files it contains.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp>
    (output) Combines files into an archive and transfers the archive to the standard output. The files to be processed are often determined by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> and then passed on to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cpio</samp> via a pipe.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>
    (pass through) Transfers archives between different directories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp>
    Displays the contents of an archive from the standard input.

Details of these actions can be controlled by additional options.

#### Example

The following commands first archive all files from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc</samp> directory. Then, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cpio -t</samp> displays the list of backed up files as a check.

```
root# cd /etc
root# find . | cpio -o > /tmp/etc-backup.cpio
root# cpio -t < /tmp/etc-backup.cpio 
```

### crontab [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">crontab</samp> command helps you administrate custom cron jobs in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/spool/cron/username</samp> file (see [crontab](#C_001.xhtml_crontab)). Cron jobs are executed automatically in the background at the scheduled times, such as once an hour or every Sunday evening.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-e</samp>
    Opens an editor for editing the crontab file. Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vi</samp> is used as the editor. If you want to use a different editor, you must set the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">EDITOR</samp> environment variable accordingly. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">crontab</samp> checks compliance with the crontab syntax rules when saving.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Lists the current crontab entries.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Deletes all crontab entries.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">username</samp>
    Edits the crontab file of the specified user. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> option is only available to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>.

### cryptsetup [options] command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cryptsetup</samp> from the package of the same name uses functions of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dm_crypt</samp> kernel module. It sets up, activates, and deactivates crypto devices. A sufficiently large image file can also be used instead of a device. This can be created in advance, for example, via [dd](#D_001.xhtml_dd) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">if=/dev/zero of=cryptoImage bs=1M count=n</samp>, where <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> is the desired size in mebibytes (MiB).

At this point, I’ll only describe the most important LUKS-specific commands of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cryptsetup</samp>:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">luksAddKey</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Sets up an additional password that provides access to the crypto container. To run the command, an existing password must be entered (use any password you like). A maximum of eight passwords are allowed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">luksClose</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device mappingname</samp>
    Deactivates a crypto device.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">luksDump</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Provides meta information about the crypto container (e.g., the encryption algorithm).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">luksFormat --type luks2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Sets up a crypto container in the specified device in the current LUKS2 format. Without the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--type</samp> option, the command uses the still supported but obsolete LUKS1 format.

    You must then enter the passphrase twice, which should be at least 20 characters long for security reasons. You can select the desired encryption algorithm with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-c</samp> and set a different key length with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp>. The algorithms available for selection are listed in the pseudo file; <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/crypto</samp>. The output of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cryptsetup --help</samp> command reveals in the last lines which algorithm and which key length are used by default. This is currently the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aes-xts-plain64</samp> algorithm with a 256-bit key.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">luksOpen</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device mappingname</samp>
    Activates the crypto container in the specified device and assigns it a name. The resulting crypto device can then be used via <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/mapper/mappingname</samp>.

#### Example

The following commands show how to first format a USB flash drive (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdh1</samp>) as a crypto device (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">luksFormat</samp>) and then activate the device under the arbitrarily chosen name of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mycontainer</samp> (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">luksOpen</samp>). Needless to say, your data is only as secure as your password or your passphrase, which consists of several words. A password length of at least 20 characters is recommended.

You can then use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/mapper/mycontainer</samp> like a hard disk partition or a logical volume—that is, set up a file system, integrate it into the directory tree, and so on. After <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">umount</samp>, you must remember to deactivate the crypto device again (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">luksClose</samp>) to release <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdh1</samp>. Only at this point can you remove the USB flash drive.

```
root# cryptsetup luksFormat --type luks2 /dev/sdh1
This will overwrite data on /dev/sdh1 irrevocably.
Are you sure? (Type uppercase yes): YES
Enter LUKS passphrase: ********************
Verify passphrase: ********************
Command successful.
root# cryptsetup luksOpen /dev/sdh1 mycontainer
Enter LUKS passphrase: ********************
root# mkfs.ext4 /dev/mapper/mycontainer
root# mount /dev/mapper/mycontainer /test
root# ... use the encrypted file system ...
root# umount /test/
root# cryptsetup luksClose mycontainer 
```

### csplit [options] file splitting position

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">csplit</samp> splits a text file into several individual files at predefined points. The splitting position can be specified either by a direct line specification or by a search pattern. As a result, the command returns the files <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xx00</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xx01</samp>, and so on and then displays their lengths on the screen. By specifying the appropriate options, “nicer” file names are of course also possible.

[cat](#C_001.xhtml_cat) can reassemble the original file from these individual files. Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">csplit</samp>, the split command can be used to split binary files.

#### Specification of the Splitting Positions

The splitting positions are specified either by a number of lines or by a search pattern. In the former case, the file is split after <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> lines, whereas in the latter case, it’s split before or after the occurrence of the search pattern. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">csplit</samp> is to split the file multiple times, which is usually the case, the number of lines or the split pattern must be followed by the number of times the operation is to be repeated.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp>
    Splits the file in the line before the pattern occurs. (The line with the pattern found becomes the first line of the subsequent file.)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/+</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Splits the file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> lines after (+) or before (-) the occurrence of the pattern.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Splits the file after <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> lines.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">}</samp>
    Splits the file into <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>+1 individual files (and not just two files).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{*}</samp>
    Splits the file into the corresponding number of individual files each time the search pattern occurs or each time after <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> lines.

#### Options

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--prefix=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Uses the specified file name to name the output files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-k</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--keep-files</samp>
    Prevents files that have already been created from being deleted again if an error occurs. The option must be used in particular for pattern specifications in the form n <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">{*}</samp>. The pattern is specified as in [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-z</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--elide-empty-files</samp>
    Prevents the creation of empty files. Without this option, empty files can occur in particular if the first line of the source file already matches the search pattern.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">csplit</samp> splits <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">total.txt</samp> into the files <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">part.00</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">part.01</samp>, and so on. The individual files are each 100 lines long. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat</samp> then creates a copy of the original file.

```
user$ csplit -k -f part. total.txt 100 {*}
user$ cat part.* > copy.txt 
```

In the second example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">csplit</samp> splits the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">total.txt</samp> file into smaller files, whereby the split always occurs when a line begins with the text <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">% ===</samp>.

```
user$ csplit -k -f part. total.txt '/^% ===/' {*} 
```

### curl [options] [url]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">curl</samp> helps with the transfer of files from or to a server, whereby all conceivable protocols are supported (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SFTP, SCP, etc.).

The external file or directory is specified by a URL string (Uniform Resource Locator) that starts with the protocol name (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">http://server.com/file)</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--data 'data'</samp>
    Sends the specified data with the request. For <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--data</samp>, the following alternatives are available: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--data-binary</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--data-raw</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--data-urlencode</samp>. With all variants, the data can also be read from the specified file via <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@file</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--limit-rate</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Limits the transfer rate to the specified number of bytes per second. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> can be followed by the letter <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">k</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">m</samp> to limit the transfer rate to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> KiB or MiB per second.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--netrc</samp>
    Instructs the command to read the login data from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.netrc</samp> file. Using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--netrc-file file.txt</samp>, you can alternatively specify a different location for this file. Both variants are more secure than the password transfer via <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Saves the downloaded data in the specified file instead of forwarding it to the standard output.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--oauth2-bearer 'token'</samp>
    Sends the specified bearer token with the request.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n1-n2</samp>
    Transfers the specified byte range of the file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--silent</samp>
    Dispenses with status outputs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Uploads the specified file to the server, that is, in the opposite direction of the usual use of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">curl</samp> (transfer). Instead of the file name, the hyphen character (-) can also be entered to process data from the standard input.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name:password</samp>
    Specifies the login name and password.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-X</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--request GET|POST|PUT|...</samp>
    Specifies the desired request type (by default, this is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GET</samp>).

#### Examples

The following command transfers the specified file to the FTP server <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">backupserver</samp> and saves it in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir</samp> directory:

```
user$ curl -T file -u username:password ftp://backupserver/dir 
```

To process data from the standard input channel, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-T</samp> to specify a hyphen as the file name. The following command saves the result of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">tar</samp> command directly in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name.tgz</samp> file on the FTP server:

```
user$ tar czf - dir/ | curl -T - -u usern:pw ftp://bserver/name.tgz 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">curl</samp> is also suitable for testing REST APIs as follows:

```
user$ $ curl -X PUT https://httpbin.org/put?para=123 -d @mydata.json \
             -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
```

#### Alternatives

To download files via FTP or HTTP, you can also use [wget](#W_001.xhtml_wget) instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">curl</samp>. If, on the other hand, you’re more interested in debugging REST APIs, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">curlie</samp> is a good choice (see [https://github.com/rs/curlie](https://github.com/rs/curlie)). This <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">curl</samp> alternative displays the transferred header by default, formats JSON documents in color, and more.

### cut [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cut</samp> extracts the columns specified by options from each line of text.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--bytes</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp>
    Extracts the characters specified in a list. Individual entries may be separated by commas (but not by spaces). Instead of individual characters, entire ranges can also be specified, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">–b 3-6,9,11-15</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">character</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--delimiter</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">character</samp>
    Specifies the separator for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp> to be used instead of the tab character.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--fields</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp>
    Extracts like <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-b</samp>, but now for fields (data records) that must be separated by tab characters.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--only-delimited</samp>
    Eliminates all lines that don’t contain any data corresponding to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp> option. This can’t be used together with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-b</samp>.

In practice, the extraction of individual text columns is often much easier via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">awk</samp> than by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cut</samp>.

#### Example

In the following example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cut</samp> reads the first, third, and seventh columns from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/passwd</samp> file, that is, the username, the UID, and the default shell. The separator in this file is the colon.

```
root# cut -d\: -f1,3,7 /etc/passwd
root:0:/bin/bash
bin:1:/sbin/nologin
daemon:2:/sbin/nologin
adm:3:/sbin/nologin
... 
```

## D

### date [options] [+format]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">date</samp> returns the current date and time or changes this data. Changes may only be made by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">date</samp> can display the time in various formats.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">time span</samp>
    Adds or subtracts a time span to or from the current time (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d +3days</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d -4hours</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newtime</samp>
    Changes the date and/or time of the computer clock.

The following list shows the most important format codes. The format string must be enclosed in quotation marks.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%Y</samp>
    The year as a four-digit number

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%l</samp>
    The month as a number (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">12</samp>)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%m</samp>
    The month as a two-digit number (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">01</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">12</samp>)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%b</samp>
    The month as a short character string (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Jan</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Dec</samp>)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%B</samp>
    The month as a long string (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">January</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">December</samp>)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%d</samp>
    The day of the month as a two-digit number (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">01</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">31</samp>)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%e</samp>
    The day of the month as a number (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">31</samp>), with single-digit numbers preceded by a space

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%H</samp>
    The hour as a two-digit number (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">00</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">23</samp>)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%M</samp>
    The minute as a two-digit number (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">00</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">59</samp>)

#### Examples

The following three statements provide the current time in ISO format, the date in three weeks, and the time four hours ago:

```
user$ date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
2025-03-12 17:46:39
user$ date -d +3weeks "+%Y-%m-%d"
2025-04-02
user$ date -d -4hours "+%H:%M:%S"
13:47:25 
```

The following script creates a compressed <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">tar</samp> archive of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/home/kofler/data</samp> directory. The archive is saved under two file names: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mydata-day-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dd</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.tar.gz</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mydata- month-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mm</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.tar.gz</samp>.

If the script is run daily, you’ll have 43 backup versions over time reflecting the state of the backup directory for the past 28 to 31 days and for the past 12 months.

```
#!/bin/bash
fname1=/backup/mydata-day-$(date "+%d").tar.gz
fname2=/backup/mydata-month-$(date "+%m").tar.gz
tar czf $fname1 /home/kofler/data
cp $fname1 $fname2
chmod 600 $fname1 $fname2 
```

### dconf command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dconf</samp> is a low-level command for changing the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dconf</samp> database, in which Gnome stores countless settings. Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dconf</samp>, you should generally use the [gsettings](#G_001.xhtml_gsettings) command, which contains more control mechanisms.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dump/load</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir</samp>
    Reads an entire configuration directory recursively and writes it to the standard output (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dump</samp>) or reads it from the standard input (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">load</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir</samp>
    Outputs the entries of a directory (not recursive).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">read</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">key</samp>
    Reads an entry.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reset</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">key/dir</samp>
    Resets an entry or an entire configuration directory to the initial value(s). The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp> option must be specified for directories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">write</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">key value</samp>
    Saves or overwrites an entry.

#### Examples

The following two commands show you how to make a backup of all Gnome settings and restore the saved state later:

```
user dconf dump / > dconf.bak
user dconf load / < dconf.bak 
```

The following command causes a total reset of all Gnome settings:

```
user$ dconf reset -f / 
```

### dd options

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp> transfers data between different storage media (SSD, USB flash drive, etc.) and converts the data if required. The command can be used to exchange data between different computer architectures.

Not only can <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp> copy individual files, but it also can access devices directly. This allows you to copy entire hard disks (partitions), change the boot sector of the hard disk, and so on. No file system needs to be set up on the data medium. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp> is used without options, it reads the data from the standard input (ending with Ctrl+Z) and writes to the standard output. The options of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp> are specified without preceding minus signs!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bs=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Determines the block size for the input and output file. (The block size indicates how many bytes are read or written in one pass.) Caution: By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp> uses a block size of only 512 bytes. That is extremely inefficient! If you read or write to hard disks or SSDs and use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp>, you should work with at least <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bs=1M</samp>. The suffix <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">M</samp> stands for 1,024 × 1,024 bytes, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">K</samp> stand for 1,024 bytes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">conv=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mode</samp>
    Converts the data during copying. Various settings are permitted for mode, including <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lcase</samp> (convert uppercase to lowercase), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ucase</samp> (convert lowercase to uppercase), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">swab</samp> (swap 2 bytes at a time), and so on. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">conv=fsync</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp> ends its work with a sync call, that is, waits for the physical completion of the write process. This is particularly important if you suspect that the storage medium may be defective. Only with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">conv=fsync</samp> does <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp> receive error messages from the kernel in this case.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">count=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Copies only <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> blocks (and not the entire data).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ibs=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Determines the block size of the source file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">if=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">source file</samp>
    Specifies the source file (instead of the standard input).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">obs=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Determines the block size of the target file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">of=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">target file</samp>
    Specifies the target file (instead of the standard output).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">seek=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Skips <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> blocks before starting the output.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">skip=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Skips <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> blocks before starting to read.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status=progress</samp>
    Displays the progress of the copying process. (By default, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status=none</samp>.)

Note that direct access to devices (e.g., via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cat /dev/xxx ></samp>) is often faster than <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp>. You also don’t need to worry about the ideal block size.

#### Examples

The following command transfers the ISO file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">opensuse.iso</samp> directly to the data medium with the device <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdc</samp>, for example, to a USB flash drive. You should note that all previously saved data on this data medium will be lost! For this reason, make sure that you enter the correct device name. If the device specified with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">of</samp> is your current hard disk, you’ll lose its contents!

```
root# dd if=opensuse.iso of=/dev/sdc bs=1M status=progress 
```

The second command creates a 10 GiB raw image file for a virtualization program (e.g., QEMU/KVM). This image file simply consists of zeros that are read from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/zero</samp> device.

```
root# dd if=/dev/zero of=image.raw bs=1M count=10000 
```

#### Alternatives

Depending on the intended use, the following two variants are available instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp>:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd_rescue</samp> or, depending on the distribution, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ddrescue</samp> (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gddrescue</samp> package), attempts to create a copy even if individual data sectors of the source device are defective.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dcfldd</samp> is optimized for forensic tasks. Among other things, the command can use checksums to verify that the copy is really identical.

You can find a good comparison between <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dd_rescue</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dcfldd</samp> at the following address:

[https://superuser.com/questions/355310](https://superuser.com/questions/355310)

### declare [options] var[=value]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">declare</samp> assigns a new value and/or various properties to shell variables. The command is mainly used in shell scripts. If it’s called without parameters, all known variables will be listed with their contents. Note that no spaces may be entered before or after the equal sign!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-A</samp>
    Declares the variable as an associative array.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Declares the variable as read-only. The variable can only be read, but not changed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp>
    Declares the variable as an environment variable (similar to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">export</samp>). The variable is therefore also available to other commands or in subshells.

### delgroup [options] name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">delgroup</samp> deletes the specified group on Debian and Ubuntu systems, following the rules from [etc/deluser.conf](#04_001.xhtml_deluser.conf). In Fedora and Red Hat, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">delgroup</samp> is a link to the [groupdel](#G_001.xhtml_groupdel) command, which has other options.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--only-if-empty</samp>
    Deletes the group only if no users are assigned to it.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--system</samp>
    Deletes the group only if it’s a system group.

### delta [options] file1 file2

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">delta</samp> is a variant of [diff](#D_001.xhtml_diff). The command from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git-delta</samp> package compares the contents of two text files and displays the differences graphically (see also [https://dandavison.github.io/delta](https://dandavison.github.io/delta)). While <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff</samp> is optimized for use in scripts and for patch management, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">delta</samp> excels in interactive use.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--help</samp>
    Displays a help text. (There is no <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page.)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--light</samp>
    Uses colors that are suitable for a terminal with a light background. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">delta</samp> is intended for dark terminals (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--dark</samp> option).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--side-by-side</samp>
    Shows the differences next to each other instead of below each other.

### deluser [options] name deluser name group

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">deluser</samp> deletes the specified user on Debian and Ubuntu systems and follows the rules from [etc/deluser.conf](#04_001.xhtml_deluser.conf). As a result, the home directory is usually not deleted. In Fedora and Red Hat, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">deluser</samp> is a link to the [userdel](#U_001.xhtml_userdel) command with other options.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--remove-all-files</samp>
    Deletes the user’s home directory and all other files (e.g., various spool and mail files).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--remove-home</samp>
    Also deletes the user’s home directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--system</samp>
    Deletes the user only if it’s a system user.

If the command is run as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">deluser</samp> name group, it removes the user from the specified group. The command is therefore complementary to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">adduser</samp> name group.

### depmod [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">depmod</samp> creates the module dependency file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">modules.dep</samp> as well as various <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.map</samp> files in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/lib/modules/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kernelversion</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp> directory. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*-map</samp> files specify which kernel module is to be loaded for which hardware component.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-A</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--quick</samp>
    Tests first whether existing <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.dep</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.map</samp> files are still up-to-date. In this case, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">depmod</samp> doesn’t regenerate the files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--basedir</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp>
    Specifies the directory for which the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.dep</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.map</samp> files are to be generated. By default, the command updates the files for the running kernel.

### df [options] [directory]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">df</samp> provides information about where hard disks (partitions) or other drives are mounted in the file tree and how much storage space is available on them. Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">df</samp> returns a list of all active partitions. If you pass a directory to the command, however, it only displays the data of the partition in which this directory is physically located. On systems with many partitions, you can easily determine in which partition a specific directory is saved.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp>
    Indicates the storage space in an easily readable form in MiB or GiB.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--inodes</samp>
    Provides information about the available I-nodes (instead of the free storage space in KiB).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fs</samp>
    Considers only file systems of the specified type, such as only ext4 file systems with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t ext4</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T</samp>
    Specifies the file system for each partition or data medium.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fs</samp>
    Ignores the specified file system.

#### Example

On the example system, the system partition <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp> still has 15 GiB of free disk space. The other file systems are used for administrative purposes (dynamic display of devices) and for storing Ubuntu-specific snap packages. Due to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-x tmpfs</samp> option, numerous temporary file systems, that is, those only located in RAM, aren’t taken into account.

```
root# df -h -T -x tmpfs
Filesystem                Type      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
udev                      devtmpfs   16G     0   16G   0% /dev
/dev/nvme0n1p1            vfat     1021M  254M  768M  25% /boot/efi
/dev/nvme0n1p4            ext4      119G   32G   81G  29% /
/dev/mapper/mycryptpart   ext4      1.5T  767G  634G  55% /crypt
/dev/loop0                squashfs   62M   62M     0 100% /snap/authy/5
/dev/loop1                squashfs   56M   56M     0 100% /snap/core18/1885
... 
```

#### Alternatives

There are several alternatives to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">df</samp> that present the result more legibly. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">duf</samp> command from the package of the same name automatically differentiates between “real” and virtual file systems, and it formats the output much more clearly than <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">df</samp> (see [Figure 1](#D_001.xhtml_bD.1)). We also recommend <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dysk</samp> (see the [https://dystroy.org/dysk](https://dystroy.org/dysk) project page).

[![“duf” Providing a Good Overview of the Free Storage Space on All Data Media](bilderklein/kleinduf.png)](img-bD.1.xhtml)

**Figure 1**     “duf” Providing a Good Overview of the Free Storage Space on All Data Media

### dhclient interface

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dhclient</samp> command from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dhcp-client</samp> package obtains the parameters for the network configuration from a DHCP server in most distributions. The command is ideal for an ad hoc network configuration for new server installations. Some distributions use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dhclient3</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dhcpcd</samp> commands as alternatives to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dhclient</samp>.

#### Example

The following command performs an automatic network configuration for the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">eth0</samp> interface:

```
root# dhclient eth0 
```

### diff [options] file1 file2

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff</samp> usually compares two text files. The result is a list of all lines that differ from each other. The command is relatively “intelligent”; that is, if some lines are inserted in one file compared to the other, only this deviation will be reported. Other lines are recognized as identical again, although they now have different line numbers. The command can therefore be used to quickly document the differences between two versions of a program listing.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff</samp> can also compare two directories in the form <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-r dir1 dir2</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Treats multiple spaces and lines as single spaces or lines.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-q</samp>
    Only indicates whether two files are different or not. In this variant, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff</samp> dispenses with the detailed listing of all differences.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Recursively compares two directories. The result lists which files only exist in the first directory and which only exist in the second directory. For files that exist in both directories but have different content, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff</samp> displays the differences. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff -r</samp> can be combined well with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-q</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp>
    Ignores spaces and blank lines completely.

#### Example

The following command compares the contents of your own MySQL configuration file with the configuration suggested by the package. The lines beginning with < show the current status (i.e., text from the first file passed to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff</samp>), and the lines beginning with > show the corresponding passage from the second file.

```
root# diff /etc/mysql/my.cnf /etc/mysql/my.cnf.dpkg-dist
100,101c87,88
< server-id             = 100
< log_bin                       = /var/log/mysql/mysql-bin.log
---
> #server-id            = 1
> #log_bin                      = /var/log/mysql/mysql-bin.log
... 
```

#### Alternatives

To put it mildly, “reading” <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">diff</samp> results takes some getting used to. It’s much more convenient to use the [delta](#D_001.xhtml_delta) command. If you have a graphical user interface, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">meld</samp> program can be very helpful. Most editors can also highlight the difference between two files (e.g., VS Code).

### dig [options] [@dnsserver] host/ipaddr [type]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dig</samp> runs queries on a domain name server in a similar way to [host](#H_001.xhtml_host) and [whois](#W_001.xhtml_whois). Using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dig</samp>, you can control the process by means of a particularly large number of options that can’t even be hinted at here (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man dig</samp>).

In its simplest form <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dig host</samp> contacts the DNS server set in [etc/resolv.conf](#04_001.xhtml_resolv.conf) and returns the A-record. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">@1.2.3.4</samp>, you can specify the IP address of an alternative DNS server. If you’re not interested in the A-record but in other data, you must enter its type in the third parameter.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-4 / -6</samp>
    Uses only IPv4 or only IPv6.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+nocomments</samp>
    Doesn’t output any comments.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+nostats</samp>
    Doesn’t output any statistical data on the query (query time, query size, etc.).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+short</samp>
    Formats the output in a reader-friendly way. (By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dig</samp> provides the data in the confusing notation of the DNS server <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bind</samp>.)

#### Example

The following command contacts the public name server of Google, determines the MX entry of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kofler.info</samp> there, and displays it in abbreviated form:

```
user$ dig +short @8.8.4.4 kofler.info MX
10 mail.kofler.info. 
```

### dircolors [optionen] [file]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dircolors</samp> provides the program code for setting the colors the [ls](#L_001.xhtml_ls) command uses to identify different file types. If a file is passed to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dircolors</samp>, the command shows the settings saved in this file. The file must adhere to the syntax specified by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dircolors -p</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Uses the syntax of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp> shell (applies by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp>
    Uses the syntax of the C shell.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>
    Uses a very detailed syntax that can be processed by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dircolors</samp> itself. The file contains comments that explain the syntax and in particular the color codes.

#### Example

In many distributions, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.dircolors</samp> file is analyzed when the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp> is started and used to set the colors. To change the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> colors, you must first create your own version of this file by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dircolors -p</samp> and then make changes to it in an editor. The changed settings take effect as soon as you open a new terminal window or dialog.

```
user$ cd   
(change to home directory)
user$ dircolors -p > .dircolors
user$ yourFavoriteEditor .dircolors 
```

If changing the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.dircolors</samp> file isn’t sufficient for your distribution, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dircolor</samp> to create a statement for setting the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LS_COLORS</samp> variable and add this statement to the end of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.bashrc</samp> file:

```
user$ dircolors .dircolors >> .bashrc 
```

### dirname string

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dirname</samp> returns the path of a complete file name. Thus, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dirname /usr/bin/groff</samp> returns <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/bin</samp>.

### dirs

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dirs</samp> returns the list of all directories saved by [pushd](#P_001.xhtml_pushd). The command is primarily intended for script programming.

### disown [options] [jobspec]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">disown</samp> removes the specified process from the shell. This means the process continues to run even if the shell is closed. The process is specified either by the process ID (PID) or by the shell job number, whereby the shell job number must be preceded by the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%</samp> character. Without specifying a job number, the current (background) process is meant.

If you plan to run a program separately from the shell from the outset, you can use [nohup](#N_001.xhtml_nohup) at startup to avoid having to call <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">disown</samp> later.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Triggers all processes started in the shell.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Triggers all processes started in the shell that are currently running.

#### Example

In the following example, a longer download process is started first. Ctrl+Z interrupts the download, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bg</samp> continues it in the background. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">disown</samp> separates the download process from the shell so that the download continues even after the shell logout.

```
user$ wget -q http://mirror.switch.ch/.../AlmaLinux-n.n.iso
user$ <Ctrl>+<Z>
user$ bg
user$ disown 
```

### dmesg [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dmesg</samp> outputs the kernel messages contained in the buffer memory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp>
    Deletes the buffer memory for the kernel messages after the output. This option requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-H</samp>
    Performs the output in color and displays times in an easier to read form (human readable).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T</samp>
    Displays the absolute time prior to each message.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp>
    Displays all kernel messages and then continues to run until the command is terminated via Ctrl+C.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-W</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--follow-new</samp>
    Waits for new kernel messages and displays them until the command is terminated via Ctrl+C.

In some Linux distributions, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dmesg</samp> requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions. If you want to give all users the right to read kernel messages, you need to enter <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kernel.dmesg_#restrict=0</samp> in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/sysctl.conf</samp> file and then run [sysctl](#S_001.xhtml_sysctl) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p</samp>.

### dnf [options] command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> is the package management command of Fedora, RHEL, and compatible distributions. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> has replaced the formerly used <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yum</samp> command.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> downloads the packages from the package sources defined in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo</samp>. (The name of this directory makes clear the origin of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> and hasn’t changed along with the change from <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yum</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp>.)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">check-update</samp>
    Checks whether updates are available for already installed packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">clean metadata</samp>
    Removes the package metadata from the cache. At the next start, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> updates the data by reloading the metadata of all package sources.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">clean packages</samp>
    Removes downloaded and already installed package files from the cache.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config-manager [options]</samp>
    Manages DNF/YUM package sources:

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--add-repo</samp> url adds a package source.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--set-enabled</samp> name or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--set-disabled</samp> name (de)activates a package source.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">copr [enable|disable|remove|list|search] [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package source</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Manages Copr package sources. Copr is an automated build system used by some developers to offer their own packages to the public. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">copr</samp> isn’t a built-in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> command. It can only be used if the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf-plugins-core</samp> package has been installed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">downgrade</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package</samp>
    Replaces a package with a package from an older distribution. You can enter the version number of the distribution using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--releasever=n</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">download</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package</samp>
    Downloads a package to the current directory, but doesn’t install it. In combination with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--source</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> downloads the source code package. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--resolve</samp>, the command also takes dependent packages into account. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--url</samp>, it only shows the links to the packages, but doesn’t download the packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grouplist, groupinfo, groupinstall, groupupdate, groupremove</samp>
    Provides information about, installs, updates, or removes package groups. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf grouplist -v</samp> lists the corresponding internal English-language group ID in parentheses together with each package group.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">history</samp>
    Provides a numbered list of the most recently performed <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dnf</samp> actions. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dnf history info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> provides details on transaction <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Provides information on the specified package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1 name2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Searches for the packages <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name2</samp>, and so on from all package sources, and then downloads and installs them. If necessary, additional packages are also loaded and installed or updated to fulfill package dependencies.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rpmfile</samp>
    Installs an RPM package that is stored in the local file system. Package dependencies are taken into account. Missing packages are downloaded from the package sources and installed, if necessary.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install @</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package:version</samp>
    Installs the package in the specified version. This is a short notation for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf module install</samp> package:version.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp>
    Provides a two-part list. The first part contains (in alphabetical order) all packages already installed; the second part contains all packages not yet installed that are available in the package sources. An optional parameter can be used to restrict the result to packages whose name matches a pattern (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf list xorg*</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list available/updates/installed/extras/recent</samp>
    Restricts the output of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf list</samp> to specific packages. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf list updates</samp> provides a list of all packages for which updates are available. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf list recent</samp> provides an overview of the packages that have recently been added to the package sources.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">makecache [fast]</samp>
    Creates a cache with the directory of all packages available on the package sources. With the additional keyword <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fast</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> checks whether the cache is up-to-date and only performs the update if this is really necessary.

    Running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf makecache</samp> is only necessary in exceptional cases. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> automatically checks the other commands to ensure that the cache isn’t too old and updates it itself if necessary.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">module install/update/remove/enable/disable/lock/unlock/list/info ...</samp>
    Manages packages that are available in different versions. This extension of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> command is part of the modules and streams introduced with Fedora 28 and RHEL 8\. During installation, you must specify the desired version and profile in addition to the package name, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf module install nodejs:13/development</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">remove</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1 name2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Uninstalls the specified packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">repoquery</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Determines the complete package name for the specified package. It doesn’t matter whether or not the package has already been installed. With the additional <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf repoquery</samp> provides a lot more metadata in a table, such as the version number, license, package source, and project URL. With the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--location</samp> option, the command specifies an address from which the package can be downloaded manually.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">repo query term</samp>
    Returns a list of all packages that contain the search term in the description.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update</samp>
    Displays all installed packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name1 name2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Updates only the specified packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">upgrade</samp>
    Causes the same effect as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">update</samp> in combination with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--obsoletes</samp> option (see the following list).

You can influence the behavior of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> by using some very rarely needed options:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--enablerepo=name</samp>
    Activates a package source that is deactivated. This option avoids having to change the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.repo</samp> file if you only want to install a single package from an inactive package source.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--exclude=package</samp>
    Excludes the specified package from the selected operation (e.g., an update).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--obsoletes</samp>
    Causes <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> to delete packages that are no longer required after an update. This is only useful for a distribution update (version n to n+1).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-y</samp>
    Answers all questions from <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> with yes. This means <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> can be used for installation without further interaction (e.g., in a script).

#### Examples

The following two commands first update all existing packages and then install the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">emacs</samp> editor:

```
root# dnf update
...
Transaction Summary
Install      1 Package(s)
Update      42 Package(s)
Remove       0 Package(s)
Total download size: 52 M
Is this ok [y/N]: y
...

root# dnf install emacs
Installing:
 emacs                    aarch64   1:29.2-2.fc39  updates   32 M
Installing dependencies:
 dejavu-sans-mono-fonts   noarch    2.37-20.fc39   updates  469 k
 emacs-common             aarch64   1:29.2-2.fc39  updates   42 M
...
Transaction Summary: Install  20 Packages, total download size: 139 M,
installed size: 728 M
Is this ok [y/N]: y 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf repoquery</samp> provides a lot of metadata about a package. The following listing was created on AlmaLinux 9, whereby I had to install the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf-utils</samp> package beforehand:

```
root# dnf repoquery -i joe
Name         : joe
Version      : 4.6
Release      : 12.el9
Summary      : An easy to use, modeless text editor ... 
```

The following two commands determine which versions of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nodejs</samp> package are available and then install the latest version in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">minimal</samp> profile:

```
root# dnf module list --all nodejs
AlmaLinux 9 - AppStream
Name         Stream  Profiles                               Summary
nodejs       18      common [d], development, minimal,s2i   Javascript runtime
nodejs       20      common [d], development, minimal,s2i   Javascript runtime
Hint: [d]efault, [e]nabled, [x]disabled, [i]nstalled
root# dnf module install nodejs:20/minimal 
```

The last command downloads the source code package of the Gnome text editor:

```
user$ dnf download --source gedit 
```

### docker [options] command

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker</samp> command manages Docker containers. Before using the command for the first time, you must install <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker</samp>, ideally from a current Docker package source (see [https://docs.docker.com/get-docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker)).

In Fedora and RHEL-compatible distributions, the almost compatible <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">podman</samp> command is available instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker</samp>. Even if there are various differences in the technical implementation, almost all the commands described in the following list work in the same way as with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker</samp>:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">build</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory/url</samp>
    Reads the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Dockerfile</samp> file located at the specified location and creates a corresponding local image from it. With the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp> name:tag option, the image can be named and marked with a tag.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">compose up|down</samp>
    Evaluates <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">docker-compose.yml</samp> (obsolete) or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">compose.yaml</samp>, creates the container setup described there, and executes it or stops it again. The command isn’t yet available for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">podman</samp> (as of spring 2025); in the Red Hat world, you can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">podman-compose</samp> script instead. A reference for the syntax permitted in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker-compose.yml</samp> can be found at the following address: [https://docs.docker.com/compose/compose-file](https://docs.docker.com/compose/compose-file).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">create</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">imagename/id</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cmmand</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Creates a container similar to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker run</samp>, but doesn’t start it.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">exec</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">containername/id command</samp>
    Runs the specified command in an already running container. As with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker run</samp>, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-i</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp> options enable interactive operation. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp>, the command is executed in the background.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">image prune|pull|push|rm [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">imagename/id</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Deletes all unused images, downloads images from or uploads images to the Docker Hub, or deletes a single image. (Docker Hub is a collection of public Docker images, see [https://hub.docker.com](https://hub.docker.com).)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">images</samp>
    Lists local images and specifies their size. With the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-q</samp> option, only the image IDs are listed, which enables automated further processing.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">inspect</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">containername/id</samp>
    Provides detailed information on the specified container.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">logs</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">containername/id</samp>
    Displays the logged messages of the container. This only works if the underlying image is configured accordingly.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">network create|connect|inspect|rm [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">networkname/id</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Administrates networks for Docker containers.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">port</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">containername/id command</samp>
    Lists the port assignments of a container.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ps</samp>
    Outputs all running containers. With the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-a</samp> option, stopped containers are also taken into account. If you add <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp>, the command also displays the container size.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rename</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">oldname/id newname</samp>
    Renames a container.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rm</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">containername/id</samp>
    Deletes the specified container. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp>, the command gets executed even if the container is still running.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rmi</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">imagename/id</samp>
    Deletes the specified image.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">run</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">imagename/id</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[command]</samp>
    Creates and starts a new container from the specified image and then executes either the default command or the specified command in it. The required image is downloaded from the Docker Hub if it’s not already available locally. The properties of the new container are controlled by countless options. The most important ones are listed here:

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp> executes the container in the background.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-e</samp> var=value defines an environment variable for the container.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-h</samp> hostname assigns a hostname to the container.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-i -t</samp> enables interactive operation of the container.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--name</samp> cname assigns a name to the container.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--network</samp> netname uses the specified Docker network.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p</samp> localport:cport connects a local port with a port of the container.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--rm</samp> deletes the container again as soon as the execution ends.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-v</samp> localdir:cdir connects a local directory with a volume of the container.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">service create|inspect|logs|ls|ps|remove|update</samp>
    Administrates the services in a Docker cluster (swarm).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">start/stop</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">containername</samp>
    Starts or stops a container that has already been set up.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">system df</samp>
    Lists the space requirements of all images, containers, and volumes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">system info</samp>
    Displays comprehensive information about the Docker installation.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">system prune</samp>
    Deletes containers that aren’t running, unused images, and—with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--volumes</samp> option—also volumes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">containername/id</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newname:tag</samp>
    Renames a container.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">volume ls|inspect|prune|rm</samp>
    Manages volumes.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker run</samp> creates a derived container from the official MariaDB image on Docker Hub and gives it the name <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mydb</samp>. If the image hasn’t yet been downloaded locally, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker run</samp> will take care of this. The command then takes a little longer to execute the first time.

All database files are saved in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/home/<username>/varlibmysql</samp>. Port 3306 of the container is accessible in the host system via the local port 13306.

```
root# mkdir /home/<username>/varlibmysql
root# docker run -d --name mydb -p 13306:3306 \
         -v /home/<username>/varlibmysql/:/var/lib/mysql mariadb 
```

The container runs in the background until it’s terminated via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">docker stop</samp>:

```
root# docker stop mydb 
```

If you don’t want to use the container again, you can now delete it:

```
root# docker rm mydb 
```

### dpkg options [filename/packagename]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dpkg</samp> takes care of low-level package management in all Debian- and Ubuntu-based distributions. However, instead of using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dpkg</samp> for package installation, users often use a command based on it, usually [apt-get](#A_001.xhtml_apt-get).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--configure</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Runs the configuration scripts of the specified package. This is usually done during the installation, but, in some cases, it may be necessary to carry out this step explicitly. Some packages have interactive setup programs in addition to the automatic configuration scripts. If you need such a setup program again later, you should run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dpkg-reconfigure</samp> package name.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--get-selections</samp>
