    Returns a list of all installed packages, similar to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--list</samp>. However, the result contains less detailed information and is therefore much easier to read. If you redirect the list to a text file and save it, you can install all packages later on a different computer by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--set-selections</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename.deb</samp>
    Installs the specified package file. If an older version is already installed, it will be uninstalled and replaced by the new version. The configuration scripts provided in the package are also executed during the installation.

    Before the installation starts, it’s ensured that all package dependencies are fulfilled. If that’s not the case, the error message will usually indicate which packages are missing. Instead of laboriously installing all dependent packages, it’s best to run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt install ./filename.deb</samp> to perform the installation with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt</samp>.

    Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dpkg</samp> allows only the installation of packages in the appropriate architecture for the distribution. If you use a 64-bit Linux distribution, but a program is only available as a 32-bit package, you can force the installation with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--force- architecture</samp>. However, whether or not the program actually works is another matter. In any case, you must also install all required 32-bit libraries.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list</samp>
    Provides a list of all installed packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp>
    Provides a list of installed and available packages. The first column of the package list contains a two-letter code.

    The first letter indicates the desired status of the package:

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">i</samp> = install

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> = do not install

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">r</samp>/<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">p</samp> = remove

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">h</samp> = hold

    The second letter describes the actual status:

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">i</samp> = installed

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> = not installed

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">c</samp> = configured

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">u</samp> = unpacked, but not yet configured

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">f</samp> = failed

    The information comes from the Debian package database, a collection of files in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/dpkg</samp> directory. Meta information about all installed and available packages is stored there.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--listfiles</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Returns a list of all files in the specified package. This only works for packages that are already installed. You can determine the contents of uninstalled packages using the command; <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dpkg-deb</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--contents</samp> file name.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-P</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--purge</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Removes the specified package including all package files (even if you’ve modified them).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--remove</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Removes the specified package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--search</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename</samp>
    Determines the package from which the specified file originates.

#### Example

The first <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dpkg</samp> command installs a new package. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dpkg --search</samp> determines the package from which the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/sensors3.conf</samp> file originates. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dpkg --listfiles</samp> returns a list of all files in this package.

```
root# dpkg --install paketname.deb
root# dpkg --search /etc/sensors3.conf
libsensors-config: /etc/sensors3.conf
root# dpkg --listfiles libsensors-config
...
/.
/etc
/etc/sensors.d
/etc/sensors.d/.placeholder
/etc/sensors3.conf
... 
```

### dracut [options] initrd file kernel version

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dracut</samp> is responsible for creating an initrd file on Fedora, RHEL, and (open)SUSE. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dracut</samp> is executed without additional parameters, it creates an initrd file named <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/initrd-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kernelversion</samp> for the latest kernel in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot</samp> directory. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dracut</samp> takes into account the settings in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/dracut.conf</samp> as well as countless options described in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">man dracut</samp>. Only the three most important options are summarized here:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d a,b,c</samp>
    Integrates the kernel modules <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">a</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">b</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">c</samp> into the initrd file. Usually, this option isn’t required. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dracut</samp> automatically recognizes which modules are required for the start process.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp>
    Overwrites an existing initrd file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--regenerate-all</samp>
    Creates new initrd files for all kernel versions installed on the system.

Debian and Ubuntu use [update-initramfs](#U_001.xhtml_update-initramfs) instead.

#### Example

To manually create an initrd file for a self-compiled kernel 5.7.3 in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/vmlinuz-5.7.3</samp> file, you need to run the following command:

```
root# dracut /boot/initrd-5.7.3 5.7.3 
```

### du [options] [directory]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">du</samp> outputs information about the memory requirements of files or directories. If a file specification is given in the directory parameter (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">*</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">*.tex</samp>), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">du</samp> will receive a list indicating the size of all files. If, however, only one directory is specified, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">du</samp> will determine the memory requirements for all child directories. The memory details also include the memory requirements of all child directories. The last numerical value indicates the total memory requirement of all files and subdirectories from the specified directory onward. All figures are in KiB.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--bytes</samp>
    Displays the sizes in bytes (instead of KiB).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--total</samp>
    Displays the final total as the final value. This option is only necessary if <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">du</samp> applies to files (and not to directories), which makes it relatively easy to determine how much memory all files with a certain ID (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.pdf</samp>) take up.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--human-readable</samp>
    Displays the sizes in an easy-to-read format. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">K</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">M</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">G</samp> are abbreviations for KiB, MiB, and GiB.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--max-depth=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--max</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Outputs the directory size only for the specified number of directory levels.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--summarize</samp>
    Displays only the final total. This option is only useful if the memory requirements of directories are displayed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--dereference</samp>
    Displays only the memory requirements directly in the directory. The memory requirements in subdirectories are not taken into account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--one-file-system</samp>
    Ignores directories where other file systems are mounted. (This option is almost always recommended. On my computer, I’ve defined a corresponding alias with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">alias du="du -x"</samp>.)

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">du</samp> determines which directories take up how much space. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--max 1</samp>, subdirectories aren’t listed individually but are included in the result.

```
user$ du -h --max 1
15M     ./Downloads
29M     ./Videos
69M     ./.local
... 
```

#### Alternatives

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">du</samp> doesn’t provide the option to sort the result. This is exactly what the interactive [ncdu](#N_001.xhtml_ncdu) command can do. It also provides the option to navigate through subdirectories using the cursor keys. I highly recommend this!

### dumpe2fs device

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dumpe2fs</samp> provides countless internal information about the state of an ext file system, in particular about the superblocks and the organization of the block groups of the data medium.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Lists only defective blocks on the data medium.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp>
    Provides a summary of the superblock data.

### dvips [options] name.dvi

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dvips</samp> creates a PostScript file from a <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.dvi</samp> file. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dvips</samp> is used without the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-o</samp> option, the command redirects the resulting PostScript file to the default printer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-A</samp>
    Converts odd pages only.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-B</samp>
    Converts even pages only.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-D</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Uses a resolution of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> dpi (dots per inch) when generating LaTeX bitmap fonts. The default resolution is usually 600 dpi (see <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/texmf/config.ps</samp>). Alternatively, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> may also be <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">300</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">400</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1270</samp> (see <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/bin/mktexpk</samp>). This option is only relevant for bitmap fonts. PostScript fonts are always resolution-independent.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-E</samp>
    Creates an EPS file (Encapsulated PostScript) with a bounding box that contains only the part of the page that is actually used. This only makes sense if the DVI file doesn’t comprise more than one page and the resulting EPS file is then to be embedded in another document.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i -S</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Splits the output into files of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> pages each. The files are numbered automatically.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">last page</samp>
    Ends the conversion with the specified page.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">target file</samp>
    Writes the result to the specified file (instead of forwarding it to the [lpr](#L_001.xhtml_lpr) program).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">first page</samp>
    The conversion starts with the specified page.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-pp</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n1,n2-n3,n4,n5,n6-n7</samp>
    Prints the specified pages. Note that there must be no spaces in the page list.

Global default settings for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dvips</samp> are defined in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config.ps</samp> file. Depending on the distribution, this file can be found in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/texmf</samp> directory or in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/share/texlive/texmf-dist/dvips/config</samp>.

## E

### e4defrag [options] file/directory/device

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">e4defrag</samp> defragments either a file, the entire contents of a directory, or an entire ext4 file system. Users without <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions can only defragment their own files.

Defragmentation means that the blocks of a file are reserved on the data medium in m close a sequence as possible. This speeds up read access, especially with conventional hard disks. The effects of defragmentation are less pronounced with SSDs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp>
    Displays a defragmentation counter for the file(s) in question, but doesn’t make any changes. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">e4defrag</samp> is executed with this option for the entire file system, the command returns a list of the most fragmented files after some time.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Displays information before and after the defragmentation of each file.

### echo [options] string

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">echo</samp> outputs the specified character string. If the string contains spaces or special characters, it must be enclosed in double or single quotation marks, depending on whether shell variables are to be output or not.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-e</samp>
    Interprets various backslash character combinations, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\a</samp> as a signal tone, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\n</samp> as the end of a line, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\t</samp> as a tab (see also <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">help echo</samp>). Thus, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">echo –e "\a"</samp> outputs a warning signal.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp>
    Doesn’t switch to a new line at the end of the output. The output can be continued by using another <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">echo</samp> statement.

#### Example

The following command displays the current contents of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$PATH</samp> variable:

```
user$ echo "The PATH variable contains: $PATH" 
```

### efibootmgr [options]

In Linux systems that have been installed and started in EFI mode, various EFI settings can be changed using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">efibootmgr</samp> command. These settings are stored in a nonvolatile memory (NVRAM) on the mainboard. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">efibootmgr</samp> is primarily used to set up new EFI boot entries, remove existing entries, and define the default boot sequence. The command requires the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">efivars</samp> kernel module to be loaded. If this isn’t the case, you need to run [modprobe](#M_001.xhtml_modprobe) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">efivars</samp>.

Note that the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">efivars</samp> module can only be used if Linux was booted in EFI mode (not in BIOS mode!). If necessary, you can use a Linux live system that can be started in EFI mode for repair work.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-B</samp>
    Deletes the specified EFI boot entry. You can determine the numbers of the EFI boot entries by running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">efibootmgr</samp> without parameters.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c -l \EFI\</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">distrib</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grubfile.efi</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">–L</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Creates a new EFI boot entry (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp>) and specifies the location of the corresponding boot loader file. The path is relative to the EFI partition <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/efi</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\</samp> must be used as the directory separator. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp> specifies the name of the EFI boot entry (usually the distribution name, which is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Linux</samp> by default).

    The new entry automatically becomes the default entry. Optionally, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> to specify the number of the EFI boot partition (usually 1) and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> to specify the device name of the first hard disk/SSD (usually <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sda</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sad</samp>
    Determines which EFI boot entry is used at the next restart. The setting isn’t permanent, but only applies to the next computer start.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-N</samp>
    Deletes the setting specified with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> for the next restart.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n1</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n2</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n3</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,...</samp>
    Sets the new order of the EFI boot entries permanently. If you only want to specify the entry in the first position, it’s sufficient to enter its number.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Determines in which partition the EFI boot partition is located (usually in the first partition).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-q</samp>
    Specifies that no output is required (quiet).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies how long EFI should wait before activating the default boot entry after a restart (in seconds). However, it depends on the EFI implementation whether the EFI menu is displayed automatically during this wait time. On one of my test computers, the EFI menu generally gets displayed only when I press a corresponding key (F8, ASUS mainboard P8H67-M Evo).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T</samp>
    Deletes the wait time setting, which has been set using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp>; that is, the default boot entry gets activated immediately.

#### Example

If the command is executed without any further options, it lists the EFI boot entries and some other parameters of the EFI boot loader:

```
root# efibootmgr
BootCurrent: 0000
Timeout: 1 seconds
BootOrder: 0000,0005,0003,0001,0002
Boot0000* ubuntu
Boot0001* Hard Drive
Boot0002* CD/DVD drive
Boot0003* Windows Boot Manager
Boot0005* Fedora 
```

On the next reboot, Fedora is supposed to be started (deviating from the saved boot sequence, in which Ubuntu is in first place).

The next command creates a new EFI boot entry. The doubling of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\</samp> characters is necessary because the shell interprets a single <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\</samp> character as an identifier for special characters.

```
root# efibootmgr -c -l \\EFI\\test\\abc.efi -L abc 
```

### egrep [options] search pattern file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">egrep</samp> searches the specified text file for a search pattern and displays the text passages found. The rules of Extended Regular Expressions (EREs) apply to the search pattern.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">egrep</samp> isn’t a command in its own right, but merely an alias or a small script that runs the [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep) command with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-E</samp> option. The GNU documentation advises against calling <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">egrep</samp> and recommends running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grep -E</samp> directly. Further information and examples can be found in [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep).

### enscript [options] source file -p target file

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">enscript</samp> command from the package of the same name converts a text file into either PostScript, HTML, or RTF format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--color</samp>
    Performs syntax highlighting with colors (must be combined with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-E</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-E</samp>
    Performs syntax highlighting for program code (bold, italics).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f font</samp>
    Uses the specified font (10-point Courier by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-M</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">paper size</samp>
    Uses the specified paper format (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">A3</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">A4</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Letter</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Formats the text with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> columns. Thus, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-2</samp> results in two-column formatting.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--landscape</samp>
    Fills the sheet in landscape format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-W</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">format</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--language=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">format</samp>
    Specifies the desired format. The available options include <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PostScript</samp> (applies by default), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">html</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rtf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-X</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">charset</samp>
    Specifies the character set of the text (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ascii</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">latin</samp> n). Unfortunately, Unicode isn’t supported. To convert Unicode texts to PostScript format, you must use the [paps](#P_001.xhtml_paps) command.

### epstopdf [options] file.eps

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">epstopdf</samp> converts the EPS file into a PDF file and saves the result as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file.pdf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--exact</samp>
    Evaluates the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ExactBoundingBox</samp> (instead of the regular bounding box).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--hires</samp>
    Evaluates the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HiresBoundingBox</samp> (instead of the regular bounding box).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--nocompress</samp>
    Doesn’t compress the PDF data.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--outfile=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Saves the result under the specified file name.

### erd [options] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">erd</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">erdtree</samp> package combines the functions of [du](#D_001.xhtml_du), [ls](#L_001.xhtml_ls) in a single command. The output is graphically appealing in colors (see [Figure 2](#E_001.xhtml_bE.2)). The command takes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.gitignore</samp> into account and doesn’t display the files excluded there.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-.</samp>
    Also displays hidden files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d line|word|block</samp>
    Displays the size of files in lines, words, or blocks.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-H</samp>
    Indicates the size of files in KiB, MiB, or GiB (instead of bytes).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp>
    Ignores <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.gitignore</samp>; that is, it displays all files in a Git directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--long</samp>
    Displays access rights, owners, and groups.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--level</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Tracks subdirectories only to the desired depth. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">erd</samp> runs through all subdirectories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--pattern</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">regex</samp>
    Displays only files that match the regular pattern.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sort name|rname|size|rsize|access|raccess|mod|rmod</samp>
    Sorts the output according to file name, file size, access, or modification time. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">r</samp> variants reverse the sort order. Thus <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s rsize</samp> displays the largest file first.

    [![erd Provides an Overview of the /etc/systemd Directory](bilderklein/kleinerd.png)](img-bE.2.xhtml)

    **Figure 2**     erd Provides an Overview of the /etc/systemd Directory

### etherwake [options] mac

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">etherwake</samp> command from the package of the same name sends a special network packet to a MAC address and attempts to “wake up” the device from sleep mode. The device must support the Wake On LAN standard.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp>
    Sends the packet via the specified network interface (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">eth0</samp> by default).

#### Example

The following command activates the NAS device in my household, which is located in the basement and is normally in sleep mode to save energy:

```
root# etherwake -i wlp0s20f3  00:11:32:12:DD:0D 
```

### ethtool [options] device [parameter]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ethtool</samp> determines or changes (hardware) parameters of Ethernet adapters. If you simply pass an interface name to the command without any further options, you’ll receive a list of the most important key data. These include the supported ports, the link modes, the speed, the duplex mode, and so on.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device n</samp>
    Switches the interface LED on for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> seconds. For servers with multiple adapters, this simplifies the identification of the connector socket. With some adapters, the LED then flashes for the specified time. Other adapters don’t support LED control at all—in this case, the error message Operation not supported gets displayed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device para1 value1 para2 value2 ...</samp>
    Changes several parameters of the interface. Permitted parameter names include <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">speed</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">duplex</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">port</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mdix</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">autoneg</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">advertise</samp>.

#### Example

The following command explicitly sets the speed of the network adapter to 100 MBit/second, activates duplex mode, and deactivates the auto-negotiate function:

```
root# ethtool -s eth0 speed 100 duplex full autoneg off 
```

### eval $var

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">eval</samp> interprets the contents of the variable as a command line, evaluates this line with all known substitution mechanisms, and finally executes the command. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">eval</samp> is always required if a command stored in a variable is to be executed and this command contains various special characters of the shell.

#### Example

The command stored in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kom</samp> variable can’t be executed until <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">eval</samp> is used. The first attempt to run the command fails because the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> no longer evaluates the pipe character <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">|</samp> after it has replaced <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$kom</samp> with its content.

```
user$ kom="ls | more"
user$ $kom
ls: |: No such file or directory
ls: more: No such file or directory
user$ eval $kom 
```

### exec command

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exec</samp> starts the command specified in the parameter as a replacement for the running shell. The command can be used, for example, to start another shell. This terminates the running shell. With a normal command start without <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exec</samp>, however, the shell continues to run and accepts further input after the end of the command or continues the running script.

### exfatlabel device [label]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exfatlabel</samp> reads or changes the name of an exFAT file system. The command can be found in many distributions in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exfat-utils</samp> package. To set up an exFAT file system, you can use [mkfs.exfat](#M_001.xhtml_mkfs.exfat).

### exiftool [options] file/directory

The Perl script <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exiftool</samp> from the package of the same name can extract and modify the Exchangeable Image File Format (EXIF) data from JPEG and TIFF files. EXIF describes how additional metadata, for example, the time a photo was taken, is stored in bitmap files. If the command is called without options, it simply lists all the EXIF information of the specified file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"</samp>
    Reads only the specified information, such as the creation date with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-CreateDate</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag=value</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"</samp>
    Overwrites the information with the specified value.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag1<tag2</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"</samp>
    Overwrites a tag with another tag. A formatting string specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp> can be taken into account (see the following example).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-lang de</samp>
    Outputs the EXIF elements in German.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Reveals what’s currently happening (verbose).

Countless other options are documented at [https://exiftool.org](https://exiftool.org).

#### Example

The following command renames all images in the current directory. The new file name is derived from the date of creation (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">2025-12-31-124500</samp>) plus a consecutive number for multiple photos created in the same second (format string <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%.c</samp>), plus the original file identifier (format string <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%%e</samp>).

```
user$ exiftool -v '-Filename<CreateDate' -d '%Y-%m-%d-%H%M%S-%.c.%%e' .
user$ ls *.jpg
2025-02-27-161642-0.jpg  2024-10-27-194700-0.jpg ... 
```

### exit [return value]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exit</samp> terminates a shell script or the running shell. If no return value is specified, the shell returns <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>, that is, “OK”.

### expand [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">expand</samp> replaces all tab characters in the specified text file with a corresponding number of spaces. If no options are specified, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">expand</samp> assumes a tab spacing of eight characters. The result is sent to the standard output.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Changes the tab spacing to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> characters.

#### Example

The following command removes the tab characters in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">test.java</samp> and saves the result in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">test-no-tabs.java</samp>. The original file was written with an editor that equated tab characters with four spaces.

```
user$ expand -n 4 test.java > test-no-tabs.java 
```

### export [options] variable [=value]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">export</samp> declares the specified shell variable as an environment variable. This means that the variable is also available in all called commands and subshells. Optionally, variables can also be assigned. If the command is called without parameters, all environment variables are displayed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp>
    Turns an environment variable back into a normal shell variable. The command therefore has exactly the opposite effect to when used without options.

### exportfs [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exportfs -a</samp> command reports changes in the NFS configuration file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/exports</samp> to the running NFS server. The command must therefore be executed for changes made in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/exportfs</samp> to take effect.

### expr expression
expr string : pattern

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">expr</samp> evaluates the specified expression arithmetically or performs a pattern comparison for character strings. There must be spaces between the specified variables, numbers, and operators! A short description of all permissible operators can be found in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> command for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">expr</samp>. Note that many operator characters in the shell must be protected from immediate evaluation by the \ character.

If you use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> as a shell, you can also make calculations in it without using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">expr</samp>: arithmetic expressions can be specified there via <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$[expression]</samp>. The wildcard characters described in [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep) can be used in the pattern. Usually, the pattern must be placed in apostrophes to prevent the shell from evaluating the special characters.

#### Examples

The first <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">expr</samp> command performs a simple calculation. The second command returns the maximum number of characters that correspond to the pattern expression. The third command extracts the bracketed part of the pattern from a character string.

```
user$ expr 3 + 7 \* 19
136
user$ expr abcdefghi : 'a.*g'
7
user$ expr abc_efg_hij : '.*_\(.*\)_.*'
efg 
```

## F

### fail2ban-client [options] command

Fail2ban is a security program that monitors logins and blocks the IP address in question for a certain period of time after repeated incorrect logins. If Fail2ban has been set up, its function can be checked and changed via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fail2ban-client</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">get</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parameter</samp>
    Imports a configuration parameter.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reload [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">jailname</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Reloads the entire configuration or the configuration of a jail. In Fail2ban, a jail is a program to be monitored.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">jailname</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parameter value</samp>
    Changes a general configuration parameter or the parameter of a jail.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">start/stop [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">jailname</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Starts or stops Fail2ban completely or starts/stops only one jail.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">jailname</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Displays the list of all active jails or details of a jail.

If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fail2ban-client</samp> is executed without commands only with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp> option, the command outputs the entire currently valid configuration, whereby only the filters, jails, and actions that are actually in use are taken into account. This is very helpful in troubleshooting due to the confusing configuration files.

#### Examples

The following commands show that four jails are active on the test computer. The jail for the SSH server has already temporarily blocked 1,418 IP addresses in the past. Currently, 3 addresses are blocked.

```
root# fail2ban-client status
Status
  Number of jail:  4
  Jail list:       dovecot, postfix, sshd, sshd-ddos
root# fail2ban-client status sshd
Status for the jail: sshd
    Filter
       Currently failed: 4
      Total failed:     151362
      Journal matches:  _SYSTEMD_UNIT=sshd.service + _COMM=sshd
   Actions
      Currently banned: 3
      Total banned:     1418
      Banned IP list:   58.218.nnn.nnn 58.242.nnn.nnn 180.76.nnn.nnn 
```

You can unblock an erroneously blocked IP address using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fail2ban-client set</samp> (here, we do this for the SSH jail):

```
root# fail2ban-client set sshd unbanip 1.2.3.4 
```

### fc-list [pattern]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fc-list</samp> lists all scalable fonts that match the (optional) search pattern. The result can be sorted using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">| sort</samp>.

### fdisk [options] [device]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fdisk</samp> is an outdated program for partitioning hard disks. It can only process disks with MBR partition tables! For this reason, you should make friends with [parted](#P_001.xhtml_parted), which is compatible with both the master boot record (MBR) and the more modern GUID Partition Tables (GPTs).

### ffmpeg [inopts] [-i infile] [outopts] outfile

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ffmpeg</samp> command from the package of the same name converts video files from one format to another. When specifying options, note that these only apply to the video file specified next. The order of the options is therefore decisive for the correct function of the command. Unless you make different settings, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ffmpeg</samp> uses the same codecs and settings for the result file as in the source file.

In addition to the options listed here, there are countless others. The ideal setting of the options is a science in itself. If you don’t want to deal with this, it’s advisable to use a graphical user interface for video recoding, such as HandBrake.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-acodec/-vcodec</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type</samp>
    Specifies the desired audio or video codec. A list of available codecs is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ffmpeg -codecs</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the desired bit rate in bits per second (200 kBit/s by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">format</samp>
    Uses the specified format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-formats</samp>
    Lists the supported formats, codecs, filters, and so on.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the desired frame rate (25 frames per second by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">size</samp>
    Specifies the desired frame size in the form <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">w</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">h</samp> (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">800x600</samp>). Alternatively, you can specify a predefined character string (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vga</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hd720</samp>; see <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">man ffmpeg</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-ss</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">position</samp>
    Starts the conversion at the specified time. The time can be specified either in seconds or in the format <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hh:mm:ss[.xxx]</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">duration</samp>
    Converts only the specified time span (and not the entire file). The time span is specified in the same way as with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-ss</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-target</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type</samp>
    Specifies the desired target file format (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vcd</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dvd</samp>, etc.).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-vpre</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">quality</samp>
    Selects a file with predefined options (presets) for the specified codec (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">default</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">medium</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">max</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fast</samp>). The preset files available for selection are usually located in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/share/ffmpeg</samp> directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-y</samp>
    Overwrites existing files.

#### Example

The following command creates a movie file in DVD resolution:

```
user$ ffmpeg -i in.avi -target pal-dvd -y out.avi 
```

The second example converts an OGV movie file into a YouTube-compatible MPEG file:

```
user$ ffmpeg -i in.ogv -vcodec libx264 -vpre medium -acodec copy -y out.mpg 
```

### fg [process]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fg</samp> continues a process in the foreground that has been interrupted using Ctrl + Z. If no process is specified, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fg</samp> applies to the last interrupted process or the last process started in the background. Otherwise, the process must be specified by its name or by the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>-internal job number (not PID).

Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fg process</samp>, the abbreviation <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%process</samp> is also permitted.

### fgconsole [--next-available]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fgconsole</samp> outputs the number of the currently active console. With the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--next- available</samp> option, the command determines the number of the first free (unused) console. To change the active console, you can use the [chvt](#C_001.xhtml_chvt) command.

### file [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">file</samp> attempts to determine the file type of the specified file. As a result, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">file</samp> returns a character string with the file name and file type. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> doesn’t evaluate the file name or its identifier, but the contents of the file!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-z</samp>
    Attempts to recognize the data type of a compressed file.

#### Example

As the file name suggests, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name.jpg</samp> contains a JPEG bitmap file:

```
user$ file name.jpg
name.jpg: JPEG image data, JFIF standard 1.02 
```

### find [path] [search options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> helps you search for files. Various search criteria (pattern for the file name, file size, date of creation or last access, etc.) can be taken into account in the search. It’s even possible to apply further selection criteria to all files that meet these conditions using another program (e.g., [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep)). In this way, for example, all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.tex</samp> files that have been edited in the preceding three days and that contain the text “Graphics programming” could be found. Due to the large number of possible search criteria, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man find</samp> provides a description of the command that is several pages long.

The following syntax description explicitly refers to the GNU <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> implementation commonly used on Linux. It’s characterized by some minor syntax differences compared to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> variants of other Unix systems: There, a path must be specified, while GNU <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> uses the current directory as the start directory. In addition, most <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> implementations require the use of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-print</samp> option to display the search results, which isn’t necessary with GNU <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp>.

#### General Options

Unlike most other commands, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> automatically searches all subdirectories. If this isn’t desired, the number of subdirectories must be limited via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-maxdepth</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-depth</samp>
    First processes the current directory and only then the subdirectories. Depending on where you suspect the file you’re looking for is located, this procedure will lead to initial results much more quickly.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-follow</samp>
    Also edits directories that are captured by symbolic links.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-maxdepth</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Restricts the search to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> directory levels. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-maxdepth 1</samp>, no subdirectories are taken into account at all.

#### Search Criteria

You can specify multiple search criteria at the same time. These criteria are logically linked by using AND. The search is aborted as soon as the first criterion isn’t met—the order of the criteria can therefore influence the speed of the command. Criteria can be grouped using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\(</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\)</samp>, negated via <samp class="listingcharacter programmierelement">!</samp>, and logically OR-linked using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-o</samp> (see the examples).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-anewer</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reference file</samp>
    Works like <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-newer</samp> (see that entry), but takes into account the time of the last read access.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-atime</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">days</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-cmin</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">minutes</samp>
    Takes into account the time of the last read access (access). The specification is in days or minutes (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-mtime</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-cnewer</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reference file</samp>
    Works like <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-newer</samp> (see that entry), but takes into account the time of the last change to metadata.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-ctime</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">days</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-cmin</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">minutes</samp>
    Evaluates the time at which the metadata of the file (access rights, etc.) was last changed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-executable</samp>
    Finds files that are executable, that is, where the execute bit is set.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-group</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">crime name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-nogroup</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">group name</samp>
    Finds files that belong to the specified group (or that don’t belong to it).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-mmin</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Works like <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mtime</samp>, but the time is given in minutes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-mtime</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">days</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-mmin</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">minutes</samp>
    Finds files whose content was last modified exactly n days or minutes ago (modify). If a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">+</samp> is entered before the number, then all files older than n are captured. A preceding <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-</samp> returns files that are younger than n. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-mtime 0</samp> returns files that have been changed in the past 24 hours.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search pattern</samp>
    Finds files that match the specified search pattern. If the search pattern contains wildcards, it must be placed in apostrophes. If you don’t want <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> to distinguish between uppercase and lowercase, you should use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-iname</samp> option instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-name</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-newer</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reference file</samp>
    Finds files that are newer than the reference file, that is, files that were created or modified after the reference file. For example, you can create a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">timestamp</samp> file at the start of a backup using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">touch</samp>. For an incremental further backup at a later point in time, only the files for which <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">–newer</samp> timestamp applies are taken into account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-path</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search pattern</samp>
    Finds files that match the specified search pattern. The option goes beyond <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-name</samp> because the search pattern now affects not only the file name but also the path to it. This option is more flexible than the direct path specification in the first argument of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> because here the wildcard characters also include the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp> character.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-perm</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">access bits</samp>
    Finds files whose access bits correspond exactly to the specified octal value (see [chmod](#C_001.xhtml_chmod)). If the octal value is preceded by a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-</samp>, the file may also have access rights beyond this. If a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">/</samp> is placed in front, it’s sufficient if at least one of the searched access bits is set.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-size</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file size</samp>
    Specifies the desired file size. The default specification is in multiples of 512\. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-size 3</samp> therefore denotes files between 1,024 and 1,536 bytes. The additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">c</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">k</samp> characters can be used to specify the size in bytes or KiB. A prefixed <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">+</samp> includes all larger files, and a prefixed <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-</samp> includes all smaller files. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-size +10k</samp> therefore returns all files that are larger than 10 KiB.

    Note the somewhat unique logic of this command when using this option! <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find -size 1M</samp> considers files with a size between 1 byte and 1 MB. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-size -1M</samp> only finds empty files. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-size +1M</samp>, you get files in the result that are larger than 1 MB.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-type</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">character</samp>
    Restricts the search to specific file types. The most important characters are <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">f</samp> for regular files, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">d</samp> for directories, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">l</samp> for symbolic links.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-user</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">username</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-nouser</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">username</samp>
    Finds files that belong to the specified user (or that don’t belong to them).

#### Actions When Finding a File

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-exec</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command [options]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{} \;</samp>
    Calls the specified command and passes the file name of the file found that has fulfilled all the criteria processed so far. The command can then perform a test to check whether the file meets additional criteria. A typical program that is called by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-exec</samp> is [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep). Alternatively, you can also call commands here that move, copy, or otherwise process the files found.

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{}</samp> is a placeholder for the file name. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">;</samp> concludes the command call; that is, additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> options can be specified after it. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\</samp> is required within the shell to prevent the interpretation of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">;</samp> as a special character.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-exec</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command [options]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{} +</samp>
    As in the preceding paragraphs, but the specified command isn’t called for every file found. Instead, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> tries to pass as many results as possible to the command at once, which is much more efficient. The number of files is only limited by the maximum length of a command. This is approximately 2 million characters in current Linux distributions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-ls</samp>
    Provides detailed information on each file found (similar to [ls](#L_001.xhtml_ls) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-l</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-print</samp>
    Displays the file names found on the screen. This option is the default setting unless <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-exec</samp> is used.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-print0</samp>
    Separates the file names of the result list by 0 bytes. This enables further processing of file names with spaces via [xargs](#X_001.xhtml_xargs).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-printf</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">format</samp>
    Displays the file names found and other information on the screen. The format string can be used to specify the format of the output and the additional information that is also to be output (e.g., the file size or the date of the last change). The syntax for the format string is described in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> pages.

#### Examples

The first <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> command returns all files in the current directory (including hidden files, but no files from subdirectories); the second command only returns ordinary files (but no invisible files):

```
user$ find -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*'
user$ find -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '[!.]*' 
```

The following command searches the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc</samp> directory for files that have been changed in the past two weeks. The command must be run with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions because some files in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc</samp> may not be read by normal users:

```
root# sudo find /etc -mtime -14 
```

The following command deletes all backup files that are identified by the ~ character at the end of the file name. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> also takes all subdirectories into account. The list of files to be deleted is redirected to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rm</samp> by the command substitution with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$(command)</samp>.

```
root# rm $(find . -name '*~') 
```

If there is a large number of files, an error will occur when you run the preceding command: the command line with all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*~</samp> files will become so long that it exceeds the maximum command line length. In such cases, you must either use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-exec</samp> option of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> command or the [xargs](#X_001.xhtml_xargs) command. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xargs</samp> variant has the advantage that it can also cope with file names that contain spaces.

```
user$ find -name '*~.jpg' -exec rm {} \; 
```

In the next example, all files in a directory are to be made readable for everyone (see [chmod](#C_001.xhtml_chmod)). It’s somewhat more difficult to use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> to set the execute bit for all subdirectories (but not for ordinary files) so that everyone on the computer can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp> to change to the directories. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+</samp> sign at the end of the command means that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod</samp> isn’t called for each directory individually, but that as many directories as possible are passed to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod</samp> at once.

```
root# cd /directory/for/all
root# chmod -R a+r *
root# find . -type d -exec chmod a+x {} + 
```

The last example first creates a reference file with the date 1/1/2025 and the directory <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">../new-images</samp> by using [touch](#T_001.xhtml_touch). All images from the local directory that have been created since 1/1/2025 are now copied there. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">new-images</samp> must not be created in the current directory; otherwise, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> will also capture the files copied there. In addition, note the OR link for the file identifiers <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.jpg</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.png</samp>.

```
user$ touch 2025 -t 202501010000
user$ mkdir ../new-images
user$ find . -newer 2025 \( -name \*.png -o -name \*.jpg \) \
       -exec cp {} ../new-images +; 
```

Further <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> examples can be found in the description of the [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep) and [xargs](#X_001.xhtml_xargs) commands.

#### Alternatives

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> is an important command, but it’s difficult to use because nobody can remember all the possible options. Accordingly, there are many attempts to create more convenient alternatives to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp>. I present two of them in this book:

*   [erd](#E_001.xhtml_erd) combines the most important functions of du, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp>, ls, and tree in a single command.

*   [fzf](#F_001.xhtml_fzf), on the other hand, excels with its interactive selection of files.

Another option is <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fd</samp> (see [https://github.com/sharkdp/fd](https://github.com/sharkdp/fd)), which is very similar to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp>. Its biggest advantages are that the options are easier to memorize and the search results are displayed in color.

### findmnt [options] [device/mountpoint]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">findmnt</samp> without parameters returns a tree-shaped list of all file systems integrated in the directory tree. The result also contains various <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/sys</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/run</samp> file systems for internal information exchange.

By specifying a device or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> point, the list is reduced to all file systems selected in this way. Other permissible entries are the UUID or the name (label) of a file system or the major and minor number of the device in the notation <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">major:minor</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-A</samp>
    Displays all file systems.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Displays the result as a table (not as a tree).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--mtab</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--fstab</samp>
    Takes into account only the entries from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/mtab</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/fstab</samp>. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">findmnt</samp> takes into account the mount table of the kernel in the pseudo file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/self/mountinfo</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">columns</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--output</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">columns</samp>
    Outputs only the information specified in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">columns</samp> column by column. Permitted column codes include <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">SOURCE</samp>:

    Device

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">TARGET</samp>: <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> path

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FSTYPE</samp>: File system type

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">OPTIONS</samp>: all <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> options

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">SIZE</samp>: Size of the file system

    Further codes are provided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fndmnt --help</samp>. The column codes are separated by commas, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE</samp>. Spaces aren’t permitted!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">typelist</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--types</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">typelist</samp>
    Returns only file systems of the specified type. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t ext2,ext3,ext4</samp>, only ext file systems in versions 2, 3, and 4 are taken into account.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">findmnt</samp> shows all active file systems on the test computer:

```
root# findmnt
TARGET                    SOURCE      FSTYPE       OPTIONS
/                         /dev/sda1   ext4         rw,relatime,errors=...
 /sys                     sysfs       sysfs        rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,...
   /sys/kernel/security   securityfs  securityfs   rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,...
   /sys/fs/cgroup         tmpfs       tmpfs        ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec,...
 ... 
```

### firewall-cmd options

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewall-cmd</samp> reads or changes the firewall configuration in Fedora, RHEL, and SUSE distributions. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewall-cmd</samp> communicates with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewalld</samp> program running in the background. This program assigns a zone to each network interface. A zone in the sense of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewalld</samp> is a collection of rules for a specific usage purpose. The following list describes the most important zones:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">block</samp>
    Blocks all network traffic; the sender receives an ICMP error message.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">drop</samp>
    Blocks all network traffic; the sender isn’t informed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">external</samp>
    Blocks most ports and activates masquerading (IPv4). The zone is intended for the interface that connects to the internet on a router.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FedoraWorkstation</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FedoraServer</samp>
    Are used by default for network interfaces of Fedora installations. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FedoraServer</samp> blocks all services except SSH and DHCP client. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">FedoraWorkstation</samp> is much more tolerant and also accepts Samba client connections and traffic through all ports between 1025 and 65535.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">home</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">internal</samp>
    Blocks most ports, but accepts Samba (only as client), CUPS, and Zeroconf/Avahi/mdns. The zones are intended for computers on a local network that is considered reasonably secure. If you want to use this zone and share Windows network directories yourself, you must also enable the Samba service.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">public</samp>
    Similar to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">home</samp>, but also blocks CUPS and Samba client functions. The zone is intended for internet use in insecure networks, for example, in a public wireless network.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">trusted</samp>
    Allows any network traffic. This zone is intended for well-secured local networks, but not for Wi-Fi connections.

Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewall-cmd</samp> only makes the changes dynamically. If changes are to be permanent, you must specify the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--permanent</samp> option. Then, the rules will be saved in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/firewalld</samp> directory.

#### Options

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--add-interface=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--remove-interface=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Assigns the specified interface to the default zone, assigns the zone specified by the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--zone</samp> option, or removes this assignment. Before an interface can be assigned to a new zone, the previous assignment must be explicitly removed!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--add-prot=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--remove-port=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Allows the use of a TCP port in the zone specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--zone</samp> or blocks the port.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--add-service=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--remove-service=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Allows the use of a network service (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">https</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ssh</samp>) in the zone specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--zone</samp> or blocks the service.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--change-interface=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iface</samp>
    Assigns the active zone to the specified network interface. To connect another zone to an interface, you must also pass the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--zone=name</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--get-active-zones</samp>
    Lists all zones that are currently in use and indicates which network interfaces are assigned to the zones.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--get-default-zone</samp>
    Determines the default zone.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--get-services</samp>
    Lists all network services known to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewall-cmd</samp>. You can specify the resulting names (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">http</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ssh</samp>, etc.) with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--add-interface</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--get-zones</samp>
    Lists all zones known by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewall-cmd</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--get-zone-of-interface=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Determines the zone that is assigned to the specified network interface.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list-all-zones</samp>
    Provides the key data of all defined firewall zones and specifies which network interfaces are assigned to the zones.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list-ports</samp>
    Lists ports that are allowed (i.e., not blocked) in the currently active firewall zone. Warning: the command only returns ports to which no service name is assigned. Port 22 will never appear in the result because it’s assigned to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ssh</samp> service. You can get nonblocked services via the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list-all-zones</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list-services</samp> options.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list-services</samp>
    Lists all network services that are permitted (i.e., not blocked) in the currently active firewall zone.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--permanent</samp>
    Saves changes to the firewall configuration permanently. However, the changes aren’t applied directly. If you want to make a change immediately and permanently, you must run the relevant command twice: once with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--permanent</samp> and once without this option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--set-default-zone=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Defines the default zone. It applies to all network interfaces that aren’t explicitly assigned a different zone.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--state</samp>
    Determines whether <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">firewalld</samp> is running or not.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--zone=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Indicates which zone is to be changed, edited, or read.

#### Examples

The following commands first determine which zone the network interface <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enp0s3</samp> is assigned to and then assign the interface to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">trusted</samp> zone. This means that all services can be used via this interface. The changes aren’t permanent, so they only apply until the next restart of the computer or the firewall daemon.

```
root# firewall-cmd --get-zone-of-interface=enp0s3
public
root# firewall-cmd --zone=public --remove-interface=enp0s3
success
root# firewall-cmd --zone=trusted --add-interface=enp0s3
success 
```

In the second example, the first command is used to determine which zone the network interface <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enp0s5</samp> is assigned to.
