The computer is supposed to provide a web server to the outside world via this interface. But instead of generally assigning the interface to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">trusted</samp> zone and thus enabling all other conceivable services, the rules for the zone are now changed (here, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FedoraWorkstation</samp>) permanently: this zone now allows the HTTP and HTTPS protocols. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reload</samp> command activates the changes to the zone.

```
root# firewall-cmd --get-zone-of-interface=enp0s5  
(determine active zone)
FedoraWorkstation
root# firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=FedoraWorkstation --add-service=http
root# firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=FedoraWorkstation --add-service=https
root# firewall-cmd --reload 
```

### flatpak [options] command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flatpak</samp> helps with the installation, removal, and administration of Flatpak packages. This is a new package format intended to simplify the installation of desktop applications independently of the package sources of a distribution. The largest official Flatpak repository is [https://flathub.org](https://flathub.org).

Compared to conventional packages, there are additional security mechanisms, such as sandboxing. However, Flatpak packages are often huge because they include all the necessary libraries and don’t take into account any existing traditional packages. The installation of multiple Flatpaks is therefore often associated with large redundancies.

Flatpak packages are usually installed directly in the desktop, for example, in the Gnome program Software or in the browser. The program is started in the Start menu or in the Gnome view Activities. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flatpak</samp> command is therefore rarely required.

Flatpak is available on Fedora and RHEL by default. However, the command can be easily installed and used in other distributions and is intended to become a platform for a distribution-independent distribution of Linux software. As an alternative to Flatpak, Snap packages can be used, which are favored by Ubuntu (see [snap](#S_001.xhtml_snap)).

Although the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flatpak</samp> command doesn’t require <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions, you must authenticate yourself repeatedly with your own password during execution (sometimes a dozen times for a single operation, such as the installation of a package).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Displays details of an already installed package. Note that the package name is always composed of several parts, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">org.gnome.gedit2</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[package source] package name</samp>
    Installs the desired package from a previously set up package source.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list [--system</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--user]</samp>
    Lists all installed Flatpacks (if applicable, only those that have been installed at the system level or for the current user). With the additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flatpak</samp> also displays the package size and a few other details.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">remote-add [--if-not-exists]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package source url</samp>
    Sets up a package source. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--if-not-exists</samp> option avoids error messages if the package source has already been defined previously.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">remotes</samp>
    Lists all installed package sources.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Flatpacks term</samp>
    Searches the configured package sources for packages that contain the search term in the package name or in the description.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uninstall</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Removes the specified package without further inquiry. You may need to enter the full package name as displayed by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flatpak list</samp>, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flatpak uninstall org.gimp.GIMP/x86_64/stable</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update [--app</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Updates all installed flatpacks or only the package specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--app</samp>.

#### Examples

The following command installs the Visual Studio Code editor at system level so that all users of the computer can use it. Note the insane download sizes for the platform packages. It wasn’t long ago that the downloads for an entire Linux distribution were smaller!

```
root# flatpak install  com.visualstudio.code
Required runtime for com.visualstudio.code/aarch64/stable (runtime/org.freedesktop.Sdk/aarch64/23.08) found in remote flathub
Do you want to install it? [Y/n]: y

com.visualstudio.code permissions:
    ipc             network         pulseaudio              ssh-auth
    x11             devices         devel
    file access [1] dbus access [2] system dbus access [3]  tags [4]

    [1] host
    [2] ...

    ID                                   ...  Remote    Download
 1\. org.freedesktop.Platform.GL.default       flathub    146 MB
 2\. org.freedesktop.Platform.GL.default       flathub    146 MB
 3\. org.freedesktop.Platform.openh264         flathub    884 kB
 4\. org.freedesktop.Sdk.Locale                flathub    366 MB (partial)
 5\. org.freedesktop.Sdk                       flathub    534 MB
 6\. com.visualstudio.code                     flathub     98 MB
Proceed with these changes to the system installation? [Y/n]: y 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flatpak search</samp> enables you to search for a package in all Flatpak sources. Unfortunately, there is no official Spotify player, but there are various compatible audio players:

```
user$ flatpak search spotify
Name                      Description                      ...    Remotes
ncspot                    Cross-platform ncurses Spotify          flathub
Moosync                   Customizable music player               flathub
Spot                      Listen to music on Spotify              flathub
Oomox theme designer      customize icons, xrdb and GTK           flathub
Tauon Music Box           Play your music with style              flathub
Clementine Music Player   Plays music files and internet          fedora,flathub 
```

### fold [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fold</samp> wraps lines of text with a length of 80 characters and displays the result on the screen.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--spaces</samp>
    Attempts to wrap at the position of a space (i.e., between two words).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--width</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Sets a maximum text width of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> characters. Without this option, 80 characters apply by default.

### for var [in list;] do
commands done

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">for</samp> creates loops in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> scripts. All list elements are inserted into the specified variable one after the other. The list can also be formed with wildcards for file names or with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{...}</samp> elements for composing file names. If the list isn’t specified, the variable runs through all the parameters that were passed to the shell file (i.e., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">in $*</samp>).

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">for</samp> can be used not only in shell scripts but also in the terminal to apply some commands to a number of files. The following command outputs the file names of all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.jpg</samp> files. You can now replace <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">echo</samp> with another command that prints, scales, and so on the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.jpg</samp> files.

```
user$ for i in *.jpg; do echo $i; done 
```

Another <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">for</samp> example can be found in the description of [cp](#C_001.xhtml_cp) commands.

### free [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">free</samp> shows how the available memory space (RAM and swap memory) is used.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp>
    Selects suitable units for specifying the memory (human readable).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m / -g</samp>
    Displays the memory requirement in MiB or GiB (instead of KiB).

#### Example

In the following example, the localization variable <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LANG</samp> is reset to run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">free</samp>. This prevents the lengthy German translations of column names, which confuse the column layout.

In the virtual machine with just under 2 GiB RAM, 1.1 GiB is used. The fact that only 170 MiB are still considered free is because the operating system uses almost 700 MiB for caching files. This memory can be released quickly if required, leaving around 680 MiB available for new processes. The swap memory space is unused except for a few MiB.

```
user LANG= free –h

          total    used    free    shared  buff/cache   available
Mem:       1.9G    1.1G    171M       10M        686M        677M
Swap:      947M    6.5M    940M 
```

### fsck [options] device

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsck</samp> checks the consistency of the file system and performs repairs if necessary. It can only be run by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>. Depending on the type of file system, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsck</samp> calls the programs <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsck.ext3</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsck.ext4</samp>, and more. Be sure to read the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> pages of this and the file system–specific command before running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsck</samp>!

Before checking a file system, you must run [umount](#U_001.xhtml_umount). To check the root file system, you first need to execute [touch](#T_001.xhtml_touch) <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/forcefsck</samp> and then restart the computer. Files containing errors or file fragments are saved in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lost+found</samp> directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-A</samp>
    Checks all file systems named in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/fstab</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type</samp>
    Specifies the type of file system (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ext3</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xfs</samp>).

### fsck.ext2 [options] device
fsck.ext3 [options] device
fsck.ext4 [options] device

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsck.ext2/3/4</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">e2fsck</samp> checks the consistency of an ext file system and performs repairs if necessary. The command can also be started via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsck -t ext2/ext3/ext4</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Reads the alternative superblock <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp>
    Answers all queries with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">n</samp> (no) and doesn’t make any changes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>
    Performs repairs (changes) in the file system without prompting.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-y</samp>
    Answers all queries with yes and makes changes.

### fstrim [options] mount directory

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fstrim</samp> runs a trim command for the file system specified by the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> point. By default, all data blocks that are no longer used by the file system are reported to the data medium.

The command is only useful if the data medium is a solid-state disk (SSD), and the file system doesn’t automatically run trim commands with every delete operation anyway (see the [mount](#M_001.xhtml_mount) option <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">discard</samp> for the ext4, Btrfs, and XFS file systems). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fstrim</samp> can be run daily or weekly by a cron job to avoid performance losses due to trim commands being executed too frequently or not at all.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--length</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Reports unused blocks only for the specified area.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--minimum</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Reports only unused contiguous blocks if they are at least <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> bytes in size. This can considerably speed up the execution of the command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--offset</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Reports only unused blocks from the specified offset (calculated from the start of the file system). The specification can be indicated by a corresponding suffix in binary KiB, MiB, GiB, or TiB (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">K</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">M</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">G</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">T</samp>) or in decimal kilobytes, megabytes, and so on (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">KB</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">MB</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GB</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">TB</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--verbose</samp>
    Returns the total of the bytes reported using the trim command.

#### Example

The following command reports all free data blocks of at least 64 KiB to the SSD:

```
root# fstrim -m 64K /
/: 13493051392 bytes were trimmed 
```

### ftp [options] ftpserver

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ftp</samp> establishes a connection to the specified FTP server. After logging in, you can interactively transfer files between the local computer and the FTP server. The most important commands for interactive use are summarized here:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">?</samp>
    Displays a list of all FTP commands

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">!</samp>
    Enables the execution of shell commands.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ascii</samp>
    Switches to text mode.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">binary</samp>
    Switches to binary mode.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bye</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">quit</samp>
    Terminates FTP.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cd</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir</samp>
    Changes to the specified FTP directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">get</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Transfers the file from the FTP archive to the current directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">help command</samp>
    Displays brief information on the specified command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lcd</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir</samp>
    Changes the current directory on the local computer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ls</samp>
    Displays the list of files on the FTP server.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lls</samp>
    Displays the list of files on the local computer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mget</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.pattern</samp>
    Transfers all matching files from the FTP archive to the current directory (see also <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">prompt</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">open</samp>
    Establishes the connection to the foreign computer (if it didn’t work at the first attempt).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">prompt</samp>
    Activates or deactivates the query before the transfer of each file by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mget</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">put</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Transfers the file from the current directory to the FTP archive (upload).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reget</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Continues the transfer of a file that has already been partially sent.

### [function] name
{{commands}

The optional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">function</samp> keyword defines a subfunction in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> scripts that can be called like a new command. You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">local</samp> to define local variables within the function. Functions can also be called recursively. Functions must be declared before their first call!

Parameters can be passed to functions. Unlike many programming languages, the parameters must not be placed in parentheses. Within the function, the parameters can be taken from the variables <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$1</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$2</samp>, and so on.

#### Example

The following mini-script outputs Hello World, abc!:

```
#!/bin/bash
function myfunc {
  echo "Hello World, $1!"
}

myfunc "abc" 
```

### fuser file name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fuser</samp> determines the program that is accessing the specified file and possibly blocking it for other programs. Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fuser</samp> returns only the process number (PID) of the program.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-k</samp>
    Terminates all processes accessing the file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp>
    Lists all processes that access any file of the file system that is specified as a device or by a file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Also specifies which user is executing the process (verbose mode).

In the output, the process number is followed by a letter indicating the type of access:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">c</samp>
    The process has set the directory as the current directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">e</samp>
    The file is being executed (executable being run).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">f</samp>
    The file is open for read access (open file). This letter is only displayed in verbose mode.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">F</samp>
    The file is open for write access. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">F</samp> is also only displayed in verbose mode.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">m</samp>
    The file is used as a library or through memory mapping.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">r</samp>
    The directory is used as the root directory.

An alternative to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fuser</samp> is the [lsof](#L_001.xhtml_lsof) command.

#### Example

The attempt to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">unmount</samp> a USB flash drive from the file system fails. This is the fault of process 32664 of the user <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kofler</samp> who is currently reading a text file on the USB flash drive using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp>.

```
root# umount /media/kofler/usb_backup
umount: /media/kofler/usb_backup: target is busy.
root# fuser -v -m /media/kofler/usb_backup
                              USER      PID ACCESS   COMMAND 
/run/media/kofler/usb_backup  kofler    32664 f....  less 
```

### fwupdmgr command

The command name <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fwupdmgr</samp> stands for firmware update manager. The command allows you to initiate firmware, BIOS, or EFI updates in modern Linux distributions. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fwupdmgr</samp> requires the background service <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fwupdmgr</samp> to be running.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">get-devices</samp>
    Provides a detailed list of all components that can be supplied with updates, as well as a list of which updates were last performed and which are currently available. You then have the option of uploading a status report to the website [https://fwupd.org](https://fwupd.org).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">downgrade</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Undoes an update and reactivates an older version.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">refresh</samp>
    Updates the update information (data source: [https://fwupd.org](https://fwupd.org)).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Initiates an update for all components or only for the specified component. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fwupdmgr</samp> only prepares the update. In most cases, the update can’t be performed until the next reboot of the computer.

#### Example

The first command updates the update information. The second command shows a status report for the Lenovo notebook with the type designation <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">20MD0001GE</samp>.

```
root# fwupdmgr refresh
Fetching metadata https://cdn.fwupd.org/downloads/firmware.xml.gz
Fetching signature https://cdn.fwupd.org/downloads/firmware.xml.gz.asc
Successfully downloaded new metadata: 5 local devices supported

root# fwupdmgr get-devices
20MD0001GE
  Thunderbolt Controller:
       Device ID:           02dcd173032b1c4f136f185c0564b059a2e3d305
       Summary:             Unmatched performance for high-speed I/O
       Current version:     39.00
       ...
   PM981 NVMe Samsung 2048GB: ...
   SAMSUNG MZVLB256HAHQ-000L7: ...
   System Firmware: ...
   UEFI Device Firmware: ...

 Devices that were not updated correctly:

   * ThinkPad P1 Thunderbolt Controller (23.00 -> 39.00)

 Devices that have been updated successfully:

   * UEFI Device Firmware (192.24.1314 -> 192.35.1427)
   * 20MD0001GE System Firmware (0.1.24 -> 0.1.25)
   * UEFI Device Firmware (192.35.1427 -> 192.47.1524)
Uploading firmware reports helps hardware vendors to quickly identify  failing and successful updates on real devices. Upload report now?
(Requires internet connection):
  0\. Do not upload reports at this time, but prompt again for future updates
  1\. Do not upload reports, and never ask to upload reports for future updates
  2\. Upload reports just this one time, but prompt again for future updates
  3\. Upload reports this time and automatically upload reports after
     completing future updates 
```

The last command initiates the update for the Thunderbolt controller:

```
root# fwupdmgr update
Upgrade available for Thunderbolt Controller from 39.00 to 50.00
Thunderbolt Controller and all connected devices may not be usable while
updating. Continue with update? [Y|n]: y 
```

### fx file.json

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fx</samp> is a command for interactively reading or searching JSON files. The components of the JSON document are color-coded and can be expanded and collapsed.

You can find the extremely useful command as a Docker image or as a binary on the GitHub project page ([https://github.com/antonmedv/fx/releases](https://github.com/antonmedv/fx/releases)). If you want to process JSON files automatically, [jq](#J_001.xhtml_jq) is the better choice.

### fzf [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> from the package of the same name stands for fuzzy finder and is a command for the interactive search and selection of files. If the command is started without any other options, it searches the current directory such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find . –type f</samp> for files and displays the result list. By entering a search pattern, you can filter the result interactively at lightning speed and then select a file or multiple files using the cursor keys or Tab, respectively. (The multiple selection requires that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> was started with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-m</samp> option.) Enter ends the command and displays the file names.

This basic function sounds rather unspectacular. The strength of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> comes from its integration into the shell. Provided that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> is installed correctly, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> can also be triggered by typing <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">**</samp> Tab, allowing the interactive completion of commands: Using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">emacs **</samp> Tab, you can open the previously selected file. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kill -9 **</samp> Tab, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> provides processes for selection, and with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ssh **</samp> Tab, it returns host names. Ctrl + T lists all files, Ctrl + R lists recently executed commands, and Alt + C changes to a subdirectory.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> has countless other keyboard shortcuts and functions that I can’t go into here for reasons of space. Instead, I recommend that you watch one of the many videos on <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp>. Even though I’m not usually a video fan, in this case, it’s worth it!

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp> therefore doesn’t replace <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> in all its functions. But once you get used to the convenience of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fzf</samp>, you’ll need <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp> much less often.

## G

### getcap [options] file name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getcap</samp>, from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">libcap</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">libcap-progs</samp> package, determines for executable files which operations are permitted for the program (capabilities). Although the Linux kernel has supported capabilities for many years, this function is only used sporadically.

Capabilities require a file system with extended attributes. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> option <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user_xattr</samp> must be used for ext file systems.

#### Example

Some distributions use capabilities for the [ping](#P_001.xhtml_ping) command. Executing this command actually requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions. Instead of simply setting the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setuid</samp> bit as it was done in the past, which often leads to security problems, we’ve switched to assigning the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cap_net_raw+ep</samp> permission to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ping</samp> via [setcap](#S_001.xhtml_setcap). This allows the command to use basic network functions, even if it’s executed by ordinary users.

The following <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getcap</samp> result was obtained on Fedora. You can see that only very few commands and Gnome programs use capabilities.

```
user$ getcap /usr/bin/*
/usr/bin/arping cap_net_raw=p
/usr/bin/clockdiff cap_net_raw=p
/usr/bin/newgidmap cap_setgid=ep
/usr/bin/newuidmap cap_setuid=ep 
```

An example of how to set capabilities yourself is shown in the description of the [setcap](#S_001.xhtml_setcap) command.

### getenforce

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getenforce</samp> provides the status of the SELinux system. The possible results are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Enforcing</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Permissive</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Disabled</samp>. To change the status, you can use the [setenforce](#S_001.xhtml_setenforce) command.

### getfacl [options] file name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getfacl</samp> determines the extended access rights of the specified files or directories. This only works if the file system supports Access Control Lists (ACLs). For ext3/ext4 file systems, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> option <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">acl</samp> must be used. An example can be found in the description of the [setfacl](#S_001.xhtml_setfacl) command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Displays the standard ACLs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp>
    Displays the ACLs of all files in all subdirectories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--skip-base</samp>
    Returns no results for files to which only the usual Unix access rights apply, but no ACL rules.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--tabular</samp>
    Displays the ACLs in a table.

### getfattr [options] file name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getfattr</samp> determines the extended attributes of the specified files or directories. This only works if the file system supports extended attributes (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> option <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user_xattr</samp> for ext file systems). An example can be found in the description of the [setfattr](#S_001.xhtml_setfattr) command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Provides a list of all user attributes and their settings.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">attribute pattern</samp>
    Returns the attributes whose names correspond to the specified pattern.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">attribute name</samp>
    Returns the value of the specified attribute. The full attribute name must be specified, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user.attrname</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp>
    Displays the EAs of all files in all subdirectories.

### getopts "format"

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">getopts</samp> command integrated in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp> helps to process passed options and parameters during script programming. You pass a character string to the command that lists several one-letter options and then run <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">getopts</samp> in a loop. It returns an option found with each loop pass until all options have been processed (see the following code example).

The following rules apply to the format string:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"abc"</samp>
    Expects the options <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> in any order, also combined (i.e. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-bc</samp> instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b -c</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">":abc"</samp>
    Works like <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"abc"</samp>, but doesn’t return any error messages for invalid parameters.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"ab:c:"</samp>
    With a colon after <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">b</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">c</samp>, it expects a parameter for each of these options (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b 1024 -c 3</samp>). During evaluation, the parameter passed with an option can be read from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$OPTARGS</samp> variable.

#### Example

During the processing of the options, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$OPTIND</samp> references the next element of the parameter list. Provided the options are passed first and then the parameters, all processed options can be removed from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$*</samp> using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">shift</samp>. (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">shift <n></samp> removes the first <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> elements from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$*</samp>. But because <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$OPTIND</samp> already references the next element, only <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$OPTIND -1</samp> elements may be pushed out of the parameters list.)

```
#!/bin/bash
while getopts ":ab:c:" opt; do
    case $opt in
       a) echo "Option a";;
       b) echo "Option b with parameter $OPTARG";;
       c) echo "Option c with parameter $OPTARG";;
       ?) echo "Invalid option"
          echo "myscript [-a] [-b data] [-c data] [...]"
       exit 2
          ;;
    esac
done
# remove processed options from $*
shift $(( $OPTIND - 1 ))
echo "More parameters: $*" 
```

#### Alternatives

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getopts</samp> can only handle one-letter options, not long options such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--search</samp>. To process such options, you can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getopt</samp> command, which is separate from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp>. It’s usually included in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">util-linux</samp> package.

### git command [options/parameters]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp> command from the package of the same name controls the Git version management system. It was originally designed only for kernel development, but it’s now the most widely used version management system outside the open-source world.

Files in Git repositories can assume three states:

*   committed
    The local file is stored in the repository and hasn’t been changed since.

*   modified
    The local file has been changed, but the changes haven’t yet been saved in the repository via a commit.

*   staged
    A modified file is to be included in the subsequent commit.

#### Commands

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">add</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">files</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directories</samp>
    Adds files or directories to the repository or marks locally modified files already in the repository for the next commit. This changes the status of the files from modified to staged.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch [-v]</samp>
    Lists the local repository branches and marks the current branch with an asterisk in front of it. With the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp> also displays the last commit in each branch.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Linux name</samp>
    Creates a new repository branch. To switch to this branch, you must also run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git checkout</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch -d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp>
    Deletes the specified branch. The command is only executed if the branch was previously connected to another branch or to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD</samp>. To delete a branch regardless of the merge status, you can use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-D</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch -u</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reponame</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp>
    Sets the upstream repository for the current branch permanently and saves the link in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.git/config</samp>. Alternatively, the upstream repository can also be set during the first push process using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git push -u</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">repo branch</samp>.

    As a rule, the local and external branch names are the same, but this isn’t mandatory. The link causes the relevant local branches to be automatically connected by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git pull</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git push</samp> and saves you having to repeatedly specify the desired repository for these commands.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">checkout [-b]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp>
    Switches to the specified branch. This sets all files in the working directory to the state they had when they were last committed to this branch. With the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> option, the specified branch is created first and then activated. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git checkout -b b1</samp> therefore corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git branch b1; git checkout b1</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">clone</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">repo-url</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Downloads an external Git repository and creates a local copy in the current or specified directory. Depending on whether the communication takes place via HTTPS or via SSH, the URLs have the following format:

    ```
    https://github.com/<account>/<reponame>.git
    git@github.com:<account>/<reponame>.git 
    ```

    Depending on where your repositories are located, you’ll need to replace <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">github.com</samp> with your Git platform, of course. In the future, the external repository will be addressed under the name <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">origin</samp>. Git allows the use of multiple external repositories that are managed <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">remotely</samp> with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">commit [-a] -m '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">snapshot description</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp>
    Creates a new local snapshot (a “commit”) in the Git repository. All changes since the last commit are saved in it, but only if the status of the files is staged. You must therefore first mark all files to be saved as staged using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">git add</samp>.

    With the additional option <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>, you can avoid this trouble as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git commit</samp> then considers all changes to already versioned files. (However, newly created files are ignored.)

    Before the first commit, you must save your name and email address in the Git configuration using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git config</samp>. This data is stored together with other metadata in the commit.

    The last snapshot in the current branch always has the name <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD</samp>. The penultimate snapshot can be addressed with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD^</samp>, the one before the penultimate snapshot with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD^2</samp>, and so on. (See [Table 1](#G_001.xhtml_tG.1) for more examples of references to other commits.)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config --list</samp>
    Determines all valid Git settings in the active directory and displays them. With the additional <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--show-origin</samp> option, the command also specifies the origin of the setting, that is, whether the setting was made locally for the repository or globally.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config [--global]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parameter value</samp>
    Saves the setting of a Git parameter in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.git/config</samp> file of the local Git repository. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--global</samp>, the parameter is instead saved in the global Git configuration file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.git/config</samp> in the home directory and is therefore the default for multiple repositories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">diff</samp>
    Without any further parameters, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git diff</samp> shows all changes made since the last commit. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git diff</samp> compares the project directory with the last commit. If you want to compare the stage area with the last commit instead, you must also specify the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--stage</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git diff</samp> displays the changes in a special patch syntax similar to [diff](#D_001.xhtml_diff). With the x<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--compact-summary</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--numstat</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--shortstat</samp> options, you get a compact summary of the number of changed lines instead.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">diff</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Shows only the changes to the specified file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">diff</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">revision</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Displays the changes between the specified commit and the current status in the project directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">diff</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">revision1</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">..</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">revision2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Displays the changes between two commits.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fetch [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reponame</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Downloads the last changes made from an external Git repository. By default, the repository specified for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">clone</samp> is read, that is, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">origin</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git fetch</samp> command therefore updates the local repository and integrates all new external commits, branches, and tags. To avoid naming conflicts, new external branches are given the name <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">origin/branchname</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">reponame/branchname</samp>.

    There’s a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git pull</samp> variant for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git fetch</samp> that not only downloads the external changes but also merges them with the local branch. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git pull</samp> corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git fetch; git merge</samp>. In doing so, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">merge</samp> connects local branches with the tracked remote branches (see also <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git branch -u</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grep</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp>
    Searches all versioned text files in the project directory for the search expression. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp> is a regular expression as in [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">init</samp>
    Sets up a Git repository for the current directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">log [--oneline] [--graph] [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[^</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">non-branch</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]]</samp>
    Provides a list of the most recent commits. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--oneline</samp> option shortens the output per commit to one line. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--graph</samp> visualizes how branches were connected to each other.

    If you specify a branch or a tag as an optional parameter, only those commits that had an influence on this branch will appear. These may well be commits that were made before this branch was created because they formed the starting point of the branch. To further reduce the commit list produced by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git log</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp>, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">^non-branch</samp> to hide commits of the specified branch. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git log bugfix ^main</samp> thus only returns those commits of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bugfix</samp> branch that have not yet been connected to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main</samp>.

    The output is guided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp> so that you can use the cursor keys to scroll through the results, most of which are several pages long. You can prevent this behavior for all <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp> commands by using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--no-pager</samp> option.

    The output of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git log</samp> can be controlled by countless other options. If necessary, you can take a look at [https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log) with approximately 40 pages of text!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">merge</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp>
    Connects the specified branch with the current branch. As with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git commit</samp>, the resulting changes are saved in a new commit for the currently active branch.

    If conflicts occur during the merge process, the process will be interrupted. You can fix the conflicts manually and then continue the merge process with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git merge --continue</samp>. Alternatively, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git merge --abort</samp> cancels the process.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mv</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">previously new</samp>
    Renames a versioned file or moves it to another directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pull [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reponame</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Transfers all commits from an external repository (like <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git fetch</samp>) and integrates them into the local repository (like <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git merge</samp>). Only the currently active branch is taken into account.

    <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git pull</samp> without any additional parameters assumes that the remote repository is configured for the current branch in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.git/config</samp>.

    With the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--rebase</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp> doesn’t perform a normal merge process, but a rebasing.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">push [-u] [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reponame</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]]</samp>
    Uploads locally executed commits for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp> to the external Git repository <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reponame</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">merges</samp> them there. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git push origin main</samp> connects all your own commits in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main</samp> branch with the branch of the same name in the external <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">origin</samp> repository. If <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp> doesn’t exist in the external repository, the branch gets automatically set up there. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> option links the local branch and the external branch of the same name (as with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git branch -u</samp>).

    The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">push</samp> command fails if there are external commits that haven’t yet been executed locally. For this reason, you should always run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git pull</samp> before <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git push</samp>.

    If you run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git push</samp> without specifying repository and branch names, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp> communicates with the default repository (usually <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">origin</samp>) and synchronizes the current linked branch (see the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">branch -u</samp> command).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rebase</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">branch name</samp>
    Variant of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git merge</samp> that changes your own commits (i.e., converts them into new commits) as if they had been created from the beginning on the basis of the commits of the external branch. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git merge</samp> has the advantage that the resulting commit sequence looks “nicer,” that is, isn’t interrupted by constant merge commits. However, local commits are created that never existed originally. This makes it difficult to trace errors.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">remote [-v]</samp>
    Lists all external repositories. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-v</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">git</samp> also displays the URL of each repository. The root repository—<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">origin</samp>—is defined by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">git clone</samp>. Additional repositories can be managed with commands such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git remote add</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git remote remove</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reset HEAD -</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Changes the status of a file mistakenly marked as staged back to modified.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reset [--hard]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">revision</samp>
    Undoes changes and reverts to an old version of the repository. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">revision</samp> specifies the desired version: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD</samp> leads back to the last commit, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD^</samp> to the penultimate one, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD^2</samp> to the one before the penultimate one, and so on. Alternatively, you can also specify the initial digits of the hexadecimal SHA1 checksum of the commit (see [Table 1](#G_001.xhtml_tG.1)). <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reset origin/main</samp> undoes all local changes and synchronizes the local branch with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main</samp> branch of the default repository. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--hard</samp> option causes local changes to be overwritten irrevocably.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reset</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Removes the file from the stage area and thus undoes <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git add</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">restore</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Restores the state of the file from the last commit. Changes made since then are overwritten without further inquiry. This command has only been available since Git version 2.23 (August 2019). If you specify a directory instead of a file, the command applies to all files changed in the directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rm</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Deletes the file from the local directory and removes it from the staging area. If the file has been modified since the last commit, you must force the deletion using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--force</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">show</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">revision</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">:</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Shows the file in the state it was in when the specified commit was made.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status [-s]</samp>
    Provides information about the current Git branch and the status of modified files. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> option makes the status output more compact. All file names are preceded by two letters, with the first letter indicating the staging state and the second one the modifying state.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag</samp>
    Without any further parameters, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git tag</samp> lists all tags (markers, version markers).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag -a '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">marker-text</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">' [-m '</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">comment</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'] [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">revision</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Adds a tag to the last commit, that is, a marker, which is a kind of bookmark. This function is ideal for marking a release version, for example. Specifying a revision makes it possible to subsequently mark an older commit.

    Git distinguishes between two types of tags: the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp> options create an annotated tag that also stores metadata. Without this option, a lightweight tag without metadata is created.

Instead of just one <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp>, a whole lot are available as each <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp> command is documented on its own page. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man git-clone</samp> provides a comprehensive description of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git clone</samp>.

#### Revision Syntax

In <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git</samp> commands, you can refer to past commits or revisions in a variety of ways (see [Table 1](#G_001.xhtml_tG.1)). The latest commit of a branch is considered the head. The notation <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@{xxx}</samp> refers to the local reference log and can therefore only be used for actions last performed locally.

| Example | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD</samp> | Head of the current branch |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@</samp> | Head of the current branch (short notation) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">develop</samp> | Head of different branch |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">develop:readme.txt</samp> | Readme file at the head of another branch |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">refs/remots/origin/feature</samp> | Head of a remote branch |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">v1.3</samp> | Commit with tag <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">v1.3</samp> |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD@{2 days ago}</samp> | Commit in the current branch two days ago |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main@{7}</samp> | Commit in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main</samp> branch prior to two actions |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD~</samp> | Predecessor (parent) of the last commit |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HEAD~3</samp> | Pre-predecessor of the last commit |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">v1.3~3</samp> | Pre-pre-predecessor of the last commit with tag <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">v1.3</samp> |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">234ae33^</samp> | First parent of merge commit <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">234ae33</samp> |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">234ae33^^</samp> | Second parent of merge commit <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">234ae33</samp> |

**Table 1**     Examples of the Git Revision Syntax

#### Examples

In the first example, you first save your name and email address in your personal Git configuration file, if you haven’t already done so. Then, you download an existing repository from GitHub:

```
user$ git config --global user.name  "Howard Hawks"
user$ git config --global user.email "hawks@my-company.com"
user$ git clone https://github.com/git-book/hello-world.git
user$ cd hello-world 
```

The second example shows how to quickly perform a bugfix in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main</samp> branch of an existing project. You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git checkout</samp> to switch to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">main</samp> branch. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git pull</samp> downloads any changes saved in the remote repository. Now, you need to correct an error, save your changes using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git commit</samp>, and transfer the changes back to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">origin repository</samp> via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">git push</samp>:

```
user$ cd directory/with/existing/git/repo
user$ git checkout main user$ git pull
user$ my-favorite-editor files ...
user$ git commit -a -m 'Bugfix login authentication'
user$ git push 
```

### glances [options]

Depending on the application, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">glances</samp> command from the package of the same name is a modern alternative to [top](#T_001.xhtml_top) or a simple monitoring program that runs in client/server mode. The latter requires a corresponding configuration but also enables access to the monitoring data via a web browser.

When called directly, the command also provides an overview of network and I/O activities as well as the status of the file systems compared to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">top</samp>. The color display is optimized for a dark terminal. If you’ve set a light background color, you run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">glances</samp> with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--theme-white</samp> option (see [Figure 3](#G_001.xhtml_bG.3)).

Various shortcut keys sort the process list according to different criteria: C by CPU usage, I by I/O activity, M by memory usage, P by name, or T by CPU runtime. By pressing Enter, you can filter the process list according to a search term. Other shortcuts show and hide information or activate different display modes. For example, U switches between the current network throughput and cumulative data volumes. The help page, which you can call by pressing H, shows even more shortcuts.

[![Simple Monitoring with “glances”](bilderklein/kleinglances.png)](img-bG.3.xhtml)

**Figure 3**     Simple Monitoring with “glances”

### gnome-session-quit [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gnome-session-quit</samp> program displays a dialog in which you can log off, switch off, or restart the computer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--force</samp>
    Performs the logout even if there are still unsaved files. This option can only be used in combination with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--logout</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--logout</samp>
    Asks the user if they want to log out.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-prompt</samp>
    Performs the logout without prompting. This option can only be used in combination with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--logout</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--power-off</samp>
    Asks the user whether they want to switch off the computer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--reboot</samp>
    Asks the user whether they want to reboot the computer.

### gpasswd [options] group

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpasswd</samp> is actually used to set group passwords. However, passwords that must be known by several members of a group are considered insecure and are therefore no longer in use.

Nevertheless, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpasswd</samp> fulfills an important function. In the following variant, it removes a user from a group:

```
root# gpasswd -d user group 
```

This makes <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpasswd -d</samp> the counterpart to [usermod](#U_001.xhtml_usermod) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-a –G group user</samp>, which adds a user to a group.

### gpg or gpg2 [options/commands]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> encrypts, decrypts, or signs files and manages keys. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> is controlled by countless options and is only to a limited extent suitable for manual use. The command is used by email clients for encrypting and signing messages and by package management tools for verifying the integrity of packages and package sources.

With the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> options, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> can be used for symmetric encryption and decryption of files. This is simple but not ideal in terms of safety. All other options assume that you want to use asymmetric encryption: encryption is then performed using the public part of your communication partner’s key, and decryption is done using the private part of your own key. This assumes that you also use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> for key management.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> is intended for server and embedded use and relies on a few external libraries. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg2</samp>, on the other hand, is designed for desktop use. This version also supports S/MIME. Apart from that, both commands support the same options.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--batch</samp>
    Activates the batch mode. Interactive commands aren’t permitted in this, and there’s no interaction. Batch mode is intended for script programming.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--symmetric</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Prompts you to enter a password, then encrypts the specified file, and finally saves the result as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file.gpg</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--cipher-algo zip/zlib/bzip2/none</samp>
    Defines the encryption algorithm. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> uses the CAST5 algorithm. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg --version</samp> command determines the algorithms available for selection.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--compress-algo zip/zlib/bzip2/none</samp>
    Specifies whether or how the data should be compressed. The ZIP procedure is used as standard. For compatibility reasons, settings other than <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zip</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">none</samp> aren’t recommended. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">none</samp> is recommended if the source data is already compressed. Recompression then takes unnecessary time without reducing the space required.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--decrypt</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Prompts you to enter a password, then decrypts the specified file, and finally writes the result to the standard output.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--decrypt</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">></samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">plain text</samp>
    Decrypts the specified file and redirects the output to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">plain text</samp> file. The file must be encrypted with the public part of your own key. To decrypt it, you must enter the password for your key.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--encrypt</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Encrypts the specified file and saves it as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file.gpg</samp>. You enter the email address of the key interactively. The key may have to be saved in the key database beforehand using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--import</samp>. If you also specify <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--armor</samp> before the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--encrypt</samp> option, the encrypted file will be saved in ASCII format. This requires more space, but simplifies forwarding by email.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--export</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name@host</samp>
    Saves a binary representation of the public part of the key for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name@host</samp> in the specified file. You must pass this file on to people who will send you encrypted files or emails. If you also specify <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--armor</samp> before the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--export</samp> option, the public key is saved in an email-compatible text format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--gen-key</samp>
    Creates a new key and saves it in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.gnupg/pubring.gpg</samp>. You’ll need to enter various data: the desired type and length of the key, as well as your name, email address, password, and so on.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--import public-key-file</samp>
    Imports the public part of another person’s key into your own key collection. This is necessary to be able to send encrypted files or emails to that person.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-k</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list-keys</samp>
    Lists all keys stored in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.gnupg/pubring.gpg</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-no-tty</samp>
    Suppresses the output of warnings.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--passphrase-file</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Reads the encryption password from the specified file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--passphrase-repeat</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies how often the password entry must be repeated (once by default). If the password is read from a file in scripts (see the <samp class="listingcharacter programmierelement">--passphrase-repeat</samp> option), you need to deactivate the repeated entry with the parameter <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-q</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--quiet</samp>
    Dispenses (to a large extent) with status outputs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--verify</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">signature file try</samp>
    Checks whether the signature file and the source file match.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--version</samp>
    Displays the version of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> and provides a list of all supported encryption and hash algorithms.

#### Examples

The following command performs a symmetric encryption of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">secret.odt</samp> document:

```
user gpg -c secret.odt
Enter the passphrase: ***********
Enter the passphrase again: *********** 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> creates the new <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">secret.odt.gpg</samp> file. The original <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">secret.odt</samp> file doesn’t get changed. If you want to prevent access to this file in the local file system, you must explicitly delete the file and its backups! To restore the encrypted file, proceed as follows:

```
user gpg -d secret.odt.gpg > secret.odt
Enter the passphrase: *********** 
```

In the second example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> is used in two scripts to encrypt and decrypt files with the AES256 algorithm. A key file is required for the scripts, which is generated using [openssl](#O_001.xhtml_openssl). (While 32 bytes may seem small, that’s 256 bits. For symmetrical procedures, 128 bits are already considered sufficiently secure.)

```
root# openssl rand  32 > key.txt
root# chmod 400 key.txt 
```

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mycrypt</samp> encryption script reads as follows:

```
#!/bin/sh
# Usage: mycrypt < in > out.crypt
gpg -c --batch --cipher-algo AES256 --compress-algo none  \
  --passphrase-file key.txt --passphrase-repeat 0 
```

To decrypt the encrypted file again, you must use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">myuncrypt</samp>:

```
#!/bin/sh
# Usage: myuncrypt < in.crypt > out
gpg -d --batch --no-tty -q --cipher-algo AES256 --compress-algo none \
  --passphrase-file key.txt --passphrase-repeat 0 
```

The application looks like this:

```
root# ./mycrypt   < backup.tar.gz       > backup.tar.gz.crypt
root# ./myuncrypt < backup.tar.gz.crypt > backup-copy.tar.gz
root# file backup.tar.gz.crypt
backup.tar.gz.crypt: GPG symmetrically encrypted data (AES256 cipher)
root# diff backup.tar.gz backup-copy.tar.gz

(no output, the files are identical) 
```

The last example shows the verification of signatures. On many websites, text files with checksums are specified in addition to the actual downloads. But how can you be sure that you’re not being tricked into false downloads and that your checksums aren’t being manipulated? On the Kali Linux download page, the checksum file is therefore signed with a key from a Kali developer. To verify the signature, you first need to import this key and then call <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg --verify</samp>:

```
user$ wget -q -O - https://www.kali.org/archive-key.asc | gpg --import
  gpg: Key 7D8D0BF6: Public key
    "Kali Linux Repository <devel@kali.org>" imported ...
  Primary key fingerprint: 44C6 513A 8E4F B3D3 0875 F758 ED44 4FF0 7D8D 0BF6
user$ gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.gpg SHA256SUMS
  Signature made Thu 09 Nov 2017 05:21:22 PM CET
  using RSA key ID 7D8D0BF6
  Good signature from "Kali Linux Repository <devel@kali.org>"
  WARNING: This key is not certified with a trusted signature!
  There is no indication that the signature belongs to the owner.
  Primary key fingerprint: 44C6 513A 8E4F B3D3 0875 F758 ED44 4FF0 7D8D 0BF6 
```

At first glance, the preceding issue doesn’t inspire confidence. In fact, however, everything is in good order: The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> command confirms that the signature and checksum file match. The third line of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpg</samp> output starts with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">Good signature</samp>. It would be fatal if the message <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">Wrong signature</samp> were displayed at this point!

The warning that appears refers to the fact that the Kali developers’ key is self-signed, but this signature couldn’t be verified. You can ignore this warning because you’ve downloaded the key from [www.kali.org](http://www.kali.org) and made sure that its fingerprint (i.e., the hexadecimal number sequence <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">44C6</samp> . . . for the preceding commands) matches the expected values. Furthermore, to verify the signature of the key itself, you and the Kali developers would have to exchange your personal GPG keys either in a face-to-face meeting or via the web of trust:

### gpioget [options] chipnr gpio1 gpio2 ...
gpioset [options] chipnr gpio1=status1 gpio2=status2 ...

With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpioset</samp>, you can set the general purpose input/output state of the Raspberry Pi. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpioget</samp> reads the state. The chip number must be transferred to the commands as the first parameter. It’s <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> for Raspberry Pi models 1 to 4\. A new hardware chip was installed with model 5\. The number <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">4</samp> must be transferred so that this is addressed correctly (internally, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/gpiochip4</samp>).

GPIO numbers are passed as additional parameters, whereby the internal designation of the GPIO is relevant rather than the pin number on the GPIO contact strip:

```
user$ chip=4              
(for Raspberry Pi 5)
user$ gpioset $chip 7=1   
(GPIO 7 = set pin 26 to high)
user$ gpioset $chip 7=0   
(GPIO 7 = set pin 26 to low) 
```

You can control multiple outputs at once (here, it’s GPIO 7, 8, and 25):

```
user$ gpioset $chip 7=0 8=1 25=0 
```

Various options allow you to control additional functions:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--bias=as-is|disable|pull-down|pull-up</samp>
    Activates or deactivates the internal pull-up or pull-down resistor of a GPIO.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--mode=exit|wait|time|signal</samp>
    Specifies how long the command should run. The default setting is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">exit</samp>, so the command is terminated immediately. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wait</samp>, the program waits until the user presses Enter. Using the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">time</samp> setting, you can set the desired wait time with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sec=n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--usec=n</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">signal</samp> means that the program continues to run until it’s terminated using Ctrl+C.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--background</samp>
    Continues the command as a background service.

#### Alternatives
