(Otherwise, countless firewall scripts would no longer work). However, there is of course also the option of controlling nftables directly by using the [nft](#N_001.xhtml_nft) command.

### iptables -P chain policy [-t table]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -P</samp>(policy) defines the default behavior for the specified chain of rules. Possible behaviors are given in the following table.

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ACCEPT</samp>: Forward packet (default setting)

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">DROP</samp>: Delete packet

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">RETURN</samp>: Return packet (rare)

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">QUEUE</samp>: Forward packet to a program outside the kernel (rare)

By default, the command applies to filter chains or custom-defined chains. If a NAT or mangle chain of rules is to be changed, the table name must be specified with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp> option, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -P POSTROUTING ACCEPT -t nat</samp>.

It’s not possible to define a standard behavior for custom defined chains. However, you can define the default behavior with the last rule if required, for example, via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -A mychain -j DROP</samp>.

### iptables -A chain [-t table] options

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -A</samp> (add) adds a new rule to the specified chain. In general, one rule applies to all possible cases (i.e., for all IP protocols, for all ports, for all sender and destination addresses, for all interfaces, etc.).
The validity can be restricted using options. Most options can also be used in the negative with an exclamation mark. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p udp</samp>, for example, a rule only applies to UDP packets. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">–p ! udp</samp>, however, it applies to all packets except for UDP packets.

Not all possible combinations of options are permitted. For example, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp> options can only be used for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">tcp</samp> packets, that is, in combination with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p tcp</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ipaddress</samp>
    Specifies the destination address (destination). Address ranges can be specified in the format; <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">192.168.0.0/24</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">192.168.0.0/255.255.255.0</samp>. In both cases, all IP numbers 192.168.0.* are meant.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[--dport</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">port[:port]</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Specifies the port or port range of the destination address (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0:1023</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp>
    Specifies the interface from which the IP packet originates (only for input, forward, and prerouting chains). In the interface name, the special character + is permitted as a placeholder for all interface numbers, that is, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ppp+</samp> for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ppp0</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ppp1</samp>, and so on.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j ACCEPT/DROP/mychain/..</samp>
    Specifies what should happen to the packet (jump). One of the predefined procedures (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ACCEPT</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">DROP</samp>, etc.) is usually specified here. For special applications, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables</samp> provides <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">REDIRECT</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">MASQUERADE</samp>.

    Instead of one of the predefined keywords, you can also specify a custom defined chain of rules. In this case, all rules of this chain will be applied. If no rule in the custom defined chain applies, the next rule in the original chain will be applied instead. In procedural programming, this would correspond to a subroutine call.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">module</samp>
    Indicates that an additional module will be used. Subsequently, special options defined by this additional module may be used. A particularly important additional module is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">state</samp>, which allows packages to be selected according to their connection status. For example, a rule with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-m state --state NEW</samp> only applies to IP packets that initiate new connections. The following table shows the status keywords that can be specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--state</samp>.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">NEW:</samp> The packet initiates a new connection.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ESTABLISHED:</samp> The packet belongs to an existing connection.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">RELATED:</samp> The packet initiates a new connection but belongs to an existing connection.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">INVALID:</samp> The packet doesn’t belong to any existing connection and doesn’t initiate a new connection.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp>
    Specifies the interface to which the IP packet is traveling (only for output, forward, and post-routing chains).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">protocol</samp>
    Determines the protocol (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">tcp</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">udp</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">icmp</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ipaddress</samp>
    Specifies the sender address (source).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sport</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">port[:port]</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Specifies the port or port range for the sender.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--syn</samp>
    Specifies that the rule should only apply to TCP packets for which the SYN bit is set. Such packets are used to initiate a connection (e.g., for all TCP wrapper functions, for HTTP, etc.).

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables</samp> provides the option of logging the effectiveness of individual rules using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">syslogd</samp>. To do this, you can enter <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LOG</samp> as the action for the rule. For a rule to be both effective and logged, it must be specified twice: once with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j LOG</samp> and a second time with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j ACCEPT</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-J DROP</samp>! Note that logging rules can very quickly result in huge log files.

### iptables -N mychain

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -N</samp> (new) creates a new chain of rules named mychain.

### iptables -L [chain] [-t table] [-v]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -L</samp> (list) returns a list of all rules for the three chains of rules of the filter table as well as for all custom-defined chains without any further options.

You can use the other options to precisely specify the desired chain (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -L mychain</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -L POSTROUTING -t nat</samp>). The additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-v</samp> option provides more detailed information. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-n</samp> causes IP and port numbers to be displayed in the output (instead of network or port names).

### iptables -D chain [-t table] options

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -D</samp> (delete) deletes the rule from the chain. Exactly the same options must be specified as for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -A</samp>.

### iptables -F chain [-t table]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -F</samp> (flush) deletes all rules from the specified chain.

### iptables -X [mychain]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables -X</samp> deletes the specified custom chain. If no chain is specified, all custom-defined chains will be deleted.

#### Example

The following <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptable</samp> commands define a mini firewall for IPv4\. Incoming packets are only accepted if they are either assigned to an existing connection or don’t originate from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">eth0</samp> interface via which the computer is connected to the internet.

The example assumes that the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables</samp> tables are initially in the default state, that is, accept all packets, and that there is only one interface to the internet.

```
root# iptables -N wall
root# iptables -A wall -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
root# iptables -A wall -m state --state NEW ! -i eth0 -j ACCEPT
root# iptables -A wall -j DROP
root# iptables -A INPUT -j wall
root# iptables -A FORWARD -j wall 
```

### ip[6]tables-save [options]
ip[6]tables-restore [options]
ip[6]tables-xml [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables-xxx</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ip6tables-xxx</samp> commands help to save the rules of a packet filter firewall in a file or to read them from it. Each command briefly described below is also available in an IPv6 variant.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables-save</samp> outputs all rules of all firewall filters. An easy-to-read syntax is used. The output can be redirected to a file by using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">></samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t name</samp> option causes only the rules of the specified filter to be saved.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables-restore</samp> reads rules from the standard input. The rules normally replace existing filter chains. If you don’t want this to happen, you must specify the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-n</samp> option. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-T name</samp>, only the rules of the specified filter are taken into account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables-xml</samp> works in a similar way to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables-save</samp>, but creates an XML document.

### iw object command

You can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iw</samp> command to control Wi-Fi adapters that support the nl80211 interface. This is the case with most current Wi-Fi adapters whose drivers are based on the mac80211 framework.

There are multiple ways to specify the object you want to control. The abbreviation <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">phy</samp> can be omitted if the interface or device name is unique.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the interface name (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev wlan0</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">phy</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">phy #</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Indicates the name or index number of the device. For notebooks with a Wi-Fi adapter, the device name is always <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">phy0</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reg</samp>
    Controls the regulatory agent, that is, a set of rules for national radio standards.

The commands available for selection depend on the object type. I’ll only present a few selected commands here:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">connect</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ssid</samp>
    Establishes a connection to the specified Wi-Fi network. This is only possible with networks that don’t use encryption. If the wireless network is secured by WEP, you must specify the key using the optional <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">keys</samp> parameter (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">keys 0:0011223344</samp>). The key is specified either in the form of 5 or 13 ASCII characters or 10 or 26 hexadecimal digits.

    If the network is secured by WPA, you must specify the key in [etc/wpa/supplicant/wpa_supplicant.conf](#04_001.xhtml_wpa_supplicant.conf) before running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iw dev connect</samp> and make sure that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wpa_supplicant</samp> is running as a background service.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">del</samp>
    Removes (deletes) the interface. If the interface is to be used again later, it must be set up again via <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface add</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">disconnect</samp>
    Terminates the connection.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp>
    Provides general information about the interface.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">link</samp>
    Provides information on the active network connection or not connected.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">scan</samp>
    Provides detailed information on all wireless networks within range.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">phy phy0 interface add wlan0 type managed</samp>
    Sets up the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wlan0</samp> interface for the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">phy0</samp> device. Other interface types are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">monitor</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wds</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mesh</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mp</samp>, as well as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ibss</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">adhoc</samp>. The new interface must then be activated using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ifconfig wlan0 up</samp>.

For troubleshooting, it’s often useful to run the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iw event</samp> command in a second window or console. This command returns all status and error messages until the end by pressing Ctrl+C.

#### Example

The following commands manually establish a network connection to a wireless network that isn’t protected by a password:

```
root# iw phy phy0 interface add wlan0 type managed
root# ifconfig wlan0 up
root# iw dev wlan0 connect hotel-wlan
root# dhclient wlan0 
```

In many current distributions, the Wi-Fi interfaces are no longer called <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wlan0</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wlan1</samp>, and so on, but <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wlpnsm</samp>.

## J

### j directory

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">j</samp> command from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">autojump</samp> package helps to change to another directory in a particularly efficient way. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">j</samp> is, so to speak, a learning variant of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp> command. For example, if you’ve executed <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">j /etc/X11/xorg.conf.d</samp> once, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">j xorg.conf.d</samp> is sufficient the second time, that is, the last part of the directory path (provided it’s unique).

You can further shorten the input with the Tab completion, for example, as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">j xorg</samp> Tab. If multiple directories match, you can simply press Tab several times. If required, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">jumpstats</samp> command provides statistics on all recently visited directories.

A modern alternative to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">j</samp> is [z](#Z_001.xhtml_z).

### john [options] [hashfile]

The program John the Ripper (command and package name <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp>) is an offline password cracker. To use the program, you must have the passwords as hash codes. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> then tests whether self-generated passwords or passwords from a predefined list correspond to the hash codes.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> can handle most common hash algorithms. In the simplest case, you simply pass the name of a text file containing hash codes line by line to the command. The lines of the text file can also have the following format: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name:hashcode:xxx</samp>.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> first tries the account name as password (if available), then passwords from a built-in word list, and finally passwords that it generates itself (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--single</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--wordlist</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--incremental</samp> mode). Cracked passwords are stored in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.john/john.pot</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--format=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hashname</samp>
    Specifies which hash method <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> should use. The command supports the following formats, among others: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">afs</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bcrypt</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bsdicrypt</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">crypt</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">descrypt</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dummy</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lm md5crypt</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tripcode</samp>. This option is only required if <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> doesn’t recognize the hash method itself.

    A brief description of the hash formats can be found on the following website. Note that this website also describes formats that are only included in the unofficial “jumbo” version (see the “Alternatives” section).
    [https://pentestmonkey.net/cheat-sheet/john-the-ripper-hash-formats](https://pentestmonkey.net/cheat-sheet/john-the-ripper-hash-formats)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--incremental[:lower|lowernum|alpha|digits|alnum]</samp>
    Generates passwords itself, first trying out short and then increasingly longer passwords. Note that, in this mode, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> runs endlessly, unless the passwords you’re looking for are trivial.

    By default, the characters a–z, A–Z, and 0–9 are taken into account in this mode (corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">alnum</samp>, 62 characters). Optionally, you can restrict the character set: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lower</samp> corresponds to a–z, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lowernum</samp> includes a–z and 0–9, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">alpha</samp> corresponds to a–z and A–Z, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">digits</samp> includes digits only. Some other modes that can be defined are provided in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/john/john.conf</samp>. (On Ubuntu, many modes don’t work because the corresponding character set files are missing in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/share/john</samp>.)

    Finally, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john --make-charset</samp> to generate your own character set file, which you can then use with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--incremental=charsetfile</samp>. The following website provides some useful tips on this: [https://security.stackexchange.com/questions/66106](https://security.stackexchange.com/questions/66106).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--restore</samp>
    Continues the execution of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> that was interrupted by Ctrl+C.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--show</samp>
    Displays passwords that have already been cracked. For this purpose, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.john/john.pot</samp> file gets evaluated.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--wordlist</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename</samp>
    Tries out the passwords contained in the file line by line.

#### Example

The starting point for this example is a Linux computer with multiple accounts. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">unshadow</samp> command supplied with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> combines <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/passwd</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/shadow</samp> into a new <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">hashes</samp> file. (The access to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">shadow</samp> file requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions.) The hash codes in the resulting file are abbreviated here for reasons of space:

```
root# unshadow /etc/passwd /etc/shadow > hashes
root# chown user hashes
user$ cat hashes
...
peter:$6$U.zGFBlF$LdNTE...:1001:1001::/home/peter:/bin/bash
maria:$6$gSJg6.d8$mN.en...:1002:1002::/home/maria:/bin/bash
hugh:$6$UinuQqJY$iD59.N...:1003:1003::/home/hugh:/bin/bash 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp> finds two particularly insecure passwords within seconds. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">peter</samp> has used his own name as his password, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">hugh</samp> used the popular password “123456”. However, Maria’s password can’t be cracked straight away, which is why the process gets stopped after a while by pressing Ctrl+C:

```
user$ john hashes
Loaded 3 password hashes with 3 different salts
Press 'q' or Ctrl-C to abort, almost any other key for status
peter            (peter)
123456           (hugh)
  <Strg>+<C> 
```

You can download lists of popular passwords from GitHub using [git](#G_001.xhtml_git). (Note that the space required for the lists is around 750 MiB!) One of these dictionaries actually contains Maria’s password! It reads <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">secret</samp>:

```
user$ git clone https://github.com/danielmiessler/SecLists.git
user$ john --wordlist=SecLists/Passwords/Common-Credentials/ \
                   10-million-password-list-top-10000.txt  hashes
Loaded 3 password hashes with 3 different salts
Remaining 1 password hash with 1 different salt
secret           (maria) 
```

#### Alternatives

On GitHub there is the greatly expanded, community-maintained “jumbo” version of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">john</samp>: [https://github.com/openwall/john](https://github.com/openwall/john).

If you want to significantly speed up the cracking of hash codes with GPU support, you should consider using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">hashcat</samp>. The biggest hurdle in this case is the installation of suitable GPU drivers. To check network services for insecure passwords, you can use the online password cracker: [hydra](#H_001.xhtml_hydra).

### journalctl [options] [search expression]

The journal is the syslog service belonging to systemd. It now runs on most common Linux distributions, sometimes in parallel with a conventional logging system (usually <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">rsyslogd</samp>).

The journal files are saved in a binary format and can only be read using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">journalctl</samp> command described here.

One or more search expressions can be formulated as a path to a program or in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">field=value</samp> syntax. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">journalctl</samp> then only shows logging entries to which all search expressions apply. Search expressions with logical OR can be formulated with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+</samp>, that is, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">field1=value1 + field2=value2</samp>.

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">MESSAGE</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PRIORITY</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ERRNO</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">_PID</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">_UID</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">_GID</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">_SELINUX_CONTEXT</samp> keywords are permitted for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">field</samp>. A reference of additional search parameters and a detailed description of their meanings can be found with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man systemd.journal-fields</samp>.

When called without further parameters, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">journalctl</samp> usually returns an almost endless list of all logged messages, but you can use options to filter the output:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Shows only the messages since the last reboot of the computer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--disk-usage</samp>
    Shows how much space the journal files take up in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/log</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-e</samp>
    Jumps immediately to the end of the messages to be displayed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp>
    Starts <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">journalctl</samp> in continuous operation, constantly displaying the currently arriving messages. Ctrl+C terminates the command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-k</samp>
    Shows only kernel messages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">systemd. Journal</samp>
    Shows only the last <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> lines.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-pager</samp>
    Writes the output directly to the standard output instead of using a pager (normally, the [less](#L_001.xhtml_less) command) for display.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Shows only messages in a certain priority level. The number range is from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">7</samp> for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">emerg</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">alert</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">crit</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">err</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">warning</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">notice</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">debug</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p 2</samp> means that only messages of levels <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">2</samp> are taken into account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Shows the latest messages first.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--since 2025-12-31 19:30:00</samp>
    Shows only messages that were logged after the specified time.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Shows only messages for the specified syslog keyword (tag, as in [logger](#L_001.xhtml_logger) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Shows only messages for the specified systemd service (unit, e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">avahi-daemon</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--user</samp>
    Displays messages from the user journal instead of the system journal. The user journal is used in modern Linux distributions to log messages from the graphics system, Gnome, or other desktop systems, as well as the programs running in them.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--until 2025-12-31 19:30:00</samp>
    Shows only messages that have been logged up to the specified time.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--vacuum-size=500M</samp>
    Deletes old logging files to such an extent that the total memory requirement is a maximum of 500 MiB.

#### Examples

The following command shows all messages from the Open SSH server in reverse order, that is, the latest messages first:

```
user$ journalctl -u sshd -r 
```

If you want to follow the logging messages live, you should call <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">journalctl</samp> as follows:

```
user$ journalctl -u sshd -f 
```

The third example shows all messages in which the IP address 10.0.0.2 appears:

```
user$ journalctl | grep 10.0.0.2 
```

### jq [options] filter expression [file.json]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">jq</samp> stands for JSON query and helps to extract data from JSON files. The command can be found in the package of the same name, which must be installed before the first use. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">jq</samp> reads the JSON document from the standard input or from the files passed as parameters. The simplest application is to format and indent JSON documents in a readable way. To do this, you simply need to enter a dot as the filter expression: <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">jq . file.json</samp>.

The following list provides some more examples of filter expressions:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.key1</samp>
    Returns the value for the specified key.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.[]</samp>
    Returns all array elements of the current level.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.[].key1.key2</samp>
    Returns all corresponding elements of the array.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Returns the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>th element.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filter | {json expression}</samp>
    Creates a new JSON document from the elements found.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filter | select {.key1.key2=="xxx"}</samp>
    Filters elements that have a specific property.

#### Examples

```
user$ echo '{"key1":"123","key2":"456"}' | jq .
{
   "key1": "123",
   "key2": "456"
}
user$ echo '{"key1":"123","key2":"456"}' | jq .key1
"123" 
```

You can find more complex application examples in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">jq</samp> tutorial:

[https://jqlang.org/tutorial/](https://jqlang.org/tutorial/)

## K

### kbdrate [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kbdrate</samp> sets the delay time and the speed of key repetitions on the keyboard. Without options, the command displays the currently valid settings.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--delay=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Indicates after how many milliseconds the key repetitions start. Permissible values are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">250</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">500</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">750</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1000</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--rate=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Controls how many characters per second the keyboard forwards for a longer keystroke. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> can be a float, but not every value is permitted (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man kbdrate</samp>). The command automatically selects the next permissible value.

### kexec [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kexec</samp> command from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kexec-tools</samp> package enables you to activate a new kernel without rebooting the computer. All processes and the init system must be shut down completely. Compared to a real reboot, a kernel reboot with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kexec</samp> is still a few seconds faster: In particular, BIOS/EFI initialization and the GRUB process are no longer required. However, there may be problems when reinitializing various hardware components.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kexec</samp> is used in two steps: first you need to prepare the kernel reboot using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kexec -l</samp>, then you actually perform the kernel exchange using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kexec -e</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">systemctl isolate kexec</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--append=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kernel parameters</samp>
    Passes the parameters to the kernel in addition to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--command-line</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--reuse- cmdline</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--command-line=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kernel parameters</samp>
    Passes the parameters to the kernel.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-e</samp>
    Restarts the previously installed kernel (exec).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--initrd=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">initrd file</samp>
    Specifies the location of the initrd file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kernel file</samp>
    Specifies the location of the new kernel to be loaded (load).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--reuse-cmdline</samp>
    Adopts the parameters used during the last kernel start.

#### Example

The following command prepares the kernel restart:

```
root# kexec -l /boot/vmlinuz-6.6.7-300 \
            --initrd=/boot/initrd.img-6.6.7-300 --reuse-cmdline 
```

In the second step, you must activate the new kernel—either immediately via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kexec -e</samp> or after you’ve shut down all running services via systemd. On a server, the second option is definitely preferable! This is the only way to ensure that a database server, for example, can complete all open transactions and close all files properly.

```
root# kexec -e                 
(immediate restart)
root# systemctl isolate kexec  
(first shut down services, then restart) 
```

### kill [-s signal] processno

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kill</samp> sends signals to a running process. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kill</samp> is used without the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp> option, the SIGTERM signal (15) is sent by default to terminate (kill, hence the name of the command) the process. In particularly obstinate cases, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-9</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s SIGKILL</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-KILL</samp> will help. However, the process then has no chance of performing any cleanup work.

However, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kill</samp> can also be used to send more harmless signals. Quite often, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-1</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">or</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s SIGHUPv</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-HUP</samp> is used to request a daemon to reload its configuration files. In this way, you can activate a new configuration for some programs without having to completely stop and restart the daemon.

The easiest way to make the required process number (PID) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kill</samp> a convenient variant is by using the [ps](#P_001.xhtml_ps) command: the program that is to be terminated can simply be “shot down” with the mouse.

### killall [-signal] process name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">killall</samp> works almost like the [kill](#K_001.xhtml_kill) command. The difference is that it’s not the process number (PID) that is specified, but the name of the process. If there are multiple processes with this name, they all receive the specified signal (again SIGTERM by default). The desired signal is specified either as the number -n or with a name such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-HUP</samp>. You can obtain a list of all signal names via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">killall -l</samp>.

#### Example

The following example terminates all running Firefox instances of the current user. If the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">killall</samp> command is executed by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>, it terminates all running Firefox processes of all users.

```
user$ killall firefox 
```

### kpartx [diskdevice]

The low-level <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kpartx</samp> command from the package of the same name determines all partitions of the specified data medium and creates the corresponding device files. Usually, the device files are created automatically by the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">udev</samp> system as soon as a new data medium is detected, for example, when a USB hard disk gets connected. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kpartx</samp> is primarily intended for editing virtual data media or virtual machine image files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Creates new device files for the specified data medium (add).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Removes the device files for the data medium (delete).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Reads the partitions of the data medium, but doesn’t create any device files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>
    Updates the device files for a changed data medium (update).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Provides information on the actions performed.

#### Example

The following command connects all partitions contained in the raw image file with loop devices:

```
root# kpartx -av image.raw
add map loop0p1 (252:12): 0 1024000 linear /dev/loop0 2048
add map loop0p2 (252:13): 0 19945472 linear /dev/loop0 1026048 
```

The entire virtual hard disk can then be accessed via the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/mapper/loop0</samp> device.

### kvm [options] [imagefile]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kvm</samp> script, which is still commonly used on Ubuntu, runs a virtual machine. The [qemu](#Q_001.xhtml_qemu) emulator and the Linux virtualization system kernel-based virtual machines (KVMs) are used. In most other distributions, virtual machines are started directly via the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">qemu</samp> command, which is why I describe the numerous identical options there.

## L

### l2ping [options] bluetoothmac

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">l2ping</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bluez</samp> package sends L2CAP echo requests to the Bluetooth device specified by its MAC address. In this way, you can test whether a connection between the local Bluetooth adapter and the external device is possible. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">l2ping</samp> must be run with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions. You can determine the MAC address of external Bluetooth devices using [hcitool](#H_001.xhtml_hcitool) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">scan</samp>.

### lame [options] in out.mp3

The LAME acronym stands for LAME Ain't an MP3 Encoder, but the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lame</samp> command is actually used to convert WAV files into compressed audio files that are compatible with the MP3 format. Alternatives to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lame</samp> are <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">toolame</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">twolame</samp>, both of which create files in MPEG-1 Layer 2 format (i.e., MP2). This type of file can also be played by most MP3 players without any problems.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    The source file is in raw format (not as a WAV file).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s 8/11.025/12/16/22.05/24/32/44.1/48</samp>
    Specifies the sampling frequency within the raw file. This option isn’t required for WAV files.

#### Example

The following command creates the MP3-compatible audio file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">title.mp3</samp>:

```
user$ lame title.wav title.mp3 
```

### last [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">last</samp> provides a list of users who were last logged on to this computer. The command evaluates the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/log/wtmp</samp> file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp>
    Displays the IP address instead of the host name of the remote computer for SSH logins.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wimpy</samp>
    Controls how many entries will be displayed, for example, 100 with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-100</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t YYYYMMDDhhmmss</samp>
    Indicates who was logged in at the specified time.

#### Example

The last user to work on the test computer was <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kofler</samp>:

```
user$ last
kofler   pts/0  62.47.230.2   Tue Sep 24 13:51   still logged in
kofler   pts/0  212.183.46.83 Mon Sep 23 19:50 - 20:22  (00:32)
kofler   pts/1  91.115.236.11 Fri Sep 13 15:39 - 17:51  (02:11)
kofler   pts/0  91.115.236.11 Fri Sep 13 15:31 - 17:51  (02:20) 
```

### lastb [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lastb</samp> shows which login attempts have recently failed. The command is controlled with the same options as [last](#L_001.xhtml_last). It can only be run by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> and evaluates the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/log/btmp</samp> file.

### ldconfig

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ldconfig</samp> updates the links to all libraries and creates the cache file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/ld.so.cache</samp>, which helps with the efficient search for libraries. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ldconfig</samp> evaluates the configuration file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/ld.so.conf</samp>. The command must be executed after the manual installation of libraries.

### ldd program

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ldd</samp> provides a list of all libraries required to run the specified program. You can also use the command to determine whether all the necessary libraries are available on the computer.

#### Example

The Gnome terminal accesses around 80 libraries on Fedora! The following lines show the first four of these in alphabetical order:

```
root# ldd /usr/bin/gnome-terminal | sort
  libatk-1.0.so.0 => /lib64/libatk-1.0.so.0 (0x0000ffffa4010000)
  libatk-bridge-2.0.so.0 => /lib64/libatk-bridge-2.0.so.0 (0x0000ffffa3d20000)
  libatspi.so.0 => /lib64/libatspi.so.0 (0x0000ffffa2aa0000)
  libblkid.so.1 => /lib64/libblkid.so.1 (0x0000ffffa3390000)
  ... 
```

### less [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp> displays the specified text file page by page. The command is often used as a filter, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls -l | less</samp>, to display a long file list on a page-by-page basis.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp>
    Shows the current text position as a percentage in the status bar.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-M</samp>
    Displays the file name and the text position in lines in the status bar.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search text</samp>
    Shows the first line in which the text to be searched for was found.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Displays formatting and color control codes (raw). The option is required in rare cases to correctly display a file that contains such control codes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp>
    Reduces multiple empty lines into one line.

While <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp> is running, pressing H displays a help text. The cursor keys allow you to navigate through the text. The space bar scrolls one page forward, B moves one page back. < and > jump to the beginning or end of the text, respectively. / allows you to enter a search text. Q terminates <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp>.

### lftp [options] [site]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lftp</samp> is an interactive FTP client. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lftp</samp> can also be used in scripts and controlled by commands.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c "</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"</samp>
    Runs the FTP commands specified in a character string and separated by semicolons (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lftp -c "open -u user,passw server; mirror -R dir"</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Reads the commands to be executed line by line from a file.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lftp</samp> login settings can be saved line by line for various servers in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.netrc</samp> file. Entries in this file look like the following pattern:

```
machine backup.hostname.com   login u123456   password x234b0CT2xCb 
```

#### Example

The following command uploads a file to an FTP server:

```
root# lftp -c "open -u username,password backupserver; put file" 
```

To transfer an entire directory to the backup server instead of a file, you can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mirror -R</samp> command. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mirror</samp> usually copies directories from the FTP server to the local computer. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-R</samp> command reverses the transfer direction. Here’s another example:

```
root# lftp -c "open -u usern,passw bserver; mirror -R directory" 
```

### libcamera-still [options]
libcamera-vid [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">libcamera-still</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">libcamera-vid</samp> take photos and videos on the Raspberry Pi. As a matter of fact, the [rpicam-still](#R_001.xhtml_rpicam-still) and [rpicam-vid](#R_001.xhtml_rpicam-vid) commands are actually used for this. The syntax of the commands is described there. The command names <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">libcamera-still</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">libcamera-vid</samp> are obsolete and are only available for compatibility reasons.

### ll [options] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ll</samp> is a predefined alias in many distributions that run the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> command with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-l</samp> option and possibly other options.

### ln [options] source [target]
ln [options] files target directory

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ln</samp> sets up fixed or symbolic links to files and directories. The [cp](#C_001.xhtml_cp) command has the same functionality as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ln</samp> if the options <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp> are specified there.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--backup</samp>
    Renames existing files with the same name to back up files (name plus ~ character) instead of overwriting them.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--directory</samp>
    Creates a fixed link for a directory. This operation is only permitted for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>. All other users can create symbolic links to directories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--symbolic</samp>
    Generates symbolic links. (Without this option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ln</samp> returns fixed links.)

#### Example

The following command creates the symbolic link <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xyz</samp> to the existing file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">abc</samp>:

```
user$ ln -s abc xyz 
```

### loadkeys [options] file name

The low-level <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">loadkeys</samp> command loads a keyboard table for text mode. The required settings files are usually located in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/lib/kbd/keymaps</samp> directory. If you enter a file name without a path, the command itself attempts to find a suitable file with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.map.gz</samp> identifier.

For this reason, the keyboard settings changed in this way only apply if you work in a text console. The settings for the graphics mode, however, must be changed as part of the X configuration; for distributions with systemd, you can also use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">localectl</samp> command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Loads the default keyboard table, which usually is the file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/lib/kbd/keymaps/defkeymap.map</samp>.

#### Example

The following command activates the German keyboard layout in the text consoles:

```
root# loadkeys de-latin1
Load /lib/kbd/keymaps/i386/qwertz/de.map.gz 
```

### local var[=value]

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">local</samp> defines a local variable in functions within shell scripts. The command can only be used in custom-defined functions (see [](#F_001.xhtml_function)). Note that you must not enter any spaces before or after the equal sign.

### localectl [options] [command]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">localectl</samp> command is used to control the language and keyboard settings in distributions with the systemd init system. It changes the following files: [etc/locale.conf](#04_001.xhtml_locale.conf), [etc/vconsole.conf](#04_001.xhtml_vconsole.conf), and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/X11/xorg.conf/00-keyboard.conf</samp>.

#### Options

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-convert</samp>
    Changes only the keyboard for the console (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">set-keymap</samp> command) or for the graphics mode (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">set-x11-keymap</samp> command).

    By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">localectl</samp> attempts to change the keyboard settings for both text and graphics mode at the same time. However, the relevant files have a different syntax, which is why the conversion of the parameters sometimes fails.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-pager</samp>
    Runs output directly on the standard output instead of using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp>.

#### Commands

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-keymaps</samp>
    Determines a list of all possible keyboard layouts for text mode.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-locales</samp>
    Determines a list of all possible language settings.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-x11-keymap-models</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-x11-keymap-layouts</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-x11-keymap-variants [layout]</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-x11-keymap-options</samp>
    Determines the permissible parameters for setting the keyboard layout in graphics system X.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set-keymap</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Activates the specified keyboard layout.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set-locale</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Activates the specified language setting.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set-x11-keymap</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">layout</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">model variant options</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Activates the specified keyboard layout for the graphics mode.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status</samp>
    Shows the current language and keyboard settings.

#### Example

The following two commands set the German language, the UTF-8 character set, and a German keyboard layout, taking into account the special features of an Apple keyboard:

```
root# localectl set-locale de_DE.UTF-8
root# localectl set-x11-keymap de de mac grp:alt_shift_toggle 
```

### locate pattern

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">locate</samp> enables a particularly fast search for files. It searches a file database, usually updated once a day, in which the specified pattern occurs in the full file name (including path). However, files that were created or changed after the last database update can’t be found.

In most cases, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">locate</samp> and the underlying <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">updatedb</samp> system must be installed separately (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mlocate</samp> package) and often also configured.

### logger [options] message

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">logger</samp> logs a message with the syslog service. Depending on the distribution, this is usually <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">rsyslogd</samp> or, in more modern distributions, the journal (see [journalctl](#J_001.xhtml_journalctl)).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Logs the message in the specified priority level between <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> = <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">emerg</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">7</samp> = <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">debug</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">facility.level</samp>
    Logs the message for the specified service and at the specified priority level. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">logger</samp> uses the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user.notice</samp> setting.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tag</samp>
    Saves the specified keyword together with the message. This simplifies a later search for corresponding messages.

#### Example

The following <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">logger</samp> command could be positioned at the end of a backup script. It logs the successful end of the backup.

```
user$ logger -p local0.notice -t mybackuptool "Backup completed" 
```

### loginctl [options] [command] [name]

Like <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">systemctl</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">journalctl</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">loginctl</samp> belongs to the systemd family. You can use the command to control the login manager (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man systemd-logind.service</samp>) or query data. Without options or parameters, the command simply displays all active logins (sessions).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">property</samp>
    Specifies which property will be queried. Without this option, subcommands such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">show-session</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">show-user</samp> provide a great deal of detail.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">active</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sessionname</samp>
    Activates the specified session. The command may also change the active console, similar to the following shortcut keys: Ctrl+Alt+F1, Alt+F2, and so on.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enable-linger</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">loginname</samp>
    Allows processes to continue after a user logout. This is useful for continuing long-lasting processes (downloads, calculations) to their end after a logout. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">loginctl disable-linger</samp> deactivates the function again.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-sessions</samp>
    Shows all active sessions (default behavior).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-users</samp>
    Shows all logged-in users.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">session-status</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sessionname</samp>
    Shows which processes were started within a session and which logging messages were logged.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">show-session</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sessionname</samp>
    Shows details of a session.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">show-user</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">username</samp>
    Shows details about a user.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">terminate-session</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sessionname</samp>
    Ends a session. All assigned processes receive a kill signal.

#### Example

There are four sessions on the sample computer. On console 1 (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tty1</samp>), the Gnome Display Manager is running and displays a login box. A user is logged in locally on console 7 (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tty7</samp>). There are also two other logins that have been made via SSH (the output of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">loginctl</samp> doesn’t reveal these).

```
root# loginctl
   SESSION    UID   USER      SEAT     TTY
         5   1000   kofler
        c1    119   gdm       seat0    tty1
         2   1000   kofler    seat0    tty7
         4   1000   kofler 
```

The second <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">loginctl</samp> command shows that the graphics system in console 7 uses Wayland. If Xorg is used instead, the output is <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">Type=x11</samp>.

```
root# loginctl show-session 2 -p Type   Type=wayland 
```

### logname

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">logname</samp> displays the login name (username).

### logout

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">logout</samp> or even shorter simply Ctrl+D terminates the session in a console or terminal window.

### lpadmin [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpadmin</samp> sets up a new printer for the CUPS printing system, changes its access rights for network operation, or deletes it again.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Defines the specified printer as the default printer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-E</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Activates the specified printer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Sets up a new printer. You can specify the configuration parameters with various other options (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man lpadmin</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Deletes the configuration for the specified printer.

### lpinfo [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpinfo</samp> lists the devices and drivers available for CUPS.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Provides particularly detailed information. The option must be combined with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-m</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-v</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp>
    Provides a list of all available printer drivers.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Provides a list of all known printing devices.

### lpoptions [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpoptions</samp> displays or changes the options of CUPS printers.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Provides a list of the available options and their current setting.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">option name=value</samp>
    Changes the setting of the specified option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the desired printer. (Without the option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpoptions</samp> refers to the default printer.)

### lpq [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpq</samp> provides a list of all cached files or print jobs. The size of the file and a job number are also specified. You can specify this job number as a parameter of [lprm](#L_001.xhtml_lprm) to remove a file from the printer spooler.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Displays the print jobs of all queues.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-P</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Displays the print jobs in the specified name queue.

### lpr file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpr</samp> prints the specified file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Bypasses the filter system and sends the printer data to the printer unchanged. This option is useful if a print file is already available in the printer-specific format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o options</samp>
    Passes various additional parameters, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o media=A4</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">–o page-ranges=23-27,29,31</samp>. Numerous examples can be found in the CUPS documentation: [www. cups.org/doc/options.html](http://www.cups.org/doc/options.html).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-P</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Uses the name queue instead of the default printer. Note that the option isn’t followed by a space!

### lprm [options] [id]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lprm</samp> cancels the current print job or the print job specified by the ID.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-P</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the queue.

### lpstat [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpstat</samp> displays information about CUPS classes, printers, and their print jobs. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lpstat</samp> works for both local and network printers.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Indicates for all printers whether they are ready to accept print jobs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp>
    Displays all classes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Displays the default printer.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp>
    Displays a status overview (default printer, list of all classes and printers, etc.).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp>
    Displays all available information.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Displays all printers.

### ls [-options] [path]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> displays a list of all files and directories. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> is used without additional parameters or options, the command returns a multicolumn table sorted by file name in which all files, links, and directories in the current directory are displayed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-all</samp>
    Also displays files whose name begins with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.</samp> Option <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-A</samp> has a very similar effect. The only difference is that the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">..</samp> files (references to the current and parent directory, respectively) won’t be displayed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--color [=never|auto|always]</samp>
    Uses different colors for different file types (links, directories, etc.) or deactivates the color display. You can configure the colors yourself using [dircolors](#D_001.xhtml_dircolors).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--directory</samp>
    Shows only the name of the directory, not its contents. This option is useful, for example, if a directory name is specified as the path, and the access rights of this directory are to be checked (and not its content).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp>
    Displays the file sizes in KiB, MiB, and GiB (human readable).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--inode</samp>
    Shows the I-node of the file in addition to the other information. (The I-node is an internal identification number of the file, which is required for Linux-internal file management.) The option can be used to recognize hard links because files linked in this way have the same I-node.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-I</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--ignore</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Excludes the specified files from being displayed. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-I*ps</samp> prevents files with the extension <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ps</samp> from being displayed. If a file pattern rather than a single file is specified after <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-I</samp>, no space may be entered between <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-I</samp> and the pattern!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--format=long</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--format=verbose</samp>
    Displays further information in addition to the file name, such as the file size in bytes, access rights, and more. A separate line is used to display each file (instead of the space-saving multicolumn list).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--dereference</samp>
    Doesn’t display the path of the link but the content of the original directory for a symbolic link to a directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-color</samp>
    Doesn’t use different colors or fonts.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-F</samp>
    Appends a special character to the file name to indicate the type of file. In some Linux distributions, this option is activated by default in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/profile</samp> by means of an <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">alias</samp> abbreviation. The most important special characters are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp> for directories, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@</samp> for symbolic links, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*</samp> for executable files, and | for FIFOs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--reverse</samp>
    Reverses the sort order. The option is often used in combination with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-S</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--recursive</samp>
    Also captures files in subdirectories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sort=size</samp>
    Sorts the files according to their size (the largest file first).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sort=time</samp>
    Sorts the files according to the date and time of the last change (the newest file first).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sort=access</samp>
    Sorts the files based on the date and time of the last read access. The option must be specified together with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t</samp> (otherwise, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> doesn’t sort at all).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Sorts numbers in file names in a reasonable way, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">tty2</samp> before <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tty10</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-X</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sort=extension</samp>
    Sorts the files according to their identifier (i.e., according to the letter combination that follows the last <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.</samp> in the file name).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Z</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--context</samp>
    Shows the SELinux context information. More information is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--lcontext</samp>; less information is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--scontext</samp>.

Unfortunately, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> doesn’t display the total memory requirements of all listed data. This task is performed by the [du](#D_001.xhtml_du) command. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> isn’t able to display the access bits of a file in octal format. To do this, you can use the [stat](#S_001.xhtml_stat) command.

#### Example

The following command displays all files in the current directory and sorts them by date (the newest file last):

```
user$ ls -ltr
-rw-r--r-- 1 kofler kofler 1681276 2025-03-02 10:01 cimg3079.jpg
-rw-r--r-- 1 kofler kofler 1582496 2025-03-02 10:01 cimg3014.jpg
-rw-r--r-- 1 kofler kofler 1615070 2025-03-02 10:01 cimg2965.jpg
... 
```

Briefly, some comments on the interpretation of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> result: The 10 characters at the beginning of the line indicate the file type and the access bits. The following file types are possible: the hyphen <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-</samp> for a normal file, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">d</samp> for a directory, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">b</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">c</samp> for a device file (block or char), or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">l</samp> for a symbolic link.

The next three characters (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rwx</samp>) indicate whether the owner is allowed to read, write, and execute the file. Analogous information follows for the members of the group as well as for all other system users.

The number following the 10 type and access characters indicates how many hard links reference the file. The other columns indicate the owner and the group of the file (in this case, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kofler</samp>), the size of the file, the date and time of the last change, and finally the file name.

#### Alternatives

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> is one of the most frequently executed Linux commands. Accordingly, there are many attempts to replace <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> with more modern commands that are easier to use, display the results in a more visually appealing way, or integrate additional functions. In this book, I’ll only go into detail about [erd](#E_001.xhtml_erd), which combines the functions of [du](#D_001.xhtml_du), [find](#F_001.xhtml_find), [ls](#L_001.xhtml_ls), and [tree](#T_001.xhtml_tree). The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">eza</samp> (formerly <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">exa</samp>) and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lsd</samp> commands are interesting as well:

[https://github.com/eza-community/eza](https://github.com/eza-community/eza)

[https://github.com/lsd-rs/lsd](https://github.com/lsd-rs/lsd)

### lsattr [options] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">lsattr</samp> displays the status of the additional attributes of files or directories in Linux file systems (ext2 to ext4, Btrfs, XFS, etc.). These additional attributes control, for example, whether files should be compressed, whether changes to files should be made using the copy-on-write procedure, and more. It depends on the implementation of the respective file system which attributes are actually taken into account—for most file systems those are only very few (see also the description of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chattr</samp> command for changing these attributes).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Also displays hidden files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Shows the attributes of directories, not the attributes of the files in the directories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp>
    Recursively displays the attributes of all files in the directory tree.

#### Example

On the test system (an openSUSE Leap installation with a Btrfs file system), the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">C</samp> attribute is set for the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/mysql</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/libvirt/images</samp> directories. It deactivates the copy-on-write function for files in this directory.

```
root# lsattr -d /var /var/lib /var/lib/libvirt/images /var/lib/mariadb
---------------- /var
---------------- /var/lib/
---------------C /var/lib/libvirt/images
---------------C /var/lib/mariadb/ 
```
