    Specifies which access rights apply for file access. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> must begin with a zero and contains the rights in the octal notation familiar from <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file_mode=0444</samp> gives all users read and write permissions. The setting is ignored if the file server supports the CIFS Unix extension.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iocharset=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the desired character set. If special characters or other non-ASCII characters are displayed incorrectly in file names, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iocharset=utf8</samp> usually helps.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nodfs</samp>
    Deactivates the distributed file system (DFS) functions, which allow standardized access to the network directories of different servers. Some old NAS hard disks also use old Samba versions with known DFS errors, which lead to problems especially when the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rsync</samp> command is used. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nodfs</samp> option provides a solution in such cases.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nounix</samp>
    Deactivates the Unix compatibility mode. At this point, a little background information is essential to understand this option. The CIFS standard has been extended by the Unix extensions to achieve better compatibility with Unix/Linux systems. On some NAS devices, these extensions are also active. In this case, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> takes the user and group information and access rights from the NAS device and ignores the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir_mode</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file_mode</samp> options.

    This sounds useful at first glance, but it’s not in most cases: The Unix extensions only make sense if the UIDs and GIDs of the local computer and the Samba server have been matched. This is rarely the case, and practically never with NAS devices. For this reason, the compatibility mode must be deactivated so that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir_mode</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file_mode</samp> remain effective.

    Sometimes, you can also avoid incompatibilities with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nounix</samp>, which is expressed in the vague error message, Operation not supported.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">password=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pw</samp>
    Specifies the password for authentication with the Windows or Samba server. Entering the password directly isn’t secure! It’s better to specify the password in a file and reference it using the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">credentials</samp> keyword.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sec=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mode</samp>
    Specifies the authentication mode. This mode controls the authentication with the Samba server. The default setting is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ntlmssp</samp>. This keyword refers to a Windows- specific procedure with password hashing, whereby the data is packed into an NTLMSSP message. Alternative settings such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ntlmssp</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">krb5i</samp> (Kerberos) are described in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man mount.cifs</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">u</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,gid=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">g</samp>
    Specifies the owner and group of the files, as with the VFAT driver. The usernames or group names can also be transferred to the options instead of the UID/GIDs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">(username</samp> for SMBFS<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">)</samp>
    Specifies the username for authentication with the Windows or Samba server. The workgroup name and password can also be transferred to the option (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">workgroup/name%password</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vers=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n.n</samp>
    Specifies which version of the SMB protocol is to be used. Current <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> versions use version 3 by default because older versions have known security problems. To communicate with an old server, you must explicitly specify the desired version, for example, using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vers=2.1</samp>.

#### exFAT Options

The exFAT file system (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t exfat</samp>) supports the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dmask</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fmask</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">noatime</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ro</samp> (read-only), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">umask</samp> options. The options have the same effect as the VFAT options of the same name, which are described a few pages further on. Only <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">noatime</samp> isn’t available for VFAT file systems. This option prevents the access time information from being updated during read accesses, thus reducing the number of write operations.

#### ext3/ext4 Options

The following options apply to the Linux standard file system ext3 or ext4:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">acl</samp>
    Activates the access control list (ACL) access management. This allows the storage of additional access information in the form of access control lists. In current kernel versions, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">acl</samp> is automatically active.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">barrier=0</samp>(only for ext4)
    Deactivates the write barriers, which ensure that changes are written to the hard disk in the correct order. This increases the speed of the file system but is only safe if the hard disk cache is protected against power failures and crashes by a battery.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">commit=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Synchronizes the journal every <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> seconds (every five seconds by default). The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">laptop-mode</samp> package increases this period for notebooks in battery mode to save energy. For <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ext3</samp> with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=ordered</samp>, all file changes are synchronized at the same time as the journal. For ext3 with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=writeback</samp> and ext4 with delayed allocation, however, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">commit</samp> interval only applies to the journal.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=journal/ordered/writeback</samp>
    Determines the journaling mode (details will follow shortly). By default, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ordered</samp> mode applies for ext4.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">errors=continue/remount-ro/panic</samp>
    Determines the behavior if an error occurs during the file system check. You can set the default behavior using the [tune2fs](#T_001.xhtml_tune2fs) command with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-e</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grpid</samp>
    Causes new files to automatically adopt the group ID of the directory in which they were created. This makes the file system behave like it’s under BSD or the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setgid</samp> bit is set in all directories. (By default, Linux assigns new files the group ID of the user that created the file.)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nodelalloc</samp> (only for ext4)
    Deactivates the delayed allocation.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">noload</samp>
    Ignores the existing journaling file for the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> command. This can be useful if the journaling file is defective.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sb=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Uses block <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> as a superblock (instead of using block 1 by default). In some cases, this makes it possible to read a damaged file system. Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mke2fs</samp> creates a copy of the superblock every 8,192 blocks. It’s therefore advisable to use the values <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">8193]</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">16385</samp>, and so on for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user_xattr</samp>
    Activates support for extended file attributes. (This option is the default for current kernel versions.)

#### ext3/ext4 Journaling Modes

The ext file system has three methods for performing journaling:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=ordered</samp>
    In this mode, only metadata is saved in the journal, that is, information about files, but no content. Files are only marked as committed in the journal when they have been saved completely. After a crash, the file system can be quickly restored to a consistent state because incompletely saved files are immediately recognized using the journal. However, it’s impossible to restore such files.

    In the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=ordered</samp> mode, the journal is synchronized with the hard disk every five seconds. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ext3</samp>, this means that all changes to any files are physically saved to the hard disk within five seconds. Although this standard behavior isn’t particularly efficient, it’s very secure: even in the event of total crashes and power failures, massive data losses are extremely rare. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=ordered</samp> has an unpleasant side effect with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ext3</samp>, however: each time the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsync</samp> function is called, not just a specific file but the entire file system is synchronized. This can result in noticeable delays.

    With ext4, the journal is also synchronized every five seconds, but the actual data changes are often not saved until much later due to delayed allocation. Only an explicit call of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsync</samp> function ensures the immediate physical storage of a file! Fortunately, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsync</samp> for ext4 doesn’t require the entire file system to be synchronized, so it can run much faster.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=writeback</samp>
    This mode is similar to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ordered</samp> mode. The only difference is that the journal and file operations aren’t always fully synchronized. The file system doesn’t wait with the committed entries in the journal for the storage operation on the hard disk to be completed. This makes the file system slightly faster than in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ordered</samp> mode. After a crash, the integrity of the file system is still ensured. However, changed files can contain old data. This problem doesn’t occur if application programs—as provided for in the POSIX standard—complete the save process using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsync</samp> (see the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fsync</samp> entry).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">data=journal</samp>
    Unlike in the other two modes, the actual data is now also saved in the journal. This means that all changes must be saved twice (first in the journal and then in the relevant file). This is why <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ext3</samp> is significantly slower in this mode. Files whose changes have already been fully entered in the journal (but not yet in the file) can be restored after a crash.

The journal is physically saved to the hard disk every five seconds. This time span can be changed using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> option; <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">commit</samp>. Internally, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kjournald</samp> journaling daemon integrated into the kernel takes care of regularly updating the journaling file.

#### NFS Options

The NFS file system (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t nfs</samp>) is the usual way to share or use network directories on Unix/Linux. Note that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t nfs</samp> refers to NFS2 and NFS3\. If you want to use NFS4, you must specify <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t nfs4</samp> in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> command.

Most NFS options apply equally to all NFS versions. A comprehensive summary of all options, including a differentiation between NFS2/3 and NFS4, can be found in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man nfs</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bg</samp>
    Causes the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> process to continue in the background if the NFS server isn’t accessible. This option is only relevant for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/fstab</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hard</samp>
    Causes a program accessing an NFS file to hang if the NFS server is no longer available. (The alternative to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hard</samp> is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">soft</samp>, which causes the kernel to give up trying to find the NFS file again after a while. This may sound safer, but in reality, it causes even more problems than <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hard</samp>.)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">intr</samp>
    Makes it possible to stop a program using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">kill</samp> or Ctrl+C even if an open NFS file is no longer available. The option is only valid in combination with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hard</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nfsvers=2/3</samp>
    Specifies the desired NFS version (only for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t nfs</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rsize=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,wsize=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the size of the buffers for read and write operations (in KiB). The default value is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">4096</samp> in each case.

The right <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> options are decisive for the speed that can be achieved with NFS! You can achieve a high speed with the these options: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hard</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">intr</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rsize=8192</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wsize=8192</samp>. If the NFS speed is still below your expectations, you should ensure that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/exports</samp> on the NFS server uses the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">async</samp> option.

#### NTFS Options

The following options apply to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ntfs3g</samp> driver, which is used by most distributions to access NTFS file systems

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">locale=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the local character set (e.g., in the format <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">locale=en_EN.UTF-8</samp>). The option is only necessary in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/fstab</samp> if the character set isn’t yet configured when the file systems are automatically mounted by the Init-V process.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">show_sys_files</samp>
    Also displays NTFS system files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">streams_interface=none|windows|xattr</samp>
    Specifies how file streams are supposed to be accessed: In the default <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xattr</samp> setting, access occurs via the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">getfattr</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">setfattr</samp> commands. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">windows</samp> allows access in the usual Windows notation: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename:streamname</samp>. The default setting is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">none</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">u</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,gid=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">g</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,umask=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">m</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">|fmask=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">f</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,dmask=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">d</samp>
    Have the same meaning as for the VFAT driver (see the next subsection). The file owner is the user who executed <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp>. All users have read and write access!

#### VFAT Options

You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount -t vfat</samp> to mount Windows VFAT partitions in all variants (FAT12, FAT16, FAT32) in the directory tree. Numerous options control who has which kind of access rights to the files, how the different character sets in the file names are processed, and more.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">codepage=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the code page (a kind of DOS character set) that applies internally to VFAT for short file names (maximum 8 + 3 characters). Long file names are always saved in Unicode format; this option is irrelevant for them. Current Windows versions also save short file names in VFAT format for long file names to maintain the correct uppercase and lowercase notation. For this reason, the option is becoming increasingly less important. The default value of the option can be determined during compilation and is usually <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cp437</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flush</samp>
    Causes the driver to immediately start saving cached data to the data medium. This option minimizes the time required to save changed data on external data media (e.g., a USB flash drive). In contrast to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sync</samp> option, the file system doesn’t wait for the synchronization to be completed. For this reason, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flush</samp> has no negative influence on the speed of write operations.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fmask=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">f</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,dmask=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">d</samp>
    sets the mask for files (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fmask</samp>) and directories (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dmask</samp>) separately. This is particularly useful because you often want to set the x access bit for directories but not for files. This allows the user to go to all directories, but not to run any files or programs.

    One possible setting is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fmask=177,dmask=077</samp>, which allows the owner (UID) to read and write files (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rw-------</samp>) and change to directories (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rwx------</samp>). All other users have no access to the files.

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fmask=133,dmask=022</samp> is often useful as well. This means that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rw-r--r--</samp> applies to files, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rwxr-xr-x</samp> applies to directories; that is, anyone can read everything, but only the owner can change anything.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iocharset</samp>
    Specifies the character set with which Windows file names will be processed on Linux systems. The default setting is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iso8859-1</samp>. As a rule, this option is only used if you work with an 8-bit character set on Linux. (Within VFAT, the Unicode character set is always used for long file names. The option only determines how the file names are displayed on Linux.)

    If you use the UTF-8 character set on Linux, you should use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">utf8</samp> option described at the end of this list instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iocharset</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iocharset=utf8</samp> also works at first glance but isn’t recommended because the VFAT driver is then case sensitive, which is contrary to Windows conventions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">shortname=lower|win95|winnt|mixed</samp>
    Specifies in which uppercase and lowercase short file names (maximum 8 + 3 characters) are presented or saved. The behavior in this regard varies on Windows depending on the version.

    On Linux, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lower</samp> setting applies by default, that is, short file names are presented in lowercase. For new files, the name is saved in VFAT format for long file names (even if the DOS limit of 8 + 3 characters isn’t exceeded), so that uppercase and lowercase is retained. The only exceptions to this rule are short file names that consist exclusively of uppercase letters; such names are saved as short file names as is typical for DOS.

    The setting has no effect on long file names, which are always case-sensitive once the file has been created.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">u</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,gid=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">g</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">,umask=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">m</samp>
    Determines who (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid</samp>) and which group (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid</samp>) “owns” the Windows files, that is, who is allowed to read or change the files. You usually enter the desired user or group number via <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid</samp>. You can pass an octal numerical value with the bit mask of the inverted access bits to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">umask</samp>. Thus, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">umask=0</samp> means that anyone can read, write, and run all files (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rwxrwxrwx</samp>). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">umask=022</samp> corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rwxr-xr-x</samp>: everyone may read all files, but only the owner may change files.

    If these options aren’t specified, the following default values apply for the VFAT file system:

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uid</samp>: UID of the user running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp>. Normally, only <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> may run the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> command, unless the corresponding line in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/fstab</samp> contains the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">users</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">owner</samp> options.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid</samp>: GID of the user running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp>.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">umask</samp>: 022, that is, everyone may read everything, but only the owner may change files or directories.

    It often happens that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fstab</samp> contains the setting <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid=users</samp>. This means that the default group of the user running <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp> applies to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gid</samp>. Without this option, it’s possible to first activate another group via <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newgrp</samp>, which then also applies to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">utf8</samp>
    Causes the driver to return the file names to Linux as UTF-8 character strings. This option is required for the correct display of non-ASCII characters if you use UTF-8 as the character set on Linux.

#### XFS Options

Most of the options for the XFS file system concern rarely used functions (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man mount</samp>). ACLs and extended attributes are available by default on the XFS file system and aren’t controlled by options.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">logdev=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">device</samp>
    Specifies the partition in which the journaling data is stored. This option is only necessary if an external journaling partition was specified when the file system was set up.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">norecovery</samp>
    Prevents the journaling data from being evaluated when the file system is mounted. At the same time, you must use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ro</samp> option (read-only access).

#### Examples

As a rule, you can integrate Linux partitions into the file system without explicitly specifying the file system (i.e., without the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> option):

```
root# mkdir /windows
root# mount /dev/sda7 /media/backup-partition 
```

The following example shows access to the data on a USB flash drive via the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/windows</samp> directory:

```
root# mkdir /usbstick
root# mount -t vfat /dev/sdc1 /usbstick 
```

More options are required so that not only <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> but also an ordinary user with the user ID 1000 and group ID 1000 has access to the USB flash drive and can write or change files:

```
root# mount -t vfat -o uid=1000,gid=1000,fmask=0022,dmask=0022 \
        /dev/sdc1 /usbstick 
```

The following command integrates a network directory of a Windows or Samba server, for example, from a NAS device, into the local directory tree. The user with the UID/GID 1000 can read and change the data.

```
root# mount -t cifs -o username=name,uid=1000,gid=1000,iocharset=utf8,nounix \
       //diskstation/myshare /media/audio-archive
Password for name: ******** 
```

You can use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mount -o remount</samp> to change options of a previously mounted file system. For example, the following command activates the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">noexec</samp> option for a USB flash drive and thus prevents programs contained on it from being executed:

```
root# mount /dev/sdc1 -o remount,noexec 
```

If problems occur when mounting the system partition during the computer startup, the partition is only mounted read-only. However, in order to fix the cause of the error—such as an incorrect entry in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/fstab</samp>—it’s often necessary to make changes to the file system. To do this, you can run the following command. It remounts the system partition, whereby write access is then also possible.

```
root# mount -o remount,rw / 
```

### mtr [options] host name

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mtr</samp> command periodically sends network packets to the specified host and analyzes the responses. The result list combines data from [ping](#P_001.xhtml_ping) and [](#T_001.xhtml_traceroute6). Note that there are two versions of this program: the text command described here and a GTK version with a graphical user interface. Desktop installations of Debian and Ubuntu have the GTK version installed by default. To install the text version instead, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">apt-get install mtr-tiny</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Performs <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> tests. (By default, the program runs until it’s terminated via Ctrl+C).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-dns</samp>
    Omits name resolution and specifies all intermediate stages as IP addresses.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--report</samp>
    Provides a report in text format after the test has been completed. This option must be combined with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-c</samp>.

#### Example

The following lines show a typical <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mtr</samp> result where the connection between a local internet WiFi router and [www.google.com](http://www.google.com) was tested:

```
user$ mtr -c 10 -r google.com

HOST: fedora.fritz.box            Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
  1.|-- fritz.box                  0.0%    10    1.4   1.1   0.9   1.5   0.2
  2.|-- dynamic-pd01.res.v6.highw  0.0%    10   37.2  36.0  20.5  42.7   5.8
  3.|-- lg206-9080-3219.as8447.a1  0.0%    10   38.5  40.9  30.0  47.8   5.0
  4.|-- lg23-9080.as8447.a1.net    0.0%    10   41.6  40.0  35.3  45.8   3.8
  5.|-- lg4-9080.as8447.a1.net     0.0%    10   48.4  48.2  46.5  50.0   1.2
  6.|-- 2001:4860:1:1::64e         0.0%    10   49.3  48.9  37.0  56.6   4.9
  7.|-- 2001:4860:0:1::88ab        0.0%    10   47.2  52.4  46.8  58.8   4.6
  8.|-- 2001:4860:0:1::8886        0.0%    10   46.8  49.2  42.0  57.7   4.7
  9.|-- 2001:4860::c:4003:364e     0.0%    10   47.5  47.6  42.5  49.1   2.0
 10.|-- 2001:4860::9:4002:6cfc     0.0%    10   51.5  49.3  26.8  53.6   8.1
 11.|-- 2001:4860:0:1::7651        0.0%    10   53.9  52.5  23.8  60.7  10.4
 12.|-- 2001:4860:0:1::2ea5        0.0%    10   51.7  50.8  22.9  61.9  10.4
 13.|-- bud02s41-in-x0e.1e100.net  0.0%    10   52.4  49.3  22.9  54.9   9.3 
```

### multitail [options] file1 [file2 file3 ...]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">multitail</samp> helps to monitor multiple logging files at the same time. In the simplest form, you should run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">multitail filei1 filei2 filei3 ...</samp>. This divides the terminal into multiple areas of equal size, each showing the last lines of the specified files. If you prefix the files with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-I</samp>, changes to multiple files are output together in one area. However, it’s then difficult to see which file has changed.

### mv source target
mv files target directory

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mv</samp> renames a file or directory or moves (one or more) files to another directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--backup</samp>
    Renames existing files with the same name to backup files (name plus ~ character) instead of overwriting them.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--interactive</samp>
    Asks before existing files are overwritten.

#### Example

The following command moves all PDF files in the current directory to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pdf</samp> subdirectory:

```
user$ mv *.pdf pdf/ 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mv</samp> can’t be used to rename multiple files. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mv *.xxx *.yyy</samp> doesn’t work. To perform such operations, you must use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">for</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sed</samp>. Corresponding examples can be found in [cp](#C_001.xhtml_cp).

### mysql [options] [database name] [ < name.sql]

The command interpreter <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> executes SQL commands on a MySQL or MariaDB server, either interactively or in batch mode from the standard input. The commands must end with a semicolon. In the batch version, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> is often used to import backups that were created using [mysqldump](#M_001.xhtml_mysqldump). If you don’t specify a database name when calling <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp>, you must set the desired database via the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">USE</samp> command.

The following options only affect the connection setup and also apply in the same form to the [mysqladmin](#M_001.xhtml_mysqladmin) and [mysqldump](#M_001.xhtml_mysqldump) commands described in upcoming entries. In real life, only the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp> options are usually required.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--default-character-set=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies which character set is to be used for the communication with the MySQL or MariaDB server (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">latin1</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">utf8</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--defaults-extra-file=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename</samp>
    Loads connection options from the specified file. This is useful, for example, if <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqldump</samp> is to be run regularly by cron and interactive password entry is impossible.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--host=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hostname</samp>
    Specifies the name or IP number of the computer on which the server is running (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">localhost</samp> by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--login-path=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">group</samp>
    Evaluates the data from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[group]</samp> in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.mylogin.cnf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-P</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--port=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the port number for the TCP/IP connection (3306 by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--password</samp>
    Prompts you to enter the password immediately after starting the command. If the option is missing, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> reads the password from the local configuration file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.my.cnf</samp>. If this file doesn’t exist or doesn’t contain any password data, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> attempts to log in without a password.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xxx</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--password=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xxx</samp>
    Transfers the password directly. However, this isn’t secure because the password appears in plain text in the process list! Unlike other options, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> option doesn’t allow you to specify a space.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--protocol=tcp/socket</samp>
    Specifies which protocol is to be used for the communication between the MySQL client and the database server. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">socket</samp> applies if client and server are running on the same computer; otherwise, it’s <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">tcp</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--socket=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the location of the socket file. This option is only required if <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> can’t find the socket file on its own. In most distributions, the file has the name <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock</samp>. Its location can be set in configuration file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/my.cnf</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/mysql/my.cnf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--user=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the MySQL or MariaDB username (by default, that’s the current username).

There are also some <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mysql</samp>-specific options:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-B</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--batch</samp>
    Separates the columns with tab characters (instead of spaces and line graphics) when outputting the results. In addition, only the results of queries are displayed, but no status information.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-e</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--execute='</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sql command</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp>
    Runs the specified command. You can also enter multiple commands separated by semicolons.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--html</samp>
    Formats the query result as HTML code.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-N</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--skip-column-names</samp>
    Doesn’t label the result columns.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--raw</samp>
    Outputs the 0, tab, newline, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\</samp> characters unchanged in query results. (Usually, these characters are output as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\0</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\t</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\n</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\\</samp>.) The option is only effective in combination with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--batch</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--silent</samp>
    Outputs only the result itself.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--xml</samp>
    Formats the query result as XML code.

#### Example

The following command imports a database backup on the local MySQL or MariaDB server. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dbname</samp> database must already exist.

```
user$ mysql -u name -p dbname < backup.sql
Enter password: ******** 
```

If the backup file was compressed, you should proceed as follows:

```
user$ gunzip -c backup.sql.gz | mysql -u name -p dbname 
```

The following lines show a small script that passes an SQL command to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> to test whether a database exists or not:

```
#!/bin/bash
dbname="ebooks"
sql="     SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemas "
sql="$sql WHERE schema_name='$dbname';"
result=$(mysql -s -N -e "$sql")
if [[ -n "$result" ]]; then
  echo "Database exists"
else
  echo "unknown database"
fi 
```

#### Alternatives

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqlsh</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mariadb-shell</samp> are new shells that have been specifically optimized for MySQL and MariaDB and provide various additional functions. However, the new shells use different options and aren’t compatible with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> command.

### mysqladmin [options] command1 command2 ...

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp> helps with various administrative tasks on a MySQL or MariaDB server, such as creating new databases. You can pass multiple commands to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp>, which are then executed in sequence. The names of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp> commands can be abbreviated as long as they are still clearly recognizable (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flush-l</samp> instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flush-logs</samp>). Most <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp> commands can also be run as SQL commands, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">CREATE DATABASE</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">DROP DATABASE</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">FLUSH</samp>, and more.

To enable <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp> to establish a connection to the database server, the connection options described in the [mysql](#M_001.xhtml_mysql) command must be used, that is, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp>, and so on. In addition, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp> knows a few more options:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--force</samp>
    Runs the command without further inquiry. The execution of multiple commands is continued even if an error occurs with one command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--sleep=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Repeats the command every <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> seconds (e.g., for regular status display). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp> then runs endlessly and must be terminated via Ctrl+C.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--relative</samp>
    In combination with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> and the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">extended-status</samp> command, shows the change compared to the previous status.

The most important <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqladmin</samp> commands are described here:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">create</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dbname</samp>
    Creates a new database.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">drop</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dbname</samp>
    Deletes an existing database irrevocably.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">extended-status</samp>
    Shows countless status variables of the server.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flush-logs</samp>
    Closes all logging files and opens them again.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flush-privileges</samp>
    Reloads the database with the relevant access rights.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kill</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">id1, id2 ...</samp>
    Closes the specified threads.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ping</samp>
    Tests whether a connection to the database server can be established.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">shutdown</samp>
    Terminates the MySQL or MariaDB server.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status</samp>
    Displays various status variables of the database server.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">variables</samp>
    Provides a list of the system variables of the database server.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">version</samp>
    Determines the version of the MySQL or MariaDB server.

#### Example

The following command creates a new database on the local MySQL or MariaDB server:

```
user$ mysqladmin -u name -p create newdb
Enter password: ******** 
```

### mysqlbinlog [options] loggingfile1 file2 ...

MySQL or MariaDB can log all changes, in particular all <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">INSERT</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">UPDATE</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">DELETE commands</samp>, in binary files. These files are used as an incremental update if necessary. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqlbinlog</samp> reads these logging files. The same options apply for establishing the connection as in [mysql](#M_001.xhtml_mysql)<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">(-u</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p</samp>, etc.).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--database=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Takes only commands into account that affect a specific database.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Evaluates only the first logging file from a certain position.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-defaults</samp>
    Doesn’t take configuration files such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.my.cnf</samp> into account. The option is required relatively often in practice if <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.my.cnf</samp> contains an option that applies to all MySQL client commands but isn’t permitted for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqlbinlog</samp> (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">default-character-set=utf8</samp>). You’ll then avoid the error message unknown variable xy.

#### Example

After importing the last complete backup, the incremental updates from two binlog files are applied:

```
root# cd /var/log/mysql
root# mysqlbinlog -j 120 mariadb-bin.001380 mariadb-bin.001380 | \
        mysql -u root -p 
```

### mysqldump [options] dbname [table1 table2 ...]
mysqldump [options] --databases [dbname1 dbname2 ...]
mysqldump [options] --all-databases

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqldump</samp> is a simple backup tool for the MySQL and MariaDB database systems. The command returns a long list of all SQL commands from which the database can be restored exactly. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqldump</samp> knows three syntax variants, depending on whether one database, several enumerated databases, or all databases managed by MySQL will be saved. Only the first variant allows for the backup to be limited to individual tables.

For <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqldump</samp> to establish a connection to the database server, the connection options described for the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysql</samp> command must be used, that is, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp>, and so on. A number of other options control the details of the backup.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--add-locks</samp>
    Inserts <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">LOCK TABLE</samp> before the first <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">INSERT</samp> command and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">UNLOCK</samp> after the last <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">INSERT</samp> command. This speeds up the reloading of MyISAM tables. However, this option isn’t suitable for InnoDB tables.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--create-options</samp>
    Includes MySQL-specific options in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">CREATE-TABLE</samp> command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--disable-keys</samp>
    Deactivates the index update during the reloading of the data. The indexes aren’t updated until the end of the process, which is faster.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--extended-insert</samp>
    Creates longer <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">INSERT</samp> commands with which several data records are inserted at the same time.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--lock-all-tables</samp>
    Runs <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">LOCK TABLE READ</samp> for the entire database. This ensures that no table can be changed during the entire backup. This option is only useful for MyISAM tables. For InnoDB tables, it’s better to use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--single-transaction</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--lock-tables</samp>
    Runs <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">LOCK TABLE READ</samp> for each individual table during the backup before the data is read.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-create-info</samp>
    Saves only the data, but not the structure of the database. In the resulting backup, there are <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">INSERT</samp> commands, but no <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">CREATE TABLE</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-data</samp>
    Saves only the structure (the schema) of the database, but not the data it contains.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-tablespaces</samp>
    Prevents <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqldump</samp> from including the SQL commands <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">CREATE LOGFILE GROUP</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">CREATE TABLESPACE</samp> in the backup. This option must be used with current MySQL server versions if you run the command in an account without the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Process</samp> privilege. Otherwise, an Access denied error will occur.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--opt</samp>
    Serves as the short notation for the following options: <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--add-drop-table</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--add-locks</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--create-options</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--disable-keys</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--extended-insert</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--lock-tables</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--quick</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--set-charset</samp>. For historical reasons, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--opt</samp> is active by default. However, the resulting settings are only optimal (hence, the name of this option) if you perform a backup of MyISAM tables.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--quick</samp>
    Outputs the data records to be saved directly without intermediate storage in RAM.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--routines</samp>
    Also saves the code of stored procedures.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--set-charset</samp>
    Causes the active character set to be changed at the beginning of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqldump</samp> output and the previous character set to be restored at the end.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--single-transaction</samp>
    Ensures that the entire backup is performed as part of a single transaction. This is useful for InnoDB tables and prevents individual tables from being changed during the backup. This ensures that the backup is consistent overall.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--skip-opt</samp>
    Deactivates the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--opt</samp> option, which is active by default.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--triggers</samp>
    Also saves the code of triggers.

#### Examples

Only a few options are required to back up a database with MyISAM tables. If you want to prevent individual tables from being changed during the backup, you need to add the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--lock-all-tables</samp> option to the command. However, note that this blocks all write operations in the database during the backup.

```
user$ mysqldump -u user -p dbname > backup.sql
Enter password: ******** 
```

If you want to save a compressed backup, you should proceed as follows:

```
user$ mysqldump -u user -p dbname | gzip -c > backup.sql.gz 
```

The optimal execution of a backup with InnoDB tables requires considerably more options because the default settings of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mysqldump</samp> aren’t optimized for this case:

```
user$ mysqldump -u user -p --skip-opt --single-transaction \
        --create-options --quick --extended-insert \
        --disable-keys --add-drop-table dbname > backup.sql 
```

If you run the backup automatically using a cron job, you must replace <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-u user -p</samp> with the following option and enter the connection parameters in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>-only file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/root/.my.cnf</samp>:

```
# in the backup script, --defaults-extra-file must be the first option
mysqldump --defaults-extra-file=/root/.my.cnf ... 
```

To restore the backup later, you must run the following commands:

```
user$ mysqladmin  -u user -p create dbname
user$ mysql  -u user -p --default-character-set=utf8 dbname < backup.sql 
```

## N

### namei [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">namei</samp> shows the access rights of all directories that form the path of the specified file:

```
user$ namei -l ~/.ssh
f: /home/kofler/.ssh
drwxr-xr-x root   root   /
drwxr-xr-x root   root   home
drwxr-xr-x kofler kofler kofler
drwx------ kofler kofler .ssh 
```

### nc [options] [hostname/ip-address] [port]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> command is better known as Netcat. It redirects TCP/UDP ports to standard input/output and provides a number of other functions. You can use the command to interactively test network protocols such as HTTP or SMTP in a way similar to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">telnet</samp>. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp>, you can also copy files via any network port, implement a chat, or set up a simple backdoor that receives and executes commands via a port. It’s therefore not surprising that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> is extremely popular among hackers and penetration testers.

On some Linux distributions, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> command is included in the package of the same name; on other distributions, you must install <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">netcat</samp>. Note that there are different implementations of Netcat. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">netcat-traditional</samp> is used on Debian and Ubuntu, while RHEL provides a variant from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> developers ([https://nmap.org/ncat](https://nmap.org/ncat)). In practice, this doesn’t result in any major differences, but individual options may be implemented differently (or not at all) depending on the version.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-4</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-6</samp>
    Uses only IPv4 or IPv6.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Waits on the specified port for a connection to be established (listen).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">portnr</samp>
    Defines the local port (source port). The port, which is usually specified at the end of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> command, is the destination port.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">proxyadr:portnr</samp>
    Uses the specified proxy address and the corresponding port.

A number of other options are described in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man nc</samp>. A possible alternative to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> is the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">socat</samp> command, which isn’t covered in this book. It also supports the SCTP, can work via proxy servers, operate serial interfaces, and encrypt the data for transmission:

[www.dest-unreach.org/socat](http://www.dest-unreach.org/socat)

#### Examples

To copy a file via any port (here, 1234) from host 1 to host 2, you first start the receiver on host 2 (right column) and then initiate the transfer of the file to host 1 (left column):

```
 host2$ nc -l 1234 > file
host1$ nc host2 1234 < file 
```

It’s just as easy to conduct a chat. All you have to do is agree on a port with the other party. The chat is initiated on a computer via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc -l</samp> (left column). This way, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> monitors the specified port 1234 and waits for a connection to be established.

On the second host, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> is started without options to connect to the first host. There’s no visible confirmation that the connection has been established, but as soon as one of the two parties enters text (standard input) and confirms it by pressing Enter, the text appears in the terminal of the other party (standard output).

```
host1$ nc -l 1234
                                     host2$ nc host1 1234
 how are you?
                                     how are you?
                                     good
good
<Ctrl>+<C> 
```

The third example shows the potential danger of Netcat: Here, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nc</samp> on host 1 is set up to pass all input received on port 1234 to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> shell. Their outputs are transferred back to the transmitter. Shell commands can now be run on host 1 from a second host. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ls</samp> therefore shows files that are located on host 1!

```
host1$  nc -l 1234 -e /bin/bash
                                        host2$ nc host1 1234
                                        ls
                                        file1
                                        file2
                                        file3 
```

However, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-e</samp> option for executing a command isn’t available with all Netcat versions. It’s especially missing in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">netcat-traditional</samp> implementation that’s common on Debian and Ubuntu. A solution to that is to install the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> package and run the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ncat</samp> command included there.

### ncdu [options] [directory]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ncdu</samp> is an interactive variant of the [du](#D_001.xhtml_du) command. Usually, it’s simply called without options and parameters. It then displays the subdirectories in the current directory that take up the most space.

You can now navigate through the subdirectories using the cursor keys and Enter. Various other functions are accessible via keyboard shortcuts. An overview of the most important shortcuts can be obtained by entering ? But be careful—D deletes the current file or directory after a query.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Runs the command in read-only mode. Accidental deletion of files or directories is therefore impossible.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp>
    Remains in the current file system, that is, doesn’t take any <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> directories into account.

#### Example

The space required by the directories in the home directory is also symbolized by bars:

```
user$ ncdu
--- /home/kofler ---
     1.5 GiB [##########] /Nextcloud
     1.0 GiB [######    ] /Downloads
   528.5 MiB [###       ] /Images
   209.4 MiB [#         ] /Documents
   ... 
```

### needs-restarting [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">needs-restarting</samp> command available on Fedora, Red Hat, and related distributions specifies whether the computer or individual programs need to be restarted due to an update of the kernel, a basic library, or a firmware file.

The command isn’t available for distributions based on Debian or Ubuntu. There, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/run/reboot-required</samp> file indicates that a reboot is required.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Indicates whether and why a computer restart is required.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>
    Lists processes of the current user that need to be restarted. This option applies by default.

#### Example

The following commands show the status of a computer that should be restarted:

```
root# needs-restarting -r
Core libraries or services have been updated since boot-up:
  * glibc
Reboot is required to fully utilize these updates.
More information: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/27943
root# needs-restarting | sort -n
782 : /usr/lib/polkit-1/polkitd --no-debug
783 : /usr/libexec/power-profiles-daemon
784 : /usr/bin/qemu-ga --method=virtio-serial ...
787 : /usr/libexec/accounts-daemon
... 
```

### netplan [command]

Netplan ([https://netplan.io](https://netplan.io)) is a framework developed by Ubuntu that configures and integrates other network backends such as the NetworkManager and networkd (a systemd component, see [networkctl](#N_001.xhtml_networkctl)). It’s used in Ubuntu and evaluates the configuration files located in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/netplan</samp> (see [etc/netplan/netplan.yaml](#04_001.xhtml_netplan.yaml)).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">apply</samp>
    Runs <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">netplan generate</samp> and then activates the changed configuration.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">generate</samp>
    Reads the Netplan configuration from the YAML files in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/netplan</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/lib/netplan</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/netplan</samp>, and then generates the corresponding configuration files for the network backends. The new files end up in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/run/NetworkManager</samp> or in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/run/systemd/network</samp>.

    The new configuration isn’t activated! The changed settings only take effect when the respective backend is requested to evaluate the files (or at the next restart).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ip leases</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp>
    Outputs the current DHCP lease data for the relevant interface. This only works if the networkd backend and a DHCP configuration are in use. Otherwise, the command will return misleading error messages.

### netstat [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">netstat</samp> provides information about the network activity on the local computer. If the command is called without options, it returns a list of all open internet connections and sockets.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Also takes into account inactive sockets, that is, services that are waiting for a connection on a network port (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LISTEN</samp> state).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-e</samp>
    Also specifies the user for internet connections.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp>
    Provides numerical addresses and port numbers instead of host and network service names.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>
    Also specifies the process number (PID) and the process name of the program responsible for the connection. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">netstat</samp> requires <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions so that it can provide information about nonnative processes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> / <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> / <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp> / <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-X</samp>
    Limits the output to connections that use the TCP, UDP, Raw, or Unix protocol.

#### Example

The following command lists all active connections (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">established</samp>) or monitored ports (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LISTEN</samp>). The output is heavily abridged due to space limitations.

```
root# netstat -atupe
Active Internet connections (servers and established)
Proto Local Address           Foreign Addr   State    User     PID/Prog name
tcp   *:nfs                   *:*            LISTEN   root     -
tcp   *:ldap                  *:*            LISTEN   root     5842/slapd
tcp   localhost:mysql         *:*            LISTEN   mysql    5785/mysqld
tcp6  [::]:ssh                [::]:*         LISTEN   root     5559/sshd
udp   *:nfs                   *:*                     root     - 
```

### networkctl [command]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">networkctl</samp> is one of the administration commands from the systemd family. If networkd is used as the network backend, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">networkctl</samp> helps to analyze the network status.

Although networkd is installed by default on many distributions, it’s only active on a few of them. One of the exceptions is Ubuntu Server, where networkd serves as a backend for Ubuntu’s own Netplan system (see [netplan](#N_001.xhtml_netplan)). networkd evaluates configuration files from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/systemd/network</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/lib/systemd/network</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/run/systemd/network</samp> directories (see [etc/systemd/network/networkd.network](#04_001.xhtml_networkd.network)).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp>
    Lists all network interfaces. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">SETUP</samp> column of the result shows whether the interface is controlled by networkd (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">configured</samp>) or not (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">unmanaged</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lldp</samp>
    Shows other devices in the network that were discovered via the Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">status [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Provides detailed information about the status of a network interface. If no interface is specified, the command attempts to summarize the entire network status.

#### Examples

The following outputs of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">networkctl</samp> were created on an Ubuntu server in a virtual machine:

```
root# networkctl list
IDX  LINK      TYPE       OPERATIONAL   SETUP
  1  lo        loopback   carrier       unmanaged
  2  ens3      ether      routable      configured
root# networkctl status ens3
      Link File: /lib/systemd/network/99-default.link
   Network File: /run/systemd/network/10-netplan-ens3.network
           Type: ether
          State: routable (configured)
             ...
     HW Address: 52:54:00:0a:8d:fc
        Address: 138.201.20.182
                 fe80::5054:ff:fe0a:8dfc
        Gateway: 138.201.20.176 (Fujitsu Technology Solutions GmbH)
            DNS: 213.133.100.100
                  213.133.98.98
   Search Domains: ubuntu-buch.info 
```

The second listing shows the status summary of another server installation with IPv6 configuration:

```
root# networkctl status
        State: routable
 Online state: online
      Address: 168.119.33.110 on eth0
               172.17.0.1 on docker0
               2a01:4f8:242:1f88::4 on eth0
               fe80::5054:ff:fe4a:7321 on eth0
      Gateway: 168.119.33.119 on eth0
               2a01:4f8:242:1f88::2 on eth0
          DNS: 213.133.100.100
               213.133.99.99
               2a01:4f8:0:1::add:1010
               2a01:4f8:0:1::add:9999 
```

### newaliases

The [etc/aliases](#04_001.xhtml_aliases) file contains an alias list for the email server, which ensures, for example, that all emails addressed to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">postmaster</samp> are forwarded to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>. For changes to this file to be taken into account by the mail server, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newaliases</samp>.

### newgrp [group name]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newgrp</samp> command determines the currently active group of a user who belongs to several groups. The active group determines which group newly created files belong to. The groups available for selection can be determined via [groups](#G_001.xhtml_groups). If no group name is specified, the primary group will be used. This group is also automatically considered an active group after a login.

#### Example

In the following example, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newgroup</samp> command makes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">docuteam</samp> the active group of the user <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kofler</samp>. As a result, the newly created <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newfile</samp> file is assigned to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">docuteam</samp> group and can be edited by other members of the documentation team.

```
user$ groups
kofler docuteam wheel
user$ newgroups docuteam
user$ touch newfile 
```

### newusers file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newusers</samp> reads a text file and creates a new user for each line. The text file basically has the same format as [etc/passwd](#04_001.xhtml_passwd). However, the passwords must be entered unencrypted in the second column. Most of the other parameters (UID, GID, etc.) are optional. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newusers</samp> creates a new account for each specified user, whereby the associated groups are also created if required. For missing parameters, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newusers</samp> selects suitable default values, taking into account the settings in [etc/login/defs](#04_001.xhtml_login.defs).

Note that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newusers</samp> creates new home directories if their location is specified in the sixth column. However, the command doesn’t take care of copying the contents of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/skel</samp> there.

#### Example

The following lines show the minimalist text file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">users.txt</samp>, which corresponds to the requirements of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newusers</samp>. As <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">users.txt</samp> contains passwords in plain text, you must make sure that no one other than <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> can read the file or that you delete the file again after running <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">newusers</samp>.

```
hawks:secret1:::Howard Hawks:/home/hawks:/bin/bash
moore:secret2:::Grace Moore:/home/moore:/bin/bash
smith:secret3:::Peter Smith:/home/smith:/bin/bash 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newusers</samp> now creates the three new users <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hawks</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">moore</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">smith</samp>, as well as primary groups of the same name. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newusers</samp> itself decides on suitable UIDs and GIDs.

```
root# newusers users.txt 
```

### nft command [options]

Most current Linux distributions now use the new nftables firewall system, which replaces its predecessor, Netfilter. However, the old [iptables](#I_001.xhtml_iptables) command is often still used to configure the firewall, which continues to work thanks to a compatibility layer.

However, new or nftables-specific functions can only be controlled using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft</samp> command. The following description provides a rough overview of the most important subcommands and options of this command. You can find a lot more details about the functionality of nftables and the syntax of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft</samp> in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man nft</samp> and the following wiki:

[https://wiki.nftables.org](https://wiki.nftables.org)

Before you call <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft</samp>, you should make sure that a firewall isn’t already running on your distribution. On Fedora, RHEL, and SUSE, for example, Firewalld is active (see [firewall-cmd](#F_001.xhtml_firewall-cmd)). Custom-defined firewall rules then often result in conflicts with the firewall of your distribution.

#### nft Terminology

A separate terminology applies to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft</samp>: Firewall rules are always part of a chain. Tables, in turn, consist of multiple chains. Unlike <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">iptables</samp>, there are neither predefined tables nor predefined chains. Thus, you can compose as many custom tables as you like from chains also defined by yourself.

Tables, chains, and rules apply to different types of network packets, which are assigned to the following families:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ip</samp>
    Rules for IPv4 only.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ip6</samp>
    Rules for IPv6 only.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">inet</samp>
    Rules that apply equally to IPv4 and IPv6.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">arp</samp>
    Level 2 rules, which are analyzed before Level 3 rules.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bridge</samp>
    Switching rules.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">netdev</samp>
    Low-level rules that are analyzed before all other rules and enable, for example, a particularly efficient defense against DDOS attacks.

#### nft Options

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Integrates handles into the output of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft list</samp>. These are numbers that uniquely identify each object within a group (e.g., a rule within a chain). Handles make it possible to delete or replace individual objects or to specify the position where new objects are to be inserted.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fname</samp>
    Reads the commands to be executed from the specified file. Two syntax variants are permitted: the file can either contain ordinary <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nft</samp> commands line by line or a hierarchically structured sequence of tables, chains, and rules. The structure of the file for the second variant corresponds to the output of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft list ruleset</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp>
    Uses the names of network services specified in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/services</samp> instead of port numbers (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ssh</samp> instead of 22).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Shows the version number.

#### nft Commands

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">add chain</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">family tname cname</samp>
