    Creates a new chain named <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cname</samp> in the specified table.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">add rule</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">family tname cname matches statements</samp>
    Adds a new rule to the specified <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cname</samp> chain. Here, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">matches</samp> specifies the packets to which the rule applies. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">statements</samp> describes what should happen to the respective packets.

    Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">add</samp>, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">insert</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">replace</samp> keywords are also permitted to insert a rule at a specific position in the rule list or to replace an existing rule with a new one.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">add table</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">family tname</samp>
    Creates a new table for the specified family.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">delete/flush chain</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">family tname cname</samp>
    Removes the specified chain from the table. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">flush</samp> deletes all rules of the chain, but not the chain itself.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">delete rule</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">family tname cname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">handle</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">came</samp>
    Deletes the rule specified by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">handle</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cname</samp> chain.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">delete/flush table</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">family tname</samp>
    Deletes the specified table. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flush</samp>, all chains and rules in the table are deleted, but the now empty table is retained.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">flush ruleset</samp>
    Deletes all tables, including all chains and rules contained therein. This corresponds to a complete reset of the firewall. The firewall now accepts every packet.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter programmierelement">list tables</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter programmierelement">list table family name</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter programmierelement">list chain</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">family tname cname</samp>
    Lists tables, chains, and rules.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list ruleset</samp>
    Lists all tables, chains, and rules. The output structured by curly brackets fulfills the syntax rules for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft -f</samp> and can therefore be used as the basis for a new rule file. With the additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-j</samp> option, the output is in JSON format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">monitor [filter criteria]</samp>
    Displays nftables events (e.g., as debugging help).

#### Examples

The first two commands show which firewall tables are defined on the test computer (Fedora 32) and which chains and rules apply to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">firewalld</samp> table within the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ip</samp> family. (nftables allows the use of matching table names for different families. For this reason, the family must also be specified in the second <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp> command.)

```
root# nft list tables
table bridge filter
table bridge nat
table inet firewalld
table ip firewalld
table ip6 firewalld
root# nft list table ip firewalld
table ip firewalld {
   chain nat_PREROUTING {
     type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat + 10; policy accept;
     jump nat_PREROUTING_ZONES
   }
   chain nat_PREROUTING_ZONES {
      iifname "enp1s0" goto nat_PRE_FedoraWorkstation
      goto nat_PRE_FedoraWorkstation
   }
   ... 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">systemctl</samp> now deactivates the default Fedora firewall daemon:

```
root# systemctl disable --now firewalld 
```

Now, you can create your own firewall using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft</samp>. It’s not usual to define the rules by repeatedly calling <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft</samp>. It’s much more elegant to formulate the rules in a text file and run this file like a script. To do this, you must enter <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft -f</samp> as a shell interpreter in the line.

```
#!/sbin/nft -f
# delete existing firewall
flush ruleset
# new table for IPv4 and IPv6
table inet myfilter {
   chain input {
      type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop;
      # block faulty packets
      ct state invalid drop
      # always accept packets from self-generated connections
      ct state {established, related} accept
      # accept internal network traffic
      iif lo accept
      # Block packets to loopback but from external addresses
      iif != lo ip daddr 127.0.0.1/8 drop
      iif != lo ip6 daddr ::1/128 drop
      # accept ICMP packets
      ip protocol icmp accept
      ip6 nexthdr icmpv6 accept
      # accept SSH connection from outside
      tcp dport 22 accept
      # for server configuration: more rules for
      # HTTP + HTTPS (Port 80 + 443), Samba etc.
      # ...
    }
    # no forwarding
    chain forward {
       type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
    }
} 
```

Now you can run the script:

```
root# chmod +x myfirewall
root# ./myfirewall 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nft -f</samp> first performs a syntax check. If it detects errors, it aborts the process with an error message. In this case, the previous firewall is retained.

The preceding script has been slightly modified from the Gentoo wiki. You can find more examples there and in the ArchLinux Wiki:

[https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Nftables/Examples](https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/Nftables/Examples)

[https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Nftables](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Nftables)

### ngrep [options] [grep-search-expression] [pcap-filter-expression]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ngrep</samp> is referred to as a packet sniffer. The command reads the network traffic of a port and filters it. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ngrep</samp> provides similar functions to the [tcpdump](#T_001.xhtml_tcpdump) command and, like this, uses the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pcap</samp> library to read the network packets. Unlike <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">tcpdump</samp>, however, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ngrep</samp> also takes the contents of the packages into account. Naturally, this only works for nonencrypted protocols, such as HTTP or FTP.

The search expression must be formulated as a regular pattern as in [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep). The syntax summarized in [tcpdump](#T_001.xhtml_tcpdump) applies to the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pcap</samp> filter expression.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">interface</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">|any</samp>
    Determines the network interface.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp>
    Ignores uppercase and lowercase in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grep</samp> search expression.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Inverts the search. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ngrep</samp> therefore only returns the packets in which the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grep</samp> search pattern was not recognized.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp>
    Interprets the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grep</samp> search expression as a word.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-W byline</samp>
    Takes line breaks into account during output, resulting in more legible output.

#### Example

The following example listens on all interfaces for HTTP packets containing the keywords <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">user</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pass</samp>, and so on:

```
root# ngrep -d any -i 'user|pass|pwd|mail|login' port 80
interface: any
filter: (ip or ip6) and ( port 80 )
match: user|pass|pwd|mail|login
T 10.0.0.87:58480 -> 91.229.57.14:80 [AP] POST /index.php
  HTTP/1.1..Host: ... user=name&pass=geheim&login=Login
... 
```

### nice [options] program

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp> starts the specified program with a reduced or increased priority. The command can be used to start non-time-critical programs with low priority so as not to affect the rest of the system too much.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n +/-</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp> value. By default (i.e., without <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp>), programs are started with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp> value of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>. A value of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-20</samp> means highest priority, and a value of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+19</samp> means lowest priority. Values less than <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> may only be specified by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>; that is, most users can only start programs with reduced priority with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp>. If this option is omitted, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp> starts the program with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp> value of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+10</samp>.

Note that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nice</samp> only controls the CPU load. If you want to reduce the I/O load of a command, it’s better to use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ionice</samp>.

#### Example

The following command starts the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mybackup.sh</samp> script with lower priority:

```
user$ nice -n 10 mybackup.sh 
```

### nl [options] file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nl</samp> numbers all nonempty lines of the specified text file and writes the result to the standard output. By setting the numerous options, you can have page-by-page numbering, the numbering of headers and footers, and more.

### nmap [options] hostname/ip-address/ip-address-range

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> command (network mapper) from the package of the same name performs a port scan and attempts to determine which network services are active on the specified computer or in the specified network. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> should only be used to analyze your own computers or after consultation with the respective administrator. A port scan of other computers can be interpreted as an attempted attack!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-A</samp>
    Performs an extensive (“aggressive”) scan, corresponding to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">–sV -O -sC --traceroute</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-F</samp>
    Considers only the 100 most important ports from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/share/nmap/nmap-services</samp> (quick scan).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-iL</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Scans the IP addresses specified in the file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-oN</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/ -oG</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/ -oX</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file.xml</samp>
    Writes the results to an ordinary text file, to a text file that can be easily processed with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grep</samp>, or to an XML file. Without the option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> uses the standard output and the ordinary text format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-O</samp>
    Attempts to recognize the operating system; this option must be combined with a scan option, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-sS</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-sT</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-sF</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p1-10,22,80</samp>
    Takes only the specified ports into account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Pn</samp>
    Doesn’t perform a ping test. This means that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> considers all hosts to be online and performs a scan in any case (slowly!).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-sL</samp>
    Lists all ports and specifies host names assigned in the past. This is particularly fast, but provides outdated data even from devices that are currently no longer online.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-sP</samp>
    Performs only a ping test (fast).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-sS</samp>
    Performs a TCP SYN scan (applies by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-sU</samp>
    Takes UDP into account as well. This option can be used together with another <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-sV</samp>
    Tries to find out which service is provided on open ports (service version detection) or which program is responsible for the service and in which version.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T0</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T5</samp>
    Selects a timing schema:

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-T5</samp> is the fastest.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-T3</samp> is the default.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-T0</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-T1</samp> are extremely slow, but minimize the risk of the scan being detected.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-v</samp>
    Outputs detailed information (verbose).

You must choose an <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s option</samp> when calling. Only <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-sU</samp> may be combined with other <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s</samp> options. In general, the right choice of options is a trade-off between thoroughness and speed.

In many cases, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nmap -v -A name</samp> is sufficient to get an initial overview of the network services of the specified computer. Advanced <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> users can find more details on the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page and on the following websites:

[https://insecure.org/nmap](https://insecure.org/nmap)

[https://nmap.org/book](https://nmap.org/book)

Graphical user interfaces also exist for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp>, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nmap-frontend</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zenmap</samp>.

#### Examples

The following command performs a quick network scan on the local network (256 IP addresses). Thanks to the focus on the most important 100 ports, the job is done within about two seconds. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> outputs have been shortened for reasons of space and only show the results of two of the devices found:

```
root# nmap -F  -T4 10.0.0.0/24
Nmap scan report for imac (10.0.0.2)
  Host is up (0.00019s latency).
  PORT    STATE SERVICE
  22/tcp  open  ssh
  88/tcp  open  kerberos-sec
  445/tcp open  microsoft-ds
  548/tcp open  afp
  MAC Address: AC:87:A3:1E:4A:87 (Apple)
Nmap scan report for raspberrypi (10.0.0.22)
  Host is up (0.00038s latency).
  Not shown: 99 closed ports
  PORT   STATE SERVICE
  22/tcp open  ssh
  MAC Address: B8:27:EB:11:44:2E (Raspberry Pi Foundation)
...
Nmap done: 256 IP addresses (6 hosts up) scanned in 2.42 seconds 
```

The second example shows the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmap</samp> result for a NAS device that is located in a different local network (again, it has been heavily shortened):

```
root# nmap -v -A 192.168.178.28
Nmap scan report for DiskStation.fritz.box (192.168.178.28)
Host is up (0.0023s latency).
...
Discovered open port 445/tcp on 192.168.178.28
Discovered open port 139/tcp on 192.168.178.28
Discovered open port 80/tcp on 192.168.178.28
Discovered open port 443/tcp on 192.168.178.28
Discovered open port 22/tcp on 192.168.178.28
```

### nmblookup [options] workgroupname

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmblookup</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">samba-common-bin</samp> (Debian/Ubuntu) or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">samba-client</samp> (Fedora/RHEL) package determines which devices or servers in the local network provide SMB shares. Previously, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">smbtree</samp> could be used for this, but this command requires the browsing functions of SMB1 and is obsolete in modern networks.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp>
    Performs a status query for each server found and then displays the detailed results.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-T</samp>
    Provides an ordered list of server names and IP addresses. In my experience, the results of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmblookup</samp> are more reliable if you run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmblookup -S</samp> first or repeat the command again after a few seconds. The first result is often incomplete.

#### Example

There are two SMB servers, a NAS device, and an appropriately configured Raspberry Pi in the local network:

```
user$ nmblookup -T WORKGROUP
DiskStation.fritz.box, 192.168.178.43  WORKGROUP<00>
pi5.fritz.box,         192.168.178.123 WORKGROUP<00> 
```

### nmcli [options] con|dev|nm command

Network Manager is usually controlled via a menu in the Gnome or KDE panel. You can also use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nmcli</samp> command to control network connections via the command line or a script.

The commands available for selection depend on which object they refer to. Options <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>, and so on can be used to control the form of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nmcli</samp> output—depending on whether the output is to be formatted properly or processed further by a script (for details, see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man nmcli</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">con down</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">con down uuid</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Deactivates the specified connection.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">con show</samp>
    Lists all configured connections, specifying the name and UUID of each connection.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">con up</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">con up uuid</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Activates the specified connection.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev disconnect</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Terminates the connection for the specified interface.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev</samp>
    Lists all network interfaces known to Network Manager and specifies their properties.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev show</samp>
    Displays detailed information on all network interfaces.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev wifi hotspot</samp>
    Configures the Wi-Fi adapter as a router.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dev wifi list</samp>
    Provides a list of all Wi-Fi networks within range, including the signal strength. The command requires the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wpa_supplicant</samp> service to be running.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">general [status]</samp>
    Displays the status of Network Manager.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">networking [on|off]</samp>
    Indicates whether there’s a network connection or not. All network connections can be interrupted or restored by selecting <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">off</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">on</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">radio [wifi|wwan|wimax|all] [on|off]</samp>
    Displays the status of the wireless networks or changes their status. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wifi</samp> refers to Wi-Fi connections, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wwan</samp> to mobile connections, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wimax</samp> to WiMAX technology.

#### Examples

The first command lists all connections known to Network Manager. The following two commands deactivate and reactivate the connection named Wired connection 1:

```
root# nmcli con show
NAME                         UUID          TYP             DEVICE
Wired connection 1           effd094d-...  802-3-ethernet  enp0s3
virbr0                       207d9f4f-...  bridge          virbr0
root# nmcli con down   id 'Wired connection 1'
root# nmcli con up     id 'Wired connection 1' 
```

The second example filters out the IP addresses of the name server from the detailed interface information. This is particularly useful on Ubuntu, where these addresses aren’t listed in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/resolv.conf</samp>. Rather, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">resolv.conf</samp> references a local name server in this distribution, that is, the address 127.0.0.1.

```
root# nmcli dev show | grep DNS
IP4.DNS[1]:  10.0.0.138
IP4.DNS[2]:  4.4.8.8 
```

The third command sets up a hotspot on a Raspberry Pi connected to the LAN via ethernet cable:

```
root# device wifi hotspot ssid 'wlan-name' password 'wlan-pw' 
```

### nohup command

If you start a command as a background process in a shell window and then close the window, or if you start the command in a text console and then log out, the background process is automatically terminated. As a rule, this is reasonable behavior.

However, sometimes you want to start a process that continues to run after you log out—and that’s exactly what <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nohup</samp> is there for. The command must be specified with its full path. It can’t write text outputs to the standard output. If necessary, such outputs are redirected to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nohup.out</samp> file in the local directory.

#### Example

In the following example, an administrator logs in to a server via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ssh</samp>, starts a backup script in the background, and then logs out again. The backup script continues to run.

```
someone@localhost$ ssh user@remotehost
user@remotehost$ nohup backup-script &
user@remotehost$ exit 
```

### nproc

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nproc</samp> indicates how many CPU cores are available. For CPUs with hyperthreading, the virtual cores are also included in the calculation. The [lscpu](#L_001.xhtml_lscpu) command and the contents of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/cpuinfo</samp> file provide more detailed information about the CPU.

### nvidia-xconfig [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nvidia-xconfig</samp> helps to configure the proprietary NVIDIA graphics driver. The command is only available if this driver is installed.

If the command is executed without parameters, it creates or changes the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/X11/xorg.conf</samp> file so that the NVIDIA graphics driver will be used in the future. If the graphics system is working after restarting the computer, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">nvidia-settings</samp> graphical user interface can be used for further configuration.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c file</samp>
    Uses the specified file instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/X11/xorg.conf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--mode=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">W</samp>x<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">H</samp>
    Adds a graphics mode for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">W</samp>×<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">H</samp> pixels to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xorg.conf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--query-gpu-infos</samp>
    Displays details of all available graphics cards and connected monitors.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp>
    Reads <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xorg.conf</samp> and displays the settings it contains in a clear tree view.

## O

### openssl command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> from the package of the same name helps with the creation and further administration of certificates as well as private and public keys. The command uses the OpenSSL library. New certificates or keys are written to the standard output if you don’t specify a target file via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-out</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dhparam [options] [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Generates or manipulates parameter files for the Diffie-Hellman method. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> parameter specifies the key size in bits. In the simplest case, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl dhparam -out keyfile 512</samp> generates a Diffie-Hellman key with a length of 512 bits.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enc [options]</samp>
    Reads data from the standard input, encodes or decodes it symmetrically (option <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp>), and writes the result to the standard output. You need to specify the algorithm to be used and the key with options, for example, in the format <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-aes-256-cbc -pass file:mykeyfile</samp>. Note that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl enc</samp> is only suitable for relatively small amounts of data. To encrypt large files, it’s better to use the [gpg](#G_001.xhtml_gpg) command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">genpkey [options]</samp>
    Generates a private key. To write a 2,048-bit RSA key to a file, the following options are required:

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 –out server.key</samp>

    If the key itself is to be encrypted, you must specify the name of the encryption algorithm with an additional option, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-aes256</samp>. During the execution of the command, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> asks for an encryption password twice.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-standard-commands | list-message-digest-commands |</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-cipher-commands | list-cipher-algorithms |</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-message-digest-algorithms | list-public-key-algorithms</samp>
    Lists the commands, algorithms, and so on that are supported by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rand [options]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Writes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> bytes of pseudo-random data to the standard output. Note that the output is binary data, not ASCII text! The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-base64</samp> option causes <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> to perform Base64 encoding in ASCII format. This increases the length of the resulting character string by around a third.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">req [options]</samp>
    Generates a request to sign a certificate (i.e., a certificate signing request [CSR] file). With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-new</samp>, you can specify that a new certificate must be set up. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-key</samp> specifies the key file to be used. Without this option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> generates a new RSA key for this purpose, which you can save in a separate file using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-keyout</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">openssl req -new -sha256 -key server.key -out server.csr</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> then interactively asks for the key data of the certificate, that is, the country code, location, your name, host name (common name), and more. With the additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-x509 -days</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> options, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> generates a self-signed certificate with a validity of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> days instead of a certificate request.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rsa [options]</samp>
    Processes RSA keys and converts them between different forms and formats. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-in file</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-out file</samp> specify the file from which the original key is read and where the new key is written. If you don’t specify any further options, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> removes the encryption (pass phrase) of the key. The form of the key can be specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-inform</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-outform</samp> (by default, it’s <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PEM</samp>, alternatively <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">DER</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">NET</samp>). With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-in file -text</samp>, you can determine the properties of an existing key, such as the key length (the number of bits).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sclient [options]</samp>

    Acts as an SSL/TLS client to test connections to an encrypted server. You can find an application example at the following address:

    [https://www.misterpki.com/openssl-s-client/](https://www.misterpki.com/openssl-s-client/)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">speed</samp>
    Performs multiple benchmark tests, each of which lasts three seconds. The result shows how many bytes were processed for the respective algorithm (the more there are, the faster it runs or the better optimized the hardware on which the test is performed).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x509 [options]</samp>
    Displays certificate data, signs certificates, and converts certificates between different forms. Again, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-in</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-out</samp> specify the file names of the source and target certificates. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-req</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> expects a certificate request as input, not the certificate itself. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-CA</samp> specifies which CA certificate is to be used for the signature. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-CAkey</samp> specifies the corresponding private key.

There are separate <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> pages available for most <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp> commands. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man req</samp> describes the countless options of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl req</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man rsa</samp> describes the options of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl rsa</samp>, and so on.

#### Examples

If you want to have a certificate signed for your web server by an official certification authority (e.g., Thawte), you should first generate a key (if you don’t already have one) and then a certificate signing request. The key isn’t encrypted here because otherwise the web server would have to ask for the encryption password every time it’s started.

```
root# genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 -out server.key
root# chmod 400 server.key
root# openssl req -new -key server.key -out server.csr
...
Common Name (eg server FQDN or YOUR name) []: company-abc.com 
```

You can take a look at the CSR file to check this:

```
root# openssl req -in server.csr -noout -text 
```

Then, you need to send the CSR file to the certification authority. You will then receive the signed certificate from there for a fee. The usual file identifier is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.pem</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.crt</samp>. You must enter this file, your own key, and a CA certificate from the certification authority in the Apache configuration.

```
# Apache configuration file
SSLCertificateFile      /etc/apache2/server.pem
SSLCertificateKeyFile   /etc/apache2/server.key
SSLCertificateChainFile /etc/apache2/sub.class1.server.ca.pem
SSLCACertificateFile    /etc/apache2/ca.pem 
```

If you don't want to pay for an official signature, you can sign your certificate yourself:

```
root# openssl x509 -req -days 1900 -in server.csr  \
         -signkey server.key -sha256 -out server.pem
Signature ok
subject=/C=DE/L=Boston/O=John Doe/CN=www.company-abc.com/
  emailAddress=webmaster@company-abc.com
Getting Private key 
```

To take a look at the certificate file, you can run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl x509 -text</samp>:

```
root# openssl x509 -text -in server.pem
Certificate:
    Data:
        Version: 1 (0x0)
        Serial Number: 12669601459972319941 (0xafd37766c36baac5)
    Signature Algorithm: sha256WithRSAEncryption
        Issuer: C=DE, L=Boston, O=John Doe,
                CN=www.company-abc.com/emailAddress=webmaster@company-abc.com
        Validity
            Not Before: Sep 28 14:48:03 2025 GMT
            Not After : Dec 10 14:48:03 2029 GMT     ... 
```

The generation of a key, a certificate request, and self-signing can also be carried out in a single command: The following command generates a self-signed certificate for a mail server that is valid for 10 years. It’s important that you enter the host name of your server as the common name when running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">openssl</samp>. Because the certificate itself is signed, your mail client will indicate during configuration that the certificate isn’t trustworthy.

```
root# openssl req -new -x509 -days 3650 -nodes \
        -out    /etc/ssl/certs/postfix.pem \
        -keyout /etc/ssl/private/postfix.key
...
Common Name (eg server FQDN or YOUR name) []: company-abc.com
root# chmod 400 /etc/ssl/private/postfix.key 
```

## P

### pacman [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pacman</samp> stands for package manager and is the package management command for Arch Linux and compatible distributions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Q</samp>
    Provides a list of all installed packages (query).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Qi</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Displays a description of the package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Ql</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Lists the files of the package.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Qo</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">filename</samp>
    Indicates to which package the specified file belongs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp>
    Removes the specified package (remove). If you use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Rs</samp> variant instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp>, dependent packages that are no longer required will also be uninstalled.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">package name</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reponame/package name</samp>
    Installs or updates the specified package, whereby in the second variant only the specified repository is taken into account. If the package has already been installed, the installation will be repeated and the package will be updated if necessary. The additional <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--needed</samp> option prevents unnecessary work and only carries out the installation if the package isn’t yet installed or is installed in an old version. The ubiquitous <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> option stands for sync, by the way.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Sy</samp>
    Reloads the package sources.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Su</samp>
    Displays all installed packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Syu</samp>
    First updates the package sources and then all installed packages, that is, performs a system update.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-Ss</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pattern</samp>
    Searches the names and short descriptions of all packages, including those not installed, for the specified search pattern.

#### Examples

The following commands first perform a complete update of all package sources and installed packages and then install the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">emacs</samp> editor, including all required libraries. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--needed</samp> prevents already installed packages from being installed again.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pacman -Qo</samp> determines which package provides the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/resolv.conf</samp> file. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pacman -Qi</samp> then provides more detailed information about this package.

```
root# pacman -Syu
root# pacman -S --needed emacs
root# pacman -Qo /etc/resolv.conf
/etc/resolv.conf is owned by filesystem 2025.01.19-1
root# pacman -Qi filesystem
  Name            : filesystem
  Description     : Base Arch Linux files
  Install Reason  : Installed as a dependency for another package
  ... 
```

#### Alternatives

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pacman</samp> only works with “ordinary” packages. However, Arch User Repository (AUR) packages are also very often used in Arch Linux. AUR is a collection of build scripts on GitHub. Because the manual installation of this type of packages is tedious, AUR helpers take over this task, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aura</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">aurman</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pacaur</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yay</samp>. These commands integrate the functions of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pacman</samp> and treat AUR packages like ordinary packages. Thus, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yay -S</samp> name installs the specified package, regardless of whether it’s an ordinary package or an AUR package.

### pactl command [parameter]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pactl</samp> controls the PulseAudio system. This network-enabled sound server is installed by default on most Linux distributions and usually uses ALSA as its basis. PulseAudio makes it possible for several programs to use the audio system in parallel without any problem. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pactl</samp> includes approximately 30 commands, of which only the most important are presented here:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info|stat</samp>
    Displays the key data or the memory consumption of the PulseAudio system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list [short] [modules|sinks|sources|clients|cards|...]</samp>
    Provides a detailed description of all modules, audio sources and outputs, streams, and so on that are managed by PulseAudio. The additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">short</samp> keyword reduces the output to one line per element. The specification of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">modules</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sinks</samp>, etc., causes <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pactl</samp> to list only the relevant elements.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set-default-sink</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Defines the default audio output. Instead of the number <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> of the audio system (see <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/asound/cards</samp>), you can also enter its name. You can determine the permitted names using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pactl list short cards</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set-sink-mute</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0|1|toggle</samp>
    Deactivates, activates, or changes the mute function for audio output <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set-sink-volume</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n vol</samp>
    Sets the volume for audio output <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>. The volume can be specified as an integer, a percentage, or as a decibel value (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">10%</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">20dB</samp>).

#### Example

The following two commands result in the first audio device being used as the standard output device at a volume of 20%:

```
user$ pactl set-default-sink 0
user$ pactl set-sink-volume 0 20% 
```

### pandoc [options] in1 [in2 in3 ...] [> out]

The primary task of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pandoc</samp> from the package of the same name is to convert Markdown text files into other formats, such as HTML files, PDF documents, or Microsoft Office files. With some limitations, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pandoc</samp> can also process other input formats instead of Markdown files, including HTML and LaTeX.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c cssfile</samp>
    Embeds the specified CSS file in the HTML document. The option can be specified multiple times if several CSS files are required.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f format</samp>
    Specifies the source format (from). Important source formats are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">asciidoc</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">docbook</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">latex</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">markdown</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pandoc</samp> attempts to recognize the desired source and target formats itself based on the file ID of the input and output files. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> options are only required if that isn’t successful.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-H header file</samp>
    Inserts the specified header file at the start of the HTML or LaTeX source text. The option can be specified multiple times if multiple header files are required.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o output.identifier</samp>
    Writes the result to the specified file instead of to standard output. This option is mandatory for binary output formats (DOCX, ODT, PDF).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp>
    Creates an independent document (standalone). This option is particularly relevant for HTML, LaTeX, and RTF output formats. Without this option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pandoc</samp> creates files without any header information; such files can’t be used on their own, but must be embedded in another document.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t format</samp>
    Specifies the target format (to). Important target formats are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">docx</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">latex</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">html</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">html5</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">man</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">odt</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rtf</samp>. Note that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pdf</samp> isn’t included in the list of supported formats. To create PDF documents, you must specify the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o out.pdf</samp> option. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pandoc</samp> first converts the source text into LaTeX format and then creates the PDF file using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pdflatex</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--toc</samp>
    Embeds a table of contents in the resulting document.

#### Examples

The first command creates an independent HTML document from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">input.text</samp> Markdown file. The second command creates an EPUB file from a book whose chapters are saved in separate files. The third command creates a PDF file, using LaTeX in the background.

```
user$ pandoc -s -c my.css input.text > output.html
user$ pandoc chap1.text chap2.text chap3.text -t epub3 -o book.epub
user$ pandoc preface.text chap01.text chap02.text -o out.pdf 
```

### paplay [options] [file]
parecord [options] [file]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">paplay</samp> plays the specified audio file via the PulseAudio system. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parecord</samp> makes a recording and saves the audio stream as a file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">id</samp>
    Indicates the output device (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">paplay</samp>) or the audio source (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parecord</samp>). Without this option, the respective default device is used.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--file-format=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the desired audio format, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">raw</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wav</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list-file-formats</samp>
    Lists all supported audio formats.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--volume=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Indicates the desired playback volume. The value range is from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">65535</samp> for maximum volume.

#### Example

The following command plays one of the audio files that were provided with LibreOffice:

```
user$ paplay /usr/lib/libreoffice/share/gallery/sounds/train.wav 
```

### paps [options] text files > out.ps

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">paps</samp> converts the specified UTF-8 text files into PostScript format and writes the result to the standard output. The UTF-8 characters aren’t displayed as letters, but as lines. For this reason, the display of the PostScript file in a PostScript viewer (Evince, Okular, etc.) may look pixelated. It’s not possible to select a text. However, the print quality is good.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--columns=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Defines the number of text columns (by default, it’s one).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--cpi=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Controls the number of characters per inch and thus the font size.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--font=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the desired character set (the default setting is monospace 12).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--landscape</samp>
    Formats the text in landscape format.

#### Example

The following command produces the two-column PostScript file <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">text.ps</samp>:

```
user$ paps --landscape --columns 2 text.txt > print.ps 
```

### parallel [options] ['command']

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp> from the package of the same name helps to run multiple commands in parallel, possibly even on different computers. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp> supports some of the same options as [xargs](#X_001.xhtml_xargs).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-eta</samp>
    Provides information on the status of parallel processing and the time at which <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp> will probably be finished, that is, the estimated time of arrival. This time estimate assumes that each job takes approximately the same amount of time.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Runs a maximum of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> instances in parallel.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j +</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j -</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    The same as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-j</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>, but the specification is relative to the number of CPUs/cores. On a CPU with eight cores, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-j +0</samp> results in a maximum of eight instances of the command that are run in parallel. Accordingly, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-j -1</samp> limits the number of parallel calls to seven.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-S</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">host1,host2,host3</samp>
    Distributes the jobs to the hosts: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">host1</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">host2</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">host3</samp>, and so on. If the host list ends with a comma, this means that the local computer will also be used.

    <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-S</samp> assumes that communication with the hosts via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ssh</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">scp</samp> is possible without a password; you must therefore set up the corresponding key files beforehand using [ssh-copy-id](#S_001.xhtml_ssh-copy-id). In addition, the command to be executed must of course be available on all hosts. Finally, the command should be installed in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp> on all hosts. It’s required to determine the number of CPUs (cores).

    <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-S</samp> is usually combined with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--transfer</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--return {.}.result</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--cleanup</samp> options to copy the local file to the external host, transfer back the new file with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.result</samp> identifier, and finally delete the temporary data on the host. A short notation for these three options is <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-trc {.}.result</samp>.

    In theory, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-S</samp> promises a simple distribution of jobs across multiple hosts that can be accessed via SSH. In my tests, however, the option proved to be extremely error-prone. If you want to parallelize tasks via SSH and, for example, run a command on dozens of hosts or cloud instances, you can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pssh</samp> (parallel SSH) or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">clusterssh</samp> commands instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp>, although these aren’t covered in this book.

#### Examples

A simple application of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp> is to compress, decompress, or otherwise process a number of files. Instead of compressing multiple files one after the other using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gunzip *.gz</samp>, you can start a separate instance of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gunzip</samp> for each file in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp>. On a computer with several CPUs/cores, this will be significantly faster than the serial processing of the files.

```
user$ ls *.gz | parallel gunzip 
```

In the second example, a number of PNG images are supposed to be converted to EPS format using [convert](#C_001.xhtml_convert). However, it’s not sufficient to simply transfer the file names. Instead, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">convert</samp> expects the original file name and the name minus the identifier <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.png</samp>, but plus the new identifier <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.eps</samp>. For this purpose, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parallel</samp> replaces <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{}</samp> in the command string with the file name, and it replaces <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{.}</samp> with the name without the identifier.

```
user$ ls *.png | parallel -eta -j +0 \
        'convert -density 90 -flatten -background white {} {.}.eps' 
```

### parted [options] [device [command [options]]]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> supports the partitioning of hard disks and SSDs. In contrast to the outdated <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fdisk</samp> command, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> also uses GUID Partition Tables (GPTs).

If you don’t pass a command to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp>, you can use the program interactively and enter multiple commands in sequence. The commands can be abbreviated as long as the input is unique (i.e., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">q</samp> instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">quit</samp>).

You should note, however, that unlike with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">fdisk</samp>, the commands are executed immediately and can’t be undone! Instead of the less convenient <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> program, you can also use its graphical user interface called <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gparted</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--align</samp>
    Specifies how new partitions are to be aligned. Permissible settings are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">none</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cylinder</samp> (alignment to cylinder limits), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">minimal</samp> (alignment to block limits), or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">optimal</samp> (alignment to multiples of 1 MiB). You should always use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-a optimal</samp> option to use the data medium at maximum speed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list</samp>
    Lists all partitions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--script</samp>
    Runs all commands passed as parameters without queries.

The most important <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> commands are briefly described here:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">align-check min/opt</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nr</samp>
    Checks whether the specified partition starts at an optimal position. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parted align-check min</samp> only tests whether the partition starts at a physical block boundary. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parted align-check opt</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> attempts to calculate the optimal start position of partitions from the key data of the data medium. If this isn’t possible, multiples of 1 MiB are considered optimal.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mklabel msdos/gpt</samp>
    Sets up a new partition table in MBR or GPT format. Caution: the entire contents of the hard disk will be lost! <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> also supports various other partition formats, but these are rarely important in the Linux environment (see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man parted</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mkpart primary/logical/extended/</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file system</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">start end</samp>
    Creates a new partition. Note that you must specify the start and end positions, not the start position and size! The end position can also be specified as a negative number and is then calculated from the end of the data medium.

    Specifying the partition type (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">primary</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">logical</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">extended</samp>) is only useful for data media with MBR partition tables. If there is a GPT on the data medium, you should give the partition a name with the first <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mkpart</samp> parameter.

    The optional specification of the file system is only used to define the partition type. However, no file system is set up on the new partition. Permitted types are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fat16</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fat32</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ext2</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">HFS</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">linux-swap</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">NTFS</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ufs</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">print</samp>
    Lists all partitions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">quit</samp>
    Terminates <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">resize</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nr start end</samp>
    Changes the size of the specified partition. Unfortunately, the command can only be used for the extended partition of an MBR disk. To change the size of other partitions, you must delete them and then set them up again with the exact same starting point. This is of course an error-prone operation, which also requires that there is free space behind the partition.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rm</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nr</samp>
    Deletes the specified partition.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nr flag</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">on/off</samp>
    Changes the flags (additional attributes) of the partition. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> can use the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">boot</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">swap</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hidden</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">raid</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lvm</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lba</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bios_grub</samp> flags, among others.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">unit</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bios grub</samp>
    Defines the unit for position and size specifications. The following options are available:

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">s</samp> (sectors)

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">B</samp> (bytes)

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kB</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">MB</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GB</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">TB</samp> (10³, 10⁶, 10⁹, and 10^(12) bytes)

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">KiB</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">MiB</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GiB</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">TiB</samp> (2^(10), 2^(20), 2^(30), and 2^(40) bytes)

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">%</samp> (percentage, relative to the total size of the data medium)

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">compact</samp> (decimal megabytes for input, reader-friendly output)

    The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">compact</samp> setting applies by default. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> was started with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--align</samp> option, the position and size specifications are adjusted accordingly when new partitions are created.

#### Examples

The following lines show how you can set up a new LVM partition on an SSD with GPT using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp>:

```
root# parted -a optimal /dev/sda
(parted) print
Model: ATA SAMSUNG SSD 830 (scsi)
Hard disk  /dev/sda:  512GB
Sector size (logical/physical): 512B/512B
Partition table: gpt
Number  Start  End     Size    Filesys  Name                Flags
 1     17.4kB  1000MB  1000MB  fat32    EFI System Part...  boot, hidden
 2     1000MB  21.0GB  20.0GB  ext4                         hidden
 3     21.0GB  21.1GB  134MB            Microsoft reser...  hidden, msftres
 4     21.1GB  61.2GB  40.1GB  ntfs     Basic data part...  hidden
 5     61.2GB  82.2GB  21.0GB  ext4                         hidden
 6     82.2GB  103GB   21.0GB  ext4                         boot, hidden
 7     103GB   124GB   21.0GB  ext4                         boot
 8     124GB   281GB   157GB   ext4
 9     281GB   386GB   105GB                                lvm
10     386GB   407GB   21.0GB  ext4
(parted) mkpart lvm-partition 407GB 450GB
(parted) set 11 lvm on
(parted) print
...
11     407GB   450GB   42.7GB           lvm-partition       lvm
(parted) quit 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> can also process commands directly without manual interaction. The following commands assume that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdb</samp> is the device of a USB flash drive or SD card. The first <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> command creates a new MBR partition table there and deletes all existing data. The second command creates a primary partition, leaving 1 MiB free at the beginning and end of the disk. [mkfs.vfat](#M_001.xhtml_mkfs.vfat) sets up a VFAT file system in this partition.

```
root# parted /dev/sdb mklabel msdos
  Warning: The existing partition table and all data
  on /dev/sdb will be deleted. Do you want to continue?
  Yes/No? yes
root# parted /dev/sdb 'mkpart primary fat32 1mib -1mib'
root# mkfs.vfat -F 32 -n FOTOS /dev/sdb1 
```

The last example shows the use of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">parted</samp> in script mode. The command sets up a GPT on the specified data medium. Caution: all previously saved data will be lost!

```
root# mkpart /dev/sdb -s mklabel gpt 
```

### partprobe [options] [devices]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partprobe</samp> is usually run without any options or other parameters after changing the partitioning of local hard disks or SSDs, for example, after [fdisk](#F_001.xhtml_fdisk) has been completed. The command then informs the kernel about the changes made so that the new or modified partitions can be used without restarting the computer.

### partx [options] [partition] [disk]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partx</samp> is a low-level command that determines information about the partitioning of data media or passes it on to the kernel. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partx</samp> is equally suitable for the MBR partition tables and GPTs.

The partition to be edited is usually specified directly by a device file. Alternatively, you can specify the data medium using its device file and the partition number via the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> option, for example, with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partx -n 3 /dev/sda</samp>. If an individual partition itself contains subpartitions and is therefore to be treated as an independent data medium, you want to precede the partition device with a hyphen, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partx - /dev/sda4</samp>.

Unlike [fdisk](#F_001.xhtml_fdisk) and [parted](#P_001.xhtml_parted), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partx</samp> doesn’t change the data medium, so it’s not suitable for setting up or deleting physical partitions! The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> options only change the partition table of the Linux kernel, but leave the disk unchanged. The sole purpose of these options is to inform the kernel about a partitioning changed by another program. This is usually easier with the [partprobe](#P_001.xhtml_partprobe) command. In practice, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partx</samp> is often used for processing virtual data media, for example, for loop devices or image files of virtual machines.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Adds new partitions. The partition must already physically exist on the data medium. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp> only updates the partition table of the kernel!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Processes size specifications in bytes.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Deletes partitions from the kernel’s partition table.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n M:N</samp>
    Specifies numerically the partitions of the data medium to be processed. Different kinds of notation are possible here, as the following examples illustrate:

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n 4</samp> denotes the fourth partition.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n -2</samp> denotes the penultimate partition.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n 3:6</samp> refers to partitions 3 to 6.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n 3:</samp> refers to all partitions, starting with partition 3.

    *   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n :5</samp> includes partitions 1 to 5.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o columns</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--output columns</samp>
    Displays selected information about the selected disk or partition. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">columns</samp> can contain the following keywords, among others: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">NR</samp> (partition number), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">START</samp> (start sector), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">END</samp> (end sector), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">SIZE</samp> (size in bytes), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">TYPE</samp> (partition type as hex code or UUID), and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FLAGS</samp> (additional information). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">partx -o NR,START,END</samp> thus provides a list of partitions with their start and end sectors. The sector size is generally 512 bytes, regardless of the actual sector size of the data medium.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--show</samp>
    Displays information on the selected data medium or partition. The data displayed with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o</samp> is determined from the physical disk and may not match the partition table of the Linux kernel.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>
    Changes the size or other data of a partition in the kernel’s partition table. The changes must first be made physically on the data medium.

#### Example

The following command provides detailed information on a hard disk with an MBR partition table:

```
root# partx -o NR,TYPE,FLAGS,START,END,SECTORS,SIZE /dev/sda
NR TYPE FLAGS  START      END  SECTORS  SIZE
 1 0x83 0x80    2048   411647   409600  200M
 2 0x8e 0x0   411648 31457279 31045632 14,8G 
```

### passwd [options] [username]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">passwd</samp> without parameters allows you to change the password of the current user. To do this, you must first enter the old password and then the new password twice in succession. The new password is entered encrypted in the [etc/shadow](#04_001.xhtml_shadow) file. However, in some distributions, the new password must comply with certain security rules to be accepted.

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> can also change the password of other users via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">passwd name</samp>. The old password doesn’t need to be entered; that is, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp> can change the password even if the user has forgotten their password. The preceding password restrictions don’t apply to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp>, so it can also define a password consisting of just a single character. However, not even <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp> is permitted to enter no password at all (i.e., simply pressing Enter).

By specifying options, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">passwd</samp> can also lock individual accounts, reactivate them, and set expiry times for the account or its password (see also the description of the [chage](#C_001.xhtml_chage) command, which offers even more setting options in this respect).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-g</samp>
    Sets the password of a group. This function is rarely used. It allows you to secure access to nonprimary groups via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">newgrp</samp> using a password. Because the group password must be known to multiple users, the procedure is inherently insecure.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Deactivates the account (lock).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>
    Reactivates a deactivated account (unlock).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-x</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the maximum number of days a password remains valid. In other words, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-x 180</samp> means that a new password must be set approximately every six months.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">passwd</samp> can only be used interactively. It’s not possible to pass the password as a parameter or option. To set passwords automatically, you must use the [chpasswd](#C_001.xhtml_chpasswd) command.

#### Example

In the following example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> sets a new password for the user <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hawks</samp>. In the future, they will have to change their password once a year.

```
root# passwd hawks
change password for user hawks.
Enter a new password: *********
Enter the new password again: *********
passwd: all authentication features successfully updated.
root# passwd -x 365 hawks 
```

### paste file1 file2 . . .

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">paste</samp> combines the lines of the specified files into new (longer) lines and displays the result on the screen. The first line of the resulting text therefore results from the first line of the first file plus the first line of the second file, and so on. Tab characters are inserted between the components of the new line. The result can be saved in a file using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">> target file</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d 'separator'</samp>

    Specifies a separator string. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">paste -d ':' file1 file2</samp>, a colon is placed in each line between the contents of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file1</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file2</samp>, that is:

    ```
    line1 from file1:line1 from file2
    line2 from file1:line2 from file2
    line3 from file1:line3 from file2
    ... 
    ```

### patch [options] < patch file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">patch</samp> applies the changes summarized in a [diff](#D_001.xhtml_diff) file. The command is generally used to apply code changes (e.g., for the kernel code).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Creates backup files for all changed files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--dry-run</samp>
    Tests the patch, but doesn’t make any changes. In general, you should make sure that no problems occur before applying any patch with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--dry-run</samp> option. Nothing is more annoying than an incorrectly or only partially applied patch!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Removes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> directory levels from the file names of the patch file. If the original file name is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/a/b/name.c</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p1</samp> makes it <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">a/b/name.c</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-p2</samp> returns <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">b/name.c</samp>. The correct value for n depends on the directory in which <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">patch</samp> is run.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-R</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--reverse</samp>
    Applies the patch inversely. This way, a patch that has already been applied will be undone.

#### Example

The following commands show how to patch the kernel code from version 6.7.5 to 6.7.6\. To do this, the patch from version 6.7 to 6.7.5 must first be undone before the patch for version 6.7.6 can be applied. Kernel patches usually refer to the latest major version, in this case, version 6.7.

```
root# cd /usr/src/linux-6.7.5
root# bunzip2 -c patch-6.7.5.bz2 | patch -R -p1 --dry-run 
(test inverse patch)
... no error messages
root# bunzip2 -c patch-6.7.5.bz2 | patch -R -p1           
(6.7.5 – > 
6.7)
root# bunzip2 -c patch-6.7.6.bz2 | patch -p1 --dry-run    
(test patch)
... no error messages
root# bunzip2 -c patch-6.7.6.bz2 | patch -p1              
(6.7 – > 
6.7.6)
root# cd /usr/src root# mv linux-6.7.5 linux-6.7.6 
```

### pdf2ps source.pdf [target.ps]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pdf2ps</samp> creates a PostScript file from a PDF document. If you don’t specify <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">target.ps</samp>, the new PDF file will be named <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">source.pdf</samp>. An alternative to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pdf2ps</samp> is the [pdftops](#P_001.xhtml_pdftops) command from the Poppler library. To convert PostScript files into PDF documents, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ps2pdf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-dLanguageLevel=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies which PostScript level is to be used for the output (by default, this is PostScript level 2; alternatively levels 1 and 3 are also supported).

### pdfimages [options] file.pdf [image name]
