The following commands set up the new user Gerald Gersin with the login name <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gersin</samp>, create a home directory, define an initial password, and then force the user to set a new password immediately on first login and every 100 days thereafter:

```
root# useradd gersin -c "Gerald Gersin" -m
root# passwd gersin
Enter a new password: *********
Enter the new password again:  *********
root# chage -d 0 -M 100 gersin 
```

### userdel name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">userdel</samp> deletes the specified user account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Also deletes the entire home directory and the user’s mail inbox.

### usermod [options] name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">usermod</samp> changes various properties of the user account, such as the home directory, the group membership, the default shell, and the UID. Most of the options are identical to those in [useradd](#U_001.xhtml_useradd). Changes to the user account don’t take effect until after a new login.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a -G</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">group</samp>
    Adds the user to the specified group.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp>
    Temporarily blocks the account. For this purpose, the ! character is placed before the hash code of the password in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/shadow</samp>, which is why a login is no longer possible.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-U</samp>
    Releases an account blocked by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-L</samp>.

#### Example

The following command adds the user <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gersin</samp> to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">docuteam</samp> group:

```
root# usermod -a -G docuteam gersin 
```

If you want to remove the user from the group again later, you must run [gpasswd](#G_001.xhtml_gpasswd) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d gersin docuteam</samp>.

## V

### vcgencmd command

This command enables you to read key data of the device or its CPU on the Raspberry Pi OS and also change a few parameters.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">commands</samp>
    Lists all <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vcgencmd</samp> commands.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">get_config</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parametername</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">|int|str</samp>
    Returns the status of the specified parameter or all integer or string parameters. The parameters are set in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/config.txt</samp> file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">get_throttled</samp>
    Provides information on potential issues with the power supply (from model 4B).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">measure_clock arm|core|hdmi|uart</samp>
    Provides the CPU frequency, the frequency of the graphics cores and the frequency of various other components.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">measure_temp</samp>
    Provides the temperature of the CPU.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">measure_volts core|sdram_c|sdram_i|sdram_p</samp>
    Specifies the voltage with which the graphics cores and the memory are supplied.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">version</samp>
    Provides the firmware version.

#### Example

The following commands show the operating status of a Raspberry Pi 5 that is currently idle:

```
pi$ vcgencmd measure_clock arm
frequency(0)=1500019456
pi$  vcgencmd measure_temp
temp=48.4'C 
```

### vgchange [options] [vgname]

The LVM command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgchange</samp> changes the attributes of a volume group (VG). The most important application is to activate or deactivate VGs.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a y|n</samp>
    Activates (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">y</samp>) or deactivates (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>) all VGs or the specified VG.

### vgcreate [options] vgname pvname1 [pvname2 ...]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgcreate</samp> creates a new VG from one or more physical volumes (PVs).

#### Example

In the following example, [pvcreate](#P_001.xhtml_pvcreate) first marks the first partition of the hard disks or SSDs <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdb1</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdc1</samp> as physical volumes. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgcreate</samp> creates the volume group <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vg1</samp> from this. Then, the [lvcreate](#L_001.xhtml_lvcreate) command reserves 100 GiB for the logical volume <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lv1</samp>. [](#M_001.xhtml_mkfs.ext2)sets up a file system in it, and [mount](#M_001.xhtml_mount) integrates the file system to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/mnt/lv1</samp> directory just created in the directory tree.

```
root# pvcreate /dev/sdb1
root# pvcreate /dev/sdc1
root# vgcreate vg1 /dev/sdb1 /dev/sdc1
root# lvcreate -L 100G -n lv1 vg1
root# mkfs.ext4 /dev/mapper/vg1-lv1
root# mkdir /mnt/lv1
root# mount /dev/mapper/vg1-lv1 /mnt/lv1 
```

### vgdisplay vgname

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgdisplay</samp> shows detailed information on the specified VG.

### vgextend vgname pvname

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgextend</samp> adds a PV to a VG.

#### Example

The following commands define the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/sdc2</samp> partition as a new physical volume and then add it to the existing <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">myvg1</samp> volume group, which has become too small:

```
root# pvcreate /dev/sdc2
  Physical volume "/dev/sdc2" successfully created
root# vgextend  myvg1 /dev/sdc2
  Volume group "myvg1" successfully extended
root# vgdisplay myvg1
...
  VG Size               180.64 GB
  Alloc PE / Size       6402 / 22.50 GB
  Free  PE / Size       41324 / 158.14 GB
... 
```

### vgmerge vgname1 vgname2

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgmerge</samp> adds <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vgname2</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vgname1</samp>. Once the command has been successfully executed, there’s only <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vgname1</samp>. It consists of all PVs that previously formed the storage pool for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vgname1</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vgname2</samp>.

### vgreduce [options] vgname [pvname1 pvname2 ...]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgreduce</samp> removes the specified PVs from the storage pool of the VG. This only works if the PVs are unused. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-a</samp> option removes all inactive PVs.

### vgrename oldvgname newvgname

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgrename</samp> gives a VG a new name. Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">oldvgname</samp>, the UUID of the VG can also be specified.

### vgscan

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vgscan</samp> lists all volume groups.

### vipw [options]
vigr [options]
visudo [options]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vipw</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vigr</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">visudo</samp> commands start the [vi/vim](#05_001.xhtml_vi) editor (see the section on keyboard shortcuts) and open the [etc/passwd](#04_001.xhtml_passwd), [etc/group](#04_001.xhtml_group), or [etc/sudoers](#04_001.xhtml_sudoers) file. When saving, a check is carried out to ensure that you’re adhering to the syntax of the respective file. As long as this isn’t the case, saving isn’t possible.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">directory</samp>
    Uses the specified directory as the root directory and edits the files relative to this directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp>
    Opens the [etc/shadow](#04_001.xhtml_shadow) file (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vipw</samp> command) or the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/gshadow</samp> file (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vigr</samp> command).

You can use the three commands even if you’re not a fan of the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vi</samp> editor. In this case, you must first set the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">VISUAL</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">EDITOR</samp> environment variable and enter the path to your favorite editor there.

### virsh [[-c connection] command]

You can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> command to administrate virtual KVM and Xen machines. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> can be used in two ways: either to run a virsh command directly or run it interactively as a shell. In the first variant, you can specify a connection string with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-c</samp> option:

```
root# virsh -c qemu:///session list --all ... 
```

The most important <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> commands are briefly described here. If you read more details in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page, then note that virtual machines are called domains in the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> terminology.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">attach-device</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name device.xml</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[--persistent]</samp>
    Adds an additional hardware component to a virtual machine (e.g., a USB device), which is described in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirt</samp> XML format. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--persistent</samp> option causes the device to be permanently connected to the virtual machine and saved in the virtual machine’s XML file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">attach-disk</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name source target</samp>
    Adds a data medium to a virtual machine, where <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">source</samp> is the device name on the host system, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">target</samp> is the device name in the guest. The command can be supplemented by numerous options that specify the driver (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--driver</samp>), the caching method (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--cache</samp>), and more. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--persistent</samp> option permanently connects the data medium to the virtual machine.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">attach-interface</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name type source</samp>
    Adds a network interface to a virtual machine. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type</samp> specifies the type of interface, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">network</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bridge</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">source</samp> specifies the interface name on the host computer (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">br0</samp>). The details of the interface can be set using additional options (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--mac</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--model</samp>, and more).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">autostart [--disable]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies that the virtual machine should be started automatically during the boot process of the host computer. By using the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--disable</samp> option, you can deactivate the automatic start again.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">connect qemu:///session</samp>
    Establishes a user connection to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirtd</samp> instance of the current user. This allows you to manage your own virtual machines.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">connect qemu:///system</samp>
    Establishes a connection to the system instance of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirtd</samp>. If you run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> automatically establishes this connection.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">connect qemu+ssh://</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user@hostname</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/system</samp>
    Establishes a connection to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirtd</samp> instance of another computer (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hostname</samp>). The communication takes place via an SSH tunnel.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">console</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Allows you to operate the specified virtual machine directly in the console. This assumes that a <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">getty</samp> process for the serial <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/ttyS0</samp> interface is running in the virtual machine. To terminate the connection, you must press Ctrl+ ].

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">define</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xml file</samp>
    Sets up a new virtual machine whose key data is summarized in the specified XML file. Caution: if a virtual machine with the same name already exists (according to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen"><name></samp> element in the XML file), its definition will be overwritten!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">destroy</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Terminates the virtual machine immediately. This is similar to unplugging the power cable on your computer, and it can have the same consequences (i.e., a destroyed file system, etc.)!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">detach-device</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name device.xml</samp>
    Removes the hardware component described by an XML file from the virtual machine.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">detach-disk</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name target</samp>
    Removes the data medium from the virtual machine. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">target</samp> specifies the device name in the guest.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">detach-interface</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name type</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--mac=xxx</samp>
    Detaches a network interface from the virtual machine.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">domstatus</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">and dominfo</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Provide information on a virtual machine.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">edit</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Loads the XML file describing the virtual machine into an editor, whereby the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$EDITOR</samp> environment variable is taken into account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list [--inactive</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--all]</samp>
    Lists all running virtual machines. If you only want to list the machines that aren’t currently active or all machines, you need to enter the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--inactive</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--all</samp> options.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">managedsave</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">managedsave-remove</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Saves the status of the virtual machine (i.e., the contents of the RAM, the CPU registers, etc.) in a file in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/libvirt/save/</samp> directory and then stops the execution of the machine. To reactivate the virtual machine, you can simply use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">start</samp>. Then, the status file gets deleted automatically. If you want to discard the saved state and restart the virtual machine completely, you should delete the state file using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">managedsave-remove</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">net-create</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xmlfile</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">net-start</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">netname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">net-destroy</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">netname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">net-undefine</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">netname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">net-list</samp>

    Support the management of virtual networks. These are private network areas that can be connected to the host system via NAT, for example, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">default</samp> network of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirt</samp> tools.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-define</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xmlfile</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-define-as</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname type</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--target</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-start</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-auto-start</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xmlfile</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-destroy</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-delete</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-list</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname</samp>

    Support the administration of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirt</samp> storage pools. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pool-define</samp> creates a new pool whose properties are described in an XML file. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool-define-as</samp> also creates a new pool, whereby the key data is passed directly as a parameter. Permitted pool types include <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dir</samp> (a local directory), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">netfs</samp> (a network directory), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">logical</samp> (a volume group), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">disk</samp> (a hard disk), or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iscsi</samp> (an iSCSI server).

    The new pool must then be started via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pool-start</samp>. If the pool is to be started automatically in the future, you must also run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pool-autostart</samp>.

    The commands for deleting a pool are somewhat confusing: A pool must be deactivated using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pool-destroy</samp> prior to the deletion. Although the command suggests something bad, the pool is merely stopped and can be restarted later by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pool-start</samp>. Only <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pool-delete</samp> deletes the pool. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">pool-delete</samp> assumes that all volumes in the pool have been deleted first, which means that only an empty pool can be deleted.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">qemu-monitor-command --hmp</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'</samp>
    Runs the specified QEMU monitor command for the virtual machine specified by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--hmp</samp> option is required because the command must otherwise be specified in JSON format.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">restore</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Reactivates a virtual machine saved using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">save</samp>. The state file can be deleted afterward.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">save</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name file</samp>
    Saves the state of the virtual machine (i.e., essentially the contents of the RAM) in a file and then stops the execution of the machine. To reactivate the virtual machine, you must use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">restore</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">schedinfo [options]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Displays or changes the scheduler parameters of the virtual machine (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--set parameter=value</samp>). These parameters can be used to control how many hardware resources a virtual machine is allowed to use. Resource control requires the activation of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cgroups</samp> functions on the host system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setmaxmem</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">setmem</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>

    Sets the limit for memory usage (RAM) and the currently allocated memory. The additional <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--config</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--current</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--live</samp> options allow you to specify whether the settings are to be saved permanently or only executed currently.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">shutdown/reboot</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Shuts down or reboots the virtual machine. The virtual machine receives a shutdown signal via ACPI. The ACPI daemon <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">acpid</samp> must be installed in the virtual machine for the signal to be processed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">snapshot-create</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vmname [xml-file [--redefine]]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">snapshot-create-as</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vmname snapshotname [description]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">snapshot-list</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vmname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">snapshot-delete</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vmname snname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">snapshot-revert</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vmname snname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[--running]</samp>

    Creates a snapshot of a running virtual machine, lists all snapshots, deletes a snapshot, or applies the contents of a snapshot to the image file. The snapshot function can only be used for virtual machines that use QCOW2 image files.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">start</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Starts the specified virtual machine. If you want to communicate with the machine in graphics mode, you should use either a VNC client (the connection data is determined by the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">virsh</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vncdisplay</samp>, see the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vncdisplay</samp> item in this list) or the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-viewer</samp> program.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">suspend/resume</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Stops the specified virtual machine temporarily or resumes execution. However, the stopped virtual machine continues to use RAM! Thus, only the virtual CPU is stopped.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ttyconsole</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies which device of the host computer is used to access the serial interface of the guest system (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/pts/5</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">undefine</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Deletes the XML file that describes the virtual machine. The image file with the virtual hard disk is retained. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">undefine</samp> can’t be run until all snapshots of the virtual machine have been deleted.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vcpuinfo</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Provides information on the (virtual) CPUs available to the virtual machine, as well as information on the CPU time used so far. The command can also be used to check the CPU pinning.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vcpupin</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name guest-cpu-nr host-cpu-list</samp>
    Links the physical CPU cores of the host system with the virtual CPUs of the guest. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vcpupin vm1 0 2</samp> permanently assigns the third CPU core of the host to the first virtual CPU of virtual machine <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vm1</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol-create</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xmlfile</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol-create-as</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname newvolname size</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol-delete</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">volname</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol-list</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol-info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">volname</samp>

    Support the administration of data media in storage pools. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vol-create</samp> creates a new data medium whose properties are described in the specified XML file. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol-create-as</samp> creates a new data medium of the desired size, whereby the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">k</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">M</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">G</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">T</samp> suffixes are permitted for KiB, MiB, GiB, and TiB. When you create an image disk, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--format raw/qcow2/qed</samp> to specify the desired format (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">raw</samp> by default).

    <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--allocation</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">size</samp> determines how much of the memory is to be allocated in advance; with raw volumes, the entire memory is always reserved.

    If there are multiple storage pools, you must specify which pool you’re referring to for all commands with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--pool</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname</samp> option.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vncdisplay</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Returns the IP address (empty for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">localhost</samp>) and port number for the VNC display of the virtual machine. You can then start any VNC client to interact with the virtual machine. For security reasons, VNC access only works from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">localhost</samp> by default (see the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/libvirt/qemu.conf</samp> file).

    <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vncdisplay</samp> doesn’t return a result if the virtual machine doesn’t share its graphics system via VNC at all, but uses the more modern Spice system instead. In this case, you can operate the virtual machine using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-viewer</samp> program. You can directly pass the virtual machine name to this program.

    However, should the need arise to determine the Spice port number, it will get difficult. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> lacks a command that determines the spice port of a virtual machine, similar to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">vncdisplay</samp>. The following command, which I found in a forum on [https://ubuntuusers.de/](https://ubuntuusers.de/), provides a solution by extracting the port number from the process list:

    ```
    spice_port=$(ps aux | grep vm_name | grep -oP "(?<=-spice port=).*?(?=,)") 
    ```

#### Examples

Once you’ve started the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirt</samp> shell via the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp> command, you can run commands to manage all virtual machines on the local computer:

```
root# virsh
virsh# list --all
 Id Name           Status
-------------------------------
 13 fedora         running
  - ubuntu         shut down
  - windows        shut down
virsh# start windows
Domain windows started
virsh# vncdisplay windows
:1
virsh# exit 
```

You can also connect to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirtd</samp> daemon on another machine via SSH. If a <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> login with password via SSH isn’t possible on the KVM host for security reasons, you must set up your public SSH key on the KVM host before the first connection is established.

```
virsh# connect qemu+ssh://user@hostname/system
user@hostname's password: ******* 
```

### virt-clone [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-clone</samp> copies a shutdown virtual machine that is managed by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirt</samp> tools. This creates a new XML definition file and a copy of the image file. The other hardware components remain largely unchanged.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--auto-clone</samp>
    Creates a new virtual machine. The VM name is composed of the previous name plus <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-clone</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-clone</samp> is also inserted into the names of the image files, so that <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rhel9.img</samp> becomes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rhel9-clone.img</samp>, for example. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--auto-clone</samp>, the explicit specification of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--name</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--file</samp> can be omitted.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--connect</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hypervisor</samp>
    Establishes a connection to the specified virtualization system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--file=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Specifies the desired name of the new image file. If the original virtual machine has multiple virtual hard disks, you must use this option multiple times. Instead of an image file, you can also specify the name of a device file, for example, if you use logical volumes of the host system as data storage.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--mac</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nn:nn:nn:nn:nn:nn</samp>
    Specifies the desired new MAC address of the network adapter. If this information is omitted, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-clone</samp> automatically uses a unique random MAC address.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reliving</samp>
    Specifies the name of the new virtual machine.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--original</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the name of the original virtual machine.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--preserve-data</samp>
    Prevents the image file from being copied. This means that the new virtual machine uses the same image file as the previous virtual machine. It’s therefore not permitted to run the old and the new virtual machine at the same time! This option is useful if you want to test a system with a new virtual hardware or network configuration.

#### Example

The following command copies Ubuntu server installation <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">userver5</samp>. The new virtual machine is named <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">userver6</samp>, and the new image file is saved in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/libvirt/images/userver6.img</samp> file. Make sure to create the new image file in a libvirt storage pool. Otherwise, the SELinux rules on RHEL/Fedora will prevent the virtual machine from running.

```
root# virt-clone --original userver5 --name userver6 \
                 --file /var/lib/libvirt/images/userver6.img 
```

### virt-install [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-install</samp> is a Python script that helps you to set up new virtual machines.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--arch</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">architecture</samp>
    Specifies the desired CPU architecture, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">i386</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">i686</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x86_64</samp>. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-install</samp> uses the same architecture as the one used on the host system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--cdrom</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Specifies the file name of the ISO file or the device name of the CD/DVD drive from which the installation data is loaded.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--connect</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hypervisor</samp>
    Establishes a connection to the specified virtualization system. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-install</samp> is started on a KVM host with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions, the script automatically establishes a connection to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">qemu:///system</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--disk</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Specifies the file name of the image file in which the virtual machine is to be saved. If you want to use multiple virtual storage devices, you must specify the option multiple times.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--disk</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">opt1=value1,opt2=value2,...</samp>
    Allows you to specify multiple image files from different <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirt</samp> storage pools. Permitted options include <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">path</samp> to specify an image file or a block device, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pool</samp> to specify a previously created <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">libvirt</samp> storage pool, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol</samp> to specify an existing image file in a storage pool (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vol=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">poolname/imagename</samp>), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">size</samp> to specify the desired size of new image files (in GiB), <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bus</samp> to select the bus system (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ide</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">scsi</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">virtio</samp>) and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cache</samp> to select the caching (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">writethrough</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">writeback</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">none</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--graphics</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type</samp>,<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">opt1=value1</samp>,<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">opt2=value2</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">...</samp>
    Specifies how the graphics system of the virtual machine is to be implemented. The possible types are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vnc</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">spice</samp>. VNC is used as standard. Various connection parameters can be specified with the other options, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">port</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">listen</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">password</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--import</samp>
    Causes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">virt-install</samp> to not perform a new installation, but to create the new virtual machine on the basis of an existing image file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type, opt1</samp>
    Specifies the name of the virtual machine.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--network</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">type,opt1=value1,opt2=value2,...</samp>
    Specifies the key data of a network device of the virtual machine. The option can be specified multiple times if required. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">type</samp> specifies how the network connection to the host computer should be established. Permissible values are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bridge=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> for a previously set up network bridge, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">network=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> for a virtual network defined using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp>, or simply <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user</samp>, if the virtual machine is to communicate with the host system via NAT.

    The other options determine the parameters of the network device: <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">model</samp> specifies which adapter is to be emulated, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">e1000</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rtl8139</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">virtio</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mac</samp> defines the MAC address of the device. If this parameter isn’t specified, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">virt-install</samp> generates a random MAC address itself. MAC addresses for KVM must start with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">52:54:00</samp>!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--nodisk</samp>
    Enables the installation without an image file (e.g.,if the installation is to take place in a network storage device).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--noreboot</samp>
    Prevents the automatic restart after the installation has been completed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--os-type</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies the type of operating system to be installed, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">linux</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">unix</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">windows</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">other</samp>. The information is used to optimize various hardware parameters.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--os-variant</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies which operating system is to be installed, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fedora28</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">virtio26</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">rhel7</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">win10</samp>. A complete list of all known operating system names is provided by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-install</samp>. If you use this option, you don’t need to specify <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--os-type</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--ram</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Indicates the size of the RAM in MiB.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-serial pty</samp>
    Equips the virtual machine with a serial interface. When the virtual machine is started, the serial interface is connected to a pseudo-TTY device on the host computer. In <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virsh</samp>, you can determine the device name using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ttyconsole</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vmname</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--soundhw=ac97/es1370/sb16</samp>
    Equips the virtual machine with a sound card.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--vcpus=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the desired number of CPU cores (one by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--video=cirrus/vga/vmvga</samp>
    Specifies which graphics adapter is to be emulated (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cirrus</samp> by default).

#### Example

Before you run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-install</samp>, you must create an image file for the virtual hard disk:

```
root# virsh
virsh# vol-create-as default disk.qcow2 10G --format qcow2
virsh# exit 
```

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-install</samp> command enables you to set up a new virtual machine:

```
root# virt-install --name myvmname --ram 2048 --cdrom install.iso \
        --os-variant rhel8  --disk vol=default/disk.qcow2 --graphics vnc \
        --noreboot 
```

### virt-top [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-top</samp> shows how much CPU capacity and memory space the running virtual machines require. While <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-top</samp> is running, you can sort the display via 0, 1, 2, and 3 according to virtual machines, CPU cores, network interfaces or disk devices. Q terminates the command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--connect hypervisor</samp>
    Establishes the connection to the specified virtualization system. By default, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-top</samp> communicates with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">qemu:///system</samp> if it has been started with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">root</samp> permissions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-o sort</samp>
    Specifies the desired sort order, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cpu</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mem</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">time</samp>, to sort the list according to CPU performance, memory requirements or total computing time.

#### Example

```
root# virt-top
virt-top 14:36:17 - x86_64 8/8CPU 1600MHz 15961MB
```

### virt-viewer [options] name/id/uuid

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">virt-viewer</samp> is a VNC and Spice client that displays the graphics system of a virtual machine. The name, ID, or UUID of the virtual machine is normally simply passed to the command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hypervisor</samp>
    Establishes a connection to the specified virtualization system. This option is only required if it’s an external KVM host.

## W

### wait [process number]

The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> command <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wait</samp> waits for the end of the specified background process. If no process number is specified, the command waits for the end of all running background processes started by the shell.

#### Example

The use of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wait</samp> is particularly useful in shell scripts if multiple background processes are to be started first and then have to wait for the end of all these processes:

```
#!/bin/bash
command1 &
command2 &
command3 &
command4 &
wait
# only continue here when command 1 to command 4 are finished
... 
```

### wakeonlan [options] mac

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wakeonlan</samp> from the package of the same name (available for Debian and Ubuntu) sends a special network packet for a MAC address and attempts to “wake up” the identified device from sleep mode. This only works if the device supports the Wake-on-LAN standard.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">host</samp>
    Sends the Wake-on-LAN packet only to the specified host or address and not to the entire network.

### watch command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">watch</samp> runs the specified command periodically and displays the output.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--differences</samp>
    Marks the differences compared to the preceding result.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-e</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--errexit</samp>
    Terminates <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">watch</samp> if the called command returns an error.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">err exit</samp>
    Specifies after how many seconds the command should be run again (by default, it’s every two seconds).

#### Example

The following command displays all changes in the list of running <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mysqld</samp> processes:

```
user$ watch -d 'ps aux | grep mysqld' 
```

### wc files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wc</samp> counts the number of lines, words, and characters in the specified files. If multiple files are entered using wildcards, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wc</samp> also calculates the total of the three entries. In addition, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wc</samp> is also well suited for combination with other programs.

#### Example

[find](#F_001.xhtml_find) returns one line for each regular file. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wc</samp> counts the lines and thus returns the total number of all files in the directory tree.

```
user$ find / -type f -print | wc 
```

### wget [options] url1 url2 . . .

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> downloads files from HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP servers. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> can resume interrupted downloads, can recursively follow links, and is suitable for automating downloads.

The files to be transferred are specified as URLs (Uniform Resource Locators), for example, as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">http://myserver.com/file.iso</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> command is controlled by countless options; only the most important of these are summarized here:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-b</samp>
    Performs the download as a background process and writes all status messages to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">wget-log</samp> file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-B</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">url</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--base=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">url</samp>
    Prefixes all relative links within the file you’ve specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">–I file</samp> with the basic <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">url</samp> address.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c</samp>
    Resumes an interrupted download. Caution: if the file has changed on the server in the meantime, the downloaded file is incorrect and contains some data from the old file and some data from the new file!

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--force-html</samp>
    Interprets the file specified with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-i</samp> as an HTML file and loads all files referenced by links in the HTML file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--ftp-user=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">user</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--ftp-password=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">pw</samp>
    Specifies the username and password for FTP downloads. This information can also be transferred in the URL (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ftp://user:password@server/file.txt</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--input-file=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">file</samp>
    Reads the files (URLs) to be transferred from the specified text file. If you pass the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-</samp> character instead of a file, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> expects the URLs from the standard input. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-i</samp> option only accepts local files as parameters, not URLs. (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-i http://server/name.html</samp> therefore doesn’t work!)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--limit-rate=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Limits the download quantity per second. The letters <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">k</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">m</samp> denote kilobytes and megabytes respectively (i.e., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--limit-rate=0.25m</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--no-check-certificate</samp>
    Doesn’t check HTTPS certificates. This makes sense if you know that the relevant server uses self-signed certificates.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-q</samp>
    Dispenses with the output of status messages (quiet).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--retry-connrefused</samp>
    Makes further attempts to download the file even after the connection refused error. This option is only useful for unreliable download servers that occasionally disappear from the network and reappear a short time later.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--spider</samp>
    Tests whether all links in the file specified by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">htmlfile</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--force-html</samp> are still valid. However, the files indicated by links aren’t downloaded.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--tries=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Makes <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> attempts to reconnect if the connection is lost (the default setting is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">20</samp>). With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t 0</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> tries its luck until the download is successful or you cancel the command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-w</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--wait=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies how many seconds <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> should wait prior to downloading the next file. This option prevents the download server from being overloaded by countless, almost simultaneous, download requests.

#### Recursive Downloads

The following options control recursive downloads:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-E</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--html-extension</samp>
    Adds the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.html</samp> extension to the file names of all downloaded files of the application/xhtml+xml or text/html type whose names don’t end with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.html</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.htm</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-H</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--span-hosts</samp>
    Also follows links to other websites.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-k</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--convert-links</samp>
    Changes the links in the downloaded HTML files so that they reference the local files. This makes it possible to view the pages offline later.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--level</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Limits the recursion level (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">5</samp> by default). <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-l inf</samp> deactivates the limitation.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--relative</samp>
    Tracks only relative links (but no absolute links to the start website).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Activates recursive downloads. For HTTP downloads, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> tracks all HTTP links on the start page, downloads the files specified in this way, tracks their links, and more. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> only takes into account relative links and links to pages on the start website. For FTP downloads, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> reads all subdirectories.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-p</samp>
    Downloads all files required to view the source file (including files that exceed the maximum recursion level).

#### Examples

In its basic form, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wget</samp> simply downloads the specified file:

```
user$ wget ftp://myftpserver.com/name.abc 
```

If the download gets interrupted for any reason, it can be resumed without any trouble by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-c</samp>:

```
user$ wget -c ftp://myftpserver.com/name.abc 
```

The following recursive download command (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-r</samp> option) helps to read a website offline later or to archive its current status. The recursion depth is limited to four levels by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-l 4</samp>.

```
user$ wget -r -l 4 -p -E -k http://website.com 
```

### whatis file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">whatis</samp> outputs a short description of the specified command or keyword. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">whatis</samp> descriptions only exist for topics for which <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> texts are installed. If <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">whatis</samp> doesn’t work, the underlying databases that can be created via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mandb</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">makewhatis</samp> are probably missing.

### whereis file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">whereis</samp> searches all common paths for binary files, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> files, and source code for the specified file name. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">whereis</samp> is therefore less thorough than <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">find</samp>, but much faster. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">whereis</samp> lists the directories that are searched.

### which command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">which</samp> searches all paths specified in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PATH</samp> for the command. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">which</samp> returns the full name of the command that would be executed if the command were called without path information. This is particularly useful if multiple versions of a command exist in different directories.

In <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>, [type](#T_001.xhtml_type) can also be used instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">which</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">type</samp> command helps you find out whether <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command</samp> is actually a built-in shell command, an alias, or a self-defined function.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">which</samp> determines where the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ls</samp> command is stored in the file system:

```
user$ which ls
/usr/bin/ls 
```

### while condition; do commands done

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">while</samp> creates loops in <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> scripts. The loop runs until the specified condition is no longer fulfilled for the first time. The loop criterion is the return value of the command that is specified as a condition. Comparisons and tests are performed using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">test</samp> command or its short form in square brackets.

#### Examples

The following loop outputs the numbers 0 to 5:

```
#!/bin/bash
i=0
while [ $i -le 5 ]; do
   echo $i
   i=$[$i+1]
done 
```

To process a text file line by line, you must formulate your <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp> script as follows:

```
#!/bin/bash
while read line; do
  echo $line
  ...
done < textfile.txt 
```

### who [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">who</samp> displays a list of all system users currently logged in. Even if you’re the only person working on your computer, you can log in with different names on different text consoles. If you want to know who was last logged in on this computer, you must run the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">last</samp> command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp>
    Provides detailed information on each user, including the console used and the login time. For SSH connections, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">who</samp> also shows the computer on which the login occurred.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-m</samp>
    Specifies the username of the currently active console. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">who am i</samp> command has the same meaning.

#### Example

In addition to the TTY processes for the six consoles, there are two active shell sessions of the user <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">kofler</samp> on the test computer:

```
user$ who -a
           system boot  2025-04-09 08:57
           run-level 2  2025-04-09 08:57
LOGIN      tty5         2025-04-09 08:57          971 id=5
LOGIN      tty2         2025-04-09 08:57          976 id=2
LOGIN      tty3         2025-04-09 08:57          977 id=3
LOGIN      tty1         2025-04-09 08:57         1802 id=1
kofler   + pts/1        2025-04-24 11:45 02:02    351 (xxx.telekom.at)
kofler   + pts/2        2025-04-24 13:47   .     2354 (xxx.telekom.at) 
```

### whois [options] host name

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">whois</samp> performs DNS queries for the specified host name and displays the result.

#### Example

```
user$ whois kofler.info
Domain Name: KOFLER.INFO
...
Domain Status: ok https://icann.org/epp#ok
Registrant Name: Kofler Michael
... 
```

### wl-copy [options] text
wl-paste

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wl-copy</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wl-clipboard</samp> package copies the text passed as a parameter to the clipboard of a Wayland system. If no text is transferred, the command expects the data from the standard input channel.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wl-paste</samp> outputs the contents of the clipboard via the standard output channel.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--type mime/type</samp>
    Defines the MIME data type for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wl-copy</samp>.

### wlr-randr [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wlr-randr</samp> without additional options lists all permissible graphic resolutions for a Wayland system. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--mode</samp>, you can change the current resolution for a monitor output. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wlr-randr</samp> is the Wayland counterpart to the X command (see [xrandr](#X_001.xhtml_xrandr)).

#### Example

The following command changes the resolution of the monitor connected to the second HDMI output to 2,560 × 1,440 pixels:

```
user$ wlr-randr --output HDMI-A-2 --mode 2560x1440 
```

### wol [options] mac

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wol</samp> from the package of the same name (available for Fedora and RHEL) sends a special network packet for a MAC address and tries to “wake up” the device from sleep mode. This only works if the device supports the Wake-on-LAN standard.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-h</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">host</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-i</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">host</samp>
    Sends the Wake-on-LAN packet only to the specified host or address and not to the entire network.

### wpa_passphrase ssid

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wpa_passphrase</samp> helps to set up a configuration file for the Wi-Fi authentication service; <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wpa_supplicant</samp>.

#### Example

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wpa_supplicant</samp> expects the name of a Wi-Fi network (i.e., service set identifier) as a parameter. You must then enter the password for the Wi-Fi. The command then outputs multiple lines in the syntax of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wpa_supplicant</samp>. You now only need to add these lines to the end of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.conf</samp>:

```
user$ wpa_passphrase my-wifi-name
# reading passphrase from stdin
strictlySecret
network={
        ssid="my-wifi-name"
        #psk="strictlySecret"
psk=9a184914197f550e1c6b350cc49b09a5fab532a8ec991f997ee77fd0a5e78d96
} 
```

### write username

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">write</samp> allows you to send a message to another user. After running the command, all characters entered prior to Ctrl+D are transferred to the terminal of the specified user.

### wsl [options] [command]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wsl</samp> isn’t a Linux command, but a Windows command. It has been included in this book because it helps you manage the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), that is, to start and remove Linux installations on Windows, and more. The command is only available if you activate the Windows subsystem for Linux option in the Activate Windows Features program.

Without further options, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wsl</samp> starts the default Linux installation or runs the command passed to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wsl</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--distribution</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Starts the specified distribution. Its further use takes place interactively in a shell.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--list</samp>
    Lists all Linux installations. With the additional <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--verbose</samp> option, the command also reveals which Linux instances are currently running and whether they are WSL1- or WSL2-compatible. (WSL2 uses a real Linux kernel to run the respective distribution, which has speed advantages. However, there are restrictions with WSL2 compared to WSL1 regarding the network connection.)

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--set-default</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Specifies which Linux installation is the default Linux system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--set-default-version</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1|2</samp>
    Determines whether new Linux installations are run with WSL1 or WSL2 by default.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--set-version</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1|2</samp>
    Specifies how the specified Linux distribution should be run (WSL1 or WSL2).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--shutdown</samp>
    Shuts down all running Linux distributions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-t</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--terminate</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Stops the execution of the specified Linux distribution.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--user</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Runs the command or login for the specified user.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--unregister</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Deletes the specified Linux installation.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wsl</samp> doesn’t provide the option of installing a new Linux distribution. To do this, you need to consult the Microsoft Store, where various Linux distributions are available for free download. The first time you start a WSL distribution, you must set up a user and password. This user has <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sudo</samp> privileges.

#### Examples

There are four Linux installations on the test computer, with Ubuntu as the default distribution:

```
> wsl --list --verbose
NAME                   STATE           VERSION
* Ubuntu               Stopped         2
kali-linux             Stopped         1
docker-desktop-data    Stopped         2
docker-desktop         Stopped         2 
```

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">wsl</samp> runs the [id](#I_001.xhtml_id) command twice, once in the standard account and once with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions. No password is required for this.

```
> wsl id
uid=1000(kofler) gid=1000(kofler) groups=1000(kofler),4(adm),...

> wsl -u root id
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root) 
```

The last example starts Kali Linux for interactive use:

```
> wsl -d kali-linux
$ cat /etc/os-release
PRETTY_NAME="Kali GNU/Linux Rolling"
NAME="Kali GNU/Linux"
...
$ ip a
8: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP> mtu 1500 group default qlen 1
   link/ether 04:d4:c4:92:65:f5
   inet 192.168.178.52/24 brd 192.168.178.255 scope global dynamic
   ...
16: eth1: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP> mtu 1500 group default qlen 1
   link/ether 00:15:5d:7e:85:98
   inet 172.31.96.1/20 brd 172.31.111.255 scope global dynamic
   ... 
```

## X

### xargs command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xargs</samp> forwards the data coming from the standard input to the command specified as a parameter. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xargs</samp> is usually used in combination with a command preceded by a pipe, that is, in the format <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command1 | xargs command2</samp>. In this way, the results of the first command can be processed with the second command. If the results of the first command are so extensive that they can’t be passed in a command line, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">command2</samp> is called in several steps.

The difference between <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">command1 | command2</samp> is that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xargs</samp> passes the standard input in the form of parameters to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">command2</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xargs</samp> must be used if <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">command2</samp> only processes the transferred parameters. Ordinary pipes, on the other hand, are suitable if <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">command2</samp> processes the data from the standard input.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--null</samp>
    Expects 0 bytes to separate file names (but not spaces and tab characters). This option is suitable for processing <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> results if <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">find</samp> was run with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-print0</samp> option.

#### Example

The following command searches the current directory and all subdirectories for backup files ending with the ~ character and deletes them. This also works for file names that contain spaces.

```
user$ find -name '*.~' -print0 | xargs --null rm 
```

### xdg-open file

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xdg-open</samp> opens a suitable program in the graphics system for editing the specified file. The command analyzes the MIME data stored in the XDG system; that is, it opens an audio player for an MP3 file, but a graphics program for a PNG file. Although XDG stands for X Desktop Group, this command also works if the graphics system uses Wayland.

On Debian and Ubuntu systems, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xdg-open</samp> can be run using the short name <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">open</samp>, as is the case on macOS.

### xdpyinfo [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xdpyinfo</samp> provides comprehensive information on the running X server in graphics mode. You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grep</samp> to extract the details relevant to you.

#### Example

The following commands determine the release number of the X server, the resolution of the screen and its pixel density (dots per inch [DPI]):

```
user$ xdpyinfo | grep release
vendor release number:    11702000
root# xdpyinfo | grep -C 1 dimensions
screen #0:
  dimensions:    1600x1200 pixels (411x311 millimeters)
  resolution:    99x98 dots per inch 
```

### xfs_admin [options] device/imagefile

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_admin</samp> shows or changes parameters of an XFS file system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-c 0|1</samp>
    Deactivates or activates the lazy counter function of the file system, which means that the superblocks of the file system are updated less frequently, noticeably speeding up certain file operations.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp>
    Indicates that the file system is located in an image file and not on a data medium device.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-l</samp>
    Outputs the label of the file system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-L</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Sets the name (label) of the file system again.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-u</samp>
    Shows the UUID of the file system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-U</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uuid</samp>
    Assigns a new UUID to the file system.

### xfs_growfs [options] mount-directory

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_growfs</samp> enlarges an XFS file system. This assumes that the underlying device (e.g., a partition or a logical volume) has previously been enlarged.

The enlargement will take place during ongoing operation. For this purpose, the file system must be integrated into the directory tree. There are no plans to reduce the size of XFS file systems.

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_growfs</samp> has various options that enable you to control which areas of the file system will be enlarged and by how much. As a rule, however, it’s not necessary to specify these options. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_growfs</samp> recognizes how large the underlying data medium is and decides for itself how large the various areas of the XFS file system should be.

### xfs_info device

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_info</samp> outputs a summary of the key data of an XFS file system. The command is equivalent to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_growfs -n</samp>.

### xfs_repair [options] device/imagefile

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_repair</samp> attempts to restore a damaged XFS file system to a consistent state.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp>
    Repairs an active read-only file system. Usually, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xfs_repair</samp> can only repair file systems that aren’t currently in use. This option is useful if you’ve started your Linux computer in single-user or emergency mode and need to repair the system partition. After the repair, you must restart the system. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man</samp> page describes the option as dangerous. It’s safer to start the computer with a live or emergency system and perform the repair from there.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp>
    Indicates that the file system is located in an image file and not on a data medium device.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-n</samp>
    Doesn’t make any changes, but shows which repairs are carried out if the command is run without this option.

### xhost +/-hostname

With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xhost +hostname</samp>, the graphics server accepts X connections from the specified host name. Similarly, X blocks connections from this host after <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xhost -hostname</samp>.

For security reasons, the X graphics system usually only allows local connections. to work from an external computer, an exception must be explicitly defined for this host via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xhost +name</samp>. Even more liberal, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xhost +</samp> completely deactivates access control, making it possible to log in from any host.

#### Example

In real life, running <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xhost</samp> is often necessary, especially if you first want to establish a connection to the graphics server as a normal user via VNC and then run a graphical program with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> permissions using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sudo</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">su</samp>. This isn’t allowed by default. The solution is <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xhost +localhost</samp> (because the connection has already been established thanks to VNC and it’s now only a matter of running programs under a different account).

The following example assumes that you first establish a VNC connection, then run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xhost</samp> in a terminal window, and finally start a program in graphics mode via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sudo</samp>—in this case, it’s the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gedit</samp> editor:

```
user$ xhost +localhost
user$ sudo gedit        
(start editor with root permissions) 
```

### xinput [command]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xinput</samp> supports the configuration of input devices (e.g., keyboard, mouse, and touchpad) for the X window system.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list</samp>
    Lists all recognized input devices.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-props</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">deviceid</samp>
