    Lists the parameters of a device. You should determine the device ID beforehand by using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xinput list</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">set-button-map</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">deviceid mapbutton1 mapbutton2 ...</samp>
    Changes the assignment of the buttons of a mouse.

### xkill [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xkill</samp> terminates a stuck or half-crashed X program. The relevant window must be clicked with the mouse after starting the command.

### xrandr [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xrandr</samp> changes the screen resolution, frame rate, and other settings during operation. As the name implies, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xrandr</samp> only works on Xorg. An alternative for Wayland is [wlr-randr](#W_001.xhtml_wlr-randr).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--addmode</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">output name</samp>
    Adds a new graphics mode, possibly previously defined with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--newmode</samp>, for the specified display output.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--dpi</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Indicates how many pixels per inch are displayed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--left-of output</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--right-of</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--below</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--above</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Activates the signal output specified by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--output</samp> and specifies how the screens are positioned relative to each other. This only works if a sufficiently large virtual resolution has been set in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xorg.conf</samp> so that both screens can be covered.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--newmode</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name freq x1 x2 x3 x4 y1 y2 y3 y4</samp>
    Defines a new mode (a new resolution). The syntax corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">ModeLine</samp> lines in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xorg.conf</samp>. You can use the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gtf</samp> command to determine the correct number combination.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--off</samp>
    Switches off the signal output specified with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--output</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--orientation</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x</samp>
    Changes the image position. Permitted settings are <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">normal</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">inverted</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">left</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">right</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--output</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Indicates that the other options relate to a specific signal output. This is useful if multiple monitors are connected. You can determine the names of the active signal outputs via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xrandr -q</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--primary</samp>
    Makes the screen selected via <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--output</samp> the primary screen on which Gnome or KDE displays the panel, dock, and more.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-q</samp>
    Indicates which setting options are available. The result is heavily dependent on the graphics driver used.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--rate</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Changes the frame rate for the current resolution. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> is the desired frame rate in Hertz.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--size</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Changes the resolution. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> is a number from the result list of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xrandr -q</samp> or the desired resolution in the format <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">widexheight</samp>.

#### Example

The following command sets the resolution to 1280 × 1024 pixels:

```
user$ xrandr --size 1280x1024 
```

The next command activates both the DVI and the VGA signal output. (The names of the outputs vary depending on the graphics card and driver.) The same image is displayed on both monitors. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--auto</samp> option causes each monitor to be operated in the optimum resolution and frame rate for it.

```
user$ xrandr --output DVI-I-0 --auto --output VGA-0 --auto 
```

The following three commands define a new graphics mode with a resolution of 1,280 × 720 pixels and activate it for the HDMI1 output:

```
user$  xrandr --newmode 1280x720 74.18 1280 1390 1430 1650 720 725 730 750
user$  xrandr --addmode HDMI1 1280x720
user$  xrandr --size 1280x720 
```

### xset [command]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xset</samp> changes various settings of the X server.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">+dpms</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-dpms</samp>
    Activates or deactivates the energy-saving functions (display power management signaling).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dpms</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n1 [n2 [n3]]</samp>
    Specifies after how many seconds the DPMS modes Standby, Suspend, and Off of the monitor should be activated.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">q</samp>
    Provides a list of the current settings.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">s</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Activates the screen saver after <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> seconds.

### xz [options] files

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xz</samp> from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xz-utils</samp> package compresses the specified files. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xz</samp> is a relatively new compression command that provides even smaller files than [](#B_001.xhtml_bzip2). The compressed files are given the extension <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.xz</samp> by default.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-0</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-9</samp>
    Specifies how well <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xz</samp> should compress. The best results (i.e., the smallest files) are obtained with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-9</samp>, but <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xz</samp> then requires the most memory. The default is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-6</samp>. In this case, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xz</samp> requires a maximum of 100 MiB when compressing and a maximum of 10 MiB when decompressing.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-d</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--decompress</samp>
    Decompresses the specified file (corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">unxz</samp>).

In spring 2024, it became known that a backdoor had been installed in some versions of <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xz</samp>, which fortunately weren’t yet widespread. Although this wouldn’t have affected the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xz</samp> command directly, it would have affected the underlying <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">xz</samp> library, which is used by SSH, among others.

## Y

### yay [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yay</samp> is an alternative to [pacman](#P_001.xhtml_pacman). The command manages both normal Arch Linux packages and AUR packages. These are additional packages that are only provided in the form of build scripts. The same options apply for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yay</samp> as for [pacman](#P_001.xhtml_pacman), so see that entry as well.

### yum [options] command

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yum</samp> installs, updates and removes RPM packages on RHEL. Behind the scenes, however, the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> command first established in Fedora has been used since version 8\. For this reason, all commands and options are described in [dnf](#D_001.xhtml_dnf) in this book.

## Z

### z directory1 [directory2]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp> is a modern alternative to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp>. To install it, you need to download the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z.sh</samp> script from [https://github.com/rupa/z](https://github.com/rupa/z), save it in any directory, and then add the following line to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.bashrc</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.zshrc</samp>:

```
# at the end of .bashrc or .zshrc 
. /path/to/z.sh 
```

After a new login, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">cd</samp> to change the active directory. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp> remembers when and how often you use which directories. This database is then used by <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp> to complete incomplete commands. Thus, once you’ve entered the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/home/<name>/Downloads/iso</samp> directory, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z iso</samp> will simply work.

If there are multiple <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">iso</samp> directories (e.g., also <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/usr/share/iso</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/lib/libvirt/images/iso</samp>), <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp> prioritizes the most frequently or most recently visited directory. The current order of the directories reveals <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp> if you run the command without any further parameters.

To specify the desired directory more precisely, you can pass two character strings to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">z</samp> searches for the first character string in the front part of the path and for the second character string in the back part:

```
user$ z home iso   # corresponds to cd /home/<user>/Downloads/iso
user$ z var iso    # corresponds to cd /var/lib/libvirt/images/iso
user$ z usr iso    # corresponds to cd /usr/share/iso 
```

### zcat file.gz
zless file.gz
zmore file.gz

The three commands work like [cat](#C_001.xhtml_cat), [less](#L_001.xhtml_less), and [more](#M_001.xhtml_more). The only difference is that compressed files can be read directly via [gzip](#G_001.xhtml_gzip), that is, without prior decompression using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gunzip</samp>.

Instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zless</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">less</samp> can be used directly with many distributions. This command is usually configured in such a way that it can be used without distinction for compressed and uncompressed files.

### zenity [options]

<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zenity</samp> displays simple GTK dialogs for entering text, selecting a tag in the calendar, or selecting a file. The command returns the result for further processing. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zenity</samp>, you can give your <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> scripts a more modern look—provided that the script is run in a graphical desktop system.

The following options merely illustrate the concept of the command. With more than 50 options, the command provides considerably more input and control options.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--calendar</samp>
    Displays a calendar and allows you to select a tag.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--entry</samp>
    Enables text input.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--file-selection</samp>
    Allows you to select a file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--password</samp>
    Allows you to enter a password.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--text</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zenith</samp>
    Specifies which text is to be displayed within the dialog.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--title</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">text</samp>
    Gives the dialog a title.

#### Example

The following lines of a script first prompt the user to enter and then display the password:

```
pw=$(zenity --pasword --title 'Your password please ...')
echo "That was your password: $pw" 
```

### zip [options] archive.zip file1 file2 ...

The command creates the ZIP archive <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">archive.zip</samp> and inserts all the specified files into it. The archive is particularly suitable for exchanging data with Windows users. To extract the files again on Linux, you must use [unzip](#U_001.xhtml_unzip).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-r</samp>
    Recursively archives the content of directories.

#### Example

The following command inserts all HTML files passed as parameters into <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">myarchive.zip</samp>:

```
user$ zip myarchive.zip *.html 
```

### zipinfo [options] file.zip

The command returns the table of contents of a ZIP archive.

### zramctl [options] command

In modern distributions (e.g., Fedora), part of the RAM is used as swap space. This is useful because data blocks stored there are compressed. Assume that a virtual machine has 4 GiB of RAM. The ZRAM memory may hold a maximum of 2 GiB of data. If an average compression by a factor of 2 is achieved, the full swap space only uses 1 GiB of RAM. The system can therefore use a total of 5 GiB of memory. Of course, swapping and compressing involves a loss of efficiency, but in practice, the system works amazingly well.

Without any additional parameters, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zramctl</samp> provides information about the use of the system. In this case, ZRAM can hold 2.8 GiB of data. The swap space currently only contains 752 MiB of data. This data can be compressed to 222 MiB. Including various metadata, the swap space takes up 238 MiB.

```
user$ zramctl
NAME       ALGORITHM DISKSIZE   DATA COMPR  TOTAL STREAMS MOUNTPOINT
/dev/zram0 lzo-rle       2,8G 752,3M  222M 238,3M       6 [SWAP] 
```

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-a</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--algorithm lzo|lzo-rle|lz4|lz4hc|842|zstd</samp>
    Uses the desired compression algorithm.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-f</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--find</samp>
    Uses the first free ZRAM device.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-s</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--size</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Creates a ZRAM device of the specified size (e.g., <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-s 1GiB</samp>).

#### Example

The following commands show how to manually set up a (further) ZRAM area for 1 GiB of data:

```
root# zramctl --find --size 1GiB
/dev/zram1
root# mkswap /dev/zram1
root# swapon /dev/zram1 
```

With Fedora, systemd takes care of activating the ZRAM system.

### zypper [options] command

The SUSE-specific <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper</samp> command helps with RPM Package Manager. It installs and updates packages, sets up package sources, and so on. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper</samp> requires the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">libzypp</samp> library, which is an integral part of all current SUSE distributions. The following commands can be abbreviated as long as the meaning is clear, for example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper in</samp> name instead of <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper install</samp> name.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">addrepo [options]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">uri name</samp>
    Sets up a new package source and gives it an alias. The Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) describes the package source, for example, in the following form:

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">http://download.opensuse.org/distribution/leap/15.0/repo/oss/</samp>

    By default, package sources are activated (enabled column in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zypper repos</samp>) and marked for refreshing (refresh column). However, the package source isn’t loaded into the cache for the first time. For this to happen, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper refresh</samp>.

    For package sources whose content doesn’t change, you can avoid regular updates by using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-n</samp> (no refresh) option.

    When you set up a package source, you have the option of importing the key with which the packages are signed. If you’re convinced of the authenticity of the package source, you should agree to the relevant queries.

    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zypper addrepo</samp> doesn’t provide the option of specifying the name of a package source. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zypper repos</samp> therefore displays the alias again in the name column. If you want to set the name and alias separately, you must change the file describing the package source in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/zypp/repos.d/</samp> directory directly.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">clean [--all]</samp>
    Deletes downloaded packages from the cache. The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--all</samp> option also deletes the metadata cache, that is, the description of the packages available in the repositories. This data must be downloaded again before the next package gets installed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dup</samp>
    Performs a distribution update, for example, from openSUSE 15.0 to version 15.1\. You must first perform a regular update and then convert the package repositories to the new version. A restart is required after the update.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">info</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Provides information on the specified package, patch, product, and so on.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">install [-y]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Installs the specified package. Instead of a package, the name of a product, a patch, or a language may also be specified. To install all packages of a predefined pattern, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper install -t pattern</samp> name. With the additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-y</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper</samp> dispenses with queries.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">lifecycle</samp>
    Provides a tabular overview of how long the installed packages will continue to be supplied with updates and for which packages this is no longer the case.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">list-updates [-t package]</samp>
    Shows all available patches, with <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t package</samp> listing both patches and updates.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">patches</samp>
    Lists all available patches.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">patch-check</samp>
    Determines the number of all available patches.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">patch-info [</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Provides information on all patches or the specified patch.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">refresh</samp>
    Tests whether the tables of contents of the package sources have changed and reloads them if necessary—even for package sources that have been set up with the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-n</samp> (no refresh) option. Using the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-f</samp> (force) option, you can reaccess the table of contents even if <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper</samp> believes that nothing has changed.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">remove [-y]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Removes the specified package. The additional <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">--clean-deps</samp> option also uninstalls dependent packages that are no longer required. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-y</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper</samp> waives queries.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">removerepo</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    Removes the package source specified by the URI or alias.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">renamerepo</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">old new</samp>
    Assigns a new alias to the package source.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">repos</samp>
    Lists all installed package sources. The command displays the name and alias of each package source, but not the address (URI). For package sources set up using YaST, the address is used as an alias, which is why the alias column often looks like an address column. However, this doesn’t apply to package sources that are set up using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">zypper addrepo</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">search [options]</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">expression</samp>
    Searches for packages with the specified search expression. By default, only the package names are searched. With <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-d</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper</samp> also searches the package description. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-i</samp> restricts the search to packages that have already been installed, and <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-u</samp> restricts searches to packages that haven’t yet been installed. You can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">–t pattern</samp> to determine a list of predefined package groups.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">update [-t package] [-y]</samp>
    Updates all packages for which patches are available. With the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">-t package</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">zypper</samp> also takes updates, that is, newer program versions, into account.

    Here’s a brief explanation: Updates are complete packages that are available in a newer version than the one installed. Patches, on the other hand, are supplementary or update packages (delta RPMs) that only contain the changes and are therefore much smaller.

#### Example

The first command updates all package sources, the second installs the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">nano</samp> editor, and the third determines which updates are available. The output is heavily abridged due to space limitations.

```
root# zypper refresh
All repositories have been refreshed.

root# zypper install nano
Reading installed packages...
>The following NEW package is going to be installed:  nano
Overall download size: 335.0 K. After the operation, additional 1.2 M
will be used.
Continue? [YES/no]: yes

root# zypper list-updates
...
Repository              Name      Current Version  Available Version  Arch
Haupt-Repository (OSS)  7zip      23.01-4.2        23.01-5.1          aarch64
Haupt-Repository (OSS)  argyllcms 3.1.0-2.1        3.1.0-3.1          aarch64
Haupt-Repository (OSS)  avahi     0.8-31.3         0.8-32.1           aarch64
... 
```

## Special bash Characters

### #&%!

Both when entering commands and in shell programming, you can use a vast number of special characters for various actions. [Table 1](#Sbc_001.xhtml_tSbc.13) summarizes the meaning of the most important special characters.

| Character | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">;</samp> | Separates multiple commands |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">:</samp> | Shell command that does nothing |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.</samp> | Starts the shell program without a separate subshell (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">. file</samp>, corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">source file</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">#</samp> | Introduces a comment |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">#!/bin/sh</samp> | Identifies the desired shell for the shell program |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">&</samp> | Runs the command in the background (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">com &</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">&&</samp> | Conditionally executes the command (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">com1 && com2</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">&></samp> | Redirects standard output and errors (corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">>&</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">&#124;</samp> | Creates pipes (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">com1 &#124; com2</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">&#124;&#124;</samp> | Conditionally executes the command (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">com1 &#124;&#124; com2</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*</samp> | Wildcard character for file names (any number of characters) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">?</samp> | Wildcard character for file names (any character) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">abc</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp> | Wildcard character for file names (one character from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">abc</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">expression</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp> | Short notation for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">test</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">expression</samp> |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[[</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">expr</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]]</samp> | Extended <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">test</samp> syntax, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>-specific |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">(...)</samp> | Executes commands in the same shell (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">(com1; com2)</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{...}</samp> | Groups commands |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{ , , }</samp> | Assembles strings (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">a{1,2,3}</samp> ![image for unicode &#x2192;](bilder/unicode-2192.png) <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">a1 a2 a3</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">{a..b}</samp> | Assembles strings (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">b{4..6}</samp> ![image for unicode &#x2192;](bilder/unicode-2192.png) <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">b4 b5 b6</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">~</samp> | Abbreviation for the home directory |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">></samp> | Redirects output to a file (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">com > file</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">>></samp> | Redirects output to append to existing file |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">>&</samp> | Redirects standard output and errors (corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">&></samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">2></samp> | Redirects standard error output |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen"><</samp> | Redirects input from a file (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">com < file</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen"><<</samp> <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">end</samp> | Redirects input from active file to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">end</samp> |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$</samp> | Marks variables (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">echo $var</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$!</samp> | PID of the last started background process |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$</samp> | PID of the current shell |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$0</samp> | File name of the currently executed shell script |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$1</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$9</samp> | The first nine parameters passed to the command |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$#</samp> | The number of parameters passed to the shell program |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$*</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$@</samp> | The totality of all transferred parameters |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$?</samp> | Return value of the last command (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> = OK or error number) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$(...)</samp> | Command substitution (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">echo $(ls)</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$((...))</samp> | Arithmetic analysis (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">echo $((2+3))</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">${...}</samp> | Various special functions for editing strings |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"..."</samp> | Prevents analysis of most special characters |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">'...'</samp> | Prevents analysis of all special characters |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">`...`</samp> | Command substitution (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">echo `ls`</samp>, corresponds to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">echo $(ls)</samp>) |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">\</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">character</samp> | Cancels the effect of the special character |

**Table 1**     Special bash Characters

# Configuration Files

This section of the Linux Command Reference summarizes the syntax of the most important Linux configuration files. The files are sorted by name, not by the path of the directory in which they are located.

Most of the files presented here apply to all distributions. I’ll explicitly point out distribution-specific peculiarities. For more details on configuration files, see <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">man 5 name</samp>. The number <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">5</samp> indicates that you want to read the documentation of a configuration file, not that of a command that may have the same name.

### /etc/adduser.conf

The Debian/Ubuntu–specific file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/adduser.conf</samp> contains default settings for setting up new users and groups using the commands [adduser](#A_001.xhtml_adduser) and [addgroup](#A_001.xhtml_addgroup). The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">adduser.conf</samp> file contains line-by-line settings in the form <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parameter=value</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ADD_EXTRA_GROUPS=0|1</samp>
    Specifies whether new users should automatically be assigned to the secondary groups listed in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">EXTRA_GROUPS</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">DHOME</samp>
    Specifies the base directory for the home directories (usually <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/home</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">DIRMODE</samp>
    Specifies the access bits with which new home directories are to be set up (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">755</samp> by default).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">DSHELL</samp>
    Specifies the default shell.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">EXTRA_GROUPS="group1,group2,..."</samp>
    Contains a list of secondary groups to which new users are assigned by default (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ADD_EXTRA_GROUPS=1</samp>) or via the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">adduser</samp> option, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">--add_extra_groups</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FIRST_GID</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LAST_GID</samp>
    Determines the range of GIDs for common groups.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FIRST_SYSTEM_GID</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LAST_SYSTEM_GID</samp>
    Determines the range of GIDs for the groups of system accounts.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FIRST_SYSTEM_UID</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LAST_SYSTEM_UID</samp>
    Determines the range of UIDs for system accounts.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">FIRST_UID</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LAST_UID</samp>
    Determines the range of UIDs for ordinary users.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GROUPHOMES=yes|no</samp>
    Specifies whether the home directories of new users should be set up at the location <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/home/groupname/username</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LETTERHOMES=yes|no</samp>
    Determines whether home directories should be placed in subdirectories with the initial letter, such as<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/home/k/kofler</samp>. This can be useful for computers with a large number of accounts.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">NAME_REGEX=yes|no</samp>
    Contains a regular expression (see [grep](#G_001.xhtml_grep)) to which new usernames must correspond.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">SKEL</samp>
    Specifies the directory from which default files are to be copied to a new user directory (usually that’s <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/skel</samp>).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">USERGROUPS=yes|no</samp>
    Specifies whether a separate group should be set up for each user.

#### Example

The following lines show excerpts of the default settings in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">adduser.conf</samp> that are valid on Ubuntu:

```
DSHELL=/bin/bash
DHOME=/home
GROUPHOMES=no
LETTERHOMES=no
SKEL=/etc/skel
FIRST_SYSTEM_UID=100
LAST_SYSTEM_UID=999
FIRST_SYSTEM_GID=100
LAST_SYSTEM_GID=999
FIRST_UID=1000
LAST_UID=29999
FIRST_GID=1000
LAST_GID=29999
USERGROUPS=yes
USERS_GID=100
DIR_MODE=0755
... 
```

### /etc/aliases

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/aliases</samp> file lists forwarding addresses for local email accounts. The email server is responsible for analyzing the file; that is, the file is only relevant if a mail transfer agent (MTA) is running on the computer, such as <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sendmail</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">postfix</samp>.

As a rule, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aliases</samp> are primarily intended for local forwarding, for example, to forward emails from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">webmaster@hostname</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">adminxy@hostname</samp>. As far as the syntax is concerned, it’s also permissible to forward local mails to external hosts; in practice, however, this often fails due to spam protection measures of the external hosts.

Many mail servers don’t analyze <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/aliases</samp> directly, but instead consider a database file that is generated from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aliases</samp> file. For this reason, changes in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">aliases</samp> file often don’t take effect until after the [newaliases](#N_001.xhtml_newaliases) command gets executed.

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/aliases</samp> contains the redirection rules line by line:

```
name: alias1, alias2, alias3 ... 
```

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp> must be a local mail account (without <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@hostname</samp>!). There are multiple options for specifying the alias, whereby it depends on the mail server which variants are supported:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name</samp>
    The email gets redirected to another local mail account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">adresse@host</samp>
    The email gets redirected to an external email address.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/path/file</samp> The email gets added at the end of the specified file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">|command</samp>
    The email gets transferred to the specified command.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">:include:</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/path/file</samp>
    The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">alias</samp> list is read from the specified file.

If multiple aliases are specified, the email gets redirected to all addresses.

#### Example

In the following example, emails addressed to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">postmaster</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">webmaster</samp> are forwarded to the local users <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">michael</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ben</samp>. Emails sent to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">support</samp> are saved in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">support</samp> mailbox and forwarded to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">michael</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">peter.parks@abc-company.com</samp>.

```
root:       michael
postmaster: michael
webmaster:  michael, ben
support:    support, michael, peter.parks@abc-company.com 
```

### /etc/bashrc

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/bashrc</samp> contains default settings for <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>. The file is executed as a <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp> script. All language constructs supported by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bash</samp> are therefore permitted. Usually, the prompt environment variable <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PS1</samp> is set in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bashrc</samp>; in some distributions, the [umask](#U_001.xhtml_umask) value is also used.

The settings in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/bashrc</samp> are supplemented by those in [etc/profile](#04_001.xhtml_profile). <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/profile</samp> applies to all shells, whereas <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">bashrc</samp> only contains the settings that apply specifically to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>. User-specific settings in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">.bashrc</samp> are also taken into account.

### /boot/firmware/config.txt

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config.txt</samp> is a Raspberry Pi–specific file for configuring the hardware. It must be located together with other boot files in the first partition of the SD card. On the Raspberry Pi OS, the file is accessible in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/firmware</samp> directory (for older versions of the Raspberry Pi OS, the file is accessible directly in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot</samp>). The file is analyzed directly by the System-on-a-Chip (SoC) of the Raspberry Pi during the boot process before the kernel gets started.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">arm_64bit=1</samp>
    Loads the 64-bit kernel at system startup (models 3B+, 4B, 400, and 5).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">arm_freq=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Specifies the desired maximum CPU frequency in MHz. The frequency is automatically reduced when the CPU has little to do. If you increase the frequency compared to the default frequency of the CPU (overclocking), you should also increase the voltage slightly (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">over_voltage_delta</samp> parameter).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">camera_auto_detect=1</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">display_auto_detect=1</samp>

    Activates DSI cameras and displays.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cmdline=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">string</samp>
    Passes the character string to the kernel. The parameter is analyzed instead of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/cmdline.txt</samp> file.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gpu_freq=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Indicates the clock frequency of the graphics unit in MHz.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">decode_MPG2=0x12345678</samp>
    <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">decode_WVC1=0x12345678</samp>

    Specifies codes to enable the MPG-2 and VC-1 decoder. The keys can be purchased at [www.raspberrypi.com](http://www.raspberrypi.com) and must match the serial number of the CPU. The serial number is stored in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/proc/cpuinfo</samp> file.

    The <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">decode</samp> parameters are only relevant for models up to 3B+, but no longer for 4B, 400, and 5. The newer models have an H264 hardware decoder. Other video formats are decoded by software. License keys aren’t required at all.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dtoverlay=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">xxx</samp>
    Activates the device tree overlay for a hardware component and loads the corresponding driver modules.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dtparam=audio=on</samp>
    Activates the audio system and loads driver <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">snd_bcm28xx</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dtparam=i2c_arm=on</samp>
    Activates the I²C bus.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dtparam=spi=on</samp>
    Activates the SPI bus.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">over_voltage_delta=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Increases the voltage for the CPU (in micro V, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">50000</samp> corresponds to 0.05V).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">sdram_freq=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Indicates the clock frequency for the main memory (RAM) in MHz.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">usb_max_current_enable=1</samp>
    Activates the USB boot process even with a weak power supply (i.e., with a weak power supply unit). This option is only available from model 5 onward and can result in an unstable operation.

Changes to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config.txt</samp> won’t take effect until the next restart. You can read many <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config.txt</samp> parameters during operation using [vcgencmd](#V_001.xhtml_vcgencmd) <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">get_config</samp>. You can read more <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">config.txt</samp> details here:

[https://elinux.org/RPiconfig](https://elinux.org/RPiconfig)

### /etc/crontab

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/crontab</samp> file is analyzed by the background process <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">crond</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">crontab</samp> contains line-by-line information about when which commands are to be executed for which user account. The cron system makes it possible to perform tasks automatically at predefined times, for example, to start a mirroring process of the file system to an external backup server at 2:30 a.m. on the first Monday in January, April, July, and October.

Each <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">crontab</samp> entry consists of seven columns in one line. The columns are separated from each other by spaces or tabs. The last line must end with a line break character, or it will be ignored. Comments are introduced with the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">#</samp> character at the beginning of the line. It’s not permitted to enter a comment following a <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">crontab</samp> entry.

*   First column (minute)
    Specifies in which minute (0–59) the program is supposed to be executed.

*   Second column (hour) Specifies the desired hour (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>--<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">23</samp>).

*   Third column (day) Specifies the day of the month (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1</samp>–<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">31</samp>).

*   Fourth column (month) Specifies the month (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1</samp>--<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">12</samp>).

*   Fifth column (weekday) Specifies the day of the week (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>--<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">7</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp>, and<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">7</samp> both represent Sunday).

*   Sixth column (user/account) Specifies for which user the command is executed (often that’s root)

*   Seventh column (command) Contains the command to be executed. The command may contain spaces; the entire text up to the end of the line is interpreted as a command.

If a * is entered in the first five columns instead of a number, this field will be ignored. For example, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">15 * * * *</samp> means that the command should always be executed 15 minutes after the full hour, in every hour, on every day, in every month, regardless of the day of the week. Likewise, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">29 0 * * 6</samp> means that the command is executed every Saturday at 0:29 am.

For the time fields, the notation */<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp> is also allowed. This means that the command will be executed every <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>th minute/hour, and so on. Therefore, <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">*/15 * * * *</samp> would mean that the command is executed every quarter of an hour (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>:00, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>:15, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>:30, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>:45).

In the time fields, multiple entries separated by commas and from-to ranges are also permitted. <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1,13</samp> in the second column means that the command is to be executed at 1 am and 1 pm. In the second column, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">2,4,6,8-18,20,23</samp> causes the command to be executed at 2 o’clock, 4 o’clock, 6 o’clock, 8 o’clock, 11 o’clock, and every hour between 6 am and 6 pm.

Instead of the five time columns, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@</samp> abbreviations summarized in [Table 1](#04_001.xhtml_t4.1) may also be used. Another additional rule states that a minus sign at the beginning of the first column prevents syslog from logging the command execution. However, this is only allowed if the sixth column contains <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>.

| Shortcut | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@reboot</samp> | – | Run after each reboot |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@yearly</samp> | <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0 0 1 1 *</samp> | Run once a year |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@annualy</samp> | <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0 0 1 1 *</samp> | Like <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@yearly</samp> |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@monthly</samp> | <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0 0 1 * *</samp> | Run once a month |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@weekly</samp> | <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0 0 * * 0</samp> | Run once a week |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@daily</samp> | <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0 0 * * *</samp> | Run once a day |
| <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">@hourly</samp> | <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0 * * * *</samp> | Run once per hour |

**Table 1**     crontab Interval Abbreviations Replace the First Five Columns

#### SHELL, PATH, and MAIL

Prior to the lines just described for the periodic start of programs, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/crontab</samp> usually contains three lines for setting environment variables. On CentOS, the default settings look as follows:

```
SHELL=/bin/bash
PATH=/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin
MAILTO=root 
```

This means that the command string is executed by the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">bash</samp>, that the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PATH</samp> directories are taken into account when searching for commands, and that emails with output or error messages are sent to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp>.

#### Example

The following three lines in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/crontab</samp> cause a maintenance script to be called 15 minutes after every full hour, a backup tool to be started every Sunday at 00:30 am, and a backup copy of a MySQL database to be created every day at 3:15 am:

```
15  *  *  *  *  root   /usr/bin/maintenance-script
30  0  *  *  0  root   /usr/bin/backup-tool
15  3  *  *  *  mysql  /usr/bin/mysql-backup 
```

#### Other cron Files

In addition to the system-wide <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/crontab</samp> file, you have various other options for defining cron jobs, depending on the distribution:

*   /etc/cron.d In addition to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/crontab</samp>, the cron daemon <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">crond</samp> also analyzed all files in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/cron.d</samp> directory in most distributions. The same syntax rules apply to these files as for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/crontab</samp>.

*   User-specific crontab files Depending on the distribution, user-specific <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">crontab files</samp> are stored in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/spool/cron/</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/spool/cron/tabs</samp> directory. The name of the file indicates which user the file applies to. The sixth column is omitted in these files. The [crontab](#C_001.xhtml_crontab) command is provided for changing user-specific cron entries.

*   cron.hourly, cron.daily, cron.weekly, und cron.monthly In most distributions, the default configuration in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/crontab</samp> contains some entries that cause all script files in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/cron.hourly/*</samp> to be executed with <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> rights once an hour and the script files in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/cron.daily/*</samp> and so on once a day. These files are ordinary script files to which no crontab syntax rules apply. But remember to set the execute bit (<samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">chmod a+x file</samp>)!

    The file names of custom scripts in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cron.daily</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cron.weekly</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">cron.monthly</samp> may only consist of numbers, letters, hyphens, and underscores. As soon as the file name contains even one dot, the script will be ignored! The scripts from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/cron.daily</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-.weekly</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">-.monthly</samp> aren’t executed if the Anacron program is installed.

### /etc/deluser.conf

The Debian/Ubuntu–specific file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/deluser.conf</samp> contains default settings for deleting users and groups using the [deluser](#D_001.xhtml_deluser) and [delgroup](#D_001.xhtml_delgroup) commands. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">deluser.conf</samp> file consists of line-by-line entries in the form <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">parameter=value</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">BACKUP=0|1</samp>
    Specifies whether backups are to be made of the files that are deleted by the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">REMOVE</samp> parameter.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">BACKUP_TO</samp>
    Specifies the location of the backup directory.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">EXCLUDE_FSTYPES="(fs1,fs2,...)"</samp>
    Specifies which file systems should be ignored when searching for the user’s files to create a backup.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ONLY_IS_EMPTY=1</samp>
    Causes groups to be deleted only if they have no members.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">REMOVE_HOME=0|1</samp>
    Specifies whether the account’s home directory should also be deleted.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">REMOVE_ALL_FILES=0|1</samp>
    Specifies whether user files outside the home directory should be deleted, such as spooling files and the email inbox.

#### Example

The following lines show the default settings in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">deluser.conf</samp> that are valid on Ubuntu:

```
REMOVE_HOME = 0
REMOVE_ALL_FILES = 0
BACKUP = 0
BACKUP_TO = "."
ONLY_IF_EMPTY = 0
EXCLUDE_FSTYPES = "(proc|sysfs|usbfs|devpts|tmpfs|afs)" 
```

### /etc/dnf/dnf.conf

The basic settings of the package management system DNF, which is commonly used on Fedora and Red Hat, can be found in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/dnf/dnf.conf</samp>. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/yum.repos.d/*.repos</samp> files also contain detailed settings for the individual package sources.

#### Basic Settings

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">clean_requirements_on_remove = true/false</samp>
    Specifies whether packages that were installed due to dependencies should be automatically removed again as soon as all packages that reference the package are uninstalled. Even if this option is <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">true</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dnf</samp> never removes packages that were explicitly installed using <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf install</samp> without being asked.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">color=never</samp>
    Causes the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dnf</samp> command in the terminal not to use any colors. If you want to use colors, use <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">color=always</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">exactarch=1</samp>
    Causes <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> to only consider updates where the architecture matches the already installed package. Therefore, i386 packages can’t be replaced by newer x86_64 packages.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gpgcheck=1</samp>
    Causes <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> to ensure the authenticity of the packages with a key. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpgcheck</samp> can also be set individually for each package source in deviation from the setting in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">dnf.conf</samp>. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">plugins</samp> decides whether <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> takes plug-ins into account.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">installonly_limit=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">n</samp>
    Controls how many old versions of kernel packages are installed at the same time. The setting affects all packages for which updates are installed in the form of new packages. This procedure ensures that older versions of the affected package are always available as a fallback.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">keepcache=0</samp>
    Causes downloaded packages to not be archived after installation. In general, this is a useful setting because the space required for the packages becomes quite large over time and there’s normally no reason to install the packages a second time. However, it can happen that <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> detects a problem during the installation and aborts the installation process. In that case, the downloaded packages will also get deleted. If you can fix the problem and then repeat the update, all packages must be downloaded again. You can avoid this situation by using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">keepcache=1</samp>. To explicitly delete the downloaded packages in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var/cache/dnf</samp>, you must run <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf clean packages</samp>.

In current Fedora versions, the file contains only a few settings:

```
# File /etc/dnf/dnf.conf on Fedora
[main]
gpgcheck=1
installonly_limit=3
clean_requirements_on_remove=True
best=False
skip_if_unavailable=True 
```

#### Package Sources

The package sources are configured using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">*.conf</samp> files in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/yum.repos.d</samp> directory. The directory wasn’t renamed to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/dnf.repos.d</samp> when switching from <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">yum</samp> to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">[</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">repovariant</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">]</samp>
    Specifies which part of the package source the following settings relate to.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">baseurl=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">url</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mirrorlist=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">url</samp>
    Specifies where the package files are located. With <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">mirrorlist</samp>, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">url</samp> refers to a list of mirror servers. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> automatically decides on one of the mirrors. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> replaces the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$releasever</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$arch</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">$basearch</samp> variables in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">url</samp> with the version number of the Linux distribution and its architecture.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">enabled=0/1</samp>
    Indicates whether the package source is active.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">name=</samp><samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">reponame</samp>
    Specifies the name of the package source.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">metadata_expires</samp>
    Controls how long the metadata downloaded from a package source is valid. <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> saves the metadata in a cache and refrains from downloading it again if the metadata isn’t yet outdated. This saves time and download volume, but can lead to <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> ignoring recent changes in the package source. If necessary, you can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf clean metadata</samp> to force the deletion of the local metadata. This forces <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dnf</samp> to reimport the metadata of all package sources the next time.

The following lines show an excerpt from the file <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/yum.repos.d/#fedora.repo</samp>. This file contains the definition of the package source with the basic packages of the Fedora distribution.

```
[fedora]
name=Fedora $releasever - $basearch
metalink=https://mirrors.fedoraproject.org/metalink? repo=fedora-$releasever&arch=$basearch
enabled=1
countme=1
metadata_expire=7d
repo_gpgcheck=0
type=rpm
gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=file:///etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-fedora-$releasever-$basearch
skip_if_unavailable=False

[fedora-source]
name=Fedora $releasever - Source
... 
```

### /etc/fstab

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/fstab</samp> contains line-by-line entries for all file systems and swap partitions that are to be integrated into the directory tree or activated when the computer is started. Each entry consists of six columns separated by spaces or tabs. Comments are introduced using the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">#</samp> character.

*   First column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Device</samp>)
    Contains the device name of the data medium. Instead of the device name, you can also specify the name or ID of the file system using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">LABEL=xxx</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">UUID=xxx</samp>, or the ID of a GPT partition by using <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">PARTUUID=xxx</samp>.

*   Second column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Path</samp>)
    Specifies the directory in which the data medium is integrated into the file tree. The directories specified in the second column must already exist. For swap partitions, you should enter the keyword <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">none</samp> here.

*   Third column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">File system type</samp>)
    Specifies the file system, such as <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">ext4</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">btrfs</samp>, or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">vfat</samp>. An overview of the most important Linux file systems can be found in the description of the [mount](#M_001.xhtml_mount) command. Due to the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">auto</samp> entry, Linux attempts to recognize the file system itself. For swap partitions that don’t contain an internal file system, you must enter the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">swap</samp> keyword.

*   Fourth column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Options</samp>)
    Contains the desired <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">mount</samp> options. A reference of the options for all important file systems can be found in this book in the [mount](#M_001.xhtml_mount) command. If you don’t require any options, you should enter the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">defaults</samp> keyword instead. Multiple options are only separated by commas, not by spaces!

*   Fifth column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Dump</samp>)
    Contains information for the Unix program <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">dump</samp>. This column is ignored on Linux. It’s common to enter <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1</samp> for the system partition and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> for all other partitions or disks.

*   Sixth column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fsck</samp>)
    Specifies whether the file systems are to be checked at system startup and in which order. Often <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">1</samp> is entered for the system partition and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">0</samp> for all other partitions. This means that only the system partition is checked for errors at computer startup and, if necessary, repaired by [fsck](#F_001.xhtml_fsck). If you want further partitions to be checked automatically, you must enter the number <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">2</samp> for these partitions. This means that the check should take place after the system partition has been checked. If entries in the fifth and sixth columns in /etc/fstab are missing, 0 is assumed.

#### Example

The following example shows the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">fstab</samp> file of a server with LVM and RAID. The boot partition is located on RAID device <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/dev/md/0</samp>. The system and data directories use logical volumes as a storage location. The file systems for <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/</samp>, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/var</samp>, and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/backup</samp> are checked on restart. If an error occurs in the root file system, the file system is mounted in read-only mode.

```
/dev/md/0        /boot    ext2   defaults           0  0  
/dev/vg0/root    /        ext4   errors=remount-ro  0  1 
/dev/vg0/var     /var     ext4   defaults           0  2 
/dev/vg0/backup  /backup  ext4   defaults           0  2 
/dev/vg0/swap    swap     swap   defaults           0  0 
```

### /etc/group

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/group</samp> contains a list of all group names with the corresponding group identification numbers (GIDs) and a list of all users who belong to the group. To administrate the groups, you usually use the commands [groupadd](#G_001.xhtml_groupadd), [groupmod](#G_001.xhtml_groupmod), and [groupdel](#G_001.xhtml_groupdel).

The line-by-line entries in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">group</samp> file consist of four columns, each separated by colons:

*   First column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Group name</samp>)
    Indicates the name of the group.

*   Second column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">unused</samp>)
    Contained the hash code of the group password in older Linux versions. Current Linux distributions save the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">x</samp> character here. If group passwords are defined, they are saved in [etc/gshadow](#04_001.xhtml_gshadow).

*   Third column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GID</samp>)
    Contains the group identification number. In most distributions, GIDs smaller than 1000 are reserved for system accounts.

*   Fourth column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Accounts</samp>)
    Contains a comma-separated list of all users who are members of this group. However, only secondary memberships are taken into account, but the primary group of each user is stored in the fourth column of [etc/passwd](#04_001.xhtml_passwd).

#### Example

The following lines show excerpts from <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/group</samp> on a computer that serves as a web server and development server. Each system account and each regular user has its own group. The members of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">admin</samp> group can use <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">sudo</samp> to perform administration work. The members of the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">devel</samp> group have special access rights to the version management system.

```
root:x:0:
bin:x:1:
admin:x:109:kofler,huber
...
kofler:x:1000:
huber:x:1001:
miller:x:1002:
devel:x:1023:kofler,huber,miller,gruber,smith
... 
```

### /etc/default.grub

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/default/grub</samp> contains default settings for the Linux boot loader GRUB 2\. These settings are only taken into account when the GRUB configuration file [boot/grub/grub.cfg](#04_001.xhtml_grub.cfg) is regenerated—either automatically during a kernel update or manually using the command [update-grub](#U_001.xhtml_update-grub) (Debian, Ubuntu) or [grub-mkconfig](#G_001.xhtml_grub-mkconfig) (Fedora, openSUSE).

The following list describes the most important keywords:

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT</samp>
    Taken into account by <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">10_linux</samp> and specify which options are to be passed to the kernel. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX</samp> options apply to every boot; the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT</samp> options are added additionally for standard boot, but not for recovery mode.

*   GRUB_DEFAULT=0
    Specifies which GRUB menu entry should be selected by default. The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">"saved"</samp> setting means that the last selected menu item is activated. However, this only works if the GRUB files are located in an ordinary partition! If, on the other hand, LVM or RAID is involved, GRUB can’t save any environment variables after the menu selection.

    Another option is to assign the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">menuentry</samp> string of the desired menu item to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_DEFAULT</samp>. However, you must be careful to keep the spelling exact.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_DISABLE_OS_PROBER=false</samp>
    Activates the search for other operating systems when recreating <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">boot.cfg</samp>. (There’s nothing like a double negative.)

    Since around 2022, GRUB has been configured in such a way that only entries for the active distribution appear in the GRUB menu, but not entries for starting other distributions or Windows. These entries used to be necessary (BIOS) but are now largely obsolete (EFI). In case something goes wrong with the EFI configuration, the GRUB menu entries are a good backup/redundancy.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_DISABLE_LINUX_UUID=true</samp>
    Causes GRUB to pass the root directory to the kernel as the device name. Without this option, GRUB passes the UUID of the file system. This setting applies only to the start of the active distribution (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">10_linux</samp> script), not to other distributions.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_DISABLE_RECOVERY=true</samp>
    Prevents <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">update-grub</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">grub2-mkconfig</samp> from adding menu entries for starting Linux in recovery mode to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grub.cfg</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR</samp>
    Is analyzed by the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/grub.d/10_linux</samp> script and specifies the name of the current distribution.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_ENABLE_BLSCFG=true</samp>
    Causes the menu items from the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/loaders/entries</samp> directory to be taken into account when booting in addition to <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grub.cfg</samp>. This makes the configuration files clearer and corresponds to the procedure of systemd-boot (an alternative boot procedure).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_GFXMODE</samp>
    Specifies the graphics mode in which GRUB should run (by default in a resolution of 640 × 480 pixels).

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_HIDDEN_TIMEOUT</samp>
    Is important if GRUB only recognizes a single Linux distribution on your computer during installation. In this case, <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_HIDDEN_TIMEOUT</samp> specifies how long the user has to press Shift to display the GRUB menu. The screen remains black during this wait time. If multiple operating systems are installed, GRUB ignores the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_HIDDEN_TIMEOUT</samp> #setting and displays the menu.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_HIDDEN_TIMEOUT_QUIET=true</samp>
    Prevents a countdown counter from being displayed during the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_HIDDEN_TIMEOUT</samp> wait time. If you want the GRUB menu to always be displayed, set the lines <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_HIDDEN_TIMEOUT=...</samp> and <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_HIDDEN_TIMEOUT_QUIET=...</samp> with the comment character <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">#</samp>.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_TIMEOUT=n</samp>
    Specifies how many seconds GRUB waits for a menu item to be selected. If this time elapses without user input, GRUB starts the selected operating system. The time set here only comes into effect when the GRUB menu appears at all.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_TERMINAL=console</samp>
    Causes GRUB to run in text mode. However, no Unicode characters can be displayed there.

#### Example

On Ubuntu, the configuration file contains the following settings:

```
# File /etc/default/grub
GRUB_TIMEOUT=5
GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR="$(sed 's, release .*$,,g' /etc/system-release)"
GRUB_DEFAULT=saved
GRUB_DISABLE_SUBMENU=true
GRUB_TERMINAL_OUTPUT="console"
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=
GRUB_DISABLE_RECOVERY="true"
GRUB_ENABLE_BLSCFG=true 
```

### /boot/grub/grub.cfg

Depending on your distribution, either <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/grub/grub.cfg</samp> or <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/grub2/grub.cfg</samp> will be the configuration file for the current GRUB version 2\. This file is generated automatically, and direct changes aren’t recommended. To influence the behavior of GRUB, you can change various default settings in [etc/default.grub](#04_001.xhtml_default.grub) or insert statements in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/grub.d/*custom</samp>, which are then adopted directly in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grub.cfg</samp>. To recreate <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grub.cfg</samp> afterward, you can run one of the following commands:

```
root# update-grub                                  
(Debian and Ubuntu)
root# grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg       
(Fedora, openSUSE) 
```

Modern GRUB versions only save the basic settings in <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">grub.cfg</samp>. The actual menu entries for starting Linux are stored in separate files (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/boot/loader/entries/*.conf</samp>; see also <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">GRUB_ENABLE_BLSCFG=true</samp> in [etc/default.grub](#04_001.xhtml_default.grub)).

### /etc/gshadow

The <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/gshadow</samp> file contains the hash codes of the group passwords and other group administration data. For security reasons, only <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">root</samp> may read and modify this file.

The line-by-line entries in the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gshadow</samp> file consist of four columns, each separated by colons:

*   First column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Group name</samp>)
    Indicates the name of the group.

*   Second column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">hash code</samp>)
    Contains the hash code of the group password or an asterisk (no password). The use of group passwords is unusual for security reasons. If you do decide to do this, you need to set the group password via the <samp class="listingcharacter konsolenbefehl">gpasswd</samp> command. Anyone who knows the group password can then switch to this group using [newgrp](#N_001.xhtml_newgrp), even if they aren’t a member of the group.

*   Third column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Administrators</samp>)
    Contains a comma-separated list of group administrators (account names). Group administrators can change the group password and add or remove other members from the group.

*   Fourth column (<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">Members</samp>)
    Contains a comma-separated list of group members who are allowed to activate the group without entering a password.

On many Linux systems, the <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">gshadow</samp> file is unused and reads as follows:

```
root:*::
daemon:*::
bin:*::
sys:*:: ... 
```

### /etc/host.conf

<samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">/etc/host.conf</samp> controls the resolver library, which specifies how unknown host names are resolved during network operations.

*   <samp class="listingcharacter listingzeichen">multi on|off</samp>
